S 级 系统治疗 RCT IF 35.9
新辅助短程放疗序贯卡瑞利珠单抗联合化疗对比标准治疗用于局部晚期直肠癌（UNION）：多中心开放标签随机III期试验预设中期分析
Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial.
The Lancet. Oncology · 2026-11 · Tao K, Lin Z, Zhang P, Chi P, Xiao Y, Hou Z, et al.
研究背景：UNION 是首个评估放疗、免疫治疗与化疗联合的新辅助策略对比局部晚期直肠癌标准治疗的 III 期试验，其前期已报告主要终点（BIRC 评估的 pCR 率 39.8% vs 15.3%）阳性，本次为预设的 EFS 期中分析。
核心结果：2021 年 7 月至 2023 年 3 月共入组 231 例患者（试验组 113 例、标准治疗组 118 例），中位随访约 35-37 个月。3 年研究者评估 EFS 率试验组为 91.3%（95% CI 83.9-95.4），标准治疗组为 77.4%（67.9-84.4），分层 HR 0.33（0.15-0.71），双侧 log-rank p=0.0029。安全性方面，3-4 级治疗相关不良事件以淋巴细胞、白细胞、中性粒细胞及血小板减少为主，试验组发生率总体不高于标准治疗组；治疗相关严重不良事件为 19% vs 13%，试验组发生 1 例治疗相关死亡（化疗相关脓毒症休克，与卡瑞利珠单抗无关）。
意义与启示：短程放疗序贯卡瑞利珠单抗联合 CAPOX 显著改善局部晚期直肠癌 3 年 EFS，且安全性可控，支持该“放疗+免疫+化疗”新辅助模式作为潜在治疗选择。对课题的启示是：需进一步与当代全程新辅助治疗（TNT）策略进行头对头比较，并探索疗效预测标志物与器官保留路径。
评分明细：设计 28/30 · 验证 12/15 · 机制 5/15 · 影响力 20/20 · 契合度 20/20 = 85/100 ｜ 等级理由：多中心随机III期试验预设中期分析，EFS获益显著（HR 0.33），具改变局部晚期直肠癌新辅助实践潜力。

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The environmental impact of endoscopic techniques remains poorly defined. We compared procedure-related environmental outcomes between conventional endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) and underwater EMR (U-EMR) for colorectal lesions. In this prospective pilot procedure-based life cycle assessment of the resection phase, 10-25-mm colorectal lesions underwent EMR or U-EMR across three endoscopy units. Outcomes included global warming potential (GWP, kg CO Forty-nine procedures were included: 23 EMR and 26 U-EMR. U-EMR was associated with lower procedure-related environmental burden than conventional EMR, persisting after normalization for en bloc resection. No. 165/26.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of mortality, with most cases refractory to immunotherapy. Distinguishing tumor-induced from steady-state mucosal T cell responses represents a critical barrier to understanding CRC immunity. Using orthotopic transplantation of CRC organoids with and without metastatic potential, combined with T cell fate-mapping, we show that nonmetastatic tumors elicit early recruitment of CD8αβ+ and CD4+ T cells with cytotoxic and Th1-like programs, whereas pro-metastatic (pro-Met) tumors induce a naïve-like, hypoactivated state. Tumor-infiltrating CD4+ T cells underwent clonal expansion, including clones recognizing microbial and dietary antigens. T cells physically interacting with tumors, identified by universal LIPSTIC, were enriched for expanded and cytotoxic clones. Fate-mapped T cells from nonmetastatic tumors suppressed tumor growth in an IFN-γ-dependent manner. Mechanistically, pro-Met tumors downregulated MHCII, and Ciita targeting in nonmetastatic organoids reduced CD4+ clonal expansion and led to tumor progression. Together, these findings define divergent early T cell trajectories associated with CRC metastasis, indicating that ineffective local immune engagement precedes metastatic dissemination.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dysregulated expression of prolyl 4-hydroxylase subunit alpha 3 (P4HA3) has been identified in Colon cancer, breast cancer, head and neck cancers, etc. and is closely associated with tumor progression. However, its specific roles in gastric cancer (GC), particularly regarding alterations in metabolic pathways, are remain unknown. This study investigated how P4HA3 influences glycolytic metabolic reprogramming and the proliferation and invasion of gastric cancer cells via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway. To determine P4HA3 levels in GC tissues and corresponding cell lines, bioinformatics methods, immunohistochemical (IHC) staining and Western blotting (WB) were conducted. Furthermore, gain- and loss-of-function experiments, including cell viability assays (CCK-8), colony-forming tests, scratch wound assays and Transwell invasion experiments, were utilized to explore the influence of P4HA3 on GC cell growth, motility and invasive capacity. Changes in cellular metabolism were assessed using the Seahorse system (under normoxic conditions), including measurements of basal metabolism, glycolytic capacity and mitochondrial respiration (oxidative phosphorylation), as well as Western blot analysis of key glycolytic proteins. Additionally, the involvement of the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling axis was examined by gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA), WB analysis and pharmacological inhibition studies. GC tissues and cell lines exhibited markedly increased levels of P4HA3, correlating significantly with decreased overall survival (OS). Experimental data indicated that P4HA3 facilitated GC cell proliferation, migration and invasion. In addition, P4HA3 enhanced glycolytic activity and increased the expression of key glycolysis-related proteins. Unexpectedly, P4HA3 also increased mitochondrial respiration under the assay conditions, suggesting that P4HA3 may induce a broader metabolic activation rather than an exclusively glycolytic shift. Mechanistically, the glycolysis-enhancing effects of P4HA3 were found to require PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling (as shown by inhibitor studies). P4HA3 promotes glycolysis via the PI3K/AKT/mTOR signaling pathway, thereby promoting the progression of gastric cancer.

展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To systematically evaluate preoperative nutritional status as a determinant of postoperative outcomes in patients undergoing surgery for colorectal cancer (CRC). This systematic review used the PRISMA 2020 framework and it was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420261292825). An extensive comprehensive literature review was performed from January 2010 to December 2025 using Embase, PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and Cochrane CENTRAL databases. All peer-reviewed articles that assessed preoperative nutrition and reported the postoperative outcomes of adult patients who had CRC surgical procedures were included. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was used to assess the risk of bias. Studies were not quantitatively pooled due to clinical and methodological heterogeneity, but instead the results were synthesized qualitatively. In total, 312 records were identified. Finally, seven studies that included 2656 patients who had CRC surgical resection fulfilled all of the full-text eligibility criteria. The seven studies had a low overall risk of bias (NOS 7-9). All studies found a relationship between poor preoperative nutrition (assessed using various tools, including Nutritional Risk Screening 2002, prognostic nutritional index, subjective global assessment/patient-generated subjective global assessment, and Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition criteria) and an increase in postoperative complications. In addition, patients with nutritionally compromised status exhibited increased morbidity due to infections, longer postoperative hospital stays, and greater mortality rates. Some studies also indicated that preoperative malnutrition was a predictor of poorer long-term oncologic outcomes (such as reduced overall survival and disease-free survival). Preoperative malnutrition and nutritional risk are associated with adverse postoperative outcomes following colorectal surgery. Routine nutritional assessment may help to identify patients at higher risk and guide perioperative management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Predicting tumour response to neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT) in locally advanced rectal cancer remains an unresolved clinical problem. The substantial inter-patient variability in pathological response means that molecular biomarkers capable of prospective patient stratification are urgently needed. However, transcriptomic biomarker studies in this setting are prone to methodological limitations - particularly data leakage - that produce irreproducible performance estimates and hinder translation. This study aimed to identify a biologically interpretable transcriptomic signature of nCRT response in rectal cancer through an integrative machine learning framework designed with strict attention to leakage prevention and methodological transparency. Gene expression microarray profiles from 46 rectal cancer patients (24 responders, 22 non-responders; GEO: GSE35452; 22,189 gene features) were analysed. Phenotype was defined by the Mandard tumour regression grade (TRG) [1]: responders = TRG 1-2 (complete or near-complete pathological response); non-responders = TRG 3-5. All patients received fluoropyrimidine-based concurrent chemoradiotherapy followed by surgery. A preliminary variance filter - applied to the complete dataset because variance is a class-label-free operation - retained the 1000 most variable genes; sensitivity analyses at 500, 2000, and 5000 genes are reported in Supplementary Note S1. A label-leakage-controlled sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline was constructed in which all preprocessing - including standardisation and feature selection - was performed independently within each training fold. Four feature selection algorithms were applied per fold (ANOVA F-statistic, mutual information, L1-penalised logistic regression, and Random Forest importance), and a fold-specific consensus gene set was constructed at each outer iteration (Algorithm ??). Eight classifiers were evaluated as an exploratory multi-algorithm comparison. The pooled out-of-fold AUC across the five outer folds was 0.987 for Gaussian Naïve Bayes (95% percentile bootstrap CI: 0.949-1.000), with a mean fold-wise AUC of 0.990 This discovery study demonstrates that an integrative, label-leakage-controlled machine learning framework can identify biologically coherent transcriptomic candidates for nCRT response prediction in rectal cancer. Given the single retrospective cohort of 46 patients and absence of independent external validation, all findings should be regarded as hypothesis-generating. External validation in independent prospective cohorts is required before any clinical or translational inference can be drawn.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The rising cancer incidence and mortality rates support continued investigation of molecular markers in breast cancer (BC), gastric cancer (GC), and colorectal cancer (CRC). mRNAs and lncRNAs are involved in cancer-related regulation, and altered expression of TRIM29, NORAD, and MIR497HG has been reported in different tumor types. This study evaluated these three transcripts as candidate diagnostic biomarkers in BC, GC, and CRC using public expression datasets and RT-qPCR validation. Bioinformatics and RT-qPCR analyses showed cancer type-specific expression patterns. MIR497HG was downregulated in BC, GC, and CRC in both public-data analysis and RT-qPCR validation. NORAD was significantly upregulated in GC and CRC, while its change in BC was not significant by RT-qPCR. TRIM29 was downregulated in BC and upregulated in CRC by RT-qPCR. In GC, GEO microarray analysis and RT-qPCR supported TRIM29 downregulation, while ENCORI analysis suggested upregulation, indicating dataset-dependent differences. ROC analysis supported the diagnostic potential of these transcripts in a cancer type-specific manner. Bioinformatics and RT-qPCR analyses revealed TRIM29 was downregulated in BC and upregulated in CRC, but It reduced in GC despite microarray data suggesting otherwise. TRIM29 showed significant interaction with hsa-miRNA-3940-5p. MIR497HG expression was notably reduced in BC, GC, and CRC across both microarray and RT-qPCR. It also exhibited strong links with MUC2, MUC4, MUC5AC, and MUC5B. While ENCORI indicated a slight decrease in NORAD expression in BC, qRT-PCR results were not significant. However, NORAD was significantly upregulated in GC and CRC, interacting with key cancer-related genes like MUC4, MUC2, MUC16, MUC3A, and MUC5AC. The findings support TRIM29, NORAD, and MIR497HG as candidate diagnostic biomarkers in GC and CRC, while TRIM29 and MIR497HG showed diagnostic relevance in BC. Pathway enrichment suggested a possible association between TRIM29-related genes and interferon-related signaling, but this result requires functional validation. The observed correlations between TRIM29 and the lncRNAs MIR497HG and NORAD should be interpreted as co-expression patterns and not as evidence of direct molecular interaction.

Daraxonrasib, an orally administered pan-RAS inhibitor, is undergoing clinical evaluation for pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma, colorectal cancer, and non-small cell lung cancer. Defining its pharmacokinetic profile is therefore critical for ongoing progress. Accordingly, a simple and sensitive UPLC-QqQ-MS/MS assay was developed and validated to quantify daraxonrasib in canine plasma and whole blood. Proteins were precipitated with a 20:80 (v/v) acetonitrile-methanol solution containing 0.1% formic acid. Chromatographic separation was performed on a Waters ACQUITY BEH C18 column (50 mm × 2.1 mm, 1.7 μm). The mobile phase consisted of 2 mM ammonium acetate and acetonitrile, each containing 0.1% formic acid, delivered at 0.4 mL/min. Multiple reaction monitoring transitions for daraxonrasib and the internal standard were m/z 811.5 → 680.3 and m/z 724.4 → 396.2, respectively. Calibration standards showed linear response from 1.0 to 1000 ng/mL (r > 0.998). The assay met validation criteria for specificity, recovery, limit of quantification, accuracy, and precision. Finally, this validated method was applied to a dog pharmacokinetic study of daraxonrasib. This report outlines the drug's pharmacokinetic characteristics and supports its continued development.

Adenomatous polyposis, defined clinically as the occurrence of 10 or more cumulative adenomatous colorectal polyps, is the most common form of polyposis. The phenotype may be classic with hundreds to thousands of polyps or attenuated with less than 100 polyps. Genetic counseling and multi-gene panel testing that includes at least all known adenomatous polyposis syndromes should be completed for either presentation. This article summarizes the established and emerging genetic etiologies of adenomatous polyposis, highlights current challenges in diagnosis and management, and discusses advances in genetic testing and potential targeted therapies.

Liposomal irinotecan, characterized by its favorable pharmacologic properties and reduced systemic toxicity compared to irinotecan, has demonstrated superior therapeutic potential. This multicenter, single-arm study was conducted to evaluate the efficacy and safety of liposomal irinotecan, capecitabine, and bevacizumab as a second-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Patients with histologically confirmed mCRC who had progressed following first-line oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy were enrolled in this study. The treatment regimen was liposomal irinotecan (70 mg/m Between March 2024 and July 2024, 63 patients were enrolled, with a median age of 60.0 years (range: 37.0-79.0). Among the patients who received at least one tumor assessment, the objective response rate and disease control rate were 22.9% (11/48; 95% CI, 12.0-37.3) and 89.6% (43/48; 95% CI, 77.3-96.5), respectively. With a median follow-up of 16.2 months (range: 0.5-28.5), the median progression-free survival was 8.1 months (95% CI, 7.3-8.9), and the median overall survival was 19.5 months (95% CI, 15.2-23.8). The most common grade 3 to 4 adverse events were diarrhea (12.7%), neutropenia (11.1%), and fatigue (6.3%). The combination of liposomal irinotecan, capecitabine, and bevacizumab demonstrated promising antitumor activity and a manageable safety profile in patients with mCRC who had failed first-line oxaliplatin-based therapy. These results suggested that this regimen is a clinically feasible second-line treatment option for mCRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Classical colorectal anastomoses performed with sutures or staples rely on tissue penetration, which may serve as a nidus for microabscess formation and contribute to anastomotic leakage. Magnetic compression anastomosis (MCA) offers a completely nonpenetrating alternative for tissue approximation. However, earlier MCA systems required delayed luminal patency, rendering them unsuitable for colorectal surgery where immediate bowel continuity is essential. A novel magnetic compression system engineered to maintain immediate luminal patency has been developed, overcoming a key limitation of prior MCA platforms. This innovation enables intracorporeal colorectal anastomosis using a nonpenetrating technique compatible with minimally invasive surgery and may represent a biologically distinct approach to anastomotic healing. This was a first-in-human, early-phase prospective safety and feasibility study conducted at a single tertiary referral center for minimally invasive colorectal surgery. A consecutive series of 25 adult patients undergoing elective laparoscopic or robotic colorectal resection received intracorporeal anastomosis using a self-forming magnetic compression system following a standardized operative protocol. The primary outcome was anastomotic leak within 30 postoperative days. Secondary outcomes included technical feasibility, adverse events, device performance, and anastomotic patency assessed during 60 days of follow-up. All procedures were completed using minimally invasive techniques without conversion to open surgery. Intracorporeal magnetic compression anastomoses were technically successful in all cases. No anastomotic leaks were observed within 30 days. Adverse events occurred in 6 patients (24%), all classified as Clavien-Dindo Grade I and managed conservatively. Postoperative imaging and/or endoscopic evaluation demonstrated complete anastomotic patency and healing in all patients, with no evidence of stenosis, obstruction, or delayed transit during 60 days of follow-up. In this first-in-human experience, intracorporeal magnetic compression colorectal anastomosis using the self-forming system was feasible and demonstrated a favorable short-term safety profile, with consistent anastomotic patency and absence of leaks. Although limited by small sample size, single-center design, and lack of a comparator group, these results support further prospective and comparative studies to define the role of MCA in colorectal surgery. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epigenetic silencing of tumour suppressor genes is a pivotal early event in colorectal cancer (CRC) pathogenesis. PDZ and LIM Domain 4 (PDLIM4) is a member of the PDZ-LIM family with context-dependent roles in tumour progression across different malignancies. However, its specific role and epigenetic regulation in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain elusive. We integrated multi-omics datasets and clinical cohorts to evaluate PDLIM4 expression and promoter methylation. Stool DNA was analyzed to assess the feasibility of non-invasive detection of PDLIM4 promoter methylation. PDLIM4 knockout and overexpression cell lines were constructed to perform functional assays including proliferation, apoptosis, and stemness. In vivo experiments were validated utilizing xenograft mice or an azoxymethane (AOM)/ dextran sulphate sodium salt (DSS) CRC mouse model with intestinal epithelial cell-specific overexpression of PDLIM4. Mechanistic investigations were conducted using coimmunoprecipitation coupled with mass spectrometry, RNA sequencing, ChIP-qPCR and pharmacological rescue experiments. We identified a progressive loss of PDLIM4 protein along the normal-adenoma-carcinoma sequence, driven by DNMT3A-mediated promoter hypermethylation, and lower PDLIM4 expression was associated with adverse patient prognosis. PDLIM4 methylation was also significantly increased in stool DNA from CRC patients compared with healthy controls. Mechanistically, genetic ablation of PDLIM4 significantly blunted the therapeutic efficacy of the DNA demethylating agent 5-Azacytidine against CRC. Functionally, PDLIM4 restoration suppressed CRC cell proliferation and stemness while enhancing apoptosis in vitro, and reduced tumour growth in both AOM/DSS and xenograft models in vivo. At the molecular level, PDLIM4 interacted with BTF3 and promoted its autophagic-lysosomal degradation, thereby limiting PI3K/Akt signalling, with NTRK2 identified as a potential transcriptional target linking BTF3 to PI3K/Akt activation. DNMT3A-mediated silencing of PDLIM4 is an early epigenetic event that facilitates CRC progression. PDLIM4 suppresses tumour growth by promoting BTF3 degradation, thereby restricting PI3K/Akt signalling. Thus, PDLIM4 methylation may have potential as a biomarker for early CRC detection. DNMT3A-mediated PDLIM4 promoter hypermethylation is an early event in colorectal tumorigenesis. Restoring PDLIM4 suppresses CRC proliferation and stemness while promoting apoptosis in vitro and in vivo. PDLIM4 promotes the autophagic-lysosomal degradation of BTF3 and restrains PI3K/Akt signalling. Stool DNA analysis supports the potential of PDLIM4 methylation as a non-invasive CRC biomarker.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A 12-year-old thoroughbred mare was presented with colic and diarrhea. Clinical examination revealed mild tachycardia with injected mucous membranes. Abdominal ultrasonography identified thickened colon walls, an irregular, mottled liver, and free fluid. The mare had elevated liver enzymes and electrolyte abnormalities that continued to worsen during hospitalization and included hypoalbuminemia. Despite intensive and varied medical treatments, the mare's condition deteriorated and she was humanely euthanized. Postmortem examination revealed a large adenocarcinoma with osseous metaplasia in the right dorsal colon and mesocolon with multifocal metastasis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The management of early-stage colorectal cancer (CRC) is undergoing a significant transformation, from traditional clinical and pathological staging to a dynamic, molecular signature-driven approach utilizing circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA). Postoperative detection of minimal residual disease (MRD) has emerged as a strong independent prognostic biomarker. It identifies patients at high risk of recurrence while reducing unnecessary exposure to adjuvant chemotherapy for those cured by surgery alone. However, this success reveals a critical therapeutic dilemma. Standard adjuvant chemotherapy has a limited ability to eliminate MRD. Consequently, the molecularly defined high-risk subgroup currently has no proven therapy that effectively eradicates MRD and improves survival. In this review, we synthesize emerging therapeutic strategies designed to address this unmet need. We discuss ongoing clinical trials investigating intensified cytotoxic regimens, MRD-guided targeted therapies, and novel immunotherapy combinations, especially for microsatellite-stable (MSS) disease. Furthermore, this review examines the role of ctDNA dynamics as a surrogate endpoint for regulatory drug approval, a crucial step in accelerating the development of these novel therapies. Finally, we address the real-world challenges of implementation, including access disparities, equity gaps, and standardized clinical algorithms. We highlight how emerging technologies and global collaborations may further refine MRD detection. The eradication of MRD represents the next frontier in curing CRC; however, this demands focused clinical research and validated surrogate endpoints to translate prognostic insights into tangible survival benefits.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Polygenic risk scores (PRS) and lifestyle factors are associated with colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether their associations and joint effects vary according to age at CRC onset remains unclear. We evaluated age-related heterogeneity in the associations of genetic risk and lifestyle with CRC and examined their additive interaction in early- and late-onset CRC. We analyzed data from 405,453 cancer-free participants aged 38-73 years at baseline in the UK Biobank. PRS and a healthy lifestyle score (based on eight modifiable factors) were assessed. Age-scale Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) for CRC risk by age at onset. Heterogeneity across age intervals was assessed using likelihood ratio tests. Additive interaction was assessed using the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI), and differences in standardized incidence rates were evaluated. During a median follow-up of 13.65 years, 6620 CRC cases were identified. Compared with low genetic risk, high genetic risk was associated with HRs of 3.72, 3.32, 2.80, and 2.01 for CRC occurring at ages < 55, 55-64, 65-74, and ≥ 75 years, respectively, with significant heterogeneity across age intervals (p for heterogeneity < 0.001). Compared with a favorable lifestyle, the corresponding HRs for an unfavorable lifestyle were 1.10, 1.50, 1.58, and 1.28, respectively, with evidence of overall heterogeneity (p for heterogeneity = 0.015). For late-onset CRC, positive additive interactions were observed for an unfavorable lifestyle combined with intermediate or high genetic risk, whereas no such interaction was detected for early-onset CRC. The associations of genetic susceptibility and baseline lifestyle with CRC varied according to age at onset. Positive additive interaction between genetic risk and an unfavorable lifestyle was observed for late-onset but not early-onset CRC. These findings provide further evidence that the relative and joint associations of genetic and lifestyle factors with CRC vary across the life course.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Phosphatidylinositol 3-kinase catalytic subunit type 3 (PIK3C3) is central to autophagy, which supports cancer adaptation to environmental stresses and may contribute to drug resistance. KRAS-mutant cancers have been reported to require autophagy for survival. We investigated the influence of KRAS mutation status on the roles of PIK3C3 in colorectal cancer (CRC) cell viability and chemosensitivity in vitro, as well as its association with patient prognosis. The clinical significance of PIK3C3 expression in relation to KRAS mutation status was evaluated by immunohistochemistry in patients with advanced CRC. Cell viability, colony formation, and spheroid formation assays were performed using CRC cell lines. In KRAS-wild-type (KRAS-WT) Caco-2 and Colo320 cells, PIK3C3 and the KRAS/ERK pathway appeared to positively regulate each other. In contrast, PIK3C3 inhibition did not reduce p-ERK levels or induce significant p62 accumulation in KRAS-mutant SW480 and HCT116 cells. PIK3C3 knockdown reduced cell viability but increased resistance to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) in Caco-2 and Colo320 cells, whereas the opposite effect was observed in SW480 and HCT116 cells. Transfection with a KRAS-mutant plasmid sensitized Caco-2 cells to 5-FU accompanied by reduced thymidylate synthase (TS) and β-catenin levels following PIK3C3 inhibition. Clinically, high PIK3C3 expression was associated with KRAS mutation and poorer survival in patients with advanced CRC. Its adverse short-term prognostic association was more pronounced in KRAS-mutant CRC than in KRAS-WT CRC. Based on preclinical in vitro findings, PIK3C3 appears to support KRAS-WT and KRAS-mutant CRCs in different ways. Notably, PIK3C3 inhibition enhances 5-FU sensitivity in KRAS-mutant CRC cells, potentially through TS regulation, and warrants further investigation as a therapeutic strategy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative complications following colorectal cancer resection remain common despite technical advances, yet associations of psychosocial and spiritual health with surgical risk are poorly characterized. This prospective cohort study enrolled 985 patients undergoing colorectal cancer resection at a single tertiary center (2013-2021). Preoperative assessments included health behaviors (Smart Management Strategy for Health Assessment Tool), self-rated health status (5 Health Status Questionnaire), and health-related quality of life (EORTC QLQ-C30). The primary outcome was any complication within 30 days; secondary outcomes were complication subtype (surgical vs. non-surgical) and severity (minor vs. major). Multivariable stepwise logistic regression was performed per outcome. Overall, 305 patients (31.0%) experienced at least one complication: 235 surgical (23.9%), 106 non-surgical (10.8%), and 32 major (3.3%). Lower positive-thinking behavior was associated with overall (OR 1.52; 95% CI 1.11-2.07) and minor complications (OR 1.52; 95% CI 1.11-2.09); lower helping-others behavior with surgical complications (OR 2.06; 95% CI 1.27-3.35); and poor spiritual health with non-surgical complications (OR 2.11; 95% CI 1.37-3.26). Preoperative fatigue showed the strongest association with major complications (OR 4.04; 95% CI 1.60-10.21). Distinct psychosocial and spiritual health domains were associated with distinct complication subtypes, with preoperative fatigue showing the strongest association with major complications. Whether these reflect modifiable contributors or markers of underlying vulnerability cannot be determined from an observational design; the findings identify patients who may benefit from additional supportive resources rather than a basis for risk stratification.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor necrosis factor-related apoptosis-inducing ligand (TRAIL) is a promising anticancer agent; however, the frequent emergence of acquired TRAIL resistance limits its therapeutic efficacy in colorectal cancer (CRC). Cancer stem cells (CSCs) contribute to therapeutic resistance, recurrence, and metastatic progression, yet the relationship between TRAIL resistance and CSC enrichment remains unclear. Here, we demonstrate that acquired TRAIL resistance drives CD44-dependent stemness and malignant behavior in CRC. TRAIL-resistant HCT116 cells (HCT116-TR) exhibited increased sphere formation, enhanced motility, and a marked expansion of CD44⁺ cells. CD44⁺ HCT116-TR cells isolated by antibody-based sorting displayed the strongest CSC-like properties, heightened TRAIL resistance, and robust activation of the SPHK1/STAT3 axis, indicating that CD44 upregulation is a major determinant of TRAIL-induced aggressiveness.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related incidence and mortality worldwide, with accumulating evidence indicating that its tumorigenesis and progression are tightly linked to epigenetic dysregulation. Histone deacetylases (HDACs) are key epigenetic regulators involved in gene transcription, cell-cycle regulation, and cancer progression, whereas the therapeutic benefits of conventional HDAC inhibitors are frequently compromised by limited selectivity and resistance development. Recently, dual-target HDAC inhibitors (HDACis) have attracted considerable attention as an emerging paradigm in anticancer drug development. These multitarget strategies can simultaneously enhance synergistic antitumor efficacy and alleviate the compensatory resistance commonly associated with single-target therapies via multi-mechanistic interventions. Accordingly, the concurrent modulation of HDACs and additional therapeutic targets represents a viable therapeutic strategy for CRC. In this review, we systematically summarize the recent progress of dual-target HDAC is in CRC treatment, with particular emphasis on their therapeutic potential and implications for future translational research and clinical practice.

Colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis is a primary cause of cancer-related mortality. The occurrence of colorectal liver metastasis (CRLM) is closely associated with tumor immune escape, through which cancer cells evade immune surveillance via multiple mechanisms, thereby promoting metastatic dissemination. RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) play crucial roles in gene expression regulation. Neuro-oncological ventral antigen 1 (NOVA1), an important RBP, is often dysregulated in cancer progression. This study aimed to investigate the molecular mechanisms underlying the role of NOVA1 in CRLM. Cell proliferation, migration, and invasion were evaluated using Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8), colony formation assays, Transwell assays and wound healing assays. Flow cytometry was used to analyze CRC cell apoptosis. Subsequently, CRC cells were co-cultured with CD8 NOVA1 expression was downregulated in CRC tissues and cell lines. Functional assays demonstrated that NOVA1 overexpression inhibited CRC cell proliferation (colony formation reduced by approximately 50%), migration (migrated cells reduced by approximately 40%), and immune escape (CD8 NOVA1 influences the immune escape, proliferation, and migration of CRC cells by directly binding to NRXN1 mRNA and regulating its mRNA stability. This study reveals the key regulatory role of the NOVA1-NRXN1 axis in CRLM, suggesting that this axis may serve as a potential therapeutic target and prognostic biomarker. Targeting the NOVA1-NRXN1 signaling pathway may provide a novel strategy for clinical intervention in CRLM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rehabilitation is increasingly recognized as an essential component of oncology care, but there remains limited evidence regarding its broader impact on patient outcomes. This study examined the associations of inpatient cancer rehabilitation with survival and post-discharge healthcare utilization among patients with diverse cancer types. We conducted a multicenter retrospective cohort study using cancer registry-linked claims data from designated cancer care hospitals in Osaka Prefecture, Japan. The study cohort comprised adults newly diagnosed with cancer from 2020 to 2022. The exposure was receipt of inpatient cancer rehabilitation during the initial cancer treatment hospitalization. The primary outcome was all-cause mortality within 1 year of diagnosis, and the secondary outcomes were unplanned readmissions and out-of-hours outpatient visits within 28 days of discharge. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards and Fine-Gray subdistribution hazards models were used, adjusting for demographic and clinical factors. Among 123,955 patients from 69 hospitals, 20,561 (16.6%) underwent inpatient cancer rehabilitation. Rehabilitation was associated with a lower risk of mortality (hazard ratio, 0.83; 95% confidence interval, 0.79-0.87). Lower mortality risks were also observed for the following cancer types: lung, upper gastrointestinal, colorectal, hepato-biliary-pancreatic, breast, and hematologic cancers. Among 115,046 patients included in the post-discharge healthcare utilization analyses, rehabilitation was associated with lower risks of unplanned readmissions (subdistribution hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval, 0.73-0.85) and out-of-hours visits (0.92; 0.84-0.999). Inpatient cancer rehabilitation was associated with lower mortality and reduced post-discharge healthcare utilization. These findings support the further integration of rehabilitation into routine oncology practice.

The albumin-derived neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (Alb-dNLR), reflecting nutritional and inflammatory status, has been reported as a prognostic marker in malignancies. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rectum-preserving colorectal surgery, with low or ultra-low anastomosis, became the standard of care with advances in laparoscopic and now robotic surgery. As a downside, it is not uncommon for function to be affected, causing low anterior resection syndrome (LARS), which is a common postoperative challenge. To determine the correlation of using the predictive preoperative POLARS scores with actual postoperative LARS scores for patients undergoing rectal resections with low pelvic anastomosis. A multicentre, prospective study evaluating LARS was conducted with patients undergoing rectal resection with restoration of bowel continuity. Defaecatory function was assessed preoperatively using the POLARS scoring questionnaire and 6 months after the surgery using the LARS scoring questionnaire. The scores were then compared to determine any correlations. A total of 310 patients from 13 centres were enrolled, of whom 95 had complete paired POLARS and postoperative LARS score data. POLARS predicted minor LARS in 69 patients (72.6%), whereas 25 patients (26.3%) reported minor LARS postoperatively. Major LARS was predicted by POLARS in 21 patients (22.1%), whereas 24 patients (25.3%) self-reported major LARS postoperatively. Only 7 of these 24 major-LARS cases (29.2%) were correctly categorized as major LARS by POLARS. For detecting major LARS, POLARS showed sensitivity of 29.2%, specificity of 80.3%, positive predictive value of 33.3% and negative predictive value of 77.0%. Spearman correlation between predicted and observed scores was weak but statistically significant (rho = 0.21, p = 0.042). Bland-Altman analysis demonstrated a mean bias of +7.99 points with 95% limits of agreement from -19.23 to 35.20, reflecting systematic overprediction. POLARS showed weak positive correlation with postoperative bowel function and demonstrated low sensitivity but moderate specificity for major LARS. It systematically overestimated LARS severity in many patients. While POLARS may help identify some individuals at elevated risk, it is insufficient as a stand-alone tool for accurate prediction of postoperative LARS severity and should be combined with clinical judgement and patient-reported follow-up.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Long non-coding RNAs play a wide role in colorectal cancer (CRC). But the function of LINC01140 in CRC has not yet been revealed. This study aims to explore the functional mechanism of LINC01140 in CRC, with the expectation of providing new therapeutic targets for CRC. The histological expression of LINC01140 was examined to evaluate its clinical predictive value in CRC prognosis. The potential downstream (miR-942-5p/NRXN1) of LINC01140 were predicted using bioinformatics methods, and their targeted relationship was verified through RNA pull-down and dual luciferase reporter assays. The effects of this regulatory axis on the functions of CRC cells and cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) were evaluated through CCK-8 or Transwell experiments. Cisplatin- and oxaliplatin- tolerant CRC cell lines were established for chemotherapy resistance studies. LINC01140 exhibited significant downregulation in CRC tumor tissues and was associated with an unfavorable prognosis. The chi-square test revealed the association between LINC01140 and TNM stage as well as lymphatic metastasis. Overexpression of LINC01140 suppressed the proliferation and migration/invasion capacities of CRC cells and alleviated their chemotherapy resistance, reducing the IC50 values of cisplatin and oxaliplatin for drug-resistant cells. LINC01140 acted as a sponge for miR-942-5p and inhibited the functions of CRC cells and CAFs by upregulating NRXN1. Co-culture with CAFs promoted the chemoresistance of CRC cells. Upregulation of LINC01140/NRXN1 or inhibition of miR-942-5p in CAFs attenuated this ability. LINC01140 may serve as a biomarker in CRC prognosis. It suppresses CRC cells and hinders CAF activation, alleviating chemotherapy resistance by regulating miR-942-5p/NRXN1.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic surgery was introduced to enhance surgical performance; however, evidence of superiority over conventional laparoscopy remains inconsistent in colorectal cancer treatment. Inspired by Sir Dave Brailsford's concept of marginal gains, we hypothesized that small improvements of robotic platforms might be associated with improved surgical outcomes. This study aimed to evaluate whether robotic surgery was associated with a higher probability of achieving a 'perfect' operation for colorectal cancer. Two consecutive periods were compared, laparoscopic surgery from January 2019 to February 2021 and robotic surgery from March 2021 to February 2025. The primary outcome was a composite measure termed 'perfect' operation defined as; no conversion, complications, reoperation, readmittance, mortality, R0 resection and mesocolic/rectal surgical plane. Multivariable logistic regression and propensity score matching were used to adjust for confounding. A total of 916 patients were included (500 robotic, 416 laparoscopic). Baseline characteristics were comparable. The rate of 'perfect' operations was higher after robotic surgery (63.6% vs. 43.8%, p < 0.001). After multivariable adjustment, robotic surgery remained independently associated with a higher likelihood of a 'perfect' operation (adjusted OR 2.60, 95% CI: 1.96-3.46; p < 0.001). Findings were consistent across colonic and rectal subgroups and after propensity score matching. In addition, length of stay (LOS) was reduced in robotic rectal cancer surgery from an average of 5-4 days. Robotic surgery was associated with a 2.5-fold increased rate of a 'perfect' operation for colorectal cancer and reduced LOS after rectal resection, supporting the concept of cumulative marginal gains associated with robotic surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival. This open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m Between July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group. In this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX. Comparison of this promising new treatment strategy with contemporary total neoadjuvant therapy strategies is warranted. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transanal total mesorectal excision (TaTME) combined with intersphincteric resection (ISR) has emerged as a sphincter-preserving surgical option for very low rectal cancer. However, multicenter data evaluating oncological outcomes and risk factors for local recurrence (LR) following TaTME with ISR remain limited. This study aimed to evaluate oncological outcomes and identify risk factors for LR in patients undergoing TaTME with ISR. This multicenter retrospective cohort study included patients who underwent TaTME with ISR for lower rectal cancer at 26 institutions participating in the Japan Society for Laparoscopic Colorectal Surgery. Oncological outcomes and clinicopathological factors associated with LR were analyzed. Multivariable analysis was performed to identify independent risk factors for LR. A total of 224 patients were included. The 3-year LR, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS) rates were 7.3%, 79.5%, and 98.1%, respectively. Multivariable analysis identified circumferential resection margin (CRM)/radial margin (RM) positivity as the key independent risk factor for LR. In contrast, pathological features, including histopathological classification, lymphatic invasion, vascular invasion, perineural invasion, and tumor budding, reflected tumor biological aggressiveness rather than surgical performance. A biological aggressiveness score demonstrated a stepwise increase in LR risk according to the number of adverse pathological factors. TaTME combined with ISR is a feasible sphincter-preserving option for lower rectal cancer, with acceptable oncological outcomes in a nationwide multicenter cohort. Both surgical factors, particularly margin status, and tumor biological characteristics may contribute to LR risk. Careful margin assessment and close postoperative surveillance are essential for optimizing oncological outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Distant metastasis remains the leading cause of colorectal cancer (CRC) mortality, yet the underlying molecular mechanisms remain incompletely defined. Integrating RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) profiling and clinical validation, we identified NDFIP2 as significantly downregulated in metastatic CRC. Functionally, NDFIP2 loss drove epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), stemness, and metastasis via PI3K/AKT hyperactivation. Mechanistically, NDFIP2 serves as an adaptor recruiting the E3 ligase NEDD4 to induce K48-linked polyubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of DDX3X. Unrestrained DDX3X resolves R-loops at the GNG13 promoter and recruits the transcription factor CTCF, synergistically enhancing GNG13 transcription to amplify PI3K/AKT signaling. Targeting this vulnerability, we engineered a cell-permeable NDFIP2-derived iRGD-conjugated peptide (ND-iRGD). In vivo administration of this construct suppressed DDX3X/GNG13/PI3K/AKT signaling, thereby attenuating distant metastasis and prolonging murine survival. Collectively, NDFIP2 acts as a critical metastasis suppressor via the DDX3X/R-loop/GNG13 axis, presenting the ND-iRGD peptide as a promising translatable therapeutic strategy for metastatic CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chronic intestinal inflammation is a major driver of colorectal cancer (CRC). As the mucosal barrier's frontline sentinel, the intestinal epithelium initiates the inflammation-to-cancer transition. However, the early cell-intrinsic events that convert inflammatory responses into a sustained pro-tumorigenic program remain unclear. In this study, we identify MAGI3 as an intestinal epithelial guardian progressively lost during inflammation-associated colorectal tumorigenesis. Low MAGI3 correlates with heightened inflammatory activity and poor prognosis. Inflammation-induced epithelial MAGI3 downregulation drives STAT3 hyperactivation, CCL2 upregulation, and recruitment of M2-like tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs), thereby promoting an immunosuppressive microenvironment and tumor progression. By contrast, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) demonstrated that MAGI3 overexpression reshapes the composition of TAMs and limits M2-like TAM infiltration. Mechanistically, the PDZ1 domain of MAGI3 binds directly to the C-terminus of STAT3, blocking the SH2 pocket, impairing the interaction between STAT3 and IL-6R/JAK2, and ultimately inhibiting STAT3 phosphorylation at Tyr705. Clinically, the MAGI3-STAT3 axis offers a new therapeutic strategy for chemotherapy-resistant CRC, with low MAGI3 expression predicting enhanced sensitivity to STAT3 inhibitors. Collectively, these findings establish MAGI3 as a gatekeeper of the intestinal epithelium in inflammation-associated CRC, with the MAGI3-STAT3 axis regulating TAM recruitment. Targeting the MAGI3-STAT3 axis could offer an early intervention to reverse inflammation-to-cancer transition.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are critical regulators of colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, yet the mechanisms governing their functional plasticity and state transitions remain incompletely understood. Here, we uncover a tumor-driven fibroblast state transition in CRC characterized by loss of leptin receptor (Lepr) expression and acquisition of pro-inflammatory features. We show that cooperative TNFα and TGFβ signaling drives this reprogramming, accompanied by repression of the Tcf21-Lepr regulatory axis. Fibroblasts undergoing this transition acquire the capacity to promote macrophage recruitment and accelerate tumor development. Loss of Lepr or Tcf21 in fibroblasts upregulates Csf3, which contributes to the enhanced macrophage-recruiting capacity of the reprogrammed fibroblasts. Consistently, blockade of TNFα and TGFβ signaling disrupts fibroblast reprogramming and attenuates macrophage infiltration. Together, our findings uncover how inflammatory signaling reshapes stromal cell states to promote macrophage accumulation, ultimately fostering a pro-tumorigenic niche that accelerates CRC progression.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies integrate immune checkpoint blockade and VEGF inhibition within a single molecule, offering a potential strategy to overcome angiogenesis-associated immune resistance. At the 2026 ASCO Annual Meeting, the randomized phase 3 HARMONi-6 trial demonstrated an overall survival benefit with ivonescimab plus chemotherapy over tislelizumab plus chemotherapy in previously untreated advanced squamous non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), extending survival evidence to an active PD-1-based first-line comparator. Exploratory phase 2 studies of pumitamig, SSGJ-707, and HB0025 reported encouraging activity in first-line NSCLC, while phase 1 and 2 studies of IMM2510 and ivonescimab-based regimens suggested activity after prior immunotherapy. Smaller exploratory studies also reported activity in perioperative head and neck cancer, colorectal cancer, endometrial cancer, and mucosal melanoma. Collectively, these findings highlight the clinical potential of PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecific antibodies, with the strongest evidence in first-line squamous NSCLC and broader applications remaining hypothesis-generating. Future development should prioritize predictive biomarkers, resistance mechanisms, optimal treatment sequencing, and careful assessment of immune-related and VEGF-associated toxicities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastatic progression is a major cause of colorectal cancer (CRC)-related mortality, but the molecular mechanisms underlying this process remain incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the role of lysine-specific demethylase 1A (KDM1A) in CRC metastasis and angiogenesis-related phenotypes. Using transcriptomic profiling, chromatin immunoprecipitation, functional assays, and preclinical models, we found that KDM1A contributes to CRC cell migration, invasion, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), with NRP2 upregulation serving as an important associated mechanism. Mechanistically, KDM1A was associated with reduced enrichment of H3K9me1/2 at the NRP2 regulatory region, supporting a chromatin-associated mechanism for NRP2 transcriptional regulation. TGF-β/Smad signaling may also provide an auxiliary input to NRP2 expression. In parallel, KDM1A increased hypoxia-inducible factor 1α (HIF-1α) protein stability and VEGFA expression, thereby contributing to angiogenesis-related activity. Our data further suggest that NRP2 and VEGFA-related signaling are linked to PI3K/AKT/mTOR pathway activation and metastatic phenotypes in CRC cells. Pharmacological inhibition of KDM1A with GSK-LSD1 reduced liver metastatic burden and vascularization within metastatic lesions in preclinical models. Together, these findings suggest that KDM1A contributes to CRC metastatic progression through related mechanisms involving NRP2 regulation, HIF-1α/VEGFA-associated angiogenesis, and AKT pathway modulation, providing a basis for further investigation of KDM1A as a potential therapeutic target in metastatic CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Temporal eating patterns, such as eating time, frequency, and regularity, may be associated with cancer outcomes through circadian and metabolic pathways, but evidence remains limited. We aimed to systematically review prospective studies examining associations between temporal eating patterns and cancer incidence or mortality. Following PRISMA guidelines, PubMed and Embase were searched from inception to September 2, 2026. Eligible studies included prospective cohorts of adults assessing eating or fasting duration, nighttime eating, breakfast frequency or timing, meal regularity, or eating frequency in relation to cancer incidence or mortality. Meta-analyses were conducted when ≥3 studies examined comparable exposure-outcome pairs, and the quality of meta-evidence was evaluated using the NutriGrade scoring system. Risk of bias was assessed using the Risk of Bias for Nutrition Observational Studies tool. Seventeen prospective cohort studies were included. Findings for eating or fasting duration and nighttime eating varied across studies for both cancer incidence and mortality. Lower breakfast frequency was associated with higher cancer mortality and colorectal cancer incidence in some studies, but not with breast cancer incidence. Greater eating-time variability and unrestrained eating were associated with higher cancer mortality, with unrestrained eating also associated with higher colorectal cancer incidence. Associations between eating frequency and cancer outcomes varied across studies and cancer sites. A meta-analysis of three studies showed a non-significant inverse association between eating frequency and colorectal cancer incidence in both categorical (HR = 0.81, 95% CI: 0.64-1.03) and dose-response analyses (HR per 1 time/day increase = 0.95, 95% CI: 0.89-1.01), with very low-quality meta-evidence. Risk of bias varied across domains, with common concerns related to confounding and exposure changes over follow-up. Findings from cohort studies suggest potential associations between temporal eating patterns and cancer outcomes, but the evidence remains limited and heterogeneous, underscoring the need for further investigation. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Xianlian Jiedu Decoction (XLJDD) has long been used clinically in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC). Our preliminary work indicated that XLJDD exerts anti-CRC activity by attenuating inflammation, restoring gut microbiota balance, and modulating signaling pathways such as CXCR2/PI3K/AKT. However, the bioactive constituents and the precise molecular mechanisms underlying these effects remain poorly defined. The present study sought to clarify the active components and mechanisms of XLJDD in CRC, thereby providing a scientific basis for its further therapeutic application. This study aimed to investigate the inhibitory effect of XLJDD on tumor stemness in CRC and to elucidate the underlying molecular mechanisms. An orthotopic CRC mouse model was established and treated with XLJDD for 21 days. The chemical constituents of XLJDD were characterized by UPLC-MS/MS, and treatment-related metabolic alterations were profiled by plasma metabolomics. Tumor tissues were subjected to single-cell RNA sequencing to identify differentially expressed genes, which were validated by Western blot and immunohistochemistry. In vitro, HCT116 and HT29 cells were evaluated for proliferation, sphere-forming capacity, stemness-marker (CD44/CD133) populations by flow cytometry, and protein expression by Western blot. CRYAB-knockdown cell lines were generated to assess proliferation (CCK-8), apoptosis, cell-cycle distribution, and stemness-marker expression. Transcriptome sequencing combined with Ingenuity Pathway Analysis (IPA) was performed across treatment groups (NC, NC+XLJDD, CRYAB-KD, CRYAB-KD+XLJDD) to define the downstream signaling pathways regulated by XLJDD. XLJDD significantly suppressed tumor growth in the orthotopic CRC model. Plasma metabolomics revealed clear separation between groups, with reduced phenylalanine and glycerophospholipid metabolism and enhanced energy metabolism in XLJDD-treated mice. Single-cell RNA sequencing of tumors identified cancer-cell clusters with high CRYAB and ALDH3A1 expression that were markedly suppressed following XLJDD treatment. In vitro, XLJDD reduced proliferation, sphere formation, CD44 These findings indicate that XLJDD constrains CRC stemness through a CRYAB-driven regulatory program rather than a single isolated target. By coupling CRYAB to STC1 and the OCT4/SOX2/NANOG network, the study connects XLJDD's anti-tumor activity to a defined stemness axis and positions CRYAB as a tractable node within it. Because CRYAB knockdown both reproduced and reinforced the anti-stemness effect of XLJDD, the data suggest that XLJDD acts, at least in part, by downregulating CRYAB, offering a mechanistic rationale that extends beyond its previously reported anti-inflammatory and metabolic effects. This study demonstrates for the first time that XLJDD suppresses CRC tumor stemness by targeting the CRYAB-STC1 axis. By integrating metabolomics, single-cell transcriptomics, and functional validation, this work provides new evidence that XLJDD regulates cancer stemness and offers experimental support for its therapeutic potential in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) indication in stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) remains challenging, as clinical, pathological, and ctDNA inadequately predict benefit. Immune infiltration correlates with outcome, yet transcriptional signatures have not been systematically evaluated in prospective trial cohorts. We aimed to identify a prognostic transcriptional signature in high-risk stage II CRC patients treated with ACT within the TOSCA trial. From the TOSCA trial, 124 high-risk stage II patients were selected using a matched case-control design, with matching based on center, pT stage, ACT regimen, and treatment duration. Whole-transcriptome sequencing was performed on FFPE samples. MSI status was inferred bioinformatically. Prognostic associations were assessed using log-rank tests and multivariable Cox models adjusting for MSI status and tumor sidedness. Seventy-two samples met RNA quality criteria. Median follow-up was 70.9 months; 40% were right-sided, 60% received FOLFOX, 54% 3-month ACT, and 19% were MSI-high. Transcriptomic analyses highlighted immune-regulatory and TGF-β/stromal programs associated with outcome. A biologically defined Immune Exclusion (IE) phenotype, characterized by low ICR and high Hallmark TGF-β signaling, was observed in approximately 28% of patients and was associated with shorter DFS (HR=2.22, p = 0.036). This association persisted after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness (HR=2.47, p = 0.018). A reduced seven-gene IE signature (rIE) was subsequently derived and was also associated with shorter DFS after multivariable adjustment (HR=2.83, p = 0.012). The IE phenotype and its reduced rIE signature were associated with shorter DFS in high-risk stage II colon cancer and represent exploratory candidate prognostic biomarkers requiring validation in independent cohorts. Identifying stage II colorectal cancer (CRC) patients who will relapse despite standard adjuvant chemotherapy (ACT) remains an unmet clinical need. Current clinicopathological and ctDNA-based approaches do not fully resolve risk stratification in this setting. In this study, whole-transcriptome profiling of high-risk stage II CRC from the prospective TOSCA trial identified an Immune Exclusion (IE) signature associated with significantly shorter disease-free survival, which remained associated with DFS after adjustment for MSI status and tumor sidedness. These findings provide a biological framework for further validation in independent cohorts and for future hypothesis-generating studies aimed at refining risk stratification and exploring alternative therapeutic approaches.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Overcoming therapeutic resistance in colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major clinical challenge, highlighting the need for strategies targeting epigenetic drivers. Targeted protein degradation emerged as a powerful approach to selectively eliminate disease-relevant proteins. We reported the development of two series of PROTACs based on the clinical-stage HDAC inhibitor entinostat, by recruiting either VHL or CRBN E3 ligases. Compounds 4b and 4h, representative of the two series of degraders, induced robust, time-dependent HDAC degradation with a clear-cut preference for HDAC3, leading to apoptosis and reduced viability in CRC models. The antitumor activity of the new degraders was proved in patient-derived colon cancer organoids and in the CRC CAM model. The role of acetylation in gene regulation and expression in CRC was investigated measuring p21 and stemness markers such as CD44 and LGR5. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that new degraders effectively target HDAC3 and exert anti-tumor activity across multiple CRC models.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Perioperative sleep disturbances and anxiety may worsen postoperative pain, increase opioid consumption, and delay recovery. Melatonin and zolpidem improve sleep, but their effects on postoperative pain remain incompletely characterized. PubMed, Embase, and Scopus were searched for studies published between 2000 and 2025 investigating preoperative melatonin or zolpidem in surgical patients. Two reviewers independently screened records using Rayyan, resolving discrepancies through consensus. Of 404 records identified, 119 duplicates were removed. Of 285 screened records, 269 were excluded, leaving 16 articles for inclusion. Melatonin demonstrated anxiolytic, analgesic, and chronobiotic effects. It reduced salivary cortisol, modulated stress responses, attenuated proinflammatory pathways, and supported circadian recovery, particularly in patients with preoperative anxiety. Its analgesic efficacy was comparable to clonidine in some trials, with a favorable safety profile. Zolpidem improved preoperative sleep quality and reduced postoperative pain and opioid consumption, potentially through improved sleep architecture. In colorectal surgery, zolpidem also reduced tumor necrosis factor-alpha (TNF-α). Melatonin demonstrated more consistent effects on cortisol, suggesting distinct physiological mechanisms. Melatonin and zolpidem offer complementary perioperative benefits. Melatonin may provide broader neuroendocrine and analgesic effects, whereas zolpidem may benefit patients with insomnia. Larger trials are needed to optimize dosing and patient selection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The da Vinci 5 introduces changes in operative workflow and instrument control, but its comparative performance in rectal cancer surgery remains uncertain. We compared operative efficiency and short-term outcomes after platform introduction and explored platform-derived intraoperative measurements. This retrospective single-center study included 202 patients undergoing robot-assisted rectal cancer surgery from July 2025 to September 2026 (Xi, n = 109; da Vinci 5, n = 93). Propensity-score overlap weighting addressed measured differences. The primary outcome was total operative time. HC3 inference was checked using 2,000 bootstrap replicates with propensity-score re-estimation. Retrieved Case Insights records were summarized descriptively. The adjusted difference in total operative time was - 6.9 min (HC3 95% confidence interval [CI], - 24.4 to 10.6; P = 0.439); the bootstrap 95% CI was - 21.8 to 7.8 min. The adjusted risk difference for Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ II complications was - 9.4% points (HC3 95% CI, - 19.8 to 0.9; P = 0.074). Margin positivity occurred in only three patients and was reported descriptively. Inference for postoperative hospital stay depended on the variance method. We did not detect a statistically clear reduction in total operative time after the introduction of the da Vinci 5. Secondary outcomes remain exploratory. Exploratory Case Insights analysis provided descriptive information on instrument-tip force and surgical workflow, warranting further prospective validation of their clinical relevance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Robotic colorectal learning-curve studies commonly define proficiency using operative time or cumulative-sum thresholds, which may not capture maturation of a heterogeneous program. In this retrospective longitudinal cohort, we analyzed 364 consecutive robotic colorectal procedures from a single-surgeon, single-center program using prior global robotic colorectal experience as a continuous exposure. Principal clinical outcomes were postoperative length of stay (LOS) and major morbidity (Clavien-Dindo grade III or higher); operative duration was the principal process/efficiency outcome. Multivariable log-linear models adjusted for procedure family, robotic platform, associated procedures, age, and American Society of Anesthesiologists (ASA) class; major morbidity was analyzed with Firth penalized logistic regression. Each doubling of (1 + prior experience) was associated with 5.1% shorter LOS (95% CI 2.2%-7.9% shorter; p < 0.001) and 5.3% shorter operative duration (95% CI 3.3%-7.4% shorter; p < 0.001). Restricted cubic spline analysis showed no evidence of LOS non-linearity (p = 0.621) but significant non-linearity for operative duration (p < 0.001). Major morbidity occurred in 15/364 procedures (4.1%); the adjusted Firth odds ratio was 1.48 per experience doubling (95% profile-likelihood CI 0.84-3.64; p = 0.208). Because cumulative experience and calendar time were essentially collinear, estimates represent longitudinal program maturation rather than an isolated causal surgeon-experience effect. Greater cumulative experience was associated with shorter LOS and operative duration, but the LOS association should be interpreted as a program-level signal that may also reflect evolving perioperative care; major morbidity remained uncommon but imprecisely estimated longitudinally.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Germline pathogenic variants (PVs) of the APC gene cause familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), whereas PVs in DNA mismatch repair (MMR) genes underlie Lynch Syndrome (LS), formerly known as hereditary non polyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC). The coexistence of both hereditary syndromes in a single individual has been reported extremely rarely and only in a few patients, and the scant literature on this topic suggests an earlier onset and a more rapidly worsening form of colorectal cancer, compared with subjects who carry a single mutation. Here we describe a 16-year-old female who presented with multiple colonic polyps as well as an invasive colorectal carcinoma, and was found to harbor heterozygous pathogenic variants (PV) both in APC and MSH2 genes. Our patient also represents the unique reported case harboring both a MSH2-EPCAM large rearrangement in association with a frameshift APC PV. This case illustrates the unique clinical phenotype that can arise from simultaneous FAP and LS pathogenic mutations, highlights the importance of comprehensive genetic testing in young patients with aggressive disease and ultimately suggests a personalized follow-up and surveillance program in this case.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Many studies have investigated the roles of exosomes in colorectal cancer (CRC), but the global research landscape and future directions in this field remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to integrate epidemiological evidence with bibliometric analysis to map the research landscape of exosome research in CRC. Global Burden of Disease (GBD) data were analyzed to assess the geographic and socioeconomic distribution of CRC incidence and mortality, and a bibliometric analysis was conducted to systematically evaluate publication trends, research clusters, and emerging themes. Network-based community detection was conducted using the Walktrap algorithm. GBD analysis revealed pronounced geographic and socioeconomic disparities in CRC incidence and mortality, indicating a heterogeneous global disease burden. Knowledge mapping demonstrated a rapid and sustained increase in publications on exosomes in CRC. Clustering analyses identified four major research domains: exosome biogenesis and molecular characteristics; tumor microenvironment and therapy resistance; exosomal non-coding RNAs in tumor progression and metastasis; and exosomal biomarkers for diagnosis and prognosis. The Walktrap analysis further identified biomarkers, diagnosis, liquid biopsy, drug delivery, and immunotherapy as highly relevant but relatively underdeveloped research directions. Overall, this integrated epidemiological and knowledge-mapping study provides a comprehensive overview of the evolution and structure of exosome research in CRC and highlights key research hotspots and emerging frontiers that may guide future investigations into precision diagnostics and therapeutic innovation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) patients with comorbid diabetic peripheral neuropathy (DPN) face an increased risk of oxaliplatin-induced dose-limiting toxicity (DLT). This study aimed to develop a machine learning model to predict chemotherapy tolerance and investigate nonlinear feature associations within the predictive framework. We retrospectively analyzed 513 CRC patients with DPN. Five machine learning algorithms were developed and evaluated, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to explore feature associations. The XGBoost model demonstrated the highest discriminative performance in predicting DLT (AUC = 0.880), significantly outperforming logistic regression (p = 0.002). SHAP analysis showed that cumulative oxaliplatin dose, poor glycemic control (HbA1c > 8.0%), and systemic inflammation (NLR) were associated with increased model-predicted risk of DLT. Interaction analyses further identified nonlinear model-level associations between oxaliplatin exposure and metabolic and neurological features. The XGBoost model combined with SHAP explanations provides an exploratory framework for dynamic risk stratification during treatment. These findings represent associative predictive patterns and require prospective, external validation before clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) detection after curative-intent treatment is one of the strongest prognostic biomarkers in colorectal cancer (CRC), but its clinical utility remains incompletely established. Randomised trials have shown that ctDNA-informed management can reduce adjuvant chemotherapy exposure in selected stage II colon cancer, yet non-inferiority was not established in stage III disease, and cytotoxic escalation for ctDNA-positive molecular residual disease (MRD) has not improved recurrence-free survival. These mixed interventional results do not diminish the prognostic validity of ctDNA, but suggest that its clinical utility depends on four interacting considerations: the biological state represented by ctDNA positivity, the timing of testing and intervention, assay and sampling heterogeneity, and trial design. Serial ctDNA dynamics may provide additional biological and prognostic information, as sustained clearance, transient clearance, persistence, and re-emergence are unlikely to represent equivalent states of MRD. Western Pacific studies have led the field, including GALAXY and ALTAIR in Japan and Taiwan, DYNAMIC in Australia, FIND and CINTS-R in China, and CLAUDIA in Korea. However, regional implementation is constrained by uneven laboratory infrastructure, cost, regulatory access, and limited evidence from Southeast Asia and Pacific lower-resource settings. Outside clinical trials, ctDNA should refine prognosis rather than dictate omission, intensification, or initiation of treatment. Future trials should align assay performance, biological timing, and intervention mechanism, and use patient-centred endpoints capable of demonstrating that acting on ctDNA improves outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Seychelles, the smallest country in Africa but with the highest GDP per capita, has experienced rapid socioeconomic development. We analysed 20-year cancer incidence trends (2005-2024) using data from the Seychelles National Cancer Registry (SNCR). Annual age-standardised incidence rates (ASRs), average annual percentage changes (AAPCs), and stage at diagnosis (for the four major cancers) were calculated. Incidence rates for the most recent decade (2015-2024) were also compared with those in selected African countries and high Human Development Index (HDI) countries. Among men, prostate cancer had the highest incidence (ASR 73.9 per 100,000) and increased significantly over time (AAPC +6.7%), reaching an ASR of 90.3 per 100,000 in 2015-2024. Significant declines were observed for oesophageal (AAPC -4.3%) and laryngeal cancers (AAPC -5.6%). Among women, breast cancer was the most common cancer (ASR 54.7 per 100,000), increasing by 3.4% annually and reaching an ASR of 70.5 per 100,000 in the most recent decade, comparable to rates in Europe. Significant increases were also observed for colorectal, cervical, and corpus uteri cancers. The observed trends reflect Seychelles' epidemiological transition, with a shift from infection-related cancers towards cancers associated with ageing and lifestyle factors, resembling the cancer profile of high-income countries. Nevertheless, the major cancers-prostate, breast, colorectal, and cervical-continue to be diagnosed at relatively advanced stages, highlighting the need for improved early detection and timely diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, with its incidence and mortality rates continuing to rise. The long noncoding RNA SNHG4, a member of the small nucleolar RNA host gene family, has emerged as a candidate regulator in human cancers. This review synthesizes the currently reported expression patterns and clinical significance of SNHG4 across various malignancies, including colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, gastric cancer, glioblastoma, prostate cancer, and lung cancer. Particular attention is given to tissue-dependent expression reversals, differences in evidence strength, and unresolved translational barriers. Additionally, this review describes the molecular mechanisms through which SNHG4 modulates oncogenic processes, including promoting cancer cell proliferation, migration, invasion, and epithelial‒mesenchymal transition and inhibiting apoptosis and ferroptosis. In summary, this review highlights the vital role of SNHG4 in cancer biology and critically evaluates its potential diagnostic and prognostic value together with the barriers to developing SNHG4-directed therapies. Despite these promising findings, the current evidence is largely derived from retrospective studies and preclinical models. Further large-scale, prospective multicenter studies with standardized detection methods are critically needed to validate the translational potential of SNHG4 before it can be considered for clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Vγ9Vδ2 T cells mediate HLA-independent targeting of tumor cells, offering unique opportunities for cancer immunotherapy, yet their therapeutic efficacy remains limited. Here, using a genome-wide CRISPR screen, we identify UDP-galactose 4-epimerase (GALE) as a tumor-intrinsic checkpoint that restricts Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated killing. GALE is a key nucleotide-sugar metabolic enzyme that controls the interconversion of UDP-galactose and UDP-glucose, thereby supporting protein glycosylation and cell-surface glycan remodeling. Mechanistically, GALE promotes complex N-glycosylation of CD155 and CEACAM1, favoring their engagement with the inhibitory receptors TIGIT and TIM3, respectively, while limiting CD155 binding to the activating receptor CD226. GALE loss potentiates Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated tumor killing in multiple mouse models and colorectal cancer patient-derived organoids. Together, these findings reveal how nucleotide-sugar metabolism shapes tumor-immune communication through complex N-glycan remodeling and identify GALE and its downstream receptor-ligand interactions as potential therapeutic targets for enhancing Vγ9Vδ2 T cell antitumor activity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical management of colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) often involves multi-organ interventions which elevate postoperative infectious risk. While thermal ablation is increasingly used as a parenchymal-sparing strategy, infectious risk when combined with colorectal resection is unclear. Adults in the ACS-NSQIP database (2020-2023) undergoing hepatic thermal ablation, hepatic resection, or colorectal resection for CRLM were identified. The primary outcome was 30-day hepatic abscess, derived from organ-space infection excluding anastomotic leaks. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the impact of concurrent colorectal resection. Propensity score-matched and exploratory analyses compared infectious outcomes across procedure combinations. Among 660 patients (median age 59, 58% male), 52% underwent concurrent colorectal resection, with more transfusions, myocardial infarctions, reoperations, and longer hospital stays. In matched analysis, adding hepatic ablation to colorectal resection was independently associated with hepatic abscess, wound complications, and serious complications (OR 9.70, 4.88, 3.77, respectively). Conversely, concurrent colorectal resection and ablation increased infectious morbidity compared to ablation alone. Ablation alone demonstrated lower infectious risk than hepatic resection; concurrent colorectal surgery increased morbidity regardless of hepatic procedure. Concurrent colorectal resection with hepatic thermal ablation for CRLM increases infectious morbidity. While ablation alone maintains a favorable infectious profile, bowel manipulation appears to drive elevated risk.
