ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Bowel Screening Programme (BSP) in Aotearoa, New Zealand, was introduced to facilitate earlier detection of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet its impact on acute CRC presentations remains incompletely characterised. This study evaluated changes in the incidence and clinical features of acutely presenting, previously undiagnosed CRC before and after BSP implementation. A single-centre retrospective cohort study was conducted at North Shore Hospital, Auckland. Adults (≥ 16 years) acutely admitted with a first diagnosis of CRC were identified in the 3 years preceding the BSP pilot (2009-2011) and the 3 years following national rollout (2018-2020). The primary outcome was the age-standardised population incidence of acute CRC. Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated using age-adjusted Poisson regression. Three-hundred twenty three patients were included (pre-BSP n = 215; post-BSP n = 108). The age-standardised incidence of acute CRC declined from 9.71 per 100 000 population (95% CI: 7.56-12.27) in 2009 to 3.79 per 100 000 (95% CI: 2.70-5.17) in 2020. Following BSP implementation, acute CRC presentations were reduced by 61% (IRR 0.39, 95% CI: 0.31-0.49, p < 0.001). Post-BSP patients were less likely to present with metastatic disease (21% vs. 35%, p = 0.010) or require palliative management on admission (9.3% vs. 19%, p = 0.023). One-year mortality was significantly lower following the BSP (28% vs. 40%, p = 0.037). Implementation of the BSP was associated with a substantial reduction in the incidence of acute CRC presentations and evidence of earlier disease at emergency diagnosis. These findings support the effectiveness of organised bowel screening in reducing the presentation of advanced CRC.

Extended pelvic resections requiring cystectomy or partial cystectomy, including pelvic exenterations and beyond total mesorectal excision (bTME) rectal cancer surgery, carry a substantial risk of urinary leak following urinary reconstruction. This study evaluated pre-operative predictors and postoperative indicators of urinary anastomotic leak. All patients who underwent pelvic exenteration or bTME with ureteric reconstruction between 2015 and 2022 in a single centre were retrospectively analysed. Exclusions included palliative resections, complete ureteric resections, and cases with intraoperative ureteric injuries. The primary outcome was radiologically confirmed urinary leak within 30 days. Baseline and operative variables were compared, and postoperative drain and serum creatinine were analysed. Among 110 patients, 14 (12.7%) developed a urinary leak. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) critically regulate colorectal cancer (CRC) progression, but the contribution of 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-induced senescent CAFs to CRC malignancy and whether this stromal response can be pharmacologically restrained remain unclear. This study investigated whether Glabridin (Gla) attenuates the pro-tumorigenic activity of 5-FU-induced senescent CAFs. Transcriptomic and integrative analyses were used to identify candidate SASP factors, followed by RT-qPCR and ELISA validation. 5-FU induced a stable senescent phenotype in primary CAFs and enhanced SASP factor expression. Functionally, CM from 5-FU plus Gla-treated CAFs exhibited weaker pro-tumorigenic effects than 5-FU-CM. Gla attenuates the pro-tumorigenic activity of 5-FU-induced senescent CAFs, at least in part by suppressing MMP1/3/12 expression and secretion. These findings suggest that Gla may help mitigate chemotherapy-associated stromal remodeling in CRC.

The accurate optical prediction of deep submucosal invasion (T1b) is critical for selecting the appropriate treatment for colorectal neoplasia. Although magnifying narrow-band imaging (M-NBI) is widely used, diagnostic uncertainty remains, particularly in lesions for which deep invasion is suspected. Sensitivity, specificity, likelihood ratios, and the effect of the addition of AEC were analyzed. The overall diagnostic accuracy was 89.3%. The sensitivity and specificity for the prediction of deep submucosal invasion were 78.1% and 95.8%, respectively, with positive and negative likelihood ratios of 18.6 and 0.23, respectively. The pretest probability of T1b (21%) increased to approximately 83% after a positive optical diagnosis. When AEC was added, the specificity improved from 56.9% to 74.5%, and the overall accuracy improved from 60.3% to 77.6% (P < .0001), which reflects significant reclassification and a reduction in overdiagnosis. The addition of AEC to M-NBI significantly improved the real-time optical prediction of deep submucosal invasion of colonic neoplasms. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fatigue is amongst the most debilitating cancer-related symptoms, affecting up to one-third of colorectal cancer (CRC) survivors. Accumulating evidence implicates dysregulation of HPA axis as a potential mechanism contributing to chronic fatigue syndrome. We examined longitudinal associations between parameters of diurnal cortisol rhythms and fatigue in CRC survivors up to 12 months after treatment. Seventy-four survivors of CRC were assessed at 6 weeks, 6 months and 12 months after treatment. At each point, salivary samples were collected five times per day over two consecutive days to measure cortisol concentrations. Relative amplitude (RA), diurnal slope, area under the curve (AUCg) and cortisol awakening response (CAR) were derived as a comprehensive assessment of diurnal cortisol rhythms. Fatigue was assessed at all time points using the Checklist Individual Strength (CIS; range overall score: 20-140; motivational subscale: 4-28) and the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire Core 30 (EORTC; range: 0-100). Longitudinal associations were analyzed using confounder-adjusted linear mixed models, with coefficients (β) indicating differences in fatigue scores over time per SD increase in cortisol parameters. A higher RA was associated with less overall fatigue (EORTC: β= -1.42; 95%CI: -2.82, -0.03; CIS: β= -1.82; 95%CI: -3.63, -0.01). A flatter diurnal slope, indicating less decline in cortisol over the day, was associated with more fatigue (EORTC: β=1.64; 0.25, 3.03) and increased motivational fatigue (CIS: β= 0.45; 0.02, 0.88). More pronounced diurnal cortisol rhythms, specifically a higher RA and steeper diurnal slope, were longitudinally associated with less fatigue in CRC survivors. These findings may suggest that improving 24-h cortisol rhythmicity could be a target for interventions to reduce fatigue in CRC survivors, but this warrants further investigations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This systematic review and network meta-analysis evaluates the efficacy and safety of different ileostomy methods (conventional, 1-stitch, modified 1-stitch, prolapse technique + 1-stitch, and modified 2-stitch) in ileostomy and stoma reversal surgery and ranks their effectiveness. We searched 8 databases (PubMed, Cochrane, Embase, Web of Science, CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, and SinoMed) from inception to December 2025. Interventions included 1-stitch, prolapse + 1-stitch, modified 1-stitch, continuous intradermal suture, modified 2-stitch, simple support + 1-stitch, 3-stitch, and 2-stitch. A total of 16 studies (1,402 patients, 9 interventions) were included. Different ileostomy methods showed differential advantages across clinical indicators. Continuous intradermal suture significantly shortened total ileostomy duration and reduced stoma retraction. Prolapse surgery + 1-stitch was associated with shorter phase I hospitalization and stoma exhaust time. Simple support bracket + 1-stitch was associated with less blood loss during reversal surgery. One-stitch shortened the interval of reversal surgery and the length of hospitalization postreversal surgery. Modified 2-stitch was associated with a lower incidence of overall complications. Three-stitch + innovative knotting effectively prevented stoma stenosis and skin-mucosal separation, whereas 3-stitch alone prevented stoma prolapse. No statistically significant differences were observed for intraoperative blood loss, parastomal hernia, irritant dermatitis, stoma infection, or ischemia/necrosis. Modified ileostomy techniques appear better than conventional methods in surgical efficiency, postoperative recovery, and complication control. Continuous intradermal suture is associated with shorter operative duration. The 1-stitch technique and its derivatives promote postoperative recovery. Multistitch techniques are better at preventing stoma prolapse and stenosis. However, because of the absence of closed loops in the evidence network and the predominantly retrospective study design, these findings may be overestimated.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Transmembrane serine protease 4 (TMPRSS4) is associated with poor prognosis in multiple cancers, including non-small cell lung, pancreatic, and colorectal cancers. We previously showed that TMPRSS4 promotes cancer stem-like properties in prostate cancer in a manner dependent on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) transcription factors. Here, we identified a novel TMPRSS4-EMT transcription factor-KRAS axis that drives cancer stem-like features and tumorigenesis in colon and lung cancers. TMPRSS4 knockdown suppressed tumor growth and cancer stem-like properties, accompanied by reduced KRAS expression and decreased phosphorylation of ERK1/2 and AKT, consistent with transcriptomic analysis showing activation of RAS, MAPK, and PI3K-AKT signaling pathways by TMPRSS4. Mechanistically, the EMT-inducing transcription factors SLUG and TWIST1 were required for TMPRSS4-mediated KRAS upregulation. These factors enhanced KRAS transcription through the E-box element within the intron 1 regulatory region of KRAS and increased KRAS expression post-transcriptionally via repression of KRAS-targeting miR-200c. Clinically, TMPRSS4 expression positively correlated with KRAS expression, and co-expression of TMPRSS4 and KRAS was associated with poor survival across multiple cancers. Together, these findings reveal a previously unrecognized TMPRSS4-SLUG/TWIST1-KRAS pathway that promotes tumor progression, highlighting the TMPRSS4-KRAS axis as a potential therapeutic target for cancers driven by KRAS mutation and/or elevation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Small pulmonary nodules (SPNs ≤ 2 cm) in metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) had heterogeneous biology and no evidence-based treatment algorithms. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) can detect molecular residual disease (MRD) but lacks prospective validation for treatment guidance in this setting. 70 mCRC patients with exclusively SPNs were assigned to Cohort 1 (≤1 cm) and Cohort 2 (1-2 cm). Tumor-informed ctDNA was detected at baseline, 30 days after optional local treatment or systemic chemotherapy, then every 3 months for 24 months or until progression. Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS). Baseline ctDNA positivity was 35.5% in Cohort 1 and 66.7% in Cohort 2. In Cohort 1, baseline ctDNA positivity significantly correlated with shorter PFS (median PFS: 3.2 months vs. 9.2 months, P = 0.013), which was not seen in Cohort 2. Systemic chemotherapy was associated with a five-fold higher ctDNA clearance than local treatment alone (63.2 % vs. 12.5 %, P = 0.033). ctDNA clearance was associated with longer median PFS (12.6 months vs. 6.8 months, P = 0.038). Longitudinal ctDNA monitoring may provide prognostic information and help identify extrapulmonary progression in mCRC patients with SPNs. These exploratory findings require prospective validation before informing clinical treatment decisions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Aberrant glutamine metabolism undermines the efficacy of cancer radiotherapy (RT) by promoting DNA repair, increasing oxygen consumption, and imposing metabolic stress that compromises the viability and function of cytotoxic T lymphocytes (CTLs). Here, we report a mitochondria-enriched, metabolism-regulating monolayered metal-organic framework (MOF) nanoplatform, Hf-Ir/DON, constructed by incorporating the glutamine antagonist 6-diazo-5-oxo-l-norleucine (DON) into a radiosensitizing hafnium-iridium (Hf-Ir) MOF to inhibit glutaminolysis. This design markedly sensitizes tumor cells to RT and, upon x-ray irradiation, enables mitochondria-targeted RT-radiodynamic therapy with substantially enhanced reactive oxygen species accumulation. The resulting oxidative stress induces extensive DNA damage, mitochondrial dysfunction, and immunogenic tumor cell pyroptosis. Concurrently, Hf-Ir/DON alleviates metabolic constraints on activated T cells, preserving CTL viability while sustaining effector and memory functions. In a murine colon cancer model, low-dose RT combined with Hf-Ir/DON achieved >95% tumor growth inhibition. Further combination with anti-PD-L1 therapy induced regression of bilateral triple-negative breast tumors and prevented lung metastasis. These results establish a radiometabolic MOF nanoplatform that potentiates RT while promoting durable antitumor immunity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Exercise reduces colorectal cancer risk, but its protective mechanisms in early carcinogenesis remain unclear. Male C57BL/6 mice (n = 10/group) were used in two experimental designs: (i) an acute molecular and epigenetic study to evaluate early changes 8h and 24h after a single Azoxymethane (AOM) dose; and (ii) a chronic carcinogenic model to assess the biological efficacy of exercise timing on premalignant lesions (Aberrant and mucin-depleted foci) after 6 weeks of AOM exposure. In both, mice underwent a 6-week progressive swimming protocol initiated either before (preconditioning) or concurrent with AOM. We demonstrate that 6-week exercise preconditioning, rather than concurrent training, conferred protection against mucin-depleted foci incidence (P = 0.03). Mechanistically, exercise preconditioning remodeled colon tissue to resist genotoxic stress, evidenced by an accelerated normalization of DNA repair kinetics (Mgmt expression returned to baseline by 24h vs sustained elevation in the AOM non-exercised group, P = 0.002). Exercise preconditioning also induced colon-specific epigenetic reprogramming, including Mgmt promoter hypermethylation (27% increase, P = 0.0043) and 3-fold reduction in expression of the mutagenic deaminase Apobec3 (P < 0.0001). These molecular changes occurred without altering global LINE-1 methylation or body composition, suggesting targeted tissue adaptation rather than systemic effects. These results demonstrate that exercise preconditioning, not concurrent training, provides colon preneoplastic prevention by enhancing DNA repair efficiency and suppressing Apobec3, a key driver of genomic instability and chronic mutational signatures, during the critical window of carcinogen attack.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pelvic floor dysfunction (PFD) includes urinary and bowel dysfunction, chronic pelvic pain, and sexual dysfunction and can substantially impair quality of life. Sacral neuromodulation (SNM) is uesd for selected refractory urinary and bowel disorders, while evidence for other PFD domains continues to develop. We aimed to characterize publication patterns, contributors, collaboration networks, co-citation structures, and keyword trends in the literature on SNM for PFD. Publications on SNM for PFD from January 2000 to November 2025 were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Bibliometric and visual analyses were conducted using VOSviewer, CiteSpace, and R software to evaluate temporal trends, geographic and institutional distributions, journal and author productivity, reference co-citation networks, and keyword dynamics. A total of 1986 publications (1520 original articles and 466 reviews) were included. Annual publication output increased overall during the study period, with year-to-year fluctuations. The United States (n = 681), the United Kingdom (n = 276), the Netherlands (n = 135), and China (n = 125) contributed the largest numbers of publications. Neurourology and Urodynamics, Colorectal Disease, and Diseases of the Colon & Rectum were the most productive journals. The strongest reference bursts were observed for Wexner SD (2010; strength 32.91), Matzel KE (2017; strength 30.40), and Lightner DJ (2019; strength 30.19). Keyword analyses were dominated by sacral neuromodulation, sacral nerve stimulation, fecal incontinence, efficacy, and quality of life; keywords with bursts continuing through 2025 included percutaneous tibial nerve stimulation, overactive bladder, and urgency urinary incontinence. This bibliometric analysis maps publication growth, major contributors, collaboration patterns, co-citation structures, and keyword themes in the literature on SNM for PFD. Urinary and bowel dysfunction were the most prominent research themes, whereas chronic pelvic pain and sexual dysfunction were less represented in the keyword analyses. By identifying major thematic concentrations, patterns of scientific collaboration, and comparatively underrepresented topics, these findings may support hypothesis generation, prioritization of future studies on SNM across different PFD domains, and stronger international and interdisciplinary collaboration.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Many digital health and AI initiatives show promising results in pilot settings but do not progress to sustainable services. Pilots can operate within a predefined collaboration, whereas operational services must accommodate changes in participating organizations, available resources, and analytical capabilities while preserving established governance and technical arrangements. This study examines the pilot-to-service transition as a problem of governed federation evolution and evaluates whether Open Health can admit new forms of participation while preserving bounded capabilities, organizational sovereignty, and auditable decision evidence. Open Health applies federated computing (FC) as a governance model separated from the analytical runtime. A governed federation context is established before execution, participants receive holder-bound capabilities, and an admission gateway produces explicit ALLOW or DENY decisions before requested operations proceed. The proof of concept uses the Flower federated learning framework and the Pathology Modified National Institute of Standards and Technology (PathMNIST) dataset from the MedMNIST collection with an initial federation comprising hospitals A and B. Mode 1A introduces hospital C as a sponsored contributor permitted to submit locally computed training updates but not invoke the resulting federated model for inference. Mode 1B examines bounded AI-agent participation, where restricted results may be transformed through policy-authorized operations into derivatives whose consumption is governed independently from the source. Evaluation considers admission conformance, signed decision evidence, analytical effects of the additional contribution, and admission overhead. The demonstrator admitted valid member operations and hospital C's sponsored contribution (mode 1A) while denying model consumption outside hospital C's capability, scope violations, holder-binding mismatch, and federation-envelope mismatch. Mode 1B extended the same bounded-governance pattern to AI-agent participation, admitting bounded inference and governed transformation but denying unauthorized source consumption and privileged governance access. Under matched training conditions, cancer-related macro recall increased from 50.2% in the A+B control to 67.4% in A+B+C (+17.2 percentage points), while noncancer macro recall changed from 85.5% to 86.3% (+0.8 percentage points). Recall increased from 19.5% to 39.9% for cancer-associated stroma and from 80.9% to 94.9% for colorectal adenocarcinoma epithelium. Median (IQR) full admission latency was 1.210 (1.141-1.333) ms for ALLOW, 1.195 (1.136-1.273) ms for capability-scope DENY, and 0.884 (0.837-0.921) ms for holder-binding DENY. Each evaluated request generated signed decision evidence recording the decision, reason, participant and request bindings, governance context, and related model run. Open Health demonstrates how a federated health-data collaboration can evolve through differentiated participation while preserving membership boundaries and bounded capability relations. The principal contribution is an executable governance boundary preserving capability relations and producing independently verifiable decision evidence separately from the federated-learning runtime. The analytical experiment showed that governed admission of an additional contributor produced a measurable effect on the intended cancer-related classes while preserving noncancer performance. The proof of concept establishes governance behavior under controlled conditions; clinical effectiveness and production-scale performance require further evaluation.

The efficacy of immunotherapy is commonly increased by simultaneous anti-angiogenesis treatment. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The centromeric and pericentromeric regions of chromosomes are essential for genome stability. Beyond their structural role, noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs) transcribed from these regions have been implicated in kinetochore assembly. In cancer, reduced centromeric heterochromatin and deregulated ncRNA expression have been associated with chromosome instability. Centromeric and pericentromeric ncRNA expression was compared between the non-transformed WI-38 cell line and the colorectal cancer cell line HCT116. CTCF and H3K9me3 occupancy were evaluated by chromatin immunoprecipitation. Cells were treated with Trichostatin A (TSA), and CTCF function was assessed by pharmacological inhibition and shRNA-mediated depletion. Cancer cells exhibited elevated ncRNA levels, accompanied by reduced H3K9me3 enrichment and differential CTCF occupancy. Functional inactivation or depletion of CTCF markedly decreased ncRNA transcription, supporting a role for CTCF in regulating centromeric and pericentromeric ncRNAs. These findings support an association between chromatin state, CTCF occupancy, and ncRNA transcription at centromeric regions, and provide insight into epigenetic patterns associated with genome stability in cancer cells. Our results further suggest that centromeric chromatin operates within constrained transcriptional states compatible with chromosome stability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Falcon is a multi-site prospective registry study of a blood-based multi-biomarker multi-cancer early detection (mb-MCED) test in individuals who seek cancer screening to characterize clinical care and outcomes and assess the psychological impact of MCED testing.Falcon is enrolling ≥ 25,000 U.S. participants who receive the MCED test annually for 3 years (MCED cohort) and a matched comparison cohort of ≥50,000 participants receiving standard-of-care clinical management only (SOC cohort). Cohorts will include individuals 50-80 years of age presenting for primary care services who have no current suspicion or history of cancer within 3 years. SOC cancer screening will continue as recommended.The MCED cohort will include MCED testing and follow-up IV-contrast computed tomography and, if necessary, positron emission tomography-CT imaging following a positive test. Self-reported measures of anxiety, worry, and distress will be collected from MCED cohort participants for ≥5 years and following an index date for the SOC cohort. Time from positive MCED to diagnostic imaging and biopsy to first oncologic appointment will be recorded. Smart phone applications will be used to remotely interact with patients to improve health care coordination. Data will be collected for ≥5 years.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Histotripsy is a nonthermal therapy that mechanically disrupts and liquefies tumor tissue by generating focused microbubbles using extracorporeal ultrasound. Following U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval for the treatment of liver tumors in 2023, its clinical use has rapidly expanded. Here, we report the first clinical implementation of histotripsy in Japan, focusing on its safety and feasibility. The first treatment was performed for a 1.8-cm postoperative recurrent hepatocellular carcinoma in segment 8, followed by a second treatment for a 2.5- cm recurrent colorectal liver metastasis in segment 2 after multiple resections of intra- and extra-hepatic metastases. Histotripsy treatment times were 22 and 40 min, respectively. Target tumor coverage was confirmed by intraoperative ultrasonography, and reduced tumor enhancement was confirmed by contrast-enhanced computed tomography performed the day after treatment. The patients were discharged on postoperative days 1 and 2, respectively. No major complications occurred during follow-up to postoperative days 14 and 19, respectively, although both patients experienced mild treatment-related pain and one developed fever. These initial experiences suggest feasibility of implementing histotripsy for liver tumors in Japan.

Accurate risk stratification for lymph node metastasis (LNM) is needed after endoscopic resection of early-stage colorectal cancer (CRC). We explored the associations of cancer-associated fibroblast (CAF)-related markers and insulin-like growth factor 2 mRNA-binding protein 3 (IMP3) expression with LNM. We analyzed data from 155 patients with pT1 CRC who were treated by primary or additional surgery after endoscopic resection. A matched case-control cohort comprising 18 patients with LNM and 29 LNM-negative controls was immunohistochemically analyzed. The area fraction and staining intensity of podoplanin (D2-40), hydrogen peroxide-inducible clone-5 (Hic-5), α-smooth muscle actin (αSMA), and IMP3 were assessed using image analysis. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early mobilization is a key component of Enhanced Recovery After Surgery (ERAS) pathways following colorectal cancer surgery; however, objective postoperative mobility quantification remains limited. We evaluated whether early postoperative step counts measured using a wearable device could be associated with the achievement of ERAS-based discharge eligibility. In this prospective pilot study, adults undergoing elective colorectal cancer resection at a single tertiary academic referral hospital wore a consumer wearable device (Galaxy Watch 5) from the day of surgery. Cumulative step counts on postoperative days (PODs) 1 and 2 were recorded. Discharge readiness was assessed daily by predefined ERAS criteria. The patients were dichotomized according to the median cumulative step count (3,781 steps). The primary endpoint was the achievement of ERAS-based discharge eligibility by POD 3, and the secondary endpoints included time to discharge readiness and postoperative length of stay. Between August 2023 and December 2024, 38 patients were evaluated. Discharge readiness by POD 3 was more frequent in the active group (68.4% vs. 26.3%; odds ratio, 6.07; 95% confidence interval, 1.49-24.76; P=0.009), which achieved discharge readiness earlier (median, POD 3 vs. POD 4; P=0.003) and had a shorter postoperative stay (median, 5 days vs. 6 days; P=0.041) than did the inactive group. Early diet tolerance differed between the groups (P=0.013). Higher early postoperative step counts were associated with earlier ERAS-based discharge readiness and shorter hospitalization. Wearable-derived mobility might provide an objective marker of recovery and target for postoperative mobilization strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to evaluate the significance of transverse colon cancer as a predictor of locoregional recurrence in patients with stage III colon cancer. This single-center retrospective cohort study included 1,302 patients who underwent curative-intent laparoscopic colectomy for stage III colon cancer between 2003 and 2021. The primary outcome was locoregional recurrence, defined as tumor recurrence near the anastomotic site, regional lymph nodes, or peritoneal recurrence around the primary tumor. Multivariate analyses were conducted to identify the factors associated with locoregional recurrence. Transverse colon cancer was identified in 151 patients (11.6%). Baseline characteristics were similar, but transverse colon cancer exhibited a higher locoregional recurrence rate than nontransverse colon cancer (7.9% vs. 2.0%, P<0.001). In transverse colon cancer, locoregional recurrence did not differ according to high ligation of the mid-colic vessel (without high ligation, 10.6% vs. high ligation, 6.7%; P=0.517), and 10 of 12 recurrences (83.3%) occurred predominantly in the regional lymph nodes. In multivariate analysis, transverse colon (hazard ratio [HR], 4.513; 95% confidence interval [CI], 2.226-9.154; P<0.001) and N2 category (HR, 2.044; 95% CI, 1.034-4.042; P=0.040) emerged as independent predictors of locoregional recurrence. Disease-free survival (73.8% vs. 79.2%, P=0.217) and overall survival (84.7% vs. 86.3%, P=0.735) in 5 years were not different between transverse and nontransverse colon cancer. Transverse colon cancer may serve as an independent predictor of locoregional recurrence in stage III colon cancer. The predominance of regional lymph node recurrence emphasizes the importance of careful regional lymph node assessment in transverse colon cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (CRT) improves local control in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) but has not consistently demonstrated a survival benefit. This study evaluated whether pathological complete response (ypCR) after CRT confers systemic oncological benefit beyond local tumor control. A total of 1,105 patients with clinically staged T3 or node-positive rectal cancer who underwent total mesorectal excision at a single tertiary center between 2004 and 2019 were categorized into 3 groups: no CRT (n=608), non-ypCR (n=414), and ypCR (n=83). Primary outcomes were 5-year overall survival (OS) and relapse-free survival (RFS). Secondary outcomes were 5-year cumulative incidences of local recurrence and distant metastasis. Five-year OS rates were 77.6%, 82.0%, and 95.7% in the no-CRT, non-ypCR, and ypCR groups, respectively. The ypCR group demonstrated superior OS compared with both no-CRT and non-ypCR groups (P=0.001 and P=0.007, respectively). The marginal OS difference between the no-CRT and non-ypCR groups (P=0.047) was no longer significant after multivariable adjustment (hazard ratio, 0.903; P=0.622). Five-year RFS rates were 69.6%, 72.5%, and 91.1% in the no-CRT, non-ypCR, and ypCR groups, respectively. The 5-year cumulative incidence of distant metastasis was lower in the ypCR group (7.5%) than in the no-CRT and non-ypCR groups (23.8% and 25.0%, respectively; P=0.005). On multivariable analysis, ypCR remained independently associated with reduced risks of death, relapse, and distant metastasis. The ypCR after neoadjuvant CRT in LARC was associated with superior survival and reduced distant metastasis, suggesting effective systemic tumor control rather than a local treatment effect alone.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To compare perioperative and oncologic outcomes between robotic and laparoscopic colectomy for colon cancer, with a focus on peritoneal recurrence, using a propensity score-matched analysis. We retrospectively reviewed 591 patients who underwent minimally invasive colectomy for colon cancer between 2016 and 2024. After 1:1 propensity score matching based on age, sex, body mass index, American Society of Anesthesiologists physical status, clinical stage, and procedure, 90 patients in each group were analyzed. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier methods and competing risk analysis with the Fine-Gray model. Robotic colectomy showed lower blood loss (median, 10 mL vs. 20 mL; P<0.001), shorter postoperative hospital stay (median, 9 days vs. 11.5 days, P<0.001), and a higher rate of intracorporeal anastomosis (92.2% vs. 24.4%, P<0.001), without prolonging operative time. Disease-free survival was comparable (P=0.519). Locoregional/peritoneal recurrence-free survival was higher in the robotic group (P=0.037); however, competing risk analysis using the Fine-Gray model showed no significant difference in the cumulative incidence of locoregional/peritoneal recurrence between groups. Multivariable analysis identified high-grade histology as an independent predictor of peritoneal recurrence, whereas surgical approach was not. Robotic colectomy provides favorable perioperative outcomes while maintaining oncologic safety comparable to laparoscopic colectomy. Peritoneal recurrence appears to be driven primarily by tumor biology, and intracorporeal anastomosis does not increase recurrence risk.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Yellow enhancement (YE) is an image processing technology available in advanced endoscopic and laparoscopic systems. By increasing the contrast of yellow tissue tones, YE is intended to improve tissue differentiation and the identification of dissection planes. However, because YE is a relatively new technology, supporting evidence remains limited. This study qualitatively explored general surgery residents' perceptions of the usefulness of YE compared with conventional white light imaging and aimed to establish a foundation for developing a qualitatively anchored scoring system for evaluating YE. A piloted online survey was electronically distributed to general surgery residents. After providing basic demographic information, respondents viewed videos with and without YE and then assessed their perceptions of the videos, provided general feedback, and reported their overall opinions of YE. Open-ended responses were coded inductively, followed by reflexive thematic analysis. A total of 34 responses were obtained. The analysis identified 7 recurring themes related to the utility of YE, including superior visualization for structure identification and enhanced contrast for tissue differentiation. Three recurring themes were noted regarding the limitations of YE, including visual distortion and fatigue, as well as issues related to transition, training, and understanding of YE. Based on video demonstrations, surgical residents generally perceived YE as beneficial in laparoscopic surgery. However, variability in perceptions highlights the subjective and context-dependent nature of YE. Ultimately, YE should be conceptualized as a specialized adjunct to, rather than a replacement for, conventional white light imaging in laparoscopic surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Young-onset rectal cancer (YORC) is increasingly common and often presents with aggressive histological features; however, its effect on recurrence remains uncertain. This study aimed to estimate the causal effect of age at diagnosis on recurrence in patients with rectal cancer using advanced causal inference methods. This multicenter retrospective cohort study was conducted at 2 university hospitals in Thailand. Patients diagnosed with rectal adenocarcinoma between 2013 and 2022 who underwent curative-intent treatment were included. The primary exposure was age at diagnosis, categorized as YORC (<50 years) or late-onset rectal cancer (LORC; ≥50 years). Confounders were prespecified using a directed acyclic graph and addressed using a confounder composite score. Age was also modeled as a continuous variable using natural splines. The primary outcome was cancer recurrence. Among 585 patients, 116 (19.8%) had YORC and 469 (80.2%) had LORC. Patients with YORC had fewer comorbidities but more unfavorable histological features than those with LORC. Overall, recurrence occurred in 40.2% of patients and most commonly involved distant metastasis. The estimated average causal effect of age on recurrence was -6.5% (95% confidence interval, -16.6% to 3.5%; P=0.202), indicating that younger age was not associated with an increased risk of recurrence, although a protective effect was not confirmed. Natural spline modeling indicated a nonlinear increase in recurrence hazard with advancing age. Younger age at diagnosis was not associated with worse recurrence outcomes despite adverse pathological features, and a potential protective association could not be excluded.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Sacral nerve stimulators (SNS) are used to treat refractory urinary symptoms, bowel symptoms, and pelvic pain. There is a risk of surgical site and implant infection; however, manufacturers have not released guidelines regarding infection prevention during their implantation. There are limited data on the pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative considerations for infection prevention. We present a scoping review detailing the current strategies for infection prevention during implantation of SNS and propose a protocol for perioperative infection control strategies based on current available literature. A scoping review was conducted using Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Review and Meta Analysis (PRISMA). A search strategy using search terms "sacral nerve stimulation," "infection," "infection control," and "infection prevention" was used. A search was conducted on medical databases, and a grey literature search was performed. Forty-three articles were included for data extraction, published between 2003 and 2022. A total of 10,401 outcomes were reported. Pre-operative, intra-operative, and post-operative considerations and outcomes were extracted. Significant peri-operative considerations included the use of pre-operative chlorhexidine wash and the use of shallow pocket depths. There was limited data to support other infection control considerations and variability in practices within the SNS implanting community. Despite implant infection being a highly morbid and detrimental outcome for the patient, there is no clear consensus on what infection control measures should be routinely performed to reduce the risk of infection during the implantation process. The peri-operative considerations currently covered in the literature have little reported evidence to support the implementation of certain infection prevention considerations, and it seems their use is primarily driven by surgeon preference.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer is the second leading cause of death worldwide and disproportionately affects older adults. As population ageing accelerates, the global cancer burden among older adults continues to increase. This study systematically evaluated the latest global cancer burden and its epidemiological characteristics among older adults. Data on the incidence and mortality of 33 malignancies, excluding non-melanoma skin cancer, among adults aged 65 + were extracted from the Global Cancer Observatory (GLOBOCAN) 2024 and Global Burden of Disease Study (GBD) 2023 databases and stratified by age, sex, region, and Human Development Index (HDI). Age-standardized incidence and mortality rates (ASIR and ASMR) were calculated. Annual percentage changes (APC) were used to characterize temporal trends. Decomposition analysis was performed to quantify the contributions of population growth, population aging, and epidemiological changes. Demographic projection methods and generalized additive model (GAM) were applied to forecast the cancer burden through 2050. In 2024, there were 9,966,392 new cancer cases and 6,001,290 cancer deaths among older adults worldwide, accounting for 51.11% and 61.84%, respectively, of all-age totals. Lung, colorectal, stomach, liver, and prostate cancers were leading causes of death. Incidence and mortality were higher in men and increased with age. The Western Pacific Region had the largest burden, whereas Europe Region had the highest ASIR. ASIR correlated positively with HDI (rs = 0.771), while mortality-to-incidence ratio (MIR) correlated negatively (rs = -0.825). From 2000 to 2023, ASIR and ASMR declined, although burden increased, primarily driven by population growth; pancreatic cancer exhibited the most rapid increase. Tobacco use remained the leading risk factor for mortality, while metabolic risks rose in importance. Under a demographic scenario assuming constant 2024 age-specific rates and changes only in population size and age structure, new cancer cases and deaths among older adults are projected to reach approximately 19.8 million and 12.5 million by 2050, roughly double the 2024 figures, with the largest increase in the Eastern Mediterranean region. Cancer burden in older adults is substantial, varying by sex, age, region, and development level. Precision prevention and control are urgently needed, particularly in low- and middle-income regions. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Primary care services are important to meet the complex needs of people living with or having survived cancer. However, there is a need for improved knowledge about how this patient group use and experience primary care. The aim of this study was to describe the utilization of primary care in people with cancer 1-2 years and 5-6 years after diagnosis, to assess satisfaction with post-diagnosis primary care contacts, and to identify patient and disease characteristics and utilization patterns associated with satisfaction. Data from a cross-sectional digital survey were used to measure primary care utilization and satisfaction among people diagnosed with breast, prostate, lung, and colorectal cancer 1-2 and 5-6 years ago. T-tests and chi2-tests were used to detect differences, and logistic regression to identify associations between satisfaction and patient, disease and caregiver characteristics. Almost all participants had been in contact with primary care since being diagnosed with cancer. A majority had been so for cancer-related reasons, even though most had only been in contact for routine matters. Among participants who had completed cancer treatment, few reported that they had been actively handed over to primary care. Around half of the participants reported that their post-diagnosis primary care contacts had been satisfactory, while 8% rated them as dissatisfactory. However, rates of satisfaction differed considerably between subgroups. Satisfaction was positively associated with having a regular physician and with active handovers, and negatively associated with problem-induced cancer-related primary care contacts and with an absence of cancer-related contacts, as well as with number of comorbidities. Overall, differences based on time since diagnosis were small. Most people utilize primary care after a cancer diagnosis, including for cancer-related reasons. Many are satisfied with their primary care contacts, but satisfaction varies between sub-groups and is associated with factors related to patients' health, the nature of contacts, and their relationship to primary care providers. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BRAF V600E-mutant metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) represents an aggressive molecular subtype associated with poor prognosis and limited response to conventional chemotherapy. Although multiple targeted strategies, including anti-vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF), anti-epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), and BRAF-directed therapies, are used in clinical practice, their comparative effectiveness remains uncertain. We performed a reconstructed individual patient-data (IPD) meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to evaluate survival outcomes across targeted therapeutic classes in BRAF-mutant mCRC. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Scopus, and Cochrane databases was conducted through July 2025 to identify RCTs reporting survival outcomes for BRAF-mutant mCRC. Kaplan-Meier curves were digitized and IPD reconstructed using established methods. A one-stage meta-analysis using Cox proportional hazards models was performed to estimate pooled overall survival (OS) and progression-free survival (PFS). Models were adjusted for study-level covariates and clustering, with Bonferroni correction applied for multiple comparisons. Eighteen RCTs comprising 11,931 participants were included. Pooled median OS was 22.3 months for BRAF-directed regimens, 17.1 months for VEGF-targeted therapy, and 10.1 months for EGFR-directed therapy across studies evaluating first-line therapy. Across first-line studies, BRAF inhibitor directed regimen was associated with significantly improved OS compared with EGFR inhibition (HR 0.43, 95% CI 0.31-0.60; P < 0.001) and improved PFS (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.42-0.53; P < 0.001). VEGF inhibition also demonstrated superior OS compared with EGFR inhibition (HR 0.56, 95% CI 0.38-0.81; p < 0.001). EGFR-directed regimen consistently demonstrated the poorest survival outcomes across analyses. In this reconstructed IPD meta-analysis, BRAF-directed therapies were associated with the most favourable survival outcomes, whereas EGFR directed regimen demonstrated limited clinical benefit in BRAF-mutant mCRC. These results highlight the importance of biologically aligned pathway-targeted therapy and provide comparative evidence to inform treatment selection in this aggressive molecular subtype.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EO-CRC; diagnosed before age 50 years) is increasing worldwide. Although current data indicate that EO-CRC may be biologically distinct from average-onset CRC (AO-CRC; diagnosed at age ≥50 years), molecular differences remain poorly defined. To address this knowledge gap, we generated a single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) atlas from 189 primary CRC tumors (54 EO-CRC, 135 AO-CRC) spanning eight decades of life, with at least 20 tumors in most age decades. Our analyses stratified tumors by microsatellite status and accounted for tumor sidedness, stage, patient sex and neoadjuvant treatment history, modeling age continuously or categorically (EO-CRC versus AO-CRC). Among microsatellite-stable (MSS) tumors, those from younger patients were characterized by increased stromal and decreased epithelial proportions, which we confirmed using multispectral immunofluorescence and machine learning in an external cohort of 712 MSS CRC tumors (18 EO-CRC, 694 AO-CRC). Tumor epithelial cells from young patients exhibited increased expression of long noncoding RNAs and FN1, with a trend toward increased heterogeneity in copy number alterations. MSS left-sided EO-CRC tumors had more cell-cell interactions, with epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition-related signaling pathways (FN1/GDF/ACTIVIN) showing increased, cell type-specific interactions. Our large high-resolution snRNA-seq atlas uncovers age-associated features of CRC and provides a resource for the community to understand EO-CRC biology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The rising incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) challenges existing paradigms of tumorigenesis. Classical models based on cumulative mutational burden, environmental exposure, and hereditary predisposition fail to explain the emergence of malignancy in individuals under 50 years of age. In this review, we propose that EOCRC may be driven by accelerated biological aging and review how core aging processes are prematurely activated in EOCRC. Importantly, these alterations extend beyond the tumor microenvironment and are present in circulating immune cells and inflammatory mediators. We propose that EOCRC develops prematurely in response to environmental, metabolic, genetic, and related factors that systemically accelerate biological aging. This approach reconciles the origin of EOCRC with traditional models of tumorigenesis, while highlighting novel opportunities for early detection, risk stratification, and therapeutic intervention.

To investigate the value of endorectal ultrasound (ERUS)-based habitat analysis in predicting pathologic response to neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NCT) in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). Consecutive patients treated between January 2018 and May 2025 were randomly divided into training and test sets at a 7:3 ratio. Tumor habitat subregions were defined using K-means clustering, and radiomic features were extracted and selected. Clinical, habitat, and fusion models were developed, and model performance was evaluated using ROC analysis, calibration curves, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Among 407 patients, tumor location, cT stage, extramural vascular invasion, and tumor-stroma ratio differed significantly between good- and poor-response groups (p < 0.05). For predicting response to NCT, the clinical, habitat, and fusion models achieved AUCs of 0.885 (95% CI: 0.840-0.927), 0.911 (95% CI: 0.872-0.943), and 0.958 (95% CI: 0.935-0.979) in the training set and 0.757 (95% CI: 0.668-0.841), 0.720 (95% CI: 0.599-0.828), and 0.829 (95% CI: 0.737-0.906) in the test set, respectively. In the test set, the fusion model outperformed the habitat model (p = 0.010), whereas the difference from the clinical model was not statistically significant (p = 0.097). The fusion model exhibited the highest sensitivity in both sets (0.956 and 0.897, respectively). In the test set, it yielded the lowest Brier score (0.174) and generally provided the greatest net benefit across most threshold probabilities of 0.12 to 0.75. The fusion model demonstrated promising performance for predicting response to NCT in LARC. Prospective multicenter external validation is required before clinical implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer and the second leading cause of cancer-related deaths worldwide. In unresectable metastatic (m)CRC, systemic therapy is the standard of care, and maintaining anti-angiogenic pressure remains important in the chemorefractory setting, as shown in 2nd and 3rd line treatment. Fruquintinib, a selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor of VEGF receptors 1, 2, and 3, recently demonstrated a 2.6-month overall survival benefit versus placebo in advanced mCRC and is now a new option for heavily pre-treated patients. However, real-world data on fruquintinib use and predictors of its efficacy remain limited. PRODIGE108-COHORTE2320 - COFRUQ (NCT07124858) is a French multicentre prospective observational cohort primarily designed to identify clinical and biological factors associated with fruquintinib efficacy under real-world conditions. The primary endpoint is investigator-assessed overall survival. Main secondary objectives include progression-free survival, objective response rate, disease control rate, safety, and quality of life. Eligible patients are ≥18 years old with histologically confirmed mCRC receiving fruquintinib within its EMA indication. Biological studies (tumour and blood collection) will identify prognostic and predictive biomarkers, alongside pharmacokinetic analyses. The cohort aims to enrol 300 patients over 3 years and has been open for enrolment in France since March 2026.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Schlafen 5 (SLFN5) is a member of the Schlafen protein family originally identified for its roles in immune regulation and cell cycle control. Structurally, SLFN5 contains an N-terminal Schlafen Core domain involved in nucleic-acid binding, a Linker domain, and a C-terminal Helicase domain required for efficient suppression of LINE-1 retrotransposition. In cancer, SLFN5 exhibits highly context-dependent functions, acting either as a tumor suppressor or as a pro-tumorigenic factor depending on tumor type and experimental conditions. It suppresses proliferation and invasion in breast cancer and renal cell carcinoma via PTEN/AKT signaling and downregulation of MMPs, while promoting progression in castration-resistant prostate cancer, glioblastoma, and colorectal cancer through AR/mTORC1, STAT1 co-repression, and IFN-JAK-STAT inhibition, respectively. Discrepant findings in lung cancer suggest that supraphysiological expression may trigger non-canonical effects. Clinically, SLFN5 expression correlates with tumor stage, metastasis, and patient survival, supporting further evaluation of SLFN5 as a potential prognostic biomarker, although its diagnostic utility remains to be established. This review summarizes the structural features, molecular functions, and tumor-type-specific roles of SLFN5, with an emphasis on recent advances in oncology research, providing insights that may contribute to personalized cancer therapy and prognostic evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The pioneer transcription factor FOXA2 controls developmental gene programmes, metabolic homeostasis and epithelial-mesenchymal plasticity, and its expression dysregulation is a recognized feature of colorectal cancer. The structural and thermodynamic consequences of FOXA2 missense variants remain poorly defined. We interrogated 659 missense SNPs across the human FOXA2 locus within an integrated multi-algorithm framework. Sequential filtering with SIFT, PolyPhen-2, PhD-SNP and SNPs&GO converged on three high-confidence deleterious variants (M190I, R197Q and L402P), which were profiled further with ConSurf, I-Mutant 2.0, MUpro, MutPred2 and DynaMut2. Conservation and structural mapping placed M190I (ConSurf-8) and R197Q (ConSurf-9) in the winged-helix DNA-binding domain (PF00250) and L402P (ConSurf-5) in the HNF_C domain (PF09354). R197Q is solvent-exposed and predicted to perturb promoter DNA contacts, whereas the buried M190I and L402P substitutions are predicted to act through local destabilization at the substitution site. In three independent 50-ns molecular dynamics replicates per system, all variants deviated from wild-type backbone behavior. M190I converged prematurely into a displaced conformational state, whereas R197Q and L402P continued to drift late in the trajectories. Backbone fluctuations increased non-locally, clustering in flexible regulatory segments (~290-316) and the C-terminal transactivation domain 2 (452-456). Principal component analysis indicated a more concentrated collective-mode structure in the mutants, and dynamic cross-correlation analysis weakened residue coupling, consistent with disrupted long-range communication. Of twelve trajectory-level comparisons, only the R197Q hydrogen-bond reduction reached nominal significance (p = 0.025, Hedges' g = -2.28), indicating a large reduction in average hydrogen-bond count relative to wild-type; the remaining eleven comparisons showed non-significant moderate-to-large effects. Expression enrichment was highest in colorectal cancer cell lines, providing expression-level context for FOXA2 in CRC biology. These findings computationally prioritize M190I, R197Q and L402P as candidates for experimental validation.

Cross-dataset concordance was highest between GSE8671 and GSE89076 (r = 0.70), with 1040 shared upregulated and 500 shared downregulated genes, whereas GSE14333 showed weak concordance with GSE8671 (r = -0.11) and GSE89076 (r = -0.01). ADMET profiling indicated the most balanced drug-likeness for MK3207, poor predicted solubility for R428, and multiple rule-based violations for Hesperidin. Each complex underwent a 100 ns all-atom MD simulation in explicit solvent. CUL4A-Hesperidin retained hydrogen bonds with GLU680, THR537, GLN673, and THR535 in > 83% of frames and a LYS459 π-cation interaction in 73.3%. USP2-R428 maintained key PHE364, SER190, and ARG363 contacts with a protein-referenced ligand RMSD of 4.84 ± 0.58 Å. Conversely, SMAD5-MK3207 showed substantial displacement (14.09 ± 0.62 Å) and < 4% docking hydrogen-bond occupancy. Single-frame 100 ns MM-GBSA endpoint energies were -107.62, -95.99, and -88.00 kcal/mol, respectively. Collectively, the results support CUL4A-Hesperidin and USP2-R428 as the most dynamically persistent complexes, while the initial SMAD5-MK3207 binding mode requires re-evaluation and experimental validation.

Fecal calprotectin (FC) can help to differentiate inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) from other causes of lower gastrointestinal (GI) symptoms. This study aimed to study FC testing in primary care, associated factors, subsequent secondary care referrals and IBD diagnoses. A retrospective cohort study was conducted using primary care data in England. Adults aged 18-60 with lower GI symptoms between 2015 and 2023 were included. FC testing 30 days before to 3 months after a recorded lower GI symptom was examined. A random-effects logistic regression model explored patient-level factors associated with FC testing. Referral pathways and diagnostic outcomes among patients with FC testing were examined. Of 830 936 symptomatic patients, 34 944 (4.2%) had FC testing. FC testing increased from 1.6% of symptomatic patients in 2015 to 7.7% in 2023 (P = .001). Factors negatively associated with FC testing included female sex (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 0.80; 95% CI, 0.78-0.82), lower socioeconomic status (aOR, 0.90; 95% CI, 0.86-0.95), smoking (aOR, 0.86; 95% CI,, 0.83-0.89) and obesity (aOR, 0.92; 95% CI, 0.89-0.95). Among patients referred to gastroenterology, 23.7% with FC >250µg/g were diagnosed with IBD, but only 4.1% with FC 100-250µg/g. Among patients with rectal bleeding and FC 100-250µg/g, 9% had IBD. Despite normal FC results (<100µg/g), 25.2% of symptomatic patients were still referred to secondary care, of whom 0.5% were diagnosed with IBD and 1% with colorectal cancer. FC can effectively triage primary care patients with suspected IBD. Despite negative FC results, a significant proportion of patients were still referred to secondary care, with very few diagnosed with IBD.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies represent a major global health burden characterized by high mortality rates, pronounced genomic heterogeneity, and resistance to conventional therapies. While cancer research has historically focused on apoptosis, non-canonical regulated cell death (RCD) pathways have recently emerged as critical regulators of oncogenesis and tumor suppression. Among these pathways, oxeiptosis is a recently identified, non-inflammatory, and caspase-independent cell death mechanism triggered by hyperphysiological levels of reactive oxygen species (ROS). This pathway is mechanistically governed by the mitochondrial Kelch-like ECH-associated protein 1 (Keap1)/phosphoglycerate mutase family member 5 (PGAM5)/ apoptosis-inducing factor mitochondria-associated 1 (AIFM1) signaling axis. Under conditions of toxic oxidative stress, elevated ROS levels activate Keap1, facilitating the PGAM5-mediated dephosphorylation of AIFM1. This review synthesizes the pathophysiological roles of oxidative stress and the regulatory landscape of oxeiptosis across major GI cancers, including esophageal, gastric, colorectal (CRC), pancreatic, and hepatocellular carcinomas (HCC) 1. Although clinical translation in esophageal and pancreatic cancers is currently constrained by a paucity of direct experimental data, recent multi-omics and bioinformatics analyses have identified oxeiptosis-related gene signatures as robust prognostic and therapeutic biomarkers in gastric cancer and HCC. Furthermore, preclinical evidence demonstrates that small molecules and natural products can successfully exploit the oxeiptotic cascade to bypass established apoptotic resistance. Specifically, the natural compounds sanguinarine and auriculasin trigger potent, PGAM5-dependent oxeiptosis in CRC models, while phenethyl isothiocyanate, dasatinib, and methyl-cantharidimide exhibit strong therapeutic synergy in HCC cell lines. Collectively, targeting oxeiptosis represents a highly promising preclinical strategy to overcome chemoresistance in GI malignancies; however, further in vitro, in vivo, and clinical investigations are essential to validate its therapeutic efficacy and determine whether modulating this pathway translates into improved patient survival and clinical outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Venous thromboembolism (VTE) is a major complication of colorectal cancer (CRC), but whether CRC-associated thrombotic susceptibility includes cell-specific inherited regulatory components in peripheral blood remains unclear. To investigate associations between CRC genetic liability and VTE-related outcomes within peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) regulatory contexts. We integrated CRC GWAS, FinnGen VTE-related outcomes, and TenK10K PBMC single-cell eQTL data across 28 immune cell types using cell-stratified Mendelian randomization (csMR). Prioritized signals were further examined in single-cell RNA-seq datasets and bulk transcriptomes. Conventional MR showed no clear evidence that CRC liability increased VTE, DVT, or PE risk, and LD Score regression detected no significant genome-wide genetic correlation. In contrast, csMR identified nominal, cell-context-dependent associations. B intermediate cells were prioritized across VTE (OR, 1.16; 95% CI, 1.03-1.32), DVT (OR, 1.30; 95% CI, 1.08-1.57), and PE (OR, 1.26; 95% CI, 1.07-1.49), while CD14 + monocytes and CD4 + central memory T cells received additional support from downstream single-cell analyses. Gene-level analyses prioritized LAMA5, LIMA1, and TRIM28 in these respective cell contexts. In bulk blood, RPS21 showed consistent disease-associated expression patterns and discriminated VTE patients from healthy controls in an external dataset (AUC, 0.865; 95% CI, 0.800-0.923). These findings suggest that genetic overlap between CRC liability and thrombotic phenotypes may be localized to selected PBMC regulatory contexts rather than broadly detectable genome-wide. Among the prioritized signals, B intermediate cells showed the most consistent csMR associations across VTE, DVT, and PE. The cell-gene pairs, together with RPS21, warrant independent genetic, functional, and prospective validation as candidates for studying peripheral immune regulation and blood-based markers of CRC-associated thrombosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The co-occurrence of germline pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants (PVs) in BRCA1/BRCA2 and mismatch repair genes (Lynch Syndrome) (BRCA-LS) is an infrequent overlap of the two most frequent hereditary cancer syndromes. Recent reviews have examined whether the cancer risk profile in BRCA-LS carriers is independent for both syndromes or if both germline variants act as mutual modifying factors, including a synergistic effect. This study on BRCA-LS Multi-locus Inherited Neoplasia Allele Syndrome (MINAS) aims to report six affected families, perform a systematic review (SR) of the literature to identify previously reported patients, and analyze the phenotype of this genetic condition. Including the reported families and the patients retrieved by the SR (40 publications), 92 patients from 69 families were analyzed. The analysis of the BRCA-LS MINAS phenotype showed a balanced distribution of BRCA and LS-related tumor patterns and tumors outside the established BRCA or LS spectra were uncommon. Carriers of PVs in MLH1 and MSH2/EPCAM were more likely to be diagnosed with ≥ 2 tumors [OR 3.60-95% CI 1.29-10.55; p = 0.0095] and with extracolonic tumors [OR 3,28 (CI95 1,26-8,84) p =0.0089] than carriers of PVs in MSH6 and PMS2, findings that are consistent with known genotype-phenotype correlations in LS. Our findings suggest that in the context of clinically ascertained patients with a personal or family history of cancer, BRCA-LS MINAS is primarily characterized by the independent expression of both syndromes and that potential synergistic effects require further evaluation in studies including systematically ascertained patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Idiopathic inflammatory myopathies (IIM, "myositis") are rare autoimmune diseases of the skeletal musculature, which are associated with an increased risk of cancer, particularly in adults. Malignant tumors occur especially frequently in dermatomyositis (DM), emphasizing the need for systematic cancer screening. This review provides a practice-oriented summary of the association between IIM and malignant diseases and addresses the recommendations of the International Myositis Assessment and Clinical Studies Group (IMACS) for cancer risk stratification and screening. A selective literature search was carried out including current studies, register data and consensus guidelines. The focus was on the IMACS recommendations on risk stratification and screening published in 2023. Approximately 20-25% of all adult patients with IIM develop a malignant disease within 3 years after disease onset. Patients with DM are at the highest risk, showing an approximately twofold increased risk of cancer compared to other IIM subtypes. Common malignancies include lung, ovarian, colorectal, breast, thyroid and nasopharyngeal carcinomas as well as lymphomas. Risk factors for paraneoplastic myositis include the presence of a DM subtype, but also specific autoantibodies such as anti-transcription intermediary factor 1‑gamma (TIF1-γ) and anti-nuclear matrix protein 2 (NXP2) antibodies, and clinical features such as age > 40 years at disease onset, persistently high and treatment-refractory disease activity, dysphagia and cutaneous necrosis. Based on these factors, the individual cancer risk can be stratified and screening and follow-up examinations are recommended in accordance with the IMACS guidelines. The systematic early detection of malignant comorbidities in IIM is essential, as malignancies represent the leading cause of death in these patients. The recently published IMACS recommendations enable a standardized, risk-adapted approach to cancer screening and are intended to facilitate early diagnosis and treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Short-course radiotherapy (SCRT)-based regimens, including SCRT-alone and SCRT-based total neoadjuvant therapy (SCRT-based TNT, defined as SCRT followed by consolidation chemotherapy), have emerged as alternative neoadjuvant options to long-course chemoradiotherapy (LCCRT) for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). This meta-analysis stratified analyses by the type of SCRT regimen and whether LCCRT arms received preoperative consolidation chemotherapy, to systematically compare their efficacy and safety and inform personalized treatment selection. A systematic search of PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, and Web of Science identified randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing SCRT-based regimens and LCCRT up to November 2025. Two reviewers independently performed study selection, data extraction, and risk-of-bias assessment. Pooled analyses were conducted using Review Manager 5.3, with relative risk (RR) or hazard ratio (HR) and 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Nine randomized trials (reported in 16 publications), involving 3,061 patients, were included. In the primary comparison of SCRT-based TNT versus standard LCCRT, the SCRT-based TNT group achieved a significantly higher pathological complete response rate (RR = 1.56, 95% CI: 1.24-1.97, P = 0.0002), whereas tumor downstaging and locoregional failure showed no significant differences from the LCCRT group. The SCRT-based TNT regimen was associated with a significantly higher incidence of grade ≥ 3 acute toxicity (RR = 1.63, 95% CI: 1.14-2.34, P = 0.008), and showed numerical trends toward improved overall survival (HR = 0.99, 95% CI: 0.76-1.28, P = 0.91) and disease-free survival (HR = 1.05, 95% CI: 0.77-1.43, P = 0.77) that did not reach statistical significance. SCRT alone was associated with lower pCR (RR = 0.13, 95% CI: 0.03-0.51, P = 0.003) and downstaging rates (RR = 0.66, 95% CI: 0.56-0.79, P < 0.00001) but a markedly lower incidence of acute toxicity (RR = 0.12, 95% CI: 0.05-0.29, P < 0.00001). An exploratory analysis based on a single small trial found no significant differences between SCRT-based TNT and LCCRT-based TNT across all major endpoints. Pooling all SCRT-based strategies obscured clinically meaningful heterogeneity and yielded no significant differences for any primary endpoint. SCRT-based TNT significantly improves pCR compared with standard LCCRT but does not translate into survival benefit, with a numerical increase in locoregional failure. SCRT-alone offers lower acute toxicity but substantially poorer tumor response, warranting use only in selected patients. The comparison between SCRT-based TNT and LCCRT-based TNT remains inconclusive. SCRT-based regimens represent heterogeneous treatment pathways rather than a uniform substitute for LCCRT, requiring individualized clinical decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Racial/ethnic disparities in colorectal cancer mortality persist in the United States despite treatment advances. We examined racial/ethnic differences in guideline-concordant care (GCC) receipt and cancer-specific mortality, estimated the proportion of the Black-White disparity mediated through GCC, and tested for heterogeneity in the GCC-survival association across groups. Population-based cohort study using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program. Adults with a first primary colorectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed 2010-2017 were included (N = 45,267). GCC was operationalized as a composite score (0-4) per NCCN recommendations. The primary outcome, cancer-specific mortality (CSM), was analyzed using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models. Race/ethnicity x GCC interactions were tested by likelihood ratio test; causal mediation decomposed effects into mediated and direct components. Among 45,267 patients (52% male), CSM occurred in 10,478 (23%) over a median 77 months. GCC receipt differed significantly across groups (all p < 0.001). Non-Hispanic Black patients had higher adjusted CSM than White patients (SHR 1.20, 95% CI 1.11-1.28); Asian/PI patients had lower CSM (SHR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.95). A significant race x GCC interaction was identified (p = 0.0036), with a stronger GCC-CSM association among Black than White patients (interaction HR 0.907, 95% CI 0.847-0.971). GCC differences accounted for only 2.2% (95% CI 0.8-4.5%) of the Black-White disparity. Racial/ethnic disparities in colorectal cancer mortality were not substantially explained by differences in GCC receipt. A significant race/ethnicity x GCC interaction indicated that Black patients derived greater survival benefit per care component. Equitable care delivery is important but insufficient to eliminate persistent disparities; structural and social determinants must also be addressed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Advanced anal squamous cell carcinoma (ASCC) is a rare human papillomavirus-associated malignancy with historically limited prospective evidence for systemic therapy. InterAAct established carboplatin-paclitaxel as a clinically favorable chemotherapy backbone compared with cisplatin-fluorouracil. POD1UM-303/InterAACT-2 subsequently showed that adding retifanlimab significantly improved progression-free survival in patients with no prior systemic therapy for advanced disease. At the final overall-survival analysis, median overall survival was 32.8 versus 22.2 months (HR 0.75, 95% CI 0.55-1.01); the regimen has received regulatory authorization in the United States, the European Union, and Japan. EA2176 is evaluating carboplatin-paclitaxel with or without nivolumab and will clarify whether first-line PD-1-based chemoimmunotherapy represents a reproducible class effect. This focused narrative review critically summarizes the evidence for retifanlimab- and nivolumab-based strategies and proposes a practical framework for treatment selection. Key considerations include performance status, immune-checkpoint-inhibitor eligibility, HIV infection, autoimmune risk, neuropathy, organ function, tumor burden, local symptom control, and post-chemoimmunotherapy sequencing. Retifanlimab plus carboplatin-paclitaxel currently has the most mature phase III evidence, whereas nivolumab-based chemoimmunotherapy remains investigational pending EA2176. Treatment decisions should distinguish phase III-validated options from class-effect extrapolation and integrate multidisciplinary local therapy when appropriate.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postoperative nutritional management is critical for gastrointestinal cancer surgery patients, yet discharge advice is often standardized and lacks individualization. Whether an AI-facilitated individualized and quantified strategy improves short-term dietary intake compared with standard generic advice remains unclear; this trial does not isolate the independent effect of AI. To determine whether AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance using structured prompts improves short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms versus standard discharge advice. In this single-center, randomized controlled trial, 90 patients undergoing laparoscopic gastric or colorectal cancer surgery were assigned 1:1 to AI-facilitated individualized guidance generated by DeepSeek v3.2 using an ABC-structured prompt plus clinician review or standard discharge dietary advice (standard care group). The intervention combined AI, individualization, quantified targets, written guidance, and clinician review; the trial cannot isolate AI alone. Primary outcome was energy intake adequacy (≥ 90% of target) at 30 days post-discharge. Secondary outcomes included protein intake adequacy, nutritional status, patient-reported outcomes, process measures (expert-rated quality scores, provider time), and 30-day complications. Outcome assessors were blinded to group assignment. Baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups. The AI-guided group achieved significantly higher energy adequacy (66.7% vs. 40.0%, OR 3.0, 95% CI 1.3-7.1, P = 0.01) and protein adequacy (62.2% vs. 35.6%, OR 2.9, 95% CI 1.2-6.8, P = 0.01) at 30 days. Expert-rated quality scores were superior in the AI-guided group for completeness (4.6 vs. 3.2), individualization (4.8 vs. 2.8), and actionability (4.5 vs. 3.5) (all P < 0.001), while provider time per patient was reduced (8.2 vs. 12.5 min, P < 0.001). Patient-reported outcomes showed significant improvements in fatigue, nausea/vomiting, appetite loss, and gastrointestinal symptoms (GSRS total score 2.1 vs. 2.5, P = 0.03) in the AI-guided group. No significant differences were observed in weight change, serum nutritional markers, or complication rates. AI-facilitated individualized nutritional guidance improved short-term dietary intake adequacy and patient-reported symptoms and reduced provider time compared with standard generic advice. These findings do not show that AI itself is superior to similarly individualized non-AI counseling and do not establish longer-term nutritional or clinical benefit. Clinical supervision remains essential.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The risk of post-operative metachronous advanced colorectal neoplasia (MAN) among patients with sporadic average-onset colorectal cancer (AOCRC: ≥50 years) is well studied, whereas comparative risk in early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC: <50 years) remains unclear. Post-operative CRC surveillance guidelines are primarily based on studies in AOCRC cohorts and may not represent optimal post-operative surveillance intervals in EOCRC. To compare the incidence of MAN between patients with sporadic AOCRC and EOCRC and to identify clinical risk factors associated with MAN. In this retrospective cohort study, patients with EOCRC and AOCRC who underwent ≥1 postoperative surveillance lower endoscopies between 2011-2021 were included. Patients with inflammatory bowel disease, total proctocolectomy, and hereditary CRC syndromes were excluded. The most advanced metachronous lesion detected during postoperative surveillance was categorized as normal, nonadvanced neoplasia (NAN), or MAN. 230 EOCRC patients and 504 AOCRC patients (median age 44 and 66, respectively) were included. Overall rates of MAN were similar between EOCRC and AOCRC groups (13% vs. 16.1%, p = 0.342), however, AOCRC patients had a significantly lower MAN-free survival than EOCRC patients. In EOCRC patients, metachronous NAN, as the most advanced lesion detected during follow-up, was less frequent (17% vs. 26%, p = 0.009), the interval between CRC surgery and first surveillance endoscopy was shorter, and the follow up time was longer than in AOCRC patients. Older age, smoking exposure, and a distally located (descending and/or sigmoid colon) index cancer were independently associated with the development of MAN. Our study did not identify a sufficiently increased burden of MAN in EOCRC to support an age-specific surveillance strategy. Smoking is associated with MAN and should be avoided in CRC patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is one of the top three cancers globally in terms of both incidence and mortality, and its development may be influenced by an inflammatory environment in the intestines, often associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis. Food bioactives could modulate gut microbiota through anti-inflammatory and epigenetic mechanisms. Given the significant role of thioproline as a food bioactive with antioxidant properties, its potential to modulate gut microbiota and mitigate CRC remains largely unexplored. This study aims to understand the effects of thioproline on gut microbiota community and investigate the mechanisms through which thioproline regulates gut microbiota and exerts its anticancer effects. Fecal and intestinal tissue samples were collected from health, CRC, and thioproline-treated CRC mice. The metagenome and metabolome data revealed that thioproline treatment significantly altered the gut microbiota community composition and metabolism in CRC mice. These CRC-associated gut microbiota and bacterial metabolites returned to normal levels. Moreover, under thioproline treatment, the microbial-metabolite interactions in CRC mice shifted toward patterns more closely resembling those observed in healthy mice. Thioproline treatment increased linoleic acid levels in mice, indicating its role in promoting linoleic acid metabolism to therapeutically restore homeostasis and alleviate inflammation in CRC. This was further supported by hematoxylin and eosin staining, which demonstrated that thioproline alleviated inflammation in CRC mice. Our study highlights thioproline's dual role in regulating the gut microbiota community and bacterial metabolism, modulating bacteria-host interactions, and ultimately reducing inflammation in CRC. These findings offer valuable insights for future research and therapeutic applications.IMPORTANCEColorectal cancer (CRC) is associated with gut microbiota dysbiosis and intestinal inflammation. While food bioactives can modulate the microbiome, whether thioproline exerts inhibitory effects against CRC through microbial regulation remains unknown. Using integrated metagenomics and metabolomics, we show that thioproline treatment restores the gut microbiota composition and bacterial metabolites disrupted by CRC to near-normal levels. Importantly, thioproline remodels microbial metabolite interaction networks, elevates linoleic acid levels, and alleviates intestinal inflammation. This study provides a systems-level perspective on how a single dietary bioactive compound reshapes the gut microbial ecosystem and its metabolic landscape to reduce inflammation in CRC. Our findings suggest a potential role for microbiome-targeted nutritional strategies in protecting against CRC progression through modulation of the gut microbiota and intestinal microenvironment.
