ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
ObjectivesTo map the existing evidence on the evolution of low anterior resection syndrome, including factors associated with stage-specific low anterior resection syndrome outcomes and longitudinal changes in symptoms.MethodsThis scoping review was conducted in accordance with the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and reported following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses extension for Scoping Reviews guideline. Seven databases were searched through 31 December 2025, with English databases searched from 1 January 2012 and Chinese databases from 1 January 2013. Eligible studies included adults aged ≥18 years who underwent sphincter-preserving anterior resection for rectal cancer and were diagnosed with low anterior resection syndrome at least twice postoperatively.ResultsTwenty-three studies were included. Major low anterior resection syndrome was most prevalent during the early follow-up period, particularly at approximately 1-3 months. Symptom improvement was most evident between 6 and 18 months, whereas overall symptom patterns tended to stabilize after approximately 18-24 months, with relatively limited changes subsequently up to 36 months. Tumor and anastomotic location, surgical approach, radiotherapy and/or chemotherapy, and stoma-related factors were associated with low anterior resection syndrome at different follow-up stages or with longitudinal symptom changes. However, only a few studies directly examined longitudinal changes or trajectory-related factors.ConclusionLow anterior resection syndrome is a dynamic condition with stage-specific patterns and substantial inter-individual variability. Understanding its temporal evolution and associated factors may help identify high-risk patients, optimize the timing of assessment, and tailor supportive care and rehabilitation across recovery stages. However, heterogeneity in study design, follow-up schedules, and outcome measures limits comparability. Future research should adopt standardized longitudinal designs, harmonized follow-up protocols, larger samples, and more comprehensive assessment tools to strengthen evidence for individualized low anterior resection syndrome management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Screening is a key tool to improve colorectal cancer (CRC) outcomes and mitigate disparities, and reliable estimates of screening variation across communities can help prioritize screening interventions. However, existing screening surveillance infrastructure relies on labor-intensive telephone survey methodology. We aimed to develop novel methods of estimating CRC utilization for small geographic areas using North Carolina multi-payer claims data and to identify patterns and determinants of geographic variation in screening adherence. Using data from the Cancer Information and Population Health Resource, a multi-payer claims database, we generated annual screen-eligible cohorts and identified screening procedures. We then used Bayesian spatial models to estimate screening adherence for 1180 zip-code-based small areal units. We used geographic contextual data to re-weight estimates from the insured to the total (uninsured + insured) population. We examined associations between area-level racial composition and screening adherence stratified by age and sex. Across all years, the observed proportion of person-years up-to-date among insured age-eligible adults statewide was 80.3%; among all age-eligible adults, 75.8% were estimated to be up-to-date. Model-estimated screening adherence in small areas ranged between 43.1% and 93.1%. Increasing Black racial composition was associated with lower screening adherence across all sexes and age strata. Older age and female sex were associated with higher screening adherence. Model-based estimation of CRC adherence from insurance claims and geographic data is feasible at scale and yields comprehensive estimates at small-area levels. There is wide variation in community-level screening adherence, with many areas falling below public health targets.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients receiving maintenance hemodialysis (HD) have limited physiologic reserve and high competing cardiometabolic risk, yet surgery remains central to cure for many gastrointestinal (GI) malignancies. Evidence describing oncologic surgery in this population is fragmented across cancer sites and data sources. A PRISMA guided systematic review of adult patients on maintenance HD undergoing resection for GI malignancy was performed. The review searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and CENTRAL through March 2026 and included comparative observational studies reporting perioperative or long-term outcomes. In parallel, a propensity-score matched TriNetX cohort of adults undergoing major GI cancer surgery between 2010 and 2025. HD was defined by preoperative ESRD and dialysis dependence codes. Patients were matched 1:1 on age, sex, race, and ethnicity. The primary outcome was 30-day mortality; secondary outcomes were 30-day sepsis, pneumonia, and acute myocardial infarction (AMI). The review included 20 studies after screening 1,744 deduplicated records and 83 full texts. Colorectal surgery provided the most robust evidence: dialysis was associated with markedly higher mortality and serious morbidity, and a published meta-analysis of colorectal surgery estimated a pooled mortality odds ratio (OR) of 4.12. Gastric, pancreatic, and hepatobiliary reports were smaller but showed the same direction of effect, with frequent infectious and cardiovascular complications and substantial competing non-cancer mortality. In the current TriNetX analysis, 3,757 HD patients were matched to 3757 non-HD controls. Thirty-day mortality was 11.4% in HD patients versus 3.0% in controls (OR: 4.21, 95% CI: 3.40-5.22). HD patients also had higher rates of sepsis (14.1% vs. 3.9%; OR 4.06), pneumonia (8.1% vs. 2.2%; OR: 4.02), and AMI (4.3% vs. 0.9%; OR: 5.18). Across GI cancer operations, maintenance HD identifies a very high-risk surgical phenotype. The dominant short-term pattern is excess death, infection, and cardiopulmonary morbidity; the dominant long-term pattern is competing non-cancer mortality. Surgery remains appropriate for selected patients with resectable disease, but perioperative dialysis timing, multidisciplinary optimization, and treatment in experienced centers are critical.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Multidisciplinary management of locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) has evolved rapidly over the past decade, guided by data from multiple prospective clinical trials. Changes in treatment of cT3-4 or N+ rectal cancer at a comprehensive cancer center between 2015 and 2023 were analyzed retrospectively. Of 1121 patients who received neoadjuvant therapy, 793 (71%) underwent active surveillance and 328 (29%) underwent surgery within 3 months. Treatments whose use increased from 2015 to 2023 included TNT with consolidation chemotherapy (from 10% to 81%), neoadjuvant chemotherapy alone (from 13% to 21%), immunotherapy or targeted therapy (from 0% to 10%), and oral capecitabine versus intravenous fluorouracil in combination with oxaliplatin (from 4% to 56%). Among patients who received TNT, nonoperative management with sustained clinical complete response rose from 38% to 50%. With more patients undergoing nonoperative management, the rate of pathologic complete response decreased from 22% to 8.3%. Robotic assistance was used in 88% of surgeries. The adoption of new diagnostic and treatment paradigms allows for longer intervals until surgery, more frequent use of active surveillance, and higher rates of organ preservation without compromising safety or oncologic outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) metastases to retroperitoneal (RP) and lateral pelvic (LP) lymph nodes are functionally classified as stage IV disease. While metastasectomy is established for select hepatic and pulmonary metastases, the role of lymphadenectomy for nodal disease remains uncertain. This study evaluates the safety, indications, and oncologic outcomes of RP/LP lymph node dissection in CRC. A single-center retrospective review identified patients undergoing RP or LP lymphadenectomy for CRC between 2011 and 2024. Patients with peritoneal metastases or incomplete data were excluded. Demographic, operative, and outcome data were analyzed. Associations with nodal positivity, recurrence-free survival (RFS), and overall survival (OS) were assessed using Fisher's exact test and univariate Cox regression. Forty-nine patients underwent lymphadenectomy, 45% for synchronous and 55% for metachronous nodal metastases. Dissection was selective in 61% and formal in 39%, with 86% undergoing concurrent major abdominal procedures. There was no perioperative mortality and dissection-specific morbidity was low (two lymphatic leaks, both after multivisceral resection). Pathologic nodal metastases were confirmed in 59% of cases. Median RFS and OS were 30.2 and 104.9 months, respectively. Node positivity was associated with initial N2 stage but did not affect RFS or OS. Formal lymphadenectomy was associated with shorter RFS, likely reflecting higher disease burden. RP and LP lymphadenectomy can be safely performed, even with multivisceral resection. Pathologic nodal status did not predict survival, suggesting potential benefit to lymphadenectomy irrespective of final pathology. These findings support its use in carefully selected patients with controlled systemic disease and isolated nodal recurrence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Canadian Armed Forces (CAF) includes a large workforce with a diverse spectrum of military occupations and potentially related exposures. The objective was to examine associations between service in distinct military occupations and the subsequent development of cancer. This retrospective cohort study used CAF administrative data linked to national cancer registry data. Personnel and Veterans with at least 2 years of CAF service between 1990 and 2017 were identified (N = 19,660 females and 129,840 males). Service in common military occupations was categorized using military occupation codes. Associations with incident primary cancer diagnoses (all cancers combined and specific cancer types) between 1990 and 2017 were analyzed using sex-stratified Cox proportional hazards models with age as the timeline for analysis, adjusted for enrollment era. For most military occupations, no significant associations with all cancers combined or specific cancer types were observed in females or males. Exceptions included occupation as an aviation systems technician, which in females was associated with an increased likelihood of breast cancer, and in males with all cancers combined as well as oral, colorectal, Hodgkin lymphoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, and kidney/renal cancers. Positive associations were also observed in females for colorectal cancer in supply technicians, and in males for non-Hodgkin lymphoma in gunners, pancreatic cancer in infanteers, and lung/bronchus cancer in supply technicians. These findings can inform health protection measures, benefits and services for military personnel and Veterans. Future research should examine specific factors linked to the increased risks observed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A significant number of patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) undergo stoma-forming surgery. For many, an ostomy is not curative, and disease exacerbations requiring ongoing therapy may be required. Despite this, IBD patients with stomas are frequently excluded from clinical trials due to the heterogeneity in outcomes and the absence of validated measurement tools. The TOAST-IBD project aimed to develop a Core Outcome Set (COS) for IBD patients with stomas undergoing interventional trials to address this issue. Candidate outcomes were identified through a systematic literature review and patient focus groups. These were refined using a two-round online Delphi process, with scoring based on the importance of each outcome in determining treatment success. Participants were recruited internationally and grouped into four stakeholder panels: patients, specialist and research nurses, colorectal surgeons, and gastroenterologists. Feedback was provided after each round to allow score refinement. A final consensus meeting determined the COS. A total of 81 outcomes were identified and categorized into five themes. In total, 76 stakeholders (73.1% response rate) from 17 countries participated in the Delphi process, carrying 37 outcomes forward. At the final consensus meeting, 37 experts and patients agreed on a six-domain COS: maintenance of hydration and volume status, maintenance of nutritional status, symptom-based clinical activity, objective marker-based disease activity, and two quality-of-life domains (IBD-related and stoma-specific). An IBD Stoma COS has been produced by all key stakeholders. This COS will standardize outcome reporting and support creation of validated measurement instruments, facilitating the inclusion of this underserved group in future clinical trials. This study has been registered with the COMET Initiative as study 2855 (https://www.comet-initiative.org/Studies/Details/2855) and followed its recommended methodological procedures. The systematic review has been registered with the PROSPERO database (PROSPERO-ID: CRD42023442388).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To discuss the concept, assessment tools, influencing factors, and intervention measures of stoma disgust. Publications on stoma disgust in colorectal cancer patients with enterostomy were retrieved, summarized, and evaluated by a team of investigators and clinical experts. Full-text articles written in English and the Chinese language, and studying stoma disgust in colorectal cancer patients with enterostomy. The research topic includes the concept, assessment tools, influencing factors, and intervention measures of stoma disgust. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) ranks third in cancer-related mortality worldwide, with current chemotherapy hampered by severe toxicity and drug resistance. This study systematically characterized polysaccharides from Ampelopsis japonica Makino (AJ) and evaluated their anti-CRC activity. Three homogeneous polysaccharides, i.e., AJP-1a (neutral glucan), AJP-2a (neutral heteropolysaccharide), and AJP-3a (acidic heteropolysaccharide rich in arabinose, galactose, mannose, and glucuronic acid) were isolated. Experimental evidence primarily from the Congo red assay, together with complementary morphological observations by ‌Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope (FESEM) and Atomic Force Microscope (AFM), indicated that AJP-3a adopts a stable triple-helical conformation. Complementary structural analyses including monosaccharide composition (HPLC-PMP), glycosidic linkage mapping (methylation-GC-MS), 1D/2D NMR spectroscopy, and GLYCAM 3D modeling of single-chain energy-minimized conformations further corroborated the fine structural features and high branching degree of AJP-3a. In a DiI-labeled HCT116 zebrafish xenograft model, all three polysaccharides dose-dependently inhibited CRC proliferation, with AJP-3a showing the strongest effect. Notably, at their respective maximum non-toxic concentrations (AJP-3a: 50 μg/mL; 5-FU: 40 μg/mL), AJP-3a exhibited stronger tumor-suppressive efficacy than 5-FU in terms of tumor fluorescence intensity and tumor area. By systematic comparison of structural features and anti-CRC potency across the three distinct polysaccharides, we observed a consistent trend between structural complexity and tumor-suppressive capacity. We hypothesize that triple-helix conformation, high branching degree, and abundant uronic acid residues are potential structural factors contributing to the superior bioactivity of AJP-3a. Collectively, this work provides systematic structural characte rization of AJ polysaccharides and demonstrates their therapeutic potential against CRC, rendering AJP-3a a potential bioactive fraction worthy of further mechanistic investigation and preclinical safety evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major cause of cancer-related mortality, with metastasis, therapeutic resistance, and the persistence and plasticity of cancer stem cells (CSCs) contributing to treatment failure. This review evaluates evidence linking defined probiotic strains, multispecies formulations, and other microbiota-directed interventions to CRC stemness and metastatic biology. Because effects vary according to strain identity, viability, dose, formulation, host context, and experimental model, findings from one microorganism or product cannot be generalized across probiotics as a class. Most available studies do not demonstrate direct targeting of colorectal CSCs. Instead, reported effects are predominantly indirect and involve changes in microbiota composition, microbial metabolites, inflammatory and immune signaling, epithelial barrier integrity, and the tumor microenvironment. A smaller group of mechanistic studies identifies strain- and context-specific effects on stemness-related pathways. Animal studies also report effects on intestinal barrier integrity, tumor growth, angiogenesis, immune-cell composition, treatment-associated toxicity, and experimental treatment sensitivity, but these findings remain preclinical. Human evidence is limited and mainly concerns gastrointestinal symptoms, microbiota changes, and treatment tolerance. None of the human studies identified in this review demonstrated that probiotic supplementation improves objective tumor response, progression-free survival, overall survival, metastasis-free survival, or checkpoint-immunotherapy efficacy in CRC. Accordingly, the current literature supports biological plausibility for selected, well-characterized microbial interventions rather than a class-wide anticancer effect of probiotics. Direct CSC eradication, prevention of metastatic recurrence, and reproducible enhancement of chemotherapy/immunotherapy efficacy remain clinically unproven. Future studies require strain-resolved reporting, standardized dosing and formulation, mechanistic validation, and adequately powered clinical trials with oncologic endpoints.

There is published data to demonstrate that colorectal cancer (CRC) occurs at a higher incidence and results in greater mortality in persons of Black ancestry, when compared to White and Hispanic populations. In the state of Georgia, the annual incidence of CRC in persons of Black ancestry was estimated to be greater than the national annual incidence in the United States. Over an 8-y period, there were 910 persons diagnosed with CRC, and 701 (77%) were of Black ancestry. This included 370 (52.8%) males and 331 (47.2%) females, with a mean age of 60.85 y (SD ± 11.51; range 26-101; median 61). Fifty-three percent of patients had locally advanced or metastatic disease at the time of diagnosis. This population of persons with Black ancestry has a greater incidence of right-sided CRC (54%). At the time of diagnosis, 53% of persons have locally advanced or metastatic disease. From a public health standpoint, there may be a need to educate this population on screening programs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Several social factors, including poverty, race, and geographic location contribute to inequalities in screening rates, incidence, and death rates in rectal cancer patients. Historical redlining graded "hazardous" regions in neighborhoods based on their population's racial composition. Previous work showed worse cancer outcomes in redlined districts and areas of poorer socioeconomic status (SES). The National Accreditation Program for Rectal Cancer (NAPRC) was established in 2017 to enhance uniformity in treatment, and reduce mortality and complication rates in rectal cancer. The study objective was to determine if there is an association between the implementation of NAPRC standards and improved outcome disparities for rectal cancer affected by areas of historical redlining or poorer SES. This was a retrospective cohort analysis in an NAPRC-certified institution in patients with rectal adenocarcinoma from 2020 to 2024. Redlining maps were obtained using Home Owners' Loan Corporation maps from ArcGIS, with zip codes labeled as A/B (desirable) and C/D (unfavorable). SES was measured with a median household income of $74,580 to define low and high status. Adherence with NAPRC standards of care, recurrence rate, survival rate, and 2-y disease free survival (DFS). Median follow-up was 25 mo. High NAPRC adherence was seen: 95% of patients received tumor board presentations, 93.4% timely treatment, 94.5% pretreatment magnetic resonance imaging, and 97.6% staging computed tomography. Overall cancer recurrence rate was 8.6%, mortality 17.7%, and 2-y DFS 87%. For redlined districts (132 patients: 26 favorable, 106 unfavorable), no differences in stage (P = 0.82), adherence, recurrence (11.5% versus 6.6%), or DFS (88.4% versus 87.8%) was seen. By income (242 low, 142 high), no differences were seen in stage (P = 0.26), adherence to protocol, recurrence (7.8% versus 9.8%), or DFS (86.7% versus 87.3%). In this NAPRC-accredited institution, there were no disparities based on redlining or SES, and this may suggest that uniformity in treatment may help mitigate existing inequalities. Further research with larger populations is recommended to establish and promote NAPRC implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The role of a comprehensive genomic profile (CGP) and molecular residual disease (MRD) in circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) for risk stratification of resectable colorectal oligometastases (CRMs) remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate the feasibility of ctDNA analysis in patients with CRM and to conduct an exploratory assessment of its recurrence risk. This study assessed ctDNA in patients with previously untreated resectable CRM scheduled for curative resection, before starting treatment and 4 weeks postoperatively. Pretreatment samples were prospectively tested for genomic alteration using a 74-gene CGP assay (Guardant360). The pathogenic mutations in BRAF, KRAS, PIK3CA, SMAD4, or TP53 were defined as poor genomic profiles. Postoperative samples were retrospectively analyzed for MRD using a methylation-based MRD assay (Guardant Reveal). Among 118 eligible patients, pretreatment ctDNA was detected in 114 (96.6%) patients, 75 (63.6%) of whom had poor profiles. MRD was detected in 34 (31.2%) patients out of 109 evaluable patients who underwent surgery. Using multivariable analysis, pretreatment poor profiles and post-operative MRD were significantly associated with shorter recurrence-free survival (RFS) [hazard ratio (HR) 3.28, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.72-6.25; HR 4.07, 95% CI 2.40-6.90, respectively] and time to surgical failure (TSF) (HR 2.76, 95% CI 1.35-5.64; HR 3.05, 95% CI 1.70-5.45, respectively). Patients with both poor pretreatment profiles and post-operative MRD demonstrated the worst prognosis in RFS (HR 13.28, 95% CI 5.86-30.10), TSF (HR 8.98, 95% CI 3.77-21.40), and overall survival (HR 9.21, 95% CI 2.06-41.18). Combining pretreatment CGP and post-operative MRD in ctDNA showed potential for improved prognostic stratification after CRM resection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) exhibits substantial molecular heterogeneity, requiring integrative approaches to define clinically meaningful tumour subtypes. Although large international consortia have extensively profiled CRC, global datasets underrepresent many ethnicities. Understanding how local tumors align with/diverge from globally characterized cohorts is essential to contextualize disease biology and refine precision oncology strategies. This study was designed as a comparative, hypothesis-generating analysis benchmarked against a Global Genomic Landscape (GGL) of 2,023 CRC tumors. Whole exome and transcriptome sequencing was performed on pathologically confirmed tumors (N = 20) and normal tissues (N = 5) using the Illumina HiSeqX. Bioinformatic pipelines identified somatic variants and dysregulated genes, which were compared with GGL data. We identified 814 dysregulated genes and ∼16,440 somatic variants. While the single base substitution (SBS) profile was similar to GGL, one double base substitution signature (DBS17) and two insertion-deletion signatures (ID7, ID19) were unique to our cohort. Six driver genes (ACVR2A/BAX/PRDM2/RGS12/RNF43/TCF7L2) with recurrent variants were observed in our cohort. Only three genes with emerging roles in CRC (MET/SOX9/TGIF1) overlapped across dysregulation, somatic variation, and GGL datasets. Indel hotspot variants in EIF2B3 (p.Ala151GlnfsTer57) and UBR5 (p.Glu2121LysfsTer28) were exclusive in non-survivors. The prevalence of canonical Western driver mutations (APC, TP53, KRAS, PIK3CA, SMAD4) was markedly lower in our cohort. Few drug-targetable genes overlapped with GGL; however, several approved or high-confidence targets were identified. Compared with the global genomic landscape, our findings suggest potential population-associated differences in driver architecture and therapeutic opportunities that warrant validation in larger independent Indian cohorts.

AimAnastomotic leak remains a life-threatening complication after colorectal surgery. Static preoperative models show only modest discrimination, whereas clinical signs often appear late. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Health systems in middle-income countries are often compromised by parallel, unintegrated subsystems (public safety-net, social security, private care), exacerbating health disparities. We evaluated how this architecture and individual socioeconomic position relate to advanced clinical stage at diagnosis, stratified by anatomic site (colon and rectal) and age cohort, in Quito, Ecuador, over a 30-year period (1990-2019). After excluding unstaged and death certificate-only cases, data from 2,552 patients were analyzed. Selection bias was evaluated using Cramer's V and rank-biserial effect sizes. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors associated with synchronous late-stage (stage IV) presentation, adjusting for demographics, socioeconomic markers, and diagnostic health sector. Secondary overall survival trends were evaluated using Kaplan-Meier estimates and exploratory stage-stratified Cox models. In patients ≥65 years, public-sector diagnosis was associated with a higher odds of late-stage colon cancer (adjusted Odds Ratio = 2.04; 95% CI, 1.24 to 3.35) compared with diagnosis in the private sector but showed no association with rectal cancer. Late-stage diagnosis probability remained stable over the 30-year study period. Exploratory survival models linked public-sector entry to higher mortality hazards (adjusted hazard ratios, 1.35-3.01), with adjusted survival trajectories exhibiting broad temporal stability across recent decades. Public-sector care s persistently associated with diagnostic delays that has spanned three decades, independent of socioeconomic position. Beyond early-detection barriers, exploratory survival models generate the hypothesis that public-sector disparities extend into longitudinal survival outcomes, reinforcing the urgent need for structural reforms such as organized screening and equitable public care pathways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant PD-1 blockade produces substantial tumor regression in mismatch repair-deficient or microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) locally advanced lower rectal cancer (LRC), but response assessment and the safety of watch-and-wait (W&W) remain uncertain. BASKET was an open-label, multicenter, single-arm, phase 2 study conducted at two Chinese centers (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04643041). Patients with non-metastatic dMMR/MSI-H LRC received six cycles of neoadjuvant sintilimab (200 mg every 3 weeks), followed by multimodal assessment including endoscopy, digital rectal examination, CEA, MRI, CT, and transrectal ultrasound-guided biopsy. Patients meeting protocol-defined clinical complete response (cCR) criteria entered W&W surveillance. Of 15 treated patients, 13 completed treatment and response assessment. All 13 per-protocol patients achieved cCR and entered W&W (13/13, 100%), corresponding to 13/15 (86.7%) in the intention-to-treat (ITT) population. Only 1 of 13 per-protocol patients (7.7%) achieved radiologic complete response on MRI; persistent radiographic abnormalities were adjudicated using the other response modalities. At a median follow-up of 37.7 months (range, 0.7-56.2) in the ITT population, one death occurred 0.7 months after treatment initiation, and no local recurrence or distant metastasis. The estimated 1-year disease-free and overall survival rates were both 93.3% (95% CI, 68.1%-99.8%). Among the 13 per-protocol patients no local recurrence, distant metastasis, or death was observed. No grade 3 or higher immune-related adverse events or biopsy-related complications occurred. These findings suggest that W&W may be feasible in carefully selected patients following rigorous multimodal response assessment and with close surveillance; however, the incremental value of biopsy and the oncologic equivalence of W&W to surgery remain unproven.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
With growing evidence and evolving guidelines, organ preservation with watch and wait for stage II to III rectal cancer after neoadjuvant therapy is increasingly implemented. However, the true frequency of watch-and-wait use is unknown. To estimate rates of intentional organ preservation with watch and wait by evaluating secular trends across age groups. This retrospective cohort study used data from the National Cancer Database (NCDB), with analyses conducted in September 2025. Patients with stage II to III rectal cancer diagnosed between 2006 and 2023 who received neoadjuvant chemoradiation in Commission on Cancer-accredited hospitals participating in the NCDB across the US were included. Age, year of diagnosis, and treatment strategy (proctectomy vs nonsurgical management). The primary outcome consisted of watch-and-wait rates, defined as excess nonsurgical management greater than baseline. To account for nonsurgical management unrelated to the decision for watch and wait, joinpoint regression estimated baseline rates of nonsurgical management and annual percentage changes. A secondary analysis examined associations of age and year with watch-and-wait rates using multivariable logistic regression. Among 101 001 patients with rectal cancer (median [IQR] age, 60 [51-69] years; 37 957 female [37.58%]), 84 324 underwent surgery and 16 677 did not. Baseline rates of nonsurgical management remained stable through 2014. Joinpoints occurred in 2014 and 2019, with annual percentage changes of -0.45% (95% CI, -2.26% to 0.78%; P = .42) in 2006 to 2014, 9.83% (95% CI, 4.66% to 13.73%; P = .001) in 2015 to 2018, and 21.71% (95% CI, 17.74% to 29.57%; P < .001) in 2019 to 2023. Baseline nonsurgical management increased with age, from 1331 of 19 785 patients younger than 50 years (6.73%) to 1748 of 6210 patients aged 80 years and older (28.15%). Earlier adoption occurred in older patients; the group aged 80 years and older surpassed 5-percentage point excess watch and wait by 2015 (33.78% annual rate vs 28.15% baseline rate [5.63-percentage point excess]) and 10% by 2017 (39.56% annual rate vs 28.15% baseline rate [11.41-percentage point excess]), compared with 2019 (12.88% annual rate vs 6.73% baseline rate [6.15-percentage point excess]) and 2021 (20.75% annual rate vs 6.73% baseline rate [14.02%] excess) in patients younger than 50 years. Overall, watch and wait increased from 140 of 6101 patients (2.30%) in 2015 to 2068 of 6280 patients (32.94%) in 2023. Increasing year (odds ratio for 2023 vs 2006, 6.23; 95% CI, 5.48 to 7.09) and older age (odds ratio for ages ≥80 vs <50 years, 4.25; 95% CI, 3.98 to 4.54) were independently associated with nonsurgical management (both P < .001). In this study, watch-and-wait rates increased across all age groups, with a marked acceleration after 2019 suggesting evidence-concordant adoption of the watch-and-wait approach. This underscores the need for careful patient selection, accurate clinical response assessment, and rigorous surveillance monitoring to ensure safe oncologic outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), typically defined as colorectal cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age, is increasing in incidence worldwide and exhibits distinctive clinical, molecular, and environmental features compared with later-onset (LOCRC) disease. However, the tumor-immune microenvironment (TiME) of EOCRC and its implications for prevention and therapy remain poorly characterized. In this review, we synthesize current evidence on the TiME of EOCRC and contrast it with that of conventional LOCRC. We first discuss global features of the EOCRC immune landscape, including innate and adaptive immune composition, functional states, and spatial organization, highlighting areas where apparent age-related differences reflect true biology versus confounding by tumor site, stage, or mismatch repair (MMR) status. We then examine immunogenomic and epigenomic determinants-such as MMR deficiency distribution, microbial mutational signatures, chromosomal instability, and age-conditioned methylation programs-that shape neoantigen landscapes, antigen presentation, and immune evasion in younger patients. Next, we review microbiome-driven immunomodulation, focusing on dysbiosis, genotoxic bacteria, and early-life and young-adult exposures as joint modifiers of mucosal immunity and tumor development. Finally, we explore how these insights inform immune-based prevention (risk stratification, screening, diet and microbiome interventions, and chemoprevention) and immunotherapy strategies, including checkpoint blockade and rational combinations in the predominant microsatellite-stable EOCRC population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the most prevalent malignancies globally. Despite significant advancements in targeted therapies, drug resistance and therapeutic target mutations continue to pose challenges. Consequently, identifying novel therapeutic targets and developing related compounds are essential for discovering new CRC treatment strategies. The RIO Kinase 1 (RIOK1) protein has emerged as a potential anti-tumor target, playing a critical role in eukaryotic ribosomal biosynthesis and modulating cellular proliferation. However, few compounds have been designed to target RIOK1, and the antitumor activity of RIOK1 inhibitors has yet to be thoroughly investigated. In this study, we report the optimization of pyridine caffeic acid benzyl amide derivatives as RIOK1 inhibitors and identified CINS-1 as a potent compound with markedly enhanced binding affinity for AfRIOK1 and RIOK1. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Three-dimensional (3D) spheroid models have become essential in cancer biology, drug screening, and tissue engineering. However, their small size, fragile structure, and tendency to disintegrate during routine histoprocessing present persistent technical challenges. Conventional paraffin embedding often results in tissue fragmentation, loss of spatial orientation, and poor section quality, whereas cryosectioning often compromises cellular morphology. Here, we present a robust, cost-effective protocol for preserving and sectioning fragile 3D spheroids, resulting in high-quality histological sections with intact architecture and excellent cellular detail. The method involves optimized handling and embedding procedures that stabilize spheroids during standard formalin fixation, paraffin infiltration, and microtomy, eliminating mechanical distortion and preserving spherical integrity for consistent sectioning. We demonstrate the successful application of this protocol across different tumor spheroids derived from distinct tissue types, including MDA-MB-231 (breast carcinoma), Caco-2 (colorectal adenocarcinoma), and A549 (lung carcinoma) cell lines, with subsequent compatibility with hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) staining protocols. This protocol is compatible with immunohistochemistry (IHC) and immunofluorescence (IF). In our qualitative comparison with conventional methods, we found that our approach effectively limits sample loss, promotes consistent inter-section reproducibility, and preserves fine structural features, such as necrotic cores, proliferative zones, and extracellular matrix components. This protocol provides a reliable, accessible solution for routine histological analysis of fragile 3D spheroids, facilitating more accurate morphological assessment in translational research settings. Key features • Cost-effective agarose-coated plates for reproducible spheroid formation. • Complete in-tube processing to minimize sample loss and damage. • Floating tube system for reliable paraffin infiltration without specialized equipment. • Produces high-quality sections compatible with H&E. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Changes in lipid metabolism have been associated with the development of colorectal cancer (CRC), and they may serve as diagnostic markers to identify patients who have developed colorectal neoplasia. This study aimed to identify such biomarkers using untargeted lipidomics. Lipidomics were performed in serum from a racially diverse series of CRC cases and controls from Chicago and Tucson. In addition, enzymatic activity of secretory acid sphingomyelinase (aSMase; S-SMase) was measured in samples from the Tucson CRC series, and two series of adenoma patients. Untargeted lipidomics in the Chicago CRC series revealed significant alterations in sphingolipids. Targeted lipidomics revealed a robust signature of five sphingomyelins (SMs) that were significantly decreased in Chicago CRC patients compared to controls and were validated in the Tucson series. S-SMase activity, which degrades serum SMs, was elevated in CRC cases (0.13 ± 0.10 Cer/SM UACC CRC cases vs. 0.05 ± 0.04 Cer/SM controls; p<0.0001). In mostly white adenoma patients from Tucson, serum S-SMase activity could predict the presence of colorectal neoplasia (0.13 ± 0.07 Cer/SM in UACC adenoma cases vs. 0.03 ± 0.02 Cer/SM in controls; p<0.0001). However, S-SMase activity was not significantly different in Black adenoma patients from Chicago compared to controls. Together, these studies demonstrate for the first time the potential for S-SMase activity to serve as a biomarker for colorectal neoplasia in specific populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC), defined as colorectal cancer in individuals under 50 years old, is a growing global epidemic, with incidence and mortality rates steadily increasing over the past several decades. Although EOCRC has been linked to established colorectal cancer risk factors, its underlying causes remain poorly understood. We propose that EOCRC may result from exposure to environmental factors, collectively known as the exposome, that have increased globally across EOCRC birth cohorts. Based on our current knowledge of EOCRC, the use of antibiotics is a potential exposome that may increase the risk for EOCRC. We hypothesized that exposure to antibiotics alters the gut microbiota resulting in dysbiosis that promotes inflammation in the distal colon and rectum, leading to increased risk of developing EOCRC. To test this, we examined the effects of repeated exposure to two commonly prescribed classes of pediatric antibiotics on gut microbiome composition, colonic inflammation, and tumor development following exposure to a carcinogen in a mouse model of EOCRC. A/J mice were subjected to multiple rounds of antibiotics followed by treatment with azoxymethane (AOM) to initiate tumor development, and assessment of colon tumor development. Antibiotic treatment induced dysbiosis and both local and systemic inflammation. Subsequent exposure to AOM showed that the two classes of antibiotics had different effects on tumor development in the distal colon and influenced the risk for EOCRC development in different ways.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) can occur in individuals who are not overweight or have obesity (normal-BMI MASLD), yet disease burden and management remain poorly characterized. We compared long-term outcomes and incretin-based therapy use between normal-BMI MASLD (nbMASLD) and overweight/obesity-associated MASLD (obMASLD) across racial and ethnic groups. We conducted a retrospective, observational study using the TriNetX United States Network. Adults diagnosed with MASLD or metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH) from 2005-2025 were classified using ethnicity-informed normal-BMI thresholds: <23 kg/m2 for Asian, <27 kg/m2 for Native Hawaiian and Pacific Islander, and <25 kg/m2 for White/others. Propensity-score matching balanced demographic and clinical covariates. Outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier analyses and Cox proportional hazards models with obMASLD as the reference group. Among 619,171 eligible patients, 51,940 matched pairs were identified. Nb-BMI MASLD was associated with higher all-cause mortality across grouped ethnic groups, with survival of 77.49% versus 83.93% in obMASLD (HR 1.735, CI 1.653-1.822). Ethnicity-specific risks included higher myocardial infarction risk in White and Black patients, higher stroke risk in White patients, higher ESRD risk in Black patients, and increased cancers (colorectal, pancreatic and multiple myeloma) among White patients. Incretin-based therapy (IBT) use was markedly lower in nbMASLD but was associated with improved survival. Patients with nbMASLD demonstrated an increased mortality and ethnicity-specific clinical complications than obMASLD despite a more favorable metabolic profile. These findings demonstrate a potential treatment gap for nbMASLD patients and the shortcomings of BMI-based strategies to risk-stratify MASLD patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metabolic reprogramming and immune evasion are hallmarks of cancer metastasis, but how tumor metabolism shapes the immune microenvironment during colorectal cancer (CRC) liver metastasis remains poorly understood. The role of E-cadherin (CDH1) beyond cell adhesion is unexplored. We integrated single-cell RNA sequencing, pseudotime trajectory inference, and in vivo/in vitro functional assays in primary and liver-metastatic CRC models. CellChat was used to map intercellular communication. Histone lactylation, ADAM10 activation, and CDH1 shedding were validated by biochemical and immunohistochemical assays. PGK1-driven glycolysis is upregulated in liver metastases and promotes metastatic progression. Elevated lactate induces histone H3K18 lactylation, activating ADAM10 expression. ADAM10 cleaves CDH1, releasing its soluble ectodomain. This fragment acts as a ligand for KLRG1 on T cells, driving exhaustion and immunosuppression. Cell-cell communication analysis confirmed CDH1-KLRG1 as a top differentially activated pathway in metastasis. Functionally, targeting PGK1 or blocking CDH1 shedding inhibits liver metastasis and restores T-cell function. We identify a metabolic-epigenetic-immune axis in which tumor glycolysis reprograms immunity via lactate-induced CDH1 shedding. Soluble CDH1 functions as an immunomodulatory signal, linking metabolic activity to T-cell exhaustion. This redefines CDH1 as a dual-function molecule and reveals actionable targets for metastatic CRC. © 2026 The Pathological Society of Great Britain and Ireland.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) undergo colonoscopy for diagnosis, disease assessment, and colorectal cancer surveillance. We used the UK National Endoscopy Database (NED) to evaluate the quality of IBD surveillance and identify factors associated with procedural quality. All colonoscopies uploaded to NED between January 1 and December 31, 2024 were analyzed. IBD procedures were identified from recorded indications and classified as assessment or surveillance. Key performance indicators (KPIs) were assessed against national guidance. Case-mix-adjusted impacts of endoscopist- and service-level factors were evaluated using multilevel mixed-effects logistic regression. Of 588 841 colonoscopies, 2.7% (n = 15 971) were IBD surveillance. Although 56.8% of endoscopists performed at least one surveillance procedure, 18.9% performed one or more per month and delivered 57.1% of all surveillance. IBD surveillance quality was high (cecal intubation 96.1%; median withdrawal time 13 min), but adequate bowel preparation was below target (80.2%). Endoscopists performing ≥1 surveillance/month had higher adjusted polyp detection (used as a surrogate marker of mucosal inspection quality rather than true dysplasia) (odds ratio [OR] 1.26), and procedures allocated extended time had higher detection (OR 1.40). These findings suggest that regular exposure to IBD surveillance, adequate procedural time, and consistent use/documentation of dye-based chromoendoscopy are associated with higher polyp detection during IBD surveillance colonoscopy. Importantly, these findings relate to polyp detection rather than histologically confirmed dysplasia detection. Further work is required to determine whether service concentration or minimum surveillance volumes improve dysplasia-related outcomes. Service-level pathways analogous to English Bowel Cancer Screening with national standards and performance monitoring may warrant consideration.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer transmission risks from deceased organ donors to recipients may be overestimated, and there is often hesitancy in accepting potential donors with a history of cancer, regardless of absolute risk. We linked all persons referred for consideration for deceased organ donation (actual donors and potential donors forgone) and transplant recipients, 2010-2018, with the population cancer registry, 1976-2018, in NSW, Australia. We sought to estimate the transmission risk for common cancers (breast, prostate, colorectal) in deceased donors and identify missed opportunities for donation. Firstly, cancer transmission rates from actual donors were assessed. We then compared suspected cancer history during medical assessment with the cancer registry for those potential donors forgone. There were 165 cancer histories verified in 993 deceased donors, with one high-risk breast, six minimal-to-high-risk prostate, and no colorectal cancers. Organs from these seven donors were transplanted in 11 recipients (10 kidneys, 1 liver) with no evidence of 'Proven/Probable' cancer transmission after a median 6-years' follow-up. Additionally, 169/3588 (5%) potential donors were forgone for a suspected Common Cancer transmission risk. Of these, 6/169 (4%) had no cancer verified, and 39/169 (23%) had a verified cancer that was of minimal-to-low risk for transmission. Accepting these 45 additional donors would have increased donation rates by 5%. A balanced review of transmission and non-transmission events in organ donation, along with improved decision support, could inform current risk assessments and improve donation rates.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The ubiquitin-specific peptidase 18 (USP18) has been implicated in colorectal cancer (CRC), but its downstream effector molecules remain incompletely defined. USP18-interacting proteins were identified by immunoprecipitation-mass spectrometry (IP-MS) and validated by co-immunoprecipitation (co-IP). The regulation of KRT16 by USP18 was examined by qPCR, Western blotting, ubiquitination assays and cycloheximide (CHX) chase experiments in SW480 cells. Functional assays were performed in SW480, HT-29 and LoVo cells, comprising CCK-8 proliferation and wound-healing assays in all three cell lines, Transwell migration assays in SW480 cells, and Transwell invasion assays in HT-29 and LoVo cells. Clinical relevance was evaluated in the TCGA and GSE39582 cohorts and in a 100-case hospital cohort by immunohistochemistry (IHC) and paired Western blotting. IP-MS identified KRT16 as a USP18-associated protein. USP18 associated with endogenous KRT16, reduced KRT16 ubiquitination and prolonged the half-life of KRT16 protein. KRT16 and USP18 were concurrently upregulated in CRC in both the TCGA and GSE39582 cohorts; KRT16 expression correlated with USP18 expression (R = 0.68, P < 2.2 × 10-16), discriminated tumor from normal tissue (AUC = 0.899; 95% CI 0.852-0.945) and indicated poor overall survival (KRT16: HR = 2.024, 95% CI 1.273-3.218, P = 0.0029; externally validated in GSE39582, P = 0.0012). In the hospital cohort, high KRT16 expression (61.0%) was associated with T stage, and paired Western blots (n = 14) confirmed coordinated upregulation of USP18 and KRT16. Functionally, KRT16 knockdown reduced proliferation and impaired wound closure across all three cell lines, reduced Transwell migration in SW480 cells, and reduced invasion in HT-29 and LoVo cells, thereby attenuating the pro-tumor effects of USP18 overexpression. USP18 stabilizes KRT16 protein through deubiquitination and thereby promotes CRC cell proliferation and migration across multiple cellular backgrounds. These findings support the USP18-KRT16 axis as a candidate molecular axis warranting further preclinical evaluation in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lysine lactylation (Kla) is a metabolite-sensitive post-translational modification implicated in DNA repair, tumorigenesis, chemoresistance, and innate immunity. Recent studies also implicate Kla in intestinal disorders. This review synthesizes current evidence on protein lactylation in intestinal inflammation, inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, irritable bowel syndrome, intestinal fibrosis, radiation-induced injury, and enteric infection. We distinguish lactate-mediated receptor signaling and metabolic effects from covalent Kla, compare evidence across cell types and disease stages, and assess preclinical strategies targeting the lactate-lactylation axis. We also discuss microbiota-host metabolic crosstalk and mucus-penetrating nanodelivery, including the cross-border emulsification effect, an oil-in-water double-emulsion concept that describes traversal of the mucus barrier rather than a biochemical form of lactylation. Collectively, the available evidence supports a metabolism-epigenetics-immunity framework for gut pathophysiology, while highlighting unresolved questions concerning stereochemistry, site specificity, causality, safety, and prospective clinical validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lactose is the principal carbohydrate in milk, serving a critical role in infant energy metabolism as well as contributing to neurodevelopment, and the establishment of a healthy gut microbiota. Later in life, lactose digestion capacity varies widely across human populations owing to the genetically determined decline of intestinal lactase expression after weaning-a condition termed 'lactase non-persistence'. Approximately two-thirds of the global adult population exhibits reduced lactase activity, yet the clinical consequences of this enzymatic reduction are far less uniform than commonly assumed. This review provides a comprehensive examination of lactose functionality, the physiology of lactose digestion, and the consequences of lactase persistence and non-persistence. We present formal definitions for the spectrum of terms used in lactose research-including lactase persistence, lactase non-persistence, lactose maldigestion, and lactose intolerance-and argue that the critical distinction between lactose maldigestion (a physiological state) and lactose intolerance (a clinical syndrome) is frequently overlooked in both research and public health. Drawing on evidence from double-blind randomised controlled trials , microbiome intervention studies, and global epidemiological data, the evidence indicates that the majority of individuals with lactose maldigestion do not develop clinically meaningful symptoms at moderate intake levels of most dairy products. We further discuss the mechanism of colonic adaptation, whereby gradual lactose exposure selectively enriches Bifidobacterium populations capable of fermenting lactose without excessive gas production resulting in greater lactose tolerance. Finally, we examine the public health implications of these findings, noting that food-based dietary guidelines worldwide-including those in populations with high prevalence of lactase non-persistence-consistently recommend dairy consumption owing to its established associations with reduced risk of type 2 diabetes, colorectal cancer, and improved bone health.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Current trends in reconstructive surgery increasingly advocate delaying vaginal reconstruction until patients can participate in decision-making. While this approach may be appropriate for conditions such as Mayer-Rokitansky-Küster-Hauser syndrome and isolated vaginal agenesis, its application to patients with complex anorectal malformations (ARM), requires careful consideration. This narrative review discusses the anatomical, surgical, and psychosocial factors influencing the timing of vaginal reconstruction in patients with complex anorectal malformations. Drawing on contemporary surgical principles and extensive clinical experience with reconstruction, differences between ARM and other causes of vaginal atresia are examined, together with reconstructive options and emerging strategies to preserve future reproductive potential. Patients with complex ARM differ substantially from patients with isolated vaginal agenesis. They frequently present with associated urinary tract anomalies, neurogenic bladder, fecal incontinence as well as previous abdominal and perineal operations. In selected patients, vaginal reconstruction performed during the initial repair offers important technical advantages, including optimal pelvic exposure before fibrosis develops, preservation of surgical options, and avoidance of later operations in a hostile pelvis. The choice of reconstructive tissue should be individualized according to anatomy and anticipated bowel function. Native vaginal tissue remains the preferred option whenever available; however, when replacement is necessary, the rectum provides the most favorable intestinal substitute in appropriately selected patients, followed by colon, whereas small bowel should generally be reserved for situations in which other options are unavailable. Delayed vaginal reconstruction should not be considered the universal standard for patients with anorectal malformations. Surgical timing should be individualized according to anatomical complexity, predicted bowel function, future urological procedures, patient circumstances, and long-term quality-of-life considerations. Management within specialized multidisciplinary centers remains essential for optimizing both functional and reproductive outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Indocyanine Green (ICG) fluorescence imaging has emerged as a valuable tool for intraoperative assessment of bowel perfusion in colorectal surgery, with the potential to reduce anastomotic leakage. However, standardized protocols for its use remain undefined. This study aimed to evaluate the feasibility and clinical impact of ICG fluorescence imaging in laparoscopic colorectal resections. A prospective cohort of 60 patients undergoing laparoscopic sigmoidectomy or low anterior resection for colorectal cancer was analyzed. ICG was administered after high vascular ligation to guide anastomotic site selection. Perfusion was assessed using ICG fluorescence and the marginal arcade test. Primary outcomes were changes in anastomotic site and leakage rates; secondary outcomes included fluorescence time and its association with clinical variables. The mean time to fluorescence appearance was 24.5 seconds (range 8-45), with no significant differences according to sex (p = 0.20), age (p = 0.24), or neoadjuvant therapy (p = 0.38). ICG imaging led to modification of the planned anastomotic site in 6.7% of cases (n = 4), none of which developed leakage. In two cases, discordance between ICG fluorescence and marginal arcade assessment was observed. Overall, anastomotic leakage occurred in 6.7% (n = 4), exclusively in patients who had received neoadjuvant radiotherapy (p = 0.04). No association was found between leakage and anastomotic height, fluorescence time, or marginal arcade findings. No adverse reactions to ICG were reported. ICG fluorescence imaging is a safe and feasible adjunct for intraoperative perfusion assessment that supports anastomotic site selection and may contribute to reducing anastomotic leakage. Further studies incorporating quantitative fluorescence metrics are warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains the third most common malignancy and the second leading cause of cancer-related death worldwide, with limited biomarkers available for accurate prognostic stratification. This study integrates multi-cohort transcriptomic data from four GEO datasets (GSE39582, GSE17536, GSE14333, GSE33113; n = 1123) and the TCGA-CRC cohort (n = 621) to identify key differentially expressed genes and construct a validated prognostic risk score model. Differential expression analysis using the limma framework identified 642 upregulated and 588 downregulated genes (|log2FC|>1, FDR<0.05). Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) extracted hub genes from modules significantly correlated with overall survival. LASSO Cox regression then reduced the hub gene set to an eight-gene prognostic signature (MMP1, AURKA, TOP2A, CDH1, COL1A1, CLDN1, ETV4, CDX2) that stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups with significantly different survival outcomes (p < 0.001, log-rank test). The model achieved AUCs of 0.824, 0.796, and 0.768 for 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival in the training cohort and was validated in three independent datasets. High-risk patients exhibited immunosuppressive microenvironments (elevated M2 macrophages, Tregs) and increased resistance to standard chemotherapy agents. Integration of the risk score with clinical variables improved prognostic accuracy (C-index 0.812). These findings offer a robust bioinformatics-derived prognostic tool with implications for immunotherapy patient selection and personalized treatment planning in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate, multiplexed microRNA detection is critical for early cancer diagnosis. We present a droplet-based digital CRISPR/Cas13a platform for simultaneous, amplification-free detection of multiple miRNAs. By integrating double emulsion (DE) microfluidics with programmable crRNAs, the system achieves orthogonal, interference-free readouts, enabling precise absolute quantification in complex biological samples. The assay demonstrates high sequence specificity, robust orthogonality, and consistent performance across target combinations and matrices. Fluorescence-positive droplet counts correlate linearly with input concentrations, allowing quantification of miRNA-21, miRNA-29a, and miRNA-92a with 10 copies/μL representing the lowest concentration experimentally evaluated in this study. The applicability of the platform is further evaluated in a small proof-of-concept cohort of plasma samples from healthy controls and colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. This platform provides an amplification-free approach for multiplexed miRNA quantification and supports further development for clinical biomarker analysis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accelerated biological aging has been reported in certain racial/ethnic groups, raising concerns about widening outcome disparities with age. This phenomenon has not been adequately explored in cancer outcomes. National Cancer Database (2010-2021) was used to analyze outcomes in colorectal cancer (CRC) patients by race/ethnicity and age at diagnosis: < 65, 65-69, 70-74, 75-79, and ≥ 80 years. Primary outcomes were overall survival (OS) and 90-day postoperative mortality (PM), analyzed with multivariable regression. In this large national cohort study of 585,729 patients, non-Hispanic Black (nHB) patients had worse OS across all age groups, with the largest disparity in the < 65 group (median OS: 64.1 in nHB vs. 127.0 months in non-Hispanic White (nHW); HR 1.28, 95% CI 1.26-1.30) and smaller disparity in ≥ 80 group (median OS: 19.2 in nHB vs. 26.5 months in nHW; HR 1.06, 95% CI 1.03-1.09). The 90-day PM in nHB patients was higher than nHW, particularly in the < 65 (OR 1.23, 95% CI 1.15-1.31) group. In contrast to non-oncological literature, we did not observe widening racial/ethnic disparities with age. Largest disparities were found in younger age groups suggesting differences in tumor biology may play a more important factor for cancer outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate polyp segmentation is important for computer-aided colorectal cancer screening, yet it remains challenging because of ambiguous boundaries, irregular morphologies, small lesion regions, and the visual similarity between polyps and surrounding mucosal tissues. Existing methods mainly enhance local details or global semantics at the whole-image level, while regional observations are often processed independently or reconstructed without explicitly considering repeated spatial coverage. To address this issue, we propose ORR-Net, an overlap-aware regional representation learning framework for polyp segmentation. ORR-Net constructs dense overlapping regional observations together with a downsampled global observation, allowing the same image location to be represented under different neighboring contexts. A CNN-Transformer dual-branch encoder extracts full-image convolutional features and hierarchical regional-global representations. During decoding, Overlapping Regional Context Attention (ORCA) introduces global contextual information into the regional representations. Overlap-Aware Average Reconstruction (OAAR) further aggregates repeatedly covered positions to recover a continuous full-image representation. A coarse structural prior and multi-level adaptive supervision are employed to support final prediction and intermediate optimization. Experiments on five public polyp segmentation benchmarks demonstrate that ORR-Net achieves competitive or leading performance in segmentation accuracy and boundary quality. The method also shows consistent improvements on unseen cross-dataset test sets. Ablation studies verify the effectiveness of the overlapping regional observation strategy, regional-global interaction, overlap-aware reconstruction, and the associated training designs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer remains a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, with the liver representing the predominant site of metastatic spread. For patients with colorectal liver metastases (CRLM) who are not candidates for surgical resection, systemic chemotherapy provides disease control but rarely achieves durable hepatic responses. Radioembolization with yttrium-90 (Y-90) microspheres, delivered via the hepatic artery to exploit the preferential arterial supply of liver tumors, has emerged as an important locoregional option in this setting. This review examines the current evidence base for radioembolization in CRLM, covering patient selection, indications across lines of therapy, dosimetric advances, and clinical outcomes. Appropriate candidacy requires careful assessment of performance status, hepatic tumor burden, tumor biology, lung shunt fraction, and extrahepatic disease extent, with the strongest outcomes observed in patients selected earlier in their disease course. Randomized controlled trials support second-line and third-line use, while unselected first-line use has not demonstrated a benefit. Dosimetric advances, including multicompartment personalized dosing, radiation segmentectomy, and radiation lobectomy, are enabling ablative and bridge-to-resection strategies in appropriately selected patients. Future investigation should prioritize biomarker-driven patient selection, personalized dosimetry, and combination strategies with systemic therapy to determine whether durable hepatic disease control can translate into a survival benefit.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The optimal timing of temporary ileostomy closure following restorative colorectal surgery remains controversial. Although previous randomized studies have demonstrated the feasibility of early closure in carefully selected patients, the influence of closure timing on operative complexity has not been prospectively evaluated. This multicenter randomized controlled trial compared a standardized 3-week ileostomy closure strategy with conventional delayed closure, with particular emphasis on technical and postoperative outcomes. In this prospective multicenter randomized controlled trial, 224 patients undergoing restorative colorectal resection with temporary diverting ileostomy were randomized to either early ileostomy closure at 3 weeks (n = 112) or conventional delayed closure (n = 112). Eligibility for reversal required rigorous confirmation of anastomotic healing using standardized clinical and endoscopic assessment, with selective computed tomography using rectal contrast when clinically indicated. The primary outcome was operative complexity, evaluated using operative duration, intraoperative adhesion severity, and the requirement for extended adhesiolysis. Secondary outcomes included postoperative morbidity, Clavien-Dindo complication grade, length of hospital stay, readmission, reoperation, re-diversion, and delay in adjuvant chemotherapy. Baseline demographic, clinical, and operative characteristics were comparable between the study groups. Early ileostomy closure was associated with significantly shorter operative duration (90 ± 12 vs. 130 ± 18 min; P < 0.001), substantially lower intraoperative adhesion severity (P = 0.04), and a markedly reduced requirement for extended adhesiolysis (5.4% vs. 21.4%; P < 0.001). Overall postoperative morbidity, Clavien-Dindo grade distribution, postoperative length of stay, readmission, reoperation, and mortality were comparable between groups. Delays in adjuvant chemotherapy occurred only in the early-closure group (3.6%), were limited to 1-4 weeks, and all affected patients subsequently commenced the planned oncologic treatment. In carefully selected patients with confirmed anastomotic healing, 3-week ileostomy closure is a technically feasible and safe strategy following restorative colorectal surgery. Compared with conventional delayed closure, reversal at 3 weeks significantly reduced operative complexity without compromising short-term postoperative outcomes. These findings support selective implementation of a standardized 3-week ileostomy closure strategy and identify operative complexity as a key determinant when selecting the optimal timing of ileostomy reversal. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Lynch syndrome is the most common hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome, yet remains substantially underdiagnosed despite effective risk reduction strategies. Identification of affected individuals is critical to enable cancer prevention, early detection, and cascade testing of at-risk relatives. Multiple complementary approaches to Lynch syndrome detection exist, each with distinct strengths and limitations across clinical settings.In this review, we summarize established and emerging strategies for Lynch syndrome identification in those with a personal and family history of colorectal neoplasia. Tumor-based mismatch repair deficiency testing remains an effective and cost-efficient screening strategy but is limited by incomplete implementation and imperfect sensitivity. Direct germline testing can overcome some of these limitations and identify additional hereditary cancer syndromes, though considerations regarding yield, cost, and interpretation remain. Family history-based approaches and risk prediction models offer additional tools but are constrained by challenges in data collection and clinical uptake.Optimizing Lynch syndrome identification will require integration of these strategies alongside system-level interventions to improve access, uptake, and equity in genetic evaluation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The Child Opportunity Index (COI) measures neighborhood-level resources for children. Children with congenital colorectal conditions are managed at few specialty centers. We compared neighborhood opportunity and urbanicity between children who travel for this care and those who do not. Retrospective cohort study of Pediatric Colorectal and Pelvic Learning Consortium registry patients with a valid ZIP code, used to assign COI and urbanicity. Travel was residence at least 50 miles (straight-line) from the treating center. Groups were compared using Fisher's exact and Cochran-Armitage trend tests; no adjusted models were fitted. Of 6258 patients, 3804 (60.8%) did not travel and 2454 (39.2%) traveled. Children who traveled were more often from low- or moderate-COI (48.6% vs. 36.5%) and rural (38.3% vs. 9.8%) neighborhoods; non-travelers were more often from very high-COI (28.2% vs. 18.3%) and, less markedly, very low-COI (12.6% vs. 10.2%) neighborhoods (all p < 0.001). Very low-COI neighborhoods accounted for 11.7% of the cohort versus approximately 20% nationally. Travel for specialty colorectal care is concentrated among children from lower-opportunity and rural neighborhoods. Because travel distance and rural residence are closely linked, and only children reaching a center are captured, these findings are descriptive and cannot quantify unmet need.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chronic disease prevalence at colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis has increased with population ageing. We evaluated the association between chronic diseases prevalent at CRC resection and recurrence. This nationwide Danish registry-based cohort study included patients who underwent curative-intent resection for stage I-III CRC from January 2002 through June 2020. Chronic diseases before resection were ascertained from hospital diagnoses using a modified Charlson Comorbidity Index that omitted malignancies and added five psychiatric disorders (20 diseases). Diseases were grouped into five clinical categories: cardiopulmonary, neurological, mental health, metabolic, and gastrointestinal. Recurrence was identified using a validated registry-based algorithm. We estimated 1-, 3-, and 5-year cumulative incidences and Cox hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), adjusting for age, sex, calendar year, smoking, alcohol, and body mass index. Among 39,239 patients, 7,326 (19%) developed recurrence within 5 years. Cumulative incidences for patients with versus without chronic disease were 5.0% versus 5.5% at 1 year, 14.7% versus 15.5% at 3 years, and 18.5% versus 19.6% at 5 years; adjusted HRs were 1.01 (95% CI, 0.96-1.07), 1.03 (0.98-1.08), and 1.03 (0.98-1.08). The 5-year adjusted HR was 1.11 (1.02-1.21) for mental health and 0.79 (0.58-1.07) for neurological diseases. Prevalent chronic diseases overall were not associated with increased CRC recurrence risk, although risk was higher with mental health diseases and lower with neurological diseases. Poorer survival in patients with CRC and chronic disease is unlikely to reflect more frequent recurrence. Future studies should clarify whether treatment tolerance contributes to these survival disparities.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The aldehyde dehydrogenase 2 (ALDH2) rs671 (G>A) variant, common in East Asians, impairs aldehyde detoxification. Pathogenic germline variants (PGVs) in homologous recombination repair (HRR) and mismatch repair (MMR) genes confer inherited susceptibility; however, their joint effects with rs671 remain poorly characterized. We conducted a case-control study of 4,418 cases of head and neck, esophageal, gastric, or colorectal cancer and 11,811 controls. Targeted sequencing identified HRR and MMR PGVs. Associations and interactions were assessed using Firth-penalized logistic regression, stratified by alcohol intake. Cumulative risk was estimated using Japanese population incidence data. HRR PGV carriers with the rs671 GA/AA genotype showed increased risk across all cancer sites compared with rs671 GG non-carriers. Joint effects were observed among drinkers for head and neck, esophageal, and gastric cancers, and among non-drinkers for gastric and colorectal cancers. Among MMR PGV carriers, rs671 GA/AA was associated with increased risk of esophageal and colorectal cancers (odds ratio, 95.62 and 24.57, respectively), with significant interactions (P = 0.017 and 0.0011, respectively). The rs671-MMR association for esophageal cancer was evident among drinkers, whereas colorectal cancer risk was elevated in both drinkers and non-drinkers. By age 80, cumulative risk (95% confidence interval) among MMR PGV carriers with rs671 GA/AA was 35.4% (7.7-90.3) for esophageal and 87.7% (46.9-99.9) for colorectal cancer. Impaired aldehyde detoxification and DNA repair deficiency jointly increase site-specific cancer risk. Integrating ALDH2 rs671 genotype, DNA repair PGVs, and alcohol exposure may improve risk stratification and prevention in East Asian populations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) are increasingly used to treat type 2 diabetes, yet little is known about its utilization patterns in patients with cancer history, given limited oncology-specific guidance. To evaluate trends and factors associated with GLP-1 RA use among Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, comparing those with and without cancer history. This retrospective cohort study used Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results-Medicare linked data to identify patients diagnosed with 7 common cancers in 2010 to 2021 and preexisting type 2 diabetes before cancer diagnosis. A noncancer cohort with type 2 diabetes was identified from a 5% random sample of Medicare beneficiaries and matched 1:1 to patients with cancer based on sociodemographic characteristics; controls were assigned a pseudo-index date corresponding to their matched patient's cancer diagnosis date. Beneficiaries were followed up annually until death or December 31, 2022, for TM or December 31, 2021, for MA. Data were analyzed from December 2025 to July 2026. Diagnosis of 1 of 7 common cancers. Any GLP-1 RA use. Proportions of beneficiaries with any GLP-1 RA use annually were stratified by traditional Medicare (TM) and Medicare Advantage (MA). Multivariable logistic regression examined (1) differences in GLP-1RA use between cancer and noncancer cohorts with and without adjusting for sociodemographic characteristics and comorbidities and diabetes-related complications; (2) cancer-specific factors associated with GLP-1RA use among the cancer cohort after 2018. A total of 373 278 Medicare beneficiaries (mean [SD] age, 76.1 [6.6] years; 188 746 [50.6%] female) with cancer and diabetes and 373 278 noncancer controls (153 358 unique beneficiaries) were included. GLP-1 RA use increased from 85 beneficiaries (0.5%) to 9083 beneficiaries (8.2%) and from 138 beneficiaries (0.9%) to 9300 beneficiaries (6.2%) in the cancer and noncancer cohorts, respectively, from 2010 to 2022 under TM; a similar increase was observed under MA. Despite higher unadjusted GLP-1 RA use among the cancer cohort than the noncancer cohort (probability difference, TM: 1.19 [95% CI, 0.94 to 1.44] percentage points [pp]; P < .001; MA: 0.45 [95% CI, 0.21 to 0.68] pp, P < .001), adjusted analysis showed no significant differences in GLP-1 RA use under TM (adjusted probability difference, 0.16 [95% CI, -0.10 to 0.41,] pp; P = .22) and lower use among cancer cohort under MA (-0.52 [95% CI, -0.76 to -0.28] pp; P < .001). Complications or comorbidities, including obesity (adjusted probability difference, TM: 3.35 [95% CI, 3.10 to 3.61] pp; P < .001; MA: 2.42 [95% CI, 2.19 to 2.64] pp; P < .001), dyslipidemia (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.26 [95% CI, 2.03 to 2.50] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.80 [95% CI, 1.57 to 2.03] pp; P < .001), neuropathy (adjusted probability difference: TM: 3.91 [95% CI, 3.64 to 4.19] pp; P < .001; MA: 3.17 [95% CI, 2.94 to 3.41] pp; P < .001), retinopathy (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.02 [95% CI, 1.78 to 2.27] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.84 [95% CI, 1.63 to 2.06] pp; P < .001), and chronic kidney disease (adjusted probability difference, TM: 2.01 [95% CI, 1.76 to 2.26] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.63 [95% CI, 1.40 to 1.85] pp; P < .001) were associated with greater likelihood of GLP-1RA use. Within the cancer cohort, breast (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.05 [95% CI, 0.43 to 1.66] pp; P = .001; MA: 0.89 [95% CI, 0.37 to 1.41] pp; P = .001), gynecologic (adjusted probability difference, MA: 1.13 [95% CI, 0.45 to 1.81] pp; P = .001), and prostate (adjusted probability difference, TM: 1.30 [95% CI, 0.72 to 1.88] pp; P < .001; MA: 1.07 [95% CI, 0.56 to 1.58] pp; P < .001) cancers were associated with higher GLP-1 RA use than colorectal cancer, while pancreatic cancer was associated with lower GLP-1 RA use (adjusted probability difference, TM: -2.55 [95% CI, -3.17 to -1.93] pp; P < .001; MA: -1.64 [95% CI, -2.23 to -1.05] pp; P < .001). In this retrospective study of Medicare beneficiaries with type 2 diabetes, GLP-1 RA use increased substantially and primarily was associated with metabolic risk profile, with limited associations with cancer status. Variation across cancer types and stages suggests oncologic context may influence prescribing.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gastrointestinal tract contains a dense multi-kingdom ecosystem in which bacteria, fungi, archaea, viruses, the mucosa, and the immune system interact. Although cancer microbiome research has focused mainly on bacteria, the gut virome dominated by bacteriophages may influence gastrointestinal carcinogenesis by reshaping bacterial communities, transferring functional genes, modulating inflammation, and altering treatment response. The strongest evidence comes from colorectal cancer, where multiple cohorts show altered phage diversity, temperate-phage enrichment, disrupted phage-bacteria networks, and reproducible stool-based diagnostic signals. Emerging studies in pancreatic cancer, esophageal adenocarcinoma, hepatocellular carcinoma, and precursor lesions suggest that virome disruption extends beyond colorectal cancer, although evidence remains uneven. Classic oncogenic viruses, including Epstein-Barr virus and hepatitis viruses, provide complementary examples of direct viral carcinogenesis in digestive organs. Anelloviruses are widespread in healthy individuals and are not established causes of cancer, but their abundance and composition may reflect immune status, inflammation, tissue injury, and altered host viral ecology. Virome-related interventions remain clinically immature: fecal microbiota transplantation has reached small phase I/II studies in gastrointestinal cancers, whereas phage, fecal-filtrate, and fecal virome approaches remain preclinical or non-oncology; direct oncolytic viruses have reached late-phase testing. Major barriers include viral dark matter, specimen and assay heterogeneity, disease-related confounding, limited external validation, and weak causal evidence. Standardized, mechanistically anchored, multi-kingdom studies are needed to establish clinical utility.
