展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) is the standard of care for the en bloc resection of large colorectal lesions but remains technically demanding, with long procedure times, a steep learning curve, and complication rates that have constrained adoption outside expert Eastern centres. Undersaline ESD (UESD) has emerged as a modification in which gas insufflation is replaced by immersion in isotonic saline, exploiting the distinct physical properties of a liquid-filled lumen to address several limitations of the conventional technique. Although frequently described as "underwater" ESD, the term "undersaline ESD" is more precise, since its advantages derive specifically from the ionic content of saline rather than from submersion alone. This narrative review synthesises the mechanistic rationale and the accumulating clinical evidence on UESD for large colorectal lesions. Saline immersion alters monopolar electrosurgical behaviour towards a coagulation-dominant profile, generates intrinsic traction on the mucosal flap through differential buoyancy, magnifies the dissection plane, and dissipates thermal energy. Across observational series and two recent meta-analyses, UESD is associated with faster submucosal dissection without compromising en bloc resection, R0 resection or short-term safety. The randomised evidence is not uniform: two of three trials reported faster dissection, while the largest found no difference in its primary endpoint, with lesion position determining the relative advantage of each technique. The benefits appear concentrated in specific settings such as submucosal fibrosis, gravity-side lesions, and, on preliminary data, non-expert operators, rather than distributed across all procedures. Key evidence gaps include the East Asian concentration of randomised data, the heterogeneity of technical implementation, and an absence of long-term oncological outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Prognostic gene expression signatures in colorectal cancer are usually reported by standalone discrimination, a standard that random gene sets can meet, and are rarely tested for what they add to routine clinical variables. TCGA-COAD and TCGA-READ were pooled into a single colorectal cohort (596 patients, 153 progression-free events). PathKAN places learnable univariate spline functions on a sparse gene-to-pathway topology drawn from MSigDB and BioGRID, reducing 20,681,472 dense weights to 127,985 edges, and is fitted under a Cox partial-likelihood objective. Performance was assessed by nested, repeated stratified cross-validation with dependence-corrected inference against clinical, elastic-net Cox and random survival forest models, and the frozen network was applied to four independent cohorts (1012 patients, 306 events) on two array platforms. The out-of-fold score was associated with progression-free interval independently of stage, age, sex and tumour site (adjusted HR 1.25 per SD, 95% CI 1.06-1.47; likelihood-ratio A pathway-masked Kolmogorov-Arnold survival model yields an interpretable transcriptomic score associated with colorectal cancer progression independently of clinical stage. It improves model fit over clinical variables, but its gain in discrimination is small and not statistically established; its transportability depends partly on outcome-blind, cohort-level standardisation of the inputs, and its clinical utility remains to be established.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ubiquitin-specific protease 30 (USP30) is a mitochondrial outer membrane-associated deubiquitinase best known for antagonizing PTEN-induced kinase 1 (PINK1)/Parkin-dependent ubiquitination and suppressing mitophagy. This established role has linked USP30 to mitochondrial quality control and neurodegenerative diseases. However, emerging studies in cancer have expanded the biological scope of USP30, revealing functions that cannot be explained by mitophagy regulation alone. USP30 regulates diverse cancer-associated substrates through deubiquitination, thereby affecting protein abundance, subcellular localization, protein interactions, and downstream transcriptional programs. These substrate-dependent effects influence mitochondrial dynamics, lipid synthesis, glucose and amino acid metabolism, redox homeostasis, apoptosis, ferroptosis, epithelial-mesenchymal transition, cancer stemness, T-cell exhaustion, and therapy resistance. Although most studies indicate tumor-promoting roles of USP30 in hepatocellular carcinoma, breast cancer, colorectal cancer, oral squamous cell carcinoma, ovarian cancer, bladder cancer, prostate cancer, and leukemia models, context-dependent tumor-restraining activities have also been reported. In this Review, we examine cancer-associated functions of USP30 that extend beyond its established role in PINK1/Parkin-dependent mitophagy, discuss the spatial and substrate-dependent mechanisms underlying these activities, and highlight opportunities and challenges for therapeutic targeting.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Digestive malignancies remain a major cause of cancer-related mortality, with tumor progression (TP) being strongly influenced by the complex interactions between tumor cells (TCs) and their microenvironment. This review summarizes recently described mechanisms of interactions between tumor cells, macrophages and CD8+ T lymphocytes in colorectal and gastric cancer. PubMed and Web of Science were searched for studies published between 2020 and 2026, with the final search being conducted on 8 July 2026. Experimental and clinical studies, together with relevant reviews, were considered to examine these interactions and their therapeutic implications. The evidence shows a bilateral crosstalk in which tumor cells influence immune cell phenotype and function, while immune cells can further support or restrict tumor progression. These interactions involve receptor-ligand systems and paracrine signaling, followed by changes in intracellular pathways regulating proliferation, invasion, macrophage polarization and CD8+ T-cell exhaustion. Considerable methodological heterogeneity among studies limits a direct comparison of the reported mechanisms. Several therapeutic approaches targeting these interactions are currently being investigated in early-phase clinical trials. However, many components of tumor-immune crosstalk and their connections remain incompletely understood. A further characterization of these mechanisms may help identify therapeutic strategies able to interfere with the immunosuppressive microenvironment of colorectal and gastric cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Hangeshashinto (HST) is a standardized seven-herb Kampo pharmaceutical used to manage gastrointestinal symptoms and chemotherapy-associated mucosal toxicity, but its direct antitumor activity remains insufficiently characterized. We examined the effects of HST in DLD-1 and SW480 colorectal cancer (CRC) cells and in non-malignant fibroblast and colonic epithelial cell models. Cell viability, colony formation, apoptosis-related endpoints, gene expression, responses to 5-fluorouracil (5-FU), and the activity of representative constituents were evaluated. Oral antitumor efficacy and tolerability were assessed in female BALB/c-nu mice bearing DLD-1 xenografts. HST preferentially reduced CRC cell viability and colony formation and increased annexin V positivity, caspase-3 activity, cleaved caspase-3 staining, and apoptotic nuclear changes. z-VAD-FMK showed a nonsignificant tendency toward partial recovery of cell viability. Reverse transcription-quantitative polymerase chain reaction findings were exploratory; statistical significance was not assessed. Co-treatment with HST (0.3 mg/mL) and 5-FU significantly reduced cell viability compared with 5-FU alone in both DLD-1 and SW480 cells; pharmacological synergy was not evaluated. Oral HST inhibited xenograft growth; tolerability assessment was limited to body weight and serum biochemistry, with reduced serum uric acid in the high-dose group after washout. These findings provide a preclinical basis for further investigation of standardized HST in CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Visceral hypersensitivity (VH) is a hallmark of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), establishing a reliable VH model is vital for investigating the disorder. While the impact of chronic stress on bile acid (BA) metabolism remains unclear. The exploratory study aimed to evaluate a heterotypic intermittent stress (HIS)-induced rat model of VH and characterize associated alterations in BA metabolism and farnesoid X receptor (FXR) signaling. Rats underwent a 9-day HIS regimen, and VH was assessed by electromyographic recording of the visceromotor response to colorectal distension. BA profiles in feces, colon, and serum were quantified by HPLC-MS/MS, and colonic FXR and CGRP expression were examined by Western blot, immunohistochemistry, and three-dimensional confocal reconstruction. HIS induced significant VH without organic colonic pathology, accompanied by increased CGRP-positive nerve fibers. The bile acid pool composition region-specific alterations in feces, colon, and serum. Specifically, the free-to-conjugated BA ratio was significantly increased in the colon and decreased in the serum of HIS rats, whereas no significant difference was detected in feces, while species-level changes were compartment-specific. Colonic FXR was upregulated and spatially associated with CGRP-positive fibers; in a preventive guggulsterone-treated group, both signals were reduced. These findings indicate that HIS-induced VH is associated with region-specific alterations in BA metabolism and colonic FXR signaling change, identifying the BA-FXR axis as a candidate pathway meriting functional validation as a potential therapeutic target for IBS.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
PSY is a three-herb formula comprising Patriniae Radix, Mori Cortex Radicis, and Coix Seed that was previously shown to inhibit STAT3 signaling in colorectal cancer (CRC) cells. Here, we investigated molecular and metabolic responses to PSY, its antitumor activity in an HCT116 xenograft model, and its interactions with chemotherapy in vitro. Representative chemical markers were qualitatively verified by UPLC-ESI-QTOF MS/MS. Exploratory RNA sequencing with two biological replicates per group highlighted stress-associated and metabolic processes for further investigation. PSY increased BiP, phosphorylated eIF2α, ATF4, and CHOP levels, intracellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels, and mitochondrial membrane depolarization, while reducing the phosphorylation of PI3K/AKT/mTOR- and ERK-associated proteins. PSY increased the p-AMPK/AMPK ratio and decreased the p-ACC/ACC ratio. PSY reduced several lipid-biosynthetic transcripts and decreased the relative abundance of selected fatty acids in xenograft tumors. Oral administration of PSY suppressed HCT116 xenograft growth without significant body-weight loss. Combination-index (CI) analysis indicated CI-defined in vitro synergistic interactions with 5-fluorouracil (5-FU) at multiple concentration pairs, with interaction patterns varying across HCT116, HT-29, and SW480 cells. Direct cell counting supported the combination response in HCT116 and SW480 cells. The combination increased apoptosis and reduced STAT3 and NF-κB p65 phosphorylation relative to single treatments. These findings characterize concurrent, partly discordant signaling and metabolic responses to PSY and support further preclinical evaluation of its in vitro interaction with 5-FU.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microbial metabolite sensing and neuroimmune signaling are increasingly recognized as interacting components of the mucosal response in inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, their organization across individuals and the cellular compartments carrying the relevant receptor machinery remain incompletely understood. We investigated whether metabolite-sensing host programs covary with neuroimmune receptor-side mucosal states at the participant level and whether the corresponding receptor transcripts map to defined mucosal compartments. HMP2 mucosal transcriptomes were analyzed at the participant level to evaluate prespecified relationships between metabolite-sensing and neuroimmune receptor-side host programs. Receptor-side neuroimmune remodeling was operationalized as cross-sectional participant-level host-program organization together with compartmental localization of the corresponding receptor transcripts, rather than longitudinal change or receptor activation. The stability and interpretation of these relationships were examined through diagnosis/inflammation adjustment, participant-grouped explanatory modeling, and tissue-composition sensitivity analyses. Complementary metabolomic, single-cell, UC, and colorectal-neoplasia datasets were used to examine synchronized metabolic associations, receptor-transcript localization, and the broader disease context of the identified mucosal programs. The microbiome, metabolomic, and transcriptomic datasets were obtained from multiple independent public cohorts. Among 251 HMP2 biopsies from 90 participants, 13 of 20 prespecified host-program associations passed FDR correction in participant-mean analyses, and 13 of 20 remained supported after diagnosis/inflammation adjustment, with 12 associations shared between the two analyses. The strongest relationships connected the SCFA receptor/barrier-response program with the inflammation-associated reactive/glial-adjacent state (ρ = 0.727) and the CGRP/adrenomedullin-family receptor-side score (ρ = 0.552), and connected the AHR-response context with the same receptor-side score (ρ = 0.531). Single-cell analyses localized CALCRL, RAMP2, and RAMP3 mainly to endothelial cells, VIPR1 to epithelial cells, and VIPR2 to stromal cells. The attenuation of incremental model fit after composition-proxy conditioning further indicated that this organization is closely embedded in mucosal tissue ecology. Matched metabolomic and premalignant-cohort analyses provided complementary evidence on the scope of this framework but did not extend it to synchronized metabolite coupling or neoplastic progression. Participant-level associations and compartment-resolved receptor localization support a cross-sectional receptor-side neuroimmune remodeling framework in IBD. The convergence of host-program organization and cellular localization prioritizes specific receptor-compartment relationships for spatial validation, functional receptor perturbation, and prospectively matched stool-mucosal studies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Dasatinib, an oral tyrosine kinase inhibitor used for chronic myeloid leukaemia (CML), is increasingly linked to gastrointestinal (GI) toxicities that remain under-recognised in clinical practice, ranging from mild, self-limiting symptoms to clinically significant GI bleeding and inflammatory colitis. This narrative review synthesises the published literature on dasatinib-associated GI bleeding and colitis, examining the mechanisms involved, including Src-family-kinase-mediated platelet dysfunction, endothelial barrier disruption and immune-driven T-cell infiltration, together with evidence on diagnosis and management. Dasatinib-associated colitis is far more extensively reported than non-colitis bleeding, has been reported across a broad adult age range and in both sexes, and has onset ranging from immediate to 9 years after initiation. Haematochezia, diarrhoea and abdominal pain are the most common presentations; endoscopic and histopathological findings are typically nonspecific and often mimic inflammatory bowel disease. The review is illustrated by two cases from a tertiary referral centre: delayed bleeding after cold-snare polypectomy of a diminutive 3 mm colorectal polyp, and chronic active colitis on combination asciminib-dasatinib therapy; formal causality assessment rated a dasatinib contribution as possible and probable, respectively. Dasatinib-associated GI complications, from delayed mucosal bleeding to chronic colitis, are clinically significant and warrant early recognition and multidisciplinary, individualised management. Standardised diagnostic criteria and peri-procedural guidance are needed to better balance bleeding risk against leukaemia control.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Santalol (STL), a sesquiterpene alcohol extracted from sandalwood oil, has reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer effects. Nevertheless, the influence of this compound on lung metastasis of colorectal cancer (CRC) cells has not been insufficiently elucidated. In this study, we investigated the anticancer activity of STL in metastatic CRC cells. STL significantly reduced cell viability and clonogenic capacity in a dose-dependent manner. This compound induced mitochondria-mediated apoptosis of CRC cells by regulating caspases and PARP. In addition, it reduced total antioxidant capacity and increased reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels. These results indicate that STL can enhance mitochondrial depolarization and activate the mitochondrial apoptotic pathway. Using an in vivo murine model, we further demonstrated that STL restricted the pulmonary dissemination of CRC cells. Taken together, these findings reveal that STL hinders lung metastasis of CRC cells via the induction of apoptosis and mitochondrial dysfunction driven by intracellular ROS accumulation. Our findings support STL as a promising therapeutic candidate for metastatic CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Diabetes Mellitus and cancer are major global health problems with rising incidence worldwide. This systematic review was conducted following PRISMA 2020 guidelines by searching PubMed, Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, and Google Scholar for studies published between 2015 and 2026. Studies investigating the association between diabetes mellitus and cancer were selected based on predefined criteria, and data were synthesized using a narrative approach. The findings indicate a strong and mechanistically complex association between diabetes mellitus and multiple cancers, particularly pancreatic, breast, colorectal, and prostate cancers. Hyperglycemia, insulin resistance, and chronic inflammation are consistently implicated in tumor initiation and progression through key signaling pathways, including Wnt/β-catenin, PI3K/AKT/mTOR, and AMPK. A bidirectional relationship is most evident in pancreatic cancer, highlighting its unique metabolic and oncogenic interplay. Shared molecular mediators such as cytokines, microRNAs, and metabolic regulators further support a common pathogenic link. Metformin, an antidiabetic drug, demonstrated potential anticancer effects via modulation of these interconnected pathways. Overall, this review underscores a biologically intertwined relationship between diabetes mellitus and cancer, supporting the development of integrated therapeutic strategies targeting shared metabolic and signaling mechanisms.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CCLM) is closely associated with poor patient prognosis, yet patient-specific molecular heterogeneity complicates the identification of recurrent molecular changes during metastasis. To address this, we performed RNA sequencing on paired primary tumors and liver metastases synchronously resected from six patients and analyzed gene expression changes using a paired design that accounted for interpatient variability. This analysis identified differentially expressed genes (DEGs) and metastasis-associated pathways through functional enrichment analysis and gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). The reproducibility of these changes was further assessed across multiple independent publicly available transcriptomic datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA). Selected candidate genes were additionally evaluated in a metastasis-selected colorectal cancer cell model, in which several genes showed expression changes consistent with the transcriptomic findings. Together, these results indicate that recurrent molecular changes accompany CCLM despite substantial interpatient heterogeneity and provide a strategy for identifying metastasis-associated molecular features and potential therapeutic targets.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
RASSF2 is a tumor suppressor gene involved in multiple cancers such as colorectal and lung cancer. Different studies have focused on promoter hypermethylation as the main inactivation pathway of this gene, which leads to cancer proliferation and metastasis. Here, using a comprehensive in silico pipeline, we investigate, for the first time, the impact of missense variants on protein structure, stability, and interactions. Multitiered computational tools were used to predict the most likely pathogenic and destabilizing nsSNPs; the impact of coding mutations on different gene expression was analyzed, and the impact of nsSNPs on PPIs using mCSM-PPI2 and MutPred-PPI was analyzed using predicted AlphaFold protein complexes. Of 454 variants, 19 variants were consistently predicted to be likely pathogenic and destabilizing, 14 variants were in the RA domain, and two variants were in the SARAH domain. V193D, L235P, L247P, and Y275C were conserved and exhibited severe structural and molecular alterations. Also, Y275C was at the interface, and it was predicted to disrupt the RASSF2-MST2 complex. KRT23 and BCL2L14 were significantly downregulated in samples containing mutated RASSF2 in COAD and LUAD, respectively. STRING illustrates the Hippo signaling pathway as the main pathway involved in the network. These findings provide promising candidates that can be important for future functional investigations. However, in vivo and in vitro experiments to validate our findings are necessary.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer remains a major global health challenge and a leading cause of mortality worldwide. As incidence continues to rise, early detection remains one of the most effective strategies for improving survival and reducing disease burden. Urine is an attractive source of biomarkers due to its non-invasive collection, ease of repeated sampling, and rich molecular composition. This scoping review evaluates the current landscape of urinary biomarkers for the early detection of cancer and their potential for clinical translation. A detailed literature search was conducted using PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science to identify studies investigating urinary biomarkers for cancer detection. Biomarkers were categorised by analyte class, and diagnostic performance, validation status, and clinical applicability were assessed. Urinary biomarkers demonstrated diagnostic potential across multiple malignancies, including lung, breast, pancreatic, hepatobiliary, colorectal, renal and ovarian cancers, while several urinary assays are already clinically available for bladder and prostate cancers. Promising diagnostic accuracy was reported for multiple biomarker classes, particularly multimarker panels integrating metabolites, proteins, nucleic acids, and epigenetic signatures. However, most studies were exploratory, involving small cohorts, methodological heterogeneity, and limited independent validation. Urinary biomarkers represent a promising and rapidly evolving approach to non-invasive cancer detection. Despite encouraging diagnostic performance, few candidates have progressed to clinical implementation. Large prospective multicentre studies, rigorous validation, and assay standardisation are essential to establish urinary biomarkers as reliable tools for cancer screening, early diagnosis, and risk stratification.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) have a higher risk of developing colorectal cancer (CRC) compared with the general population. This increased risk is mainly related to chronic colonic inflammation and is influenced by factors such as disease duration, disease extent, family history of CRC, and the presence of primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC). Although the incidence of CRC in IBD has decreased over recent decades, it remains an important cause of disease-related morbidity and mortality. CRC prevention in IBD extends beyond colonoscopic surveillance and includes high-quality endoscopic surveillance, early detection and appropriate treatment of dysplasia, and long-term control of intestinal inflammation through a personalized approach. This review summarizes current evidence on IBD-associated colorectal carcinogenesis and strategies for CRC prevention, with emphasis on risk stratification, optimization of endoscopic surveillance, dysplasia management, treat-to-target strategies and multidisciplinary management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Ulcerative colitis (UC) is associated with an increased risk of colorectal cancer, particularly in patients with long-standing and extensive disease. Although advances in medical therapy and surveillance have reduced colorectal cancer incidence, prolonged preservation of chronically inflamed colonic mucosa has increased the importance of understanding how cumulative inflammation promotes carcinogenesis. UC-associated neoplasia differs from sporadic colorectal cancer in its multifocality, pathological heterogeneity, and molecular evolution. Repeated inflammation, epithelial injury, and regeneration promote the accumulation of somatic and epigenetic alterations across histologically non-dysplastic mucosa, generating a cancerized field composed of genetically heterogeneous epithelial clones. Recent sequencing studies have shown that many clones selected in chronically inflamed mucosa harbor alterations that enhance adaptation to inflammatory stress but are not necessarily premalignant, indicating that field cancerization represents a dynamic evolutionary ecosystem rather than simple expansion of cancer-prone clones. Neoplastic progression requires further clonal selection as the selective environment shifts toward autonomous growth. Colitis-associated colorectal cancer is characterized by early TP53 alterations, a relatively late and less frequent involvement of APC, branching clonal evolution, and substantial copy-number alterations, particularly during progression from low- to high-grade dysplasia. Thus, colitis-associated carcinogenesis can be understood as a process in which chronic inflammation establishes a genetically altered field, followed by dynamic clonal selection and genomic evolution. Elucidating these processes may enable identification of high-risk fields and clones before invasive cancer develops and provide a biological basis for improved surveillance, risk stratification, and chemoprevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Genomic biomarkers are increasingly used to identify therapeutically exploitable defects in DNA damage repair (DDR). However, genomic alterations and mutational scars largely represent the evolutionary history of a tumor, whereas therapeutic sensitivity depends on its current functional state. This distinction becomes particularly relevant during cancer progression and treatment, when selective pressure may reshape DNA repair capacity without erasing the genomic footprints generated by previous repair deficiency. Here, we examine the emerging concept of genomic scar-functional state discordance, whereby persistent genomic evidence of defective DNA repair may coexist with partial or complete restoration of repair competence. Multiple mechanisms may contribute to this transition, including secondary or reversion mutations, restoration of homologous recombination, replication fork stabilization, compensatory pathway activation, clonal selection, and epigenetic reprogramming. Conversely, initially repair-proficient tumors may acquire new DDR vulnerabilities during evolution, emphasizing the bidirectional and dynamic nature of genome maintenance. These processes challenge the assumption that a single genomic assessment can reliably define a stable therapeutic vulnerability throughout the disease course. We discuss how longitudinal approaches integrating tumor genomics, circulating tumor DNA, mutational signatures, epigenomic information, and functional measures of DNA repair could distinguish historical genomic damage from active biological dependency. Particular attention is given to gastrointestinal malignancies, including pancreatic, colorectal, gastric, and biliary tract cancers, in which DDR alterations are increasingly investigated but their predictive interpretation remains heterogeneous. We propose that precision oncology should progressively move from the concept of a static genomic biomarker toward that of a dynamic genomic state, in which therapeutic vulnerabilities are periodically reassessed as tumors evolve under treatment pressure.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although adjuvant strategies such as systemic chemotherapy, regional nonsystemic chemotherapy, and ablation have been applied, the optimal adjuvant therapeutic strategy for resectable colorectal liver metastases remains uncertain in terms of overall survival and disease-free survival. This network meta-analysis aimed to determine the optimal adjuvant therapeutic strategy for patients with colorectal liver metastases. We searched potentially eligible studies in PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials, and China National Knowledge Infrastructure databases until July 2026. Pooled disease-free survival (DFS) and overall survival (OS) were estimated using R software. Eighteen studies including 18 reports were included. For the DFS, except for adjuvant hepatic arterial infusion chemotherapy (CT, HAIC) concomitant with intravenous CT, adjuvant CT and perioperative CT significantly improved DFS compared with surgery and adjuvant HAIC. There was no statistical difference between all therapeutic strategies for OS. Adjuvant HAIC concomitant with intravenous CT had the highest probability of being the best treatment for improving DFS (85.01%), followed by perioperative CT (11.75%) and adjuvant CT (3.17%); however, adjuvant HAIC concomitant with intravenous CT had the highest probability of being the best adjuvant treatment for improving OS (52.46%), followed by perioperative CT (40.25%) and adjuvant HAIC (5.25%). Adjuvant CT may be the best for improving DFS, but perioperative CT may be the best for improving OS. However, the results should be validated further.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer-related fatigue (CRF) is one of the most common and distressing symptoms experienced by patients undergoing chemotherapy, and no gold standard for the treatment of CRF has been established. This study aimed to evaluate the effects of the Danggui Buxue Medicinal Diet on CRF in patients with chemotherapy-induced anemia following colon cancer surgery. A total of 96 patients admitted to the intestinal surgery ward and daytime chemotherapy ward of a tertiary hospital from May 2021 to December 2022 who met the inclusion criteria were selected and randomly divided into 2 groups: 48 patients in the control group and 48 in the experimental group. The control group received standard treatment and nursing care for postoperative chemotherapy for colon cancer, while the experimental group followed the control group's regimen and additionally received the Danggui Buxue Medicinal Diet for 21 consecutive days. Fatigue levels, blood counts, and inflammatory factors were compared before and after the intervention in both groups. A total of 86 patients completed the study. After the intervention, the CRF scores in the experimental group were significantly lower than those in the control group (29.14 ± 2.58 vs 44.02 ± 4.25), with a between-group mean difference of -14.88 (95% confidence interval [CI], -16.38 to -13.38; P < .001). Hemoglobin levels were significantly higher in the experimental group than in the control group (115.26 ± 11.72 vs 106.52 ± 12.93), with a mean difference of 8.74 (95% CI, 3.45-14.03; P < .001). Red blood cell counts were also higher in the experimental group (mean difference 0.61; 95% CI, 0.44-0.78; P < .001). In addition, levels of inflammatory factors were significantly reduced, with interleukin-6 showing a mean difference of -16.28 (95% CI, -20.10 to -12.46; P < .001) and tumor necrosis factor-α showing a mean difference of -26.09 (95% CI, -29.80 to -22.38; P < .001). The Danggui Buxue Medicinal Diet was associated with improvements in CRF, hematological parameters, and inflammatory markers in patients with chemotherapy-induced anemia following colon cancer surgery. These findings suggest that it may have potential as a supportive nutritional intervention for managing CRF in this population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Inefficient immune synapse formation limits the therapeutic efficacy of T cell-based immunotherapy in both solid tumors and hematological malignancies. Here, we report a fully synthetic, membrane-anchored dual-targeting aptamer engager, AptE 2, that acts as a programmable artificial immunological interface to redirect cytotoxic T cells toward cancer cells without genetic engineering. Constructed entirely from DNA aptamers through optimized bioorthogonal conjugation and enzyme-mediated ligation, AptE 2 integrates multivalent tumor recognition, T cell binding, enhanced nuclease resistance, and prolonged membrane anchoring within a single modular scaffold. In colorectal cancer models, AptE 2 promoted stable T cell-tumor cell engagement, enhanced cytotoxicity and cytokine secretion, and drove pronounced tumor regression with increased intratumoral CD8+ T cell infiltration and minimal systemic toxicity. Importantly, AptE 2 also demonstrated broad applicability in leukemia. In CCRF-CEM cells, AptE 2 exhibited strong surface binding, sustained membrane retention for up to 6 h, and superior resistance to wash-off compared with monovalent aptamers and bivalent controls. AptE 2-prearmed TALL-104 cells markedly enhanced leukemia cell clustering, increased cell lysis to over 90% under optimized coculture conditions, and amplified IFN-γ secretion. In a disseminated CCRF-CEM-Luc leukemia mouse model, AptE 2-mediated T cell therapy suppressed systemic leukemia progression, improved peripheral hematological profiles, and showed favorable tolerability without detectable major organ injury. These findings establish AptE 2 as a generalizable, nonprotein-based and nonviral immune engager platform for programmable T cell redirection across both solid and hematological cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) represents one of the most commonly diagnosed malignancies in which Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) infiltration critically drives tumor progression by fostering an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) that compromises immunotherapy efficacy. Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) originating from Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 offer an attractive tumor-targeting drug delivery system, combining intrinsic immunostimulatory properties with drug-loading capacity. We therefore developed an OMV-based dual-function system coencapsulating 5-fluorouracil (5-Fu) and metronidazole (MTZ), designated 5-Fu/MTZ@OMVs. In vitro, this system effectively eliminated both CT26 cells and Fn while promoting DC maturation and driving repolarization of M2 macrophages toward M1 as well as N2 neutrophils toward N1. In vivo, upon administration to an Fn-colonized CT26 model, the system homed to tumors, reduced the Fn burden, and inhibited tumor growth, demonstrating its bactericidal and antitumor efficacy. Notably, it reversed immunosuppressive TME by promoting DC maturation, M1 macrophage, and N1 neutrophil polarization, which enhanced the recruitment and functional activation of CD4+ and CD8+ T cells within the tumor. Thus, by integrating bactericidal, antitumor, and immune remodeling activities into a single OMV platform, our strategy constitutes a viable therapeutic approach for Fn-associated CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Living alone has been associated with higher mortality, but evidence for specific causes of death and potential drivers of these associations is limited. We examined associations between living alone and cause-specific mortality, and the extent to which sociodemographic and health-related characteristics explained these associations. This study included 598 023 US adults aged ≥18 years from the 1998-2018 National Health Interview Survey-National Death Index (follow-up through 2019). Cox proportional hazards models estimated hazard ratios (HRs) and Blinder-Oaxaca decomposition quantified contributions of measured characteristics. Adults living alone aged 18-64 and ≥65 years were at higher risk of mortality from all causes combined [HR18-64 = 1.22 (95% CI: 1.18-1.26); HR≥65 = 1.06 (1.03-1.08)], heart disease [HR18-64 = 1.41 (1.32-1.50); HR≥65 = 1.11 (1.06-1.15)], suicide [HR18-64 = 1.58 (1.30-1.92); HR≥65 = 2.03 (1.47-2.81)], and all injuries [HR18-64 = 1.27 (1.16-1.40); HR≥65 = 1.16 (1.02-1.32)], respectively, compared to adults living with others. Adults living alone were also at higher risk of mortality from cerebrovascular disease [HR18-64 = 1.23 (1.04-1.46)], colorectal cancer [HR18-64 = 1.27 (1.06-1.53)], diabetes [HR18-64 = 1.34 (1.15-1.57)], and accidents [HR18-64 = 1.17 (1.04-1.31)] in ages 18-64 and from hypertension [HR≥65 = 1.28 (1.07-1.53)] in ages ≥65 years. Sociodemographic and health-related characteristics explained 57.1% and 85.4% of the all-cause mortality difference by living arrangement in ages 18-64 and ≥65 years, respectively, with some variations in contributing characteristics across causes of death. Individuals living alone had an increased risk of death from multiple causes, particularly in ages 18-64 years, with the highest risk for suicide in all ages. Mortality differences were largely explained by sociodemographic and health-related characteristics, highlighting targeted interventions to reduce mortality risks among those living alone.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Staged surgical procedures, such as two-stage hepatectomy and associating liver partition and portal vein ligation for staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) technique, use the liver regenerative capacity to stimulate growth of the future liver remnant. These procedures can be used in people with extensive colorectal liver metastases when the future liver remnant is too small to allow a safe postoperative recovery after major hepatectomy. Compared with conventional two-stage hepatectomy, although ALPPS results in faster and larger growth of the future liver remnant, the evidence regarding its impact on major postoperative complications, perioperative mortality, recurrence rates, and long-term survival is conflicting. To assess the benefits and harms of liver partition and portal vein ligation for a staged hepatectomy (ALPPS) procedure versus conventional two-stage hepatectomy in people with colorectal liver metastases. We searched the Cochrane Hepato-Biliary Group Controlled Trials Register, Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials in the Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, Embase, three other databases, online trial registries, grey literature databases, and reference lists of identified studies; we also retrieved additional information from the included trial authors. Our last study search was on 4 December 2025. Randomised clinical trials comparing ALPPS versus conventional two-stage hepatectomy in adults with colorectal liver metastases who were unable to undergo complete resection because the future liver remnant was estimated to be < 30% of the total liver volume. The critical outcomes were perioperative all-cause mortality at 90 days, all-cause mortality, serious adverse events, and health-related quality of life (HRQoL). Other important outcomes included overall survival, disease-free survival, and resection rate. For our primary analysis, we used data at the maximum follow-up, except for perioperative mortality, analysed at 90 days after operation. We used the Risk of Bias 2.0 (RoB 2) tool. We used standard Cochrane methodological procedures to develop the review. We did not perform meta-analysis because only one trial met the inclusion criteria. We expressed dichotomous outcomes as risk ratios (RR), continuous outcomes as mean differences (MD), and time-to-event outcomes as hazard ratios (HR), all with 95% confidence intervals (CIs), using RevMan. We used the GRADE approach to assess the certainty of the evidence. The included trial was a six-centre, publicly funded, Scandinavian randomised clinical trial. The trial investigators randomised 100 participants (mean age: 65 ± 10 years; male-to-female ratio: 2.34:1.0). After randomisation, two participants in the ALPPS (1 severe comorbidity; 1 total liver volume > 30%) and one participant in the two-stage hepatectomy group (progressive disease) could not proceed to the intervention and were excluded. One other participant was lost to follow-up after emigrating. The trial was described in 15 publications. The trial provided data for all outcomes of our review. We followed the analytical approach reported by the trial authors, using a modified intention-to-treat population where applicable and available data otherwise. The evidence suggests that ALPPS, compared with two-stage hepatectomy, results in little to no difference in perioperative all-cause mortality at 90 days (RR 1.36, 95% CI 0.32 to 5.76; I Current evidence derives from data from only one randomised clinical trial, with a low number of participants and events. We are very uncertain about the effect of ALPPS on health-related quality of life and the rate of serious adverse events (30 days of follow-up) compared with two-stage hepatectomy. We are uncertain whether there is little to no difference between ALPPS and two-stage hepatectomy in perioperative mortality at 90 days after operation and in disease-free survival. ALPPS, compared with two-stage hepatectomy, probably results in little to no difference in all-cause mortality at maximum follow-up (93 months) and in overall survival of people with colorectal liver metastases (median 93 months), but probably results in a large increase in resection rates (eight-week follow-up). The certainty of the evidence for the presented outcomes was very low, low, or moderate. We lack randomised trials comparing these two strategies to identify the best approach for routine use in surgical practice. Evidence from low- and middle-income countries is lacking. The choice of ALPPS should carefully consider clinical characteristics of the patients. More high-quality trials with large numbers of participants are needed to provide information on the risks and benefits of ALPPS for people with colorectal liver metastases. This review does not have dedicated funding. Protocol: published 08 March 2022, available in the Cochrane Library at https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD014608.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Elevated mast cell (MC) counts in colonic biopsies are frequently observed in patients with chronic diarrhoea or unspecific abdominal symptoms, potentially leading to a diagnosis of mast cell activation syndrome. However, the clinical relevance of MC quantification in this setting remains controversial. This study aimed to determine the proportion of patients with elevated MC counts who presented with diarrhoea compared to those with normal counts. As a secondary endpoint, we assessed how often MC quantification was performed and what the underlying clinical indications were. We analysed a large US national pathology database with 3.3 million colonoscopies performed between January 2009 and December 2023. Screening colonoscopies for colon cancer detection were excluded. For patients with multiple colonoscopies, only the first procedure was included. This resulted in a total of 2,059,147 colonoscopies. Colonic mast cells were evaluated in 3508 reports (0.17%). In 1167 cases the report contained either the expressions indicating increased MC, or a MC count > 20 MC/high power field (hpf). Diarrhoea was present in 58.3%, 54.1%, 54.7%, 50.0% and 33.3% of patients with MC count of < 20/hpf, 20-39/hpf, 40-59/hpf, 60-98/hpf and ≥ 99/hpf, respectively. These data do not show a relationship between diarrhoea and elevated MC in the colonic mucosa. Therefore, we suggest that the incorporation of MC quantification into the histologic evaluation of colonoscopic biopsies obtained for common GI indications may not be warranted.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A 73-year-old patient with newly diagnosed ulcerative colitis (UC) presented with pancolitis and no detectable neoplastic lesion at initial colonoscopy. After remission induction with corticosteroids and maintenance therapy with azathioprine, follow-up colonoscopy 1 year later revealed a 10 mm 0-IIa + IIc lesion in the ascending colon. Endoscopic submucosal dissection demonstrated well-differentiated adenocarcinoma with submucosal invasion. No dysplasia was identified in the surrounding mucosa, and p53 overexpression was confined to the tumor, a finding more compatible with a sporadic phenotype than with colitis-associated neoplasia. This case suggests that active inflammation may have masked a preexisting colorectal neoplastic lesion, highlighting the importance of colonoscopic reassessment after remission induction in elderly-onset UC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To synthesize tungsten oxide (WO₃) and a WO₃/graphene oxide (GO) nanocomposite (1:0.5 molar ratio) and investigate their physicochemical properties and anticancer activity against human colon cancer (HT-29) cells. WO₃ and WO₃/GO (1:0.5) nanocomposites were synthesized using an ex situ hydrothermal method and characterized by XRD, Raman spectroscopy, FTIR, UV-Vis spectroscopy, PL spectroscopy, zeta potential analysis, FESEM, and EDS. Anticancer activity was assessed using MTT cytotoxicity assays, AO/EtBr staining, apoptosis analysis, and ROS generation assays. The incorporation of GO improved crystallinity, particle dispersion, and charge separation while reducing the optical band gap. The WO₃/GO nanocomposite exhibited the strongest inhibition of HT-29 cell proliferation compared with pristine WO₃ and GO. Enhanced anticancer activity was associated with increased cellular internalization, membrane disruption, and ROS generation. AO/EtBr staining and flow cytometry confirmed significant apoptosis induction, while ROS assays demonstrated elevated intracellular oxidative stress that may contribute to mitochondrial dysfunction and apoptotic cell death. The WO₃/GO nanocomposite (1:0.5) demonstrated enhanced ROS-mediated anticancer activity against HT-29 cells and represents a promising nanotherapeutic platform for colorectal cancer treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Produced from Streptomyces, Dinactin is one of the most important macrolide antibiotics. Previous studies have found that dinactin exerts inhibiting the cancer stemness potential of lung cancer, making it a promising option for CRC therapy. In this study, we designed experiments to evaluate dinactin's inhibitory effects against two human colorectal cancer cells (HCT116 and HT29) and elucidate the mechanism of its anti-cancer effects. Finally, we provided the first ever investigation of the mutagenic and anti-mutagenic potentials of dinactin. We studied the effects of dinactin as part of an anti-cancer approach using MTT test, clonogenic assay, wound healing assay, and transwell migration assay in HCT116 and HT29 cells. Mechanical studies were conducted using flow cytometry and Cell Death Detection ELISA. The mutagenic and anti-mutagenic properties were demonstrated using the in vitro cytokinesis-blocked micronucleus assay in V79 cells. Dinactin was found to have dose-dependent inhibitory effects on the viability of HCT116 and HT29 cells with IC50 values of 1.6 ±0.4 and 35.0 ±14 nM, respectively. Furthermore, dinactin showed potent anti-proliferation, anti-migration, and anti-invasion activities and demonstrated similar activity to doxorubicin. Mechanically, treatment with dinactin resulted in increased DNA fragmentation and positive AnnexinV/FITC-PI staining, which demonstrated the induction of apoptosis by dinactin. From the results of the mutagenic assay, dinactin did not produce a significant increase in micronucleus frequency when compared with a negative control (p > 0.05). In order to verify dinactin's anti-mutagenic properties, a combination of MMC (a known mutagen) and dinactin were applied to V79 cells. Treatment with dinactin resulted in a significant decrease in the number of micronucleated cells. Dinactin inhibits growth and alleviates the progression of CRC cells at nanomolar concentrations. This anti-CRC activity is mediated through the induction of apoptosis. Dinactin did not exhibit mutagenic effects and has the potential to reduce the mutagenic action of MMC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Radiotherapy, commonly used in the treatment of colorectal cancer (CRC), can induce local recurrence and malignant progression in cases of intrinsic and acquired radioresistance; therefore, effective treatment strategies are required. In this study, we screened an FDA-approved drug library and identified amcinonide (AMC), a topical corticosteroid, as a potential agent that inhibits radiation-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT), cell migratory ability, and invasiveness in radioresistant colorectal cancer cells. Mechanistically, ionizing radiation-induced circRNF10 suppressed miR-296-5p, thereby increasing Snail expression and promoting EMT and aggressive phenotypes in radioresistant CRC cells. We verified in vitro, in vivo, and in CRC patient-derived organoids (PDOs) models that AMC suppresses the malignant phenotype by restoring miR-296-5p expression and reducing Snail expression. These findings identify the circRNF10/miR-296-5p/Snail axis as a key factor in CRC radioresistance and suggest that it may serve as a therapeutic target. Together, these results suggest that AMC is a promising drug for overcoming CRC radioresistance and that components of this axis may serve as potential diagnostic biomarkers. Overall, these findings highlight the therapeutic potential of targeting the ncRNA-mediated EMT circuit to overcome radioresistant CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Accurate prognostication is crucial for the individualized management of patients with colorectal cancer (CRC), while the accuracy and interpretability of current models still need to be improved. This study aims to develop and validate an explainable multimodal model for precise survival prediction. 3381 patients with resected CRC are enrolled from three medical centers, and a multimodal deep-learning framework integrating clinical variables and histopathological images is developed. The multimodal model exhibits significantly more robust performance than unimodal models in prognosis prediction across all of the cohorts. By stratifying patients into low-risk and high-risk groups based on the model-derived risk scores, high-risk patients exhibit worse outcomes, and the stratification remains an independent prognostic factor in multivariable Cox regression. The model also identifies patients with markedly poorer survival among the stage II/III subgroup. Adjuvant chemotherapy demonstrates benefits in high-risk patients with stage III CRC but not in the low-risk group. Multi-omic analyses disclose that low-risk tumors are characterized by enhanced adaptive immune responses, whereas high-risk tumors exhibit stronger angiogenesis and higher exhaustion scores of T cells, reflecting a hypoxic and immunosuppressive microenvironment. These results support the potential of the multimodal model to effectively predict survival outcomes in resected CRC with great explainability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patient-derived tumor organoids (PDTOs) are strongly influenced by culture medium. We compared OncoPro™ (OP) Tumoroid Culture medium with conventional Wnt/R-spondin/noggin (Wnt) medium. This recently developed OP medium offers a standardized, serum-free alternative to Wnt-based formulations. We compared OP and Wnt media across 36 PDTO lines from various malignancies (colorectal, pancreatic, breast, lung, gastric, gastroesophageal junction, biliary head and neck and unknown primary), assessing establishment success. Selected PDTO models were subjected to downstream characterization, including morphological assessment and bulk transcriptomic profiling with comparison to public single-cell RNA sequencing reference datasets (n = 11), whole-exome sequencing (WES) (n = 9), and pharmacological response profiling to a 33-drug panel (n = 3). Adaptation from Wnt medium to OP succeeded in 83.3% (15/18), whereas de novo establishment favored Wnt (33.3% vs 11.1%). Key oncogenic driver alterations were retained across matched organoid cultures, supporting preservation of tumor-relevant genomic features. Transcriptomic profiling confirmed preserved tumor-identity across media, while revealing different epithelial state programs: Wnt upregulated proliferation/stemness-associated genes (e.g. LGR5) and OP enriched adhesion-associated genes and inflammatory/TGF-β programs. In scRNA databases OP signatures preferentially mapped to malignant epithelial compartments in pancreatic cancer, whereas Wnt signatures were linked to non-malignant epithelium. Similarly, in colon cancer OP signature mapped predominantly to the malignant epithelial compartments. Drug (n = 33) screening in pancreatic- and colorectal cancer PDTOs (n = 3) demonstrated consistent medium-dependent shifts: Wnt-grown PDTOs were globally more sensitive in the screened subset, particularly to MAPK-axis inhibitors and apoptosis-sensitizers, while OP-grown PDTOs exhibited relative resistance. Culture medium composition is a key determinant of PDTO phenotype, transcriptome and drug sensitivity. Wnt medium was associated with drug-sensitive states, whereas OP medium was associated with adhesion- and inflammatory-related programs, relative resistance in the screened subset of 33 drugs and closer alignment with malignant epithelial programs in the analyzed pancreatic / colorectal cancer single-cell atlases.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer metabolism-associated immune suppression remains a major barrier to durable therapeutic responses. Indoleamine-2,3-dioxygenase 1 has been pursued as a therapeutic target, but incomplete pathway suppression has limited clinical success. As the aryl hydrocarbon receptor is a ligand-activated transcription factor and downstream effector of tryptophan metabolism, we investigated how myeloid-cell aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling shapes the tumor immune microenvironment and whether its inhibition can restore antitumor immunity. Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor knockout mice targeting dendritic cells or macrophages were used to evaluate the effects of genetic aryl hydrocarbon receptor ablation. Pharmacologic inhibition was assessed using DA-4505 across syngeneic lung, colorectal, and breast cancer models and an immune checkpoint inhibitor-refractory humanized patient-derived xenograft model. Therapeutic efficacy was evaluated alone or in combination with anti-programmed cell death protein 1 therapy, chemotherapy, or surgery. Tumor growth, survival, metastasis, and immune remodeling were analyzed by flow cytometry, multiplex immunohistochemistry, single-cell RNA sequencing, cytokine profiling, and human tumor datasets. Conditional aryl hydrocarbon receptor depletion in macrophages and dendritic cells enhanced innate and adaptive immune activation, increased interferon-γ-producing T cells, and strengthened antitumor immunity. In mouse tumor models, pharmacologic aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade enhanced macrophage chemotaxis and activation programs, promoted M1-like macrophage polarization, increased interferon-γ-producing CD8⁺ T cells, and reduced regulatory T cells and polymorphonuclear myeloid-derived suppressor cells. These changes promoted robust T-cell activation and durable tumor control. Aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition further synergized with chemotherapy, surgery, and immune checkpoint blockade, leading to expansion of effector and memory T-cell populations and sustained antitumor responses. In a humanized lung cancer model, aryl hydrocarbon receptor blockade increased intratumoral CD8⁺ T-cell infiltration and cytotoxic-memory programs while reducing regulatory T-cell enrichment. In human tumor datasets, aryl hydrocarbon receptor-positive macrophages correlated with FOXP3⁺ T-cell infiltration, and higher aryl hydrocarbon receptor inhibition-associated T-cell signatures were associated with improved patient survival.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Textbook outcomes (TO) are a composite measure of ideal postoperative outcomes. Using a multicentre national study, we aimed to describe the rate and associated factors with TO for colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. Stage I-III colorectal cancer who underwent curative surgery were retrospectively identified from 80 centres from 2018 to 2021 using a large national study dataset. Recurrent, synchronous, and metastatic cancer, urgent surgery, and SARS-CoV-2 infection were excluded. TO include radical resection (R0, CRM-), > 12 lymph nodes yield, adequate length of stay (LOS ≤ 75th°), no 30-day mortality, and no Clavien-Dindo ≥ III morbidity. 13842 patients were included: 9869 with colon (TO: 67%) and 3973 with rectal cancer (TO: 53%). TO were not achieved the most by inadequate lymph node yield, Clavien-Dindo classification ≥ III, and prolonged postoperative LOS. In colon cancer surgery the use of laparoscopy was the strongest predictor (OR 2.21), along with being female (OR 1.25), cT1-T2 and cT3-T4a (vs. T0-Tis) stages (OR 1.66 and OR 1.86), and cN2 (vs. N0 or N1) stage (OR 1.23) for achieving TO after colon cancer surgery. Age ≥ 65years, pulmonary comorbidities, alcoholic hepatopathy, previous CRC, anticoagulants, left-sided cancer, ASA score > 2, centre volume, additional surgery, conversion, intraoperative surgical complications, ileostomy, and mild postoperative complications only (Clavien-Dindo ≤ II) were negatively associated. In rectal cancer, female sex (OR 1.26) and high rectal cancer (OR 1.84) were positively associated, while age ≥ 75years, previous CRC, T4b stage, intraoperative surgical complications, and mild postoperative complications were negatively associated. This study reports rates and factors independently associated with TO for colon and rectal cancer using a large multicentre cohort.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Population-level evidence comparing robotic-assisted surgery (RAS) with laparoscopic surgery (LS)/video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) and open surgery (OS) across multiple procedures from a payer perspective remains limited. This study aimed to compare postoperative length of stay (LOS) and insurer-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures among RAS, LS/VATS, and OS across representative procedures following the expansion of RAS reimbursement in Taiwan. This retrospective nationwide population-based cohort study was conducted using claims data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. We identified adults (age ≥ 18 y) who underwent 1 of 12 representative procedures spanning thoracic, hepatobiliary-pancreatic, colorectal, urologic, and gynecologic specialties between September 1 and December 31, 2024. Surgical approaches were classified as robotic-assisted surgery (RAS), laparoscopic or video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (LS/VATS), or open surgery (OS) using the corresponding procedure and robotic-assistance codes in the NHI claims database. The outcomes were postoperative LOS and total NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials during the index hospitalization. Procedure-specific stabilized inverse probability of treatment weighting was applied to each pairwise comparison. This study included 17 549 patients. Of these patients, 2900, 9763, and 4886 underwent RAS, LS/VATS, and OS, respectively. RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS than LS/VATS for lung resection, colectomy, partial nephrectomy, and nephroureterectomy and with lower reimbursed expenditures for lung resection, partial pancreatectomy, nephroureterectomy, and radical prostatectomy. Compared with OS, RAS was associated with a significantly shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, with the largest difference noted for colectomy (8.38 vs. 14.80 d). Moreover, RAS was associated with lower reimbursed expenditures than OS for lung resection, minor hepatectomy, partial pancreatectomy, colectomy, and malignant hysterectomy. During the early period following the September 2024 expansion of NHI reimbursement for RAS in Taiwan, RAS was associated with shorter postoperative LOS for selected procedures, whereas differences in NHI-reimbursed in-hospital expenditures excluding special medical materials varied by procedure and comparator. Given the observational study design, residual confounding, and limited propensity-score overlap in several comparisons, particularly RAS versus OS, these findings should be interpreted as procedure-specific associations rather than evidence of clinical or economic superiority.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal cancer, particularly esophageal, gastric, or colon cancer, is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in Mexico. There are substantial delays in the early identification and timely referral of primary care patients, resulting in more advanced-stage diagnoses and poorer clinical outcomes. Our aim was to issue a position statement from the Asociación Mexicana de Gastroenterología (AMG) to guide primary care physicians in the identification of alarm features, risk stratification, and timely referral of patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer. A multidisciplinary group of 20 specialists in the fields of gastroenterology, oncology, endoscopy, epidemiology, and public health, from both public and private institutions, developed the position statement through a structured consensus process. Clinical statements were drafted and voted on, they were organized by cancer type (esophageal, gastric, and colorectal), and three clinical algorithms were designed to support decision-making in primary care. Thirteen statements were issued on alarm features, risk factors, recommended diagnostic studies, and risk-stratified referral pathways (urgent, priority, and elective). The role of upper endoscopy and high-quality colonoscopy as diagnostic procedures of choice was emphasized, clearly distinguishing them from population-based screening strategies. This position statement provides a practical, evidence-based, expert consensus-informed guide, adapted to the Mexican healthcare setting, whose aim is to implement prevention strategies, reduce diagnostic delays, improve early detection, and optimize the referral of primary care patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To investigate whether the association between platelet count or C-reactive protein (CRP) results and 1-year cancer incidence varies by patient ethnicity. Cohort study using routinely collected health records from the Clinical Practice Research Datalink Aurum, Hospital Episode Statistics Admitted Patient Care and National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service. English primary care, with linkage to secondary care records and national cancer registry data. Patients aged 40 years or older with a recorded ethnicity, no previous malignancy, and a platelet count or CRP test recorded between 1 January 2010 and 31 December 2017. Ethnicity was categorised as white, Asian, black, other or mixed. The primary outcome measures were 1-year cancer incidence following platelet count or CRP testing and variation in the association by ethnicity. Secondary outcome measures were 1-year site-specific cancer incidence and stage at diagnosis. The study included 4 901 450 patients with a platelet count record and 811 559 with a CRP record. One-year cancer incidence was highest among white patients and lowest among Asian patients. Following a normal platelet count, 1-year cancer incidence was 1.3% (95% CI 1.3 to 1.3%) for white patients and 0.63% (0.60 to 0.66%) for Asian patients; following thrombocytosis, incidence increased to 3.9% (3.8 to 4.0%) and 1.8% (1.5 to 2.1%), respectively. After a normal CRP result, cancer incidence was 1.5% (1.4 to 1.5%) for white patients and 0.81% (0.73 to 0.90%) for Asian patients, rising to 3.6% (3.5 to 3.7%) and 1.9% (1.7 to 2.2%) for a high CRP result, respectively. No significant interactions were found between ethnicity, blood test result and overall cancer diagnosis, and similar ORs were observed across all ethnic groups. However, for colorectal cancer, black patients with abnormal results showed higher ORs compared with white patients, relative to a normal result. The OR for thrombocytosis was 11.1 (7.8 to 15.6) for black patients versus 5.7 (5.4 to 6.0) for white patients (interaction p value<0.001), and for raised CRP was 4.1 (2.6 to 6.6) for black patients versus 2.5 (2.3 to 2.7) for white patients (interaction p value=0.043). This large primary care study provides reassurance that thrombocytosis and raised CRP appear to have broadly consistent associations with 1-year cancer incidence across ethnic groups in UK primary care.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastasis remains a major challenge in colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment. STIL is an oncogene, dysregulated in multiple cancers and has been known to regulate cancer stem cell maintenance through Sonic Hedgehog and Wnt signaling pathways in CRC. Although STIL has been implicated in invasion, migration, and metastasis in several malignancies, its role in CRC metastatic progression remains unclear. In the present study, we investigated the effect of STIL silencing on epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT)-associated markers in CRC. STIL knockdown both in in vitro and in vivo models resulted in reduced E-cadherin expression and increased N-cadherin and Vimentin expression, indicating EMT-associated molecular alterations. Similar expression trends and correlations were further supported by GEPIA-based analyses and clinical CRC samples. These findings suggest that STIL may play a complex and context-dependent role in CRC progression and EMT regulation. Overall, the present study provides preliminary evidence linking STIL to EMT-associated pathways in CRC and highlights the need for further mechanistic and functional studies to define its role in metastasis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Chronic inflammation and extracellular matrix (ECM) degradation are key features of carcinogenesis and tumor progression. We investigated the expression of proline-glycine-proline (PGP), an ECM-derived neutrophilic chemoattractant, in both tumor and serum samples from colorectal cancer (CRC) patients. We also correlated PGP levels with pathological and clinical outcomes. Our study included 88 previously untreated CRC patients who underwent surgical resection. Notably, PGP levels were significantly elevated in tumors compared to adjacent normal tissue, alongside neutrophilic infiltration. We explored enzymatic pathways critical to PGP persistence in the tumor microenvironment, observing increased expression of PGP-generating proteases like prolyl endopeptidase (PE) and MMP-9, and reduced PGP breakdown via LTA4H. The complementary peptide, l-arginine-threonine-arginine (RTR), impedes PGP-high expressed tumor lysates-induced chemotaxis in vitro. Elevated tumor PGP was associated with decreased disease-free survival (p=0.0235), and serum PGP levels correlated with tumor T stage. Additionally, we found a positive correlation between tumor-related cytokines in the serum and PGP expression. These findings demonstrate that PGP is associated with inflammatory and clinical features of CRC and support further investigation into its biological and clinical significance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Over the past decade, therapeutic strategies for gastrointestinal cancers have evolved towards greater personalisation, making treatment de-escalation an increasingly relevant option for selected patients. Two main approaches are explored: omitting one component of multimodality treatment or reducing radiotherapy dose or volume. For oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma, active surveillance with salvage surgery after chemoradiotherapy, offers a non-inferior alternative to systematic surgery in patients with complete clinical response, while adenocarcinoma management is shifting towards perioperative chemotherapy with fluorouracil, leucovorin, oxaliplatin, and docetaxel, with durvalumab. In rectal cancer, growing evidence from watch-and-wait strategies or chemotherapy-alone approaches supports selective omission of radiotherapy or surgery in low-risk tumours. Chemoradiotherapy combined with immunotherapy in patients with microsatellite stability increases the response rate while novel node-sparing radiotherapy volumes suggest a paradigm shift, preserving lymph nodes to sustain immune priming for checkpoint inhibitors. For early-stage anal canal carcinoma, the PLATO-ACT4 trial demonstrated that reduced-dose chemoradiotherapy (41.4Gy) achieves comparable locoregional control with improved tolerance and quality of life compared to standard-dose treatment. Together, these strategies illustrate a shift towards individualised, response and risk-adapted therapy in digestive oncology. However, most de-escalation approaches still rely on limited follow-up or selected populations, and shared decision-making incorporating patient preferences and quality-of-life trade-offs should increasingly guide these choices. Ongoing trials (NEEDS, GRECCAR 14/16, DECREASE) will help refine patient selection and confirm the long-term safety of these de-escalated strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) progression is strongly influenced by tumour-cell plasticity and dynamic transcriptional reprogramming, which contribute to heterogeneity, treatment resistance and metastatic progression. This study developed an integrated computational framework to identify anticancer peptides that interact with molecular candidates associated with CRC reprogramming. Experimentally reported colon/colorectal cancer-associated anticancer peptides were curated and filtered according to physicochemical stability, predicted toxicity and haemolytic potential. Single-cell RNA-sequencing data from GSE132465 were analysed using tumour-normal differential expression, reprogramming-related Hallmark signatures and weighted gene co-expression network analysis, followed by protein-protein interaction, functional enrichment, immune-infiltration and machine-learning analyses. Ceruloplasmin (CP) emerged as the strongest internally consensus-stable candidate, being selected by at least two machine-learning feature-ranking methods in 73.3% of bootstrap iterations, while its differential expression was independently supported in TCGA-COAD/READ. Twelve prioritised peptides were subsequently evaluated by interface-guided HADDOCK docking, and six leading complexes were subjected to three independent 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations. FLAK26VAM produced the most favourable HADDOCK score and the highest hydrogen-bond occupancy, whereas FLAK93B showed the most consistent overall post-docking profile, including lower structural deviation, greater conformational compactness and the most favourable MM/GBSA and MM/PBSA energy estimates. HAL-1/20, HAL-1/9 and FLAK50Q7 also showed favourable complementary structural characteristics. Free-energy landscape analysis further supported the presence of defined low-energy conformational states in the prioritised complexes. Collectively, these findings identify CP as an externally supported CRC-associated candidate and prioritise FLAK26VAM and FLAK93B as complementary lead peptide candidates, with FLAK93B showing the strongest overall support when dynamic stability and post-MD energetics are considered. Thus, this study provides an integrated computational framework that links CRC reprogramming biology with peptide-target prioritisation, highlighting ceruloplasmin and selected anticancer peptides as candidates for further experimental validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The 5-lipoxygenase-activating protein (FLAP) is an essential regulator of leukotriene (LT) biosynthesis, a pathway implicated in both chronic inflammation and tumor progression. Building on our benzimidazole lead, whose FLAP potency was compromised by prior structural modifications, we systematically remodeled the scaffold at the C(5) and C(2) positions to define the precise steric, electronic and polarity requirements for cellular FLAP inhibition. A structurally diverse library of derivatives was synthesized and evaluated in intact human polymorphonuclear leukocytes. Structure-activity relationship analysis revealed that conventional aromatic motifs within the address region are fully replaceable by polar, sterically hindered aliphatic substituents, yielding highly potent FLAP inhibitors. Conversely, the core bioisostere region proved considerably more restrictive, strongly favoring the parent aliphatic motif and tolerating only neutral, non-basic replacements. Comprehensive lipid mediator profiling in primary human leukocytes and distinct macrophage phenotypes confirmed that the optimized analogues selectively suppress FLAP-dependent leukotrienes while leaving alternative arachidonic acid metabolic pathways largely unaffected. Parallel screening against glioblastoma, breast, and colon carcinoma lines uncovered an additional, independent antiproliferative activity intrinsic to the benzimidazole scaffold. Several analogues successfully combined robust cellular FLAP inhibition with significant growth inhibition, particularly against colon cancer cells. Because antiproliferative efficacy did not correlate with FLAP inhibition across the series, the data establish that these complementary pharmacological activities are mechanistically distinct and independently tunable. Ultimately, these dual-action agents offer a promising novel chemotype for modulating the pro-inflammatory tumor microenvironment, providing a clear foundation for future mechanistic investigations to identify their specific distinct anticancer targets.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
VEGF-A/VEGF-R axis is well recognized for its role in tumor angiogenesis as well as tumor-induced immunosuppressive mechanisms. Targeting this pathway can help to switch tumor microenvironment toward a more immune-permissive state. Inhibition of VEGF-A/VEGFR has emerged as a strategy to enhance the efficacy of immunotherapy in some cancers leading to the approval of anti-VEGF-A/anti-PD(L)1 combinations in advanced renal cell cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, non-small cell lung cancer, and endometrial cancer. However, in other tumor types, and particularly in colorectal cancer or glioblastoma, results remain limited. In this review, we discuss the biological rationale underlying anti-VEGF-A/PD-(L)1 combinations, summarize the clinical evidence supporting their use across tumor types, discuss the disappointing results in colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, and highlight emerging strategies to improve their therapeutic efficacy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The acidic microenvironment in solid tumors is not merely a metabolic byproduct of the Warburg effect but actively promotes disease aggressiveness and treatment failure. Tumor alkalization therapy, which aims to neutralize or alkalinize the TME, has therefore emerged as a promising adjunct to conventional cancer treatments. In this study, we fabricated both SERS nanosensors and microsensors for parallel spatiotemporal monitoring of intracellular pH (pHi) and extracellular pH (pHe) within tumor spheroids derived from three human cancer cell lines: lung adenocarcinoma (H1975), pancreatic cancer (SW1990), and colorectal cancer (SW480). Over a 7-day culture period, distinct pHi and pHe profiles were observed among the different cell types. We then examined the pH modulation elicited by administration of sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3), a clinically employed alkaline agent. Exposure to 75 mM NaHCO3 for 24 h induced a marked elevation of pHe (∼0.78 units) and a modest increment in pHi (∼0.37 units). This integrated nanosensor-microsensor system, which leverages the size effect for precise spatial localization, offers a versatile approach for elucidating the complex interactions within the tumor microenvironment and helps optimize pH-modulating cancer therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
AKT hyperactivation is a hallmark of many human cancers and contributes to poor clinical outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Here, we show that AKT undergoes UFMylation, and loss of AKT UFMylation promotes colorectal tumor development and confers resistance to the AKT inhibitor AZD5363 (capivasertib). Furthermore, p53 activates ubiquitin-fold modifier 1 (UFM1) during the cell cycle to inhibit AKT activity. Conversely, AKT phosphorylates UFM1 to reduce its own UFMylation, establishing a feedback loop that sustains AKT activity. Moreover, we provide evidence that UFSP2 functions as a major cellular deUFMylase for AKT, and genetic ablation or inhibition of UFSP2 suppresses AKT activity to retard tumorigenesis in vivo. Together, these findings provide a mechanistic framework for UFMylation-dependent AKT regulation and support further investigation of UFSP2 inhibition as a potential strategy to modulate AKT signaling in colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fucoxanthin is a marine carotenoid whose broad effects in experimental models contrast with its limited oral bioavailability. Human exposure to fucoxanthin-derived compounds varies with the food matrix and dosing regimen, with fucoxanthinol being the principal reported circulating metabolite. This review evaluates the proposed fucoxanthin-gut microbiota-organ framework across the gut-liver, gut-brain, and gut-lung axes, systemic metabolism, and tumor biology and immunity, distinguishing direct fucoxanthin evidence from mechanistic extrapolation and assessing dietary dose relevance. Animal studies associate fucoxanthin with microbiota remodeling, improved intestinal barrier function, and reduced lipopolysaccharide translocation. These alterations could influence short-chain fatty acid, bile acid, and tryptophan-derived metabolite signaling, although complete microbiota-metabolite-receptor pathways remain insufficiently validated. Fecal microbiota transplantation supports a microbial contribution to colorectal cancer protection in one mouse model, whereas gut-brain and gut-lung mechanisms remain largely inferential. Many nominal human-equivalent doses derived from animal studies exceed estimated dietary intakes, and cellular fucoxanthin concentrations often exceed circulating human fucoxanthinol concentrations. Human colonic exposure remains unquantified and cannot be inferred from plasma concentrations. Future studies should integrate causal models, luminal and systemic exposure measurements, targeted metabolomics, and human trials to establish the nutritional relevance of fucoxanthin.
