ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer is one of the most prevalent malignancies and a major cause of cancer-related mortality worldwide. It remains a significant health concern, with an alarming rise in early-onset colorectal cancer cases in younger populations. Many factors are reported to have been responsible for its onset, progression, and metastasis, among which the gut microbiome is found to be a crucial one. Dysbiosis among these gut microbes impacts normal cellular functions and homeostasis, which may lead to cancer. Under unfavourable conditions biological processes such as cell differentiation, proliferation, migration, and apoptosis get disrupted and give rise to pathological traits such as invasion and metastasis. Emerging evidence indicates a rather significant role of the gut microbiome in this transition, influencing both onset and progression. Over the past few decades, our understanding of microbiome-cancer interaction has evolved considerably, yet effective microbiome-based therapies remain limited. This review highlights how these microbes modulate normal biological functions to pathological ones, and we further discuss current microbiome-based therapies along with their future prospects.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Antiangiogenic drugs are widely used in cancer therapy but are associated with various adverse events (AEs). This study systematically analyzed pharmacovigilance data from the FAERS to evaluate the safety profiles of five antiangiogenic drugs. FAERS data from Q1 2004 to Q3 2024 were retrospectively analyzed, and external validation was performed on the EudraVigilance database. To detect AE signals, disproportionality analysis was performed using four methods: the reporting odds ratio (ROR), proportional reporting ratio (PRR), Bayesian confidence propagation neural network (BCPNN), multi-item gamma Poisson shrinker (MGPS). Time-to-onset (TTO) analysis was conducted. Subgroup analyses were performed based on gender and clinical outcomes (death/non-death). Disproportionality analysis identified musculoskeletal and connective tissue disorders as the most significantly associated AE for fruquintinib (ROR: 2.45, 95% CI: 2.05-2.94). The most frequently reported AE was death (ROR: 3.11, 95% CI: 2.64-3.66). Subgroup analysis revealed that males had a higher number of AEs, with death being most frequently reported, while females predominantly reported increased blood pressure. TTO analysis showed that most AEs occurred within 30 days of treatment initiation for fruquintinib (60.62%), ramucirumab (54.48%), aflibercept (48.71%), and regorafenib (71.5%), while 90.11% of bevacizumab-related AEs occurred within 360 days. This study provides a comprehensive pharmacovigilance assessment of antiangiogenic drugs, highlighting distinct AE patterns and times. These findings may guide clinicians in optimizing AE monitoring and management strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The mitochondrial solute carrier (SLC25) family regulates solute transport across the mitochondrial inner membrane. Among them, SLC25A39 has emerged as a critical player in tumor biology, primarily through its dual role in mediating mitochondrial glutathione (mGSH) transport and maintaining iron-sulfur cluster homeostasis. Recent evidence implies that SLC25A39 dysfunction disrupts mGSH metabolism, thereby influencing iron-sulfur cluster synthesis and driving metabolic reprogramming in tumors. Notably, SLC25A39 is governed by a GSH-Fe-S-AFG3L2 feedback circuit, a feature not shared by its closest homolog SLC25A40. Additionally, upregulation of SLC25A39 is frequently observed in multiple malignancies, including colorectal, pancreatic, and liver cancers, where it correlates with enhanced proliferation, metastasis, and poor prognosis. Furthermore, SLC25A39 expression is intricately associated with remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment and the development of therapeutic resistance, although these associations are primarily based on correlative evidence and require functional validation before causal conclusions can be drawn. This review synthesizes current knowledge on the molecular mechanisms by which SLC25A39 integrates mGSH transport with iron metabolism, and critically evaluates its emerging roles across different cancer types. We propose that beyond serving as a candidate prognostic biomarker, SLC25A39 represents a potential therapeutic target whose clinical utility remains to be established, and we discuss key unanswered questions regarding its tissue-specific functions and the translational challenges that lie ahead.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To compare early and delayed diverting ileostomy closure after low anterior resection for rectal cancer, focusing on postoperative morbidity and recovery outcomes, and to assess the certainty of available evidence. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, and Web of Science were searched from inception to 26th April, 2026. Five comparative studies (four randomized trials and one prospective cohort; 512 participants) were included. Random-effects meta-analyses evaluated overall post-closure morbidity as the primary outcome and severe complications, index-to-closure interval, postoperative hospital stay, operative time, and reoperation as secondary outcomes. Certainty was assessed using GRADE. Overall morbidity occurred in 52/257 patients after early closure and 50/255 after delayed closure (RR 1.06, 95% CI 0.66-1.71; τ²=0.12; I²=40%). Severe complications and reoperation did not differ statistically, with confidence intervals compatible with benefit or harm. The index-to-closure interval was 107.09 days shorter with early closure (95% CI - 153.01 to - 61.17; τ²=2023.39; I²=96%); this process measure was largely inherent to the group definitions. Hospital stay and operative time did not differ statistically. The available evidence does not demonstrate a statistically significant difference in postoperative morbidity but does not establish equivalence. Early closure may be considered in selected patients after postoperative recovery and assessment of anastomotic integrity; however, these findings do not support routine early closure in all patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer is the leading cause of death in prison. Limited literature suggests cancer screening rates in prison are low, but population-level screening data in prisons are scarce. To determine screening rates for 5 cancer types, identify individual and incarceration characteristics associated with receipt of screening, and characterize outcomes for screen-detectable cancers in California prisons. This cohort study included individuals incarcerated in California state prisons who were eligible for breast, cervical, colorectal, liver, or lung cancer screening between January 1, 2014, and June 30, 2023. Incarceration data were linked to state cancer registry data from 2014 to 2021 to identify screen-detectable cancers diagnosed in the study population. Analyses were conducted between August 2024 and July 2025. Receipt of screening within 3 months before a cancer diagnosis. Receipt of cancer screening; screening rates; and cancer diagnosis, stage, and survival were calculated. Multivariable models evaluated characteristics associated with screening receipt and associations between screening receipt and stage at diagnosis and survival, with adjustment for demographic and incarceration characteristics. The study included 106 352 incarcerated individuals (median [IQR] age at first eligibility, 50 [47-55] years; 86 559 males [81.4%]). By June 30, 2023 (data cutoff), 89.4%, 81.2%, 80.0%, 70.1%, and 76.0% of individuals were up-to-date with screening for breast, colorectal, cervical, lung, and liver cancer screening, respectively. Characteristics associated with higher likelihood of ever receiving screening included mental health service use, prison security level 3 or 4, recent change in primary care practitioner, and incarceration within the past year before screening eligibility. Of 812 patients with screening data, 92 (11.3%) were diagnosed with screen-detectable cancer before they met eligibility for screening, including 56 with liver cancer. A total of 392 screening-eligible patients (48.3%) were diagnosed with screen-detectable cancer while in prison during the study period. Approximately 71% of patients received screening within 3 months before diagnosis, which was associated with lower odds of stage IV disease at diagnosis (odds ratio, 0.44; 95% CI, 0.23-0.85) and better survival (hazard ratio, 0.63; 95% CI, 0.44-0.88); rates of stage IV cancer were lower for individuals with recent screening than those without recent screening (10.0% vs 21.0%). In this cohort study of incarcerated individuals in California prisons, screening rates were high and associated with early-stage cancer diagnoses, suggesting that effective cancer screening is achievable in prison settings. Future work should examine whether increased screening ameliorates incarceration-related cancer disparities.

Environmental exposures and biological susceptibility contribute to the complexity in cancer vulnerability, particularly in settings where comprehensive environmental monitoring and longitudinal exposure data are limited. Scenario-based modeling can provide a structured approach for exploring potential environmental cancer risks under uncertainty and identifying priorities for future research and surveillance. We developed a scenario-based environmental cancer risk framework for Lebanon incorporating three exposure domains-perchlorate contamination, nitrate/nitrite exposure, and conflict-derived environmental contamination- and a qualitative Genetic Susceptibility Index (GSI). Monte Carlo simulations with 100,000 iterations were used to propagate uncertainty in literature-derived epidemiological effect estimates for colorectal and lung cancers under alternative hypothetical scaling assumptions. The GSI was used to organize qualitative susceptibility pathways but was not incorporated as a numerical modifier in the simulations. For lung cancer, corresponding mean simulated relative effects were 2.18% (95% UI: 1.01-3.36%), 4.41% (95% UI: 2.02-6.83%), and 9.03% (95% UI: 4.09-14.13%). ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Human papillomaviruses of the beta genus (beta-HPV) are ubiquitous components of the cutaneous virome, persistently colonizing the skin of immunocompetent individuals from early infancy. Unlike their alpha counterparts, which drive mucosal carcinogenesis through viral integration and sustained oncoprotein expression, beta-HPVs employ transient, cofactor-dependent mechanisms that operate primarily at the initiation stages of keratinocyte carcinogenesis, a paradigm known as the hit-and-run model. Although their association with cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is well supported, particularly in immunocompromised individuals, beta-HPV genotypes are being increasingly detected in patients with cervical, head and neck, anal, vulvar, and colorectal carcinomas. This raises the question of whether beta-HPVs play a broader oncogenic role. This review examines the clinical significance of beta-HPV across anatomical sites and evaluates existing and next-generation preventive strategies. Collectively, the evidence suggests that beta-HPVs may act as clinically relevant viral cofactors, although whether their detection at these sites is incidental or causal remains unclear.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical site infection (SSI) remains a major complication after colorectal surgery. Comparative evidence for commonly used perioperative intravenous antibiotic regimens is limited, and risk prediction models require external evaluation before clinical use. We examined regimen-SSI associations and secondarily evaluated models using routine perioperative variables to distinguish patients with and without electronically recorded postoperative SSI. We analysed 732 adults from MIMIC-IV for regimen association and model development and 133 adults from ICU-based eICU-CRD for external model evaluation. SSI was identified using an electronic phenotype. Four intravenous antibiotic exposure groups were compared using multivariable logistic regression and exploratory interaction analyses. Predictors selected using LASSO screening followed by clinical refinement informed six models, which were assessed using discrimination, calibration, and classification metrics. SSI was recorded in 146/732 patients (19.9%), with no evidence of an unadjusted association across observed exposure categories ( These data provide no evidence of an overall association, nor evidence of equivalent prophylactic efficacy. Heterogeneous exposures and residual confounding preclude regimen-level causal conclusions. The small ICU-based external evaluation informs higher-acuity populations, not routine elective surgery. Uncertain SSI onset, limited calibration, and false-positive burden preclude clinical implementation. Prospective multicentre studies should evaluate risk-adapted surveillance, not model-directed antibiotic selection.

Circulating Tumor DNA (ctDNA) for Minimal Residual Disease (MRD) Detection in Colorectal Cancer (CRC): Current Evidence, Clinical Applications, and Future Directions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Minimal residual disease (MRD) is a major contributor to colorectal cancer (CRC) recurrence following curative-intent treatment, yet conventional surveillance methods may fail to detect residual disease at its earliest stages. Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) has emerged as a minimally invasive biomarker for MRD detection and postoperative monitoring. We conducted a structured PubMed-based literature review and included 94 publications evaluating ctDNA in CRC. Across the literature, postoperative ctDNA positivity was consistently associated with increased recurrence risk and poorer disease-free and overall survival, while serial monitoring improved detection sensitivity and enabled assessment of treatment response. ctDNA frequently identified molecular recurrence approximately 2.5-11.5 months before conventional surveillance. Both tumor-informed and tumor-naive strategies were represented, using PCR/ddPCR, targeted next-generation sequencing, whole-exome or whole-genome sequencing, methylation-based assays, and emerging multiomic approaches. Although ctDNA demonstrates strong prognostic value, evidence supporting treatment modification based solely on ctDNA status remains limited. Further prospective randomized trials, assay standardization, and consensus clinical guidelines are required before routine implementation. Overall, ctDNA is a promising tool for recurrence prediction, surveillance, and precision management of CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Probiotics exert profound health benefits via the modulation of the intestinal microbiota. However, the efficacy of orally administered probiotics is severely constrained by a cascade of physiological barriers, including gastric acid inactivation, suboptimal intestinal release, and inadequate mucosal colonization. In response to these challenges, hydrogel-based delivery platforms have garnered considerable interest as versatile carriers capable of providing protective encapsulation, enabling spatiotemporally controlled release, and augmenting intestinal retention. This narrative review presents recent progress in the design and application of hydrogel-based oral delivery systems tailored for targeted probiotic release and effective colonization. First, the key gastrointestinal obstacles to successful probiotic delivery are delineated. Hydrogel design parameters are then critically appraised, with particular emphasis on material selection and network design. The underlying release mechanisms are subsequently examined. These encompass pH-responsive, enzyme-triggered, and inflammation-responsive modalities. Emerging colonization-enhancing strategies are discussed in detail. These include mucoadhesive hydrogel architectures and the nascent paradigm of "living hydrogels" functioning as dynamic bioreactors. The translational potential of these systems for health management is illustrated through applications in inflammatory bowel disease, colorectal cancer, and gut-brain axis modulation. Finally, key challenges in manufacturing, viability, and translational feasibility are evaluated. These include regulatory, safety, and encapsulation-related constraints. To address these, multi-responsive platforms, machine learning-assisted design, and synbiotic hydrogels are proposed. These hydrogels synergize with probiotics to target dysbiosis and repair mucosal damage for improved gastrointestinal health management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) is a programmed and reversible process that allows epithelial cells to temporarily acquire a mesenchymal cell phenotype with increased migratory and invasive capacity. Analogous phenotypic modulation can also occur in carcinoma cells, which, after undergoing EMT, exhibit cancer stem cell-like properties and actively migrate, leading to tumor invasion and metastases. This structured narrative review focuses on the molecular crosstalk between human papillomavirus (HPV) and EMT, which occurs in HPV-infected human epithelium and in HPV-positive cancers of different location (cervical, head and neck, colorectal, lung, and others). The main questions addressed here are: (i) how HPV-driven EMT may contribute to the malignant transformation of HPV-infected epithelial cells, (ii) what mechanistic links may exist between the HPV positivity and EMT in human cancers, and (iii) how EMT in various HPV-positive human tumors may influence their pathogenesis, treatment modalities and outcomes. The relationship between HPV infection and EMT program is delineated as a complex multicomponent mechanism triggered by exogenous and endogenous stimuli and involving specific ligand-receptor interactions, membrane channels, transcription factors, signaling pathways, epigenetic regulators, etc. The review also discusses some of the potential applications of EMT-related biomarkers and molecular targets in the prevention, prediction and treatment of HPV-induced cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) has been increasing in Taiwan and is associated with multiple risk factors. Increasing evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis contributes to CRC development. This study aimed to characterize microbial and metabolic alterations across premalignant and malignant colorectal lesions and to identify potential microbiome-associated biomarkers. Individuals undergoing colonoscopy for screening or surveillance at Taipei Veterans General Hospital were enrolled. Gut microbial composition was analyzed using full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing to achieve high-resolution taxonomic profiling. Predicted functional pathways were inferred from microbial communities, and targeted metabolomic profiling was performed to evaluate microbial metabolic outputs. A total of 122 individuals were included, comprising 62 healthy controls, 15 adenoma cases, and 45 CRC cases. Change in microbial composition and predicted functional pathways were observed across the control, adenoma, and CRC groups. Control-associated taxa were linked to carbohydrate fermentation and amino acid metabolism pathways, whereas CRC-associated taxa, particularly Fusobacterium, showed broad negative correlations with multiple biosynthetic pathways. Metabolomic analysis showed increased tauro-ursocholanic acid and reduced short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) in CRC. CRC-associated bacteria were negatively correlated with SCFAs and positively correlated with several bile acid metabolites, including lithocholic acid, murocholic acid, tauro-ursocholanic acid, and taurohyocholic acid. Integrative analysis of full-length 16S rRNA sequencing, predicted functional pathways, and metabolomic profiling identified microbial and metabolic differences across the control, adenoma, and CRC groups. These findings are consistent with an association between gut microbial alterations and colorectal neoplasia and may inform future studies of microbial and metabolic biomarkers for CRC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Diagnosing invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma (CRC) in limited biopsy samples can be challenging. This study evaluates fibroblast activation protein-α (FAP)'s role in diagnosing CRC and identifies potential pitfalls. To evaluate the expression pattern of FAP in CRC, we analyzed 168 cases of CRC with established diagnosis, including 30 whole slides and 138 cases from a tissue microarray (TMA). The study group includes 33 colorectal lesion biopsies with diagnostic challenges, identified retrospectively over 9 years in 1 institution. These biopsies were initially not diagnosed as CRC and confirmed to be so upon subsequent resection. Six additional cases of adenoma and 4 cases of solitary rectal ulcers were also evaluated. FAP was expressed in the cancer stroma of 161/168 (96%) of CRC cases, including 29/30 whole slides and 132/138 TMA. The diagnosis of 33 challenging cases by H&E included adenoma (n=4), high-grade dysplasia (HGD, n=16), and concerning for CRC (n=13). Among these cases, all 20 cases of adenoma or HGD were FAP-negative. Out of 13 "concerning for CRC" cases, 9 (69%) showed FAP positivity in the stroma. Five of 6 additional adenomas were FAP-negative, while 1 adenoma showed FAP staining in scar tissue from the prior biopsy site. Of the 4 cases of solitary rectal ulcers, 1 exhibited weak FAP expression in the granulation tissue. In conclusion, FAP immunohistochemistry may assist in diagnosing CRC in challenging cases. Due to FAP positivity in benign conditions, such as scar tissue and benign ulcers, awareness of the pitfalls is important when applying FAP immunostaining in practice.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Optimal sequencing of rectal and liver resection for patients with resectable synchronous liver metastases (SLM) from rectal cancer remains controversial, and rectal-specific evidence is limited. A nationwide target trial (METASYNC-R) was emulated using the French national discharge database (2014-2023). Adults undergoing both rectal and liver resection for rectal cancer with SLM were eligible. Combined resection was compared with staged strategies (rectum- or liver-first within 14 weeks). Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) estimated the average treatment effect. Thirty-day severe complications (Clavien-Dindo grade ≥III) were analysed using marginal logistic regression with robust variance; overall survival was analysed using IPTW Cox proportional hazards models with cluster-robust standard errors. Landmark analyses at 3, 6, 12, and 24 months addressed potential immortal time bias. Among 9632 patients undergoing both resections, 3057 had SLM and 1872 met the eligibility criteria (median age of 64 years); 1365 (73%) underwent combined resection and 507 (27%) underwent staged resection. Severe complications occurred in 39.7% versus 45.3% (P = 0.20); combined surgery was not associated with an increased risk of severe complications (adjusted OR 0.82 (95% c.i. 0.58 to 1.16); P = 0.27). Major hepatectomy independently increased the risk of severe complications (adjusted OR 1.81 (95% c.i. 1.06 to 3.08); P = 0.029). Thirty-day mortality was similar (1.8% versus 1.5%). Median overall survival was 52.4 months (combined) versus 57.3 months (staged) (P = 0.30). Combined surgery was not associated with worse survival (adjusted HR 0.88 (95% c.i. 0.65 to 1.19); P = 0.40), with consistent findings across landmark analyses. In this nationwide rectal cancer cohort, combined and staged strategies were associated with comparable morbidity and long-term survival. Surgical sequencing should be individualized within multidisciplinary decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Long-term oncological equivalence of robotic total mesorectal excision (R-TME) and laparoscopic total mesorectal excision (L-TME) remains unproven. The 5-year outcomes of the COLRAR RCT are reported. Adults with cT1-4a Nx M0 rectal adenocarcinoma within 10 cm of the anal verge were randomized 1 : 1 to L-TME or R-TME at three Korean tertiary centres between July 2011 and February 2016. Pre-specified secondary endpoints were 5-year overall, relapse-free, local recurrence-free, and distant recurrence-free survival. Analyses were on a modified intention-to-treat basis. Of 295 analysed patients (144 L-TME patients and 151 R-TME patients; median follow-up of 72.6 months), 5-year overall survival (92.6% versus 92.4%; P = 0.838) and relapse-free survival (81.9% versus 83.0%; P = 0.801) were similar. Local recurrence occurred in 4.9% (L-TME) and 1.3% (R-TME); 5-year local recurrence-free and distant recurrence-free survival did not differ (P = 0.076 and P = 0.655). In a post-hoc analysis of 146 patients who received neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, 5-year local recurrence-free survival was 98.6% in R-TME patients versus 90.7% in L-TME patients (P = 0.039). R-TME and L-TME produced equivalent 5-year oncological outcomes. A post-hoc analysis suggested improved local control with robotic surgery after neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy, requiring confirmation in prospectively designed studies. NCT01423214 (http://www.clinicaltrials.gov).

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
People with learning disabilities participate in cancer screening) at lower rates than people without learning disabilities. The reasons for these disparities are somewhat unclear, although in the United Kingdom (UK), community-based learning disabilities nurses are a key professional group who may help facilitate screening. Our aim was to understand how learning disabilities nurses facilitate cancer screening among their patients with learning disabilities. We interviewed 11 nurses, finding that while there are some characteristics that are unique to each screening modality, there are many similarities in accessing screening. Nurses described supporting their patients by making reasonable adjustments. These adjustments include providing easy-read information, allowing for advance appointments and providing training for people with learning disabilities, their carers, and health professionals involved in the screening. By understanding how nurses may support patients, future interventions can be implemented to increase the numbers of people with learning disabilities accessing screening and reduce this screening disparity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
We compared perioperative outcomes after robotic (rRC) and laparoscopic right hemicolectomy (lapRC) and assessed temporal changes in surgical approach and minimally invasive completion. This retrospective cohort included patients operated between January 2023 and March 2026. Primary outcomes were operative duration, open conversion, and 30-day morbidity. The main comparison was unadjusted, supplemented by elective and propensity-score-matched analyses. Temporal trends included all screened patients, including primary open procedures. A total of 221 patients were analyzed, including 122 rRC and 99 lapRC procedures. Median operative duration was greater with rRC than with lapRC (264 vs. 200 min, p < 0.001), whereas conversion to an open procedure occurred less frequently after rRC (4% vs. 20%, p < 0.001). Overall morbidity (28% vs. 35%, p = 0.246) and major complications (12% vs. 12%, p = 1) did not differ significantly. Median lymph-node yield in carcinoma resections was 26 versus 25 (p = 0.249). The conversion difference was not statistically significant in the overall elective cohort or the matched analysis of 32 pairs. Across all 390 screened patients, increasing robotic use coincided with decreasing primary open surgery (p = 0.014), while the increase in minimally invasive completion was not statistically significant (p = 0.075). Robotic right hemicolectomy may offer an advantage in reducing conversion to open surgery, although operative duration was longer. This potential benefit requires confirmation, given baseline differences and the limited size of the matched cohort.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Total mesorectal excision (TME) remains the curative operation for rectal cancer. The male pelvis, obesity, and a narrow anal canal make rectal dissection the most demanding step in abdominal surgery, even for experienced surgeons. Robotic systems were introduced to address these constraints by providing a stable three-dimensional view, wristed instruments, and ergonomic control beyond that of conventional laparoscopy. Two decades after the first robotic TME, randomized trials (ROLARR and REAL), transanal TME trials, and more than a dozen meta-analyses permit a more measured assessment. To make that assessment clear and comparable, we organize it around a prespecified core set of outcome parameters rather than every metric reported in the literature: the primary oncological and surgical-quality outcomes are conversion to open surgery, circumferential resection margin (CRM) involvement, completeness of the mesorectal specimen, and long-term locoregional recurrence and disease-free survival; the primary functional outcomes are bowel, urinary, and sexual function, measured with validated instruments at fixed time points. Overall survival, distal margin, lymph node yield, general morbidity and anastomotic leak, operative time, blood loss, length of stay, quality of life, and cost are treated as secondary outcomes. Against this core set, robotic surgery consistently reduces conversion to open surgery. In the most informative recent trial, it also improved circumferential resection margin quality and three-year locoregional control in high-risk middle and low rectal cancers, without affecting overall survival. Functional benefits, including earlier recovery of urinary function and modest improvements in bowel and sexual outcomes, are plausible but supported by low-certainty evidence. Distinct pitfalls remain, ranging from arm collision and docking errors to distal-plane deviation and anastomotic failure, and the approach is slower and more expensive than laparoscopy. This review summarizes the oncological and functional evidence, relates technical errors to the operative sequence, and examines unresolved controversies: which patients benefit most, how robotics compares with transanal dissection, and whether fluorescence imaging, neuromonitoring, and new competing platforms alter the balance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by heterogeneous disease presentations and clinical courses. Accurate diagnosis and appropriate disease monitoring play an important role in improving long-term outcomes by preventing misdiagnosis and unnecessary treatment; enabling early detection of disease progression, treatment failure, and disease-related complications; and facilitating timely adjustment of treatment strategies. The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID) developed guidelines for the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD in adults, reflecting the Korean clinical setting, to support clinical decision-making and improve the quality of patient care. To develop these guidelines, existing international clinical practice guidelines and expert consensus statements were comprehensively reviewed, along with updated evidence relevant to each clinical topic. Final recommendations were established through expert consensus using a modified Delphi process. These guidelines address major clinical areas in the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD, including initial diagnosis and baseline assessment, assessment of disease extent and activity, disease monitoring in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, nutritional assessment, and colorectal cancer surveillance. These guidelines are intended to support individualized clinical judgment and should be applied flexibly, taking into account not only individual patient characteristics and clinical circumstances but also available resources, access to diagnostic and monitoring modalities, regulatory requirements, and reimbursement policies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Later-line treatment for metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC) has shifted from purely pursuing survival prolongation to a chronic disease management model that balances survival with quality of life (QoL). Conventional line-by-line drug sequencing faces efficacy plateaus and tolerability challenges, necessitating an integrated precision framework combining biological stratification, dynamic monitoring, and multimodal therapy. This review synthesizes four evolving domains in later-line management. In systemic therapy, cross-line use of antiangiogenic agents (bevacizumab, anlotinib), trifluridine/tipiracil combination regimens, immunotherapy breakthroughs in MSI-H/dMMR populations, and targeted rechallenge strategies have demonstrated clinical value. Locoregional therapy integration offers salvage options for oligometastatic patients through selective internal radiation therapy (SIRT) of liver metastases, pressurized intraperitoneal aerosol chemotherapy (PIPAC), and stereotactic body radiotherapy (SBRT). Precision stratification builds an end-to-end care pathway via circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) trajectory monitoring, body composition assessment, and molecular biomarkers. Special population management addresses individualized considerations for elderly frail patients and early-onset colorectal cancer. The review emphasizes that treatment decisions must balance survival benefit against toxicity burden, prioritizing patient-reported outcomes (PROs), toxicity management, and early integration of palliative support. Future paradigms should establish patient-centered, multidisciplinary continuum-of-care systems that coordinate three pillars: precision molecular profiling to guide therapy selection, rational de-escalation to avoid overtreatment, and supportive care to preserve dignity throughout the disease trajectory.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin (OXA) is a cornerstone of colorectal cancer therapy, but its effects on male germ cell metabolism and signaling remain poorly understood. This study aimed to investigate the effects of OXA on redox homeostasis, lipid-related processes, and steroid-related responses in GC-1 (spg) and GC-2 (spd) spermatogenic cells. OXA exposure induced oxidative stress and mitochondrial depolarization together with pronounced changes in lipid organization and signaling pathways. Notably, instead of inducing overt lipid peroxidation, OXA prompted neutral lipid accumulation and increased intracellular free cholesterol, accompanied by changes in proteins involved in lipid and cholesterol homeostasis. These alterations were accompanied by modulation of lipid-metabolic regulators, including increased expression of ACOX1, consistent with alterations in peroxisomal fatty acid metabolism. The metabolic perturbations were further associated with stage-specific activation of signaling cascades and altered intracellular testosterone levels. Importantly, antioxidant intervention attenuated oxidative stress but did not fully reverse the observed lipid-related and steroid-related responses, suggesting that redox regulation may contribute to these changes but cannot fully explain the cellular response to OXA. Collectively, our findings indicate that OXA exposure is associated with coordinated changes in redox balance, lipid-related processes, and steroid-related responses in spermatogenic cells, revealing cell type-specific differences in their response to chemotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Multimodal treatment with chemotherapy, radiation, and surgery for locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC) is a standard of care (SOC) associated with significant toxicity/morbidity. After TNT, clinical complete response (cCR) ranges between 21-41%, highlighting the need for novel approaches. dMMR/MSI-H tumors are exceptionally responsive to PD-1 blockade: in a pilot study, patients with dMMR/MSI-H LARC achieved durable responses after neoadjuvant dostarlimab. AZUR-1 is the first global registrational study evaluating dostarlimab monotherapy in adults with previously untreated stage II/III dMMR/MSI-H LARC. Dostarlimab 500 mg was administered intravenously Q3W for 9 cycles. Key endpoints include rate of sustained cCR for 12 months (cCR12) following end of treatment (EOT) with dostarlimab alone by investigator and independent central review (ICR), and composite rate of cCR12 (INV) + pathological CR (pCR). At data cutoff (April 20, 2026), 154 patients were enrolled (median follow-up [range]: 26.3 [2-36] months). Of 144 patients with ≥12 months follow-up, 68% achieved cCR12 (INV). pCR was achieved in 12/15 patients (80%) who underwent surgery after dostarlimab alone: cCR12+pCR rate was 76%. cCR12 (ICR) was less mature than investigator, as first cCR (ICR) was identified at later timepoints. 98% who achieved cCR maintained cCR for ≥12 months. Overall, 93% of patients were on study with no evidence of disease progression after treatment (dostarlimab ± SOC); 71% achieved this outcome with dostarlimab alone. There were no reported recurrences for patients in cCR or pCR. Safety was acceptable; grade ≥3 immune-mediated AEs occurred in 4 (3%) patients. PROs showed meaningful improvements from baseline to EOT for several domains. In this AZUR-1 interim analysis, 68% of patients achieved cCR12 and 76% achieved cCR12+pCR with dostarlimab alone and had no disease recurrences. These durable responses indicate the potential to eliminate the need for current SOC and redefine the curative-intent treatment paradigm with dostarlimab in dMMR/MSI-H LARC. NCT05723562.

G-CSF use was 37.8% versus 19.1%. Adjuvant mFOLFIRINOX triplet chemotherapy did not improve DFS compared with standard doublet mFOLFOX6 in patients with high-risk stage III colon cancer. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Extracellular vesicles (EVs) hold great potential as therapeutic vehicles, but their clinical application is limited by low production yields. Here, we explored whether the pharmacological disruption of the actin cytoskeleton using cytochalasin D (CytoD) could enhance EV release while maintaining properties essential for therapeutic use. We examined monocytic U937 cells and colorectal cancer SW480 cells, discovering that CytoD increased EV production by approximately 8.27-fold in U937 cells and 10.06-fold in SW480 cells, while largely preserving the size distribution and surface charge of the EVs. Density gradient ultracentrifugation and label-free quantitative proteomics revealed that CytoD not only increased overall EV release but also selectively remodeled EV proteins. Notably, CytoD-EVs retained lineage-associated membrane proteins such as LFA-1 and showed an enrichment of cytoskeleton-related regulators, particularly MYH9, as well as proteins involved in adhesion and membrane trafficking. We observed the recruitment of MYH9 to membrane blebs,and both pharmacological inhibition with blebbistatin and MYH9 knockdown suppressed EV release, indicating that actomyosin-dependent contractility stimulates EV shedding. Importantly, CytoD-EVs proved to be highly effective drug carriers that doxorubicin-loaded EVs efficiently delivered cargo to recipient cells and induced greater cytotoxicity than free doxorubicin at equivalent doses. Overall, these findings demonstrate that CytoD-induced cytoskeletal remodeling enhances EV production through MYH9-associated membrane dynamics while preserving their capacity for therapeutic delivery. Thus, our findings establish CytoD-induced EV biogenesis as a robust, scalable, and translationally applicable platform for advanced EV-based drug delivery systems.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The network of transcription factors (TFs) is an integral component of executing macroautophagy/autophagy-lysosome gene expression to maintain cellular homeostasis. Across metazoans, conserved TFs, particularly the helix-loop-helix factor TFEB, convert upstream signals into specific genetic programs through mechanisms ranging from DNA recognition and chromatin remodeling to biomolecular condensates. The dysregulation of TF-governed gene programming disrupts the progression of metabolic disease and cancer, highlighting that dissection of transcriptional regulation makes it a promising therapeutic target. Consequently, instead of indirectly modulating the pathways in which they are involved, targeting these essential TFs directly is becoming a new trend for pharmaceutical development. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The use of indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence is a well-established technique in colorectal surgery for the evaluation of bowel stump perfusion. However, there is still no definitive acceptance, except for intraoperative macroscopic evidence, with reference to the incidence of anastomotic leakage (AL). The objective of this study is to evaluate whether ICG-guided fluorescence angiography reduces AL rates in both elective and emergency colorectal surgery. This was a single-center retrospective comparative cohort study. From January 2019 to June 2020, adult patients undergoing elective or emergency colorectal surgery (right/left hemicolectomy, rectal resection, or Hartmann reversal) were enrolled (N=79). In the ICG group (N=40), ICG angiography was used to evaluate colonic stump perfusion before and after creating the anastomosis. Results were compared to a historical control group (N=39) operated without ICG guidance. Group comparisons were analyzed using Pearson's chi-square test. Results: A total of 40 patients underwent surgery; 21 (52.50%) had benign pathology, and 19 (47.50%) exhibited malignant neoplasia. Thirteen (32.50%) were emergency surgeries, and 27 (67.50%) were planned elective surgeries. In almost all cases, the postoperative course was regular; in only one (2.5%) case of transanal total mesorectal excision (TaTME), there was an AL. Other complications were not related to the anastomosis, but some validated the excellent perfusion despite episodes of prolonged acute ischemia due to postoperative hemorrhage. Data were finally compared to a control group of 39 patients where the ICG fluorescence was not used. The study demonstrates a positive association between the use of ICG fluorescence as a method for intraoperative assessment of bowel perfusion and its effectiveness even in emergency conditions and in acute postoperative hemorrhage, detecting an incidence of 2.5% (one case out of 40) of AL. In addition, ICG fluorescence led to a change in the surgical strategy during the procedure. It's evident that to validate our results, further randomized studies on a larger data set are required. It would also be beneficial to evaluate the fluorescence between the mucous and serous layers quantitatively to confirm the reduction of AL rate, better evaluation of bowel perfusion, and, especially in emergency surgeries, the potential reduction of further operations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bacterial invasion and genotoxicity are key contributors to infectious disease progression and carcinogenesis. Yet current methods do not quantify these processes systematically and at single-cell resolution, limiting our ability to explore how interplay of virulence factors and drug effects shape pathogenicity. Here, we present MALVINA, a high-throughput deep-learning workflow integrating host-pathogen co-culture and high-content imaging to jointly measure bacterial invasion and host DNA damage. Applied to Escherichia coli isolates and human colorectal epithelial cells, we demonstrate MALVINA's versatility by deciphering (1) strains with elevated invasive or genotoxic potential, (2) interbacterial modulation of virulence, (3) pro-virulent drug effects, (4) virulence-targeting drugs, and (5) bacterial potentiation of drug toxicity. MALVINA revealed strain-specific virulence profiles and colibactin-dependent suppression of competitors' invasion coupled with enhanced genotoxicity. It also enabled identification of drug-induced modulation of bacterial invasion and genotoxicity, offering a new perspective for virulence-aware drug profiling. Overall, MALVINA offers an adaptable framework for dissecting pathogen-host-drug interactions.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A herniation sac containing the appendix, with or without inflammation, is known as Amyand's hernia, which is one of the rarest types of inguinal hernia. The condition is predominantly diagnosed during surgery, as preoperative identification via diagnostic imaging remains uncommon. This report presents two cases of Amyand's hernia. The first case was an 80-year-old male with clinical signs and symptoms of a right inguinal hernia. The ultrasound images confirm the diagnosis of Amyand's hernia. Based on established classification systems, management involved hernia reduction and mesh repair without appendectomy. The second case was a 63-year-old male with a history of rectal cancer. A CT scan revealed an incidental finding of the appendix within the right inguinal canal without evidence of inflammation, leading to a diagnosis of Amyand's hernia. Preoperative diagnosis remains essential for surgical planning to improve surgical success rates and minimize postoperative complications. Therefore, documenting Amyand's hernia in the radiology report plays a pivotal role in optimizing patient management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Mainstreaming patients with ovarian, endometrial, and colorectal cancer in the context of genetic testing at cancer diagnosis involves pre-test counseling, consent, and return of results by the clinical cancer team. This process uses significant clinician time and resources. Alternative implementation strategies might be more cost-efficient and better utilize limited cancer health professional and genetics workforce resources, but their efficacy is less well understood. To determine if direct-to-patient genetic testing for ovarian, endometrial, and colorectal cancer has equivalent uptake of genetic testing compared with mainstreaming. Patients at ovarian, endometrial, or colorectal cancer diagnosis have equivalent uptake for genetic testing through direct-to-patient compared with mainstreaming. A multicenter randomized controlled trial evaluating a digitally enabled direct-to-patient (saliva-based, at home) genetic testing approach (intervention arm) compared with mainstreaming genetic testing (control arm). After study consent and randomization, patients in the direct-to-patient arm are offered access to an app-based decision aid, consent to genetic testing via the app, and access to a helpline for additional support and counseling if needed. Control arm participants are offered routine mainstreaming genetic testing in the clinic. We include a qualitative sub-study of 1:1 interviews to understand the attitudes, experiences, and impact on emotional well-being of patients undergoing genetic testing. Inclusion criteria include diagnosis of ovarian, endometrial, or colorectal cancer fulfilling the National Health Service clinical genetic testing criteria. Exclusion criteria include prior genetic testing for or a known familial pathogenic variant in ovarian, endometrial, or colorectal cancer susceptibility genes. Absolute difference in uptake of genetic testing between arms in the intention-to-treat population, with equivalence determined using a 10% margin based on a 2-sided 95% confidence interval. Target n = 626 to 832 patients. We will test equivalence if ≥626 patients are recruited in the intention-to-treat population. Recruitment by December 2026 and publication of results in 2028. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment of multiple malignancies, yet durable clinical responses remain limited to a subset of patients. Accumulating evidence identifies the gut microbiome as a regulator of antitumour immunity that can influence treatment efficacy and toxicity through microbial metabolism, epithelial barrier integrity, inflammatory signalling, and host immune responses. This review critically evaluates the microbiome as both a predictive biomarker and therapeutic target in precision oncology. It moves beyond descriptive taxonomic associations by assessing emerging functional and mechanistic models that integrate microbial metabolites, ecological interactions, strain-level variation, and host-microbiome communication. Clinical and translational evidence from melanoma, non-small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, hepatocellular carcinoma, renal cell carcinoma, and urothelial carcinoma reveals marked differences in the reproducibility and clinical maturity of reported microbial signatures. Emerging microbiome-targeted strategies, including dietary modulation, faecal microbiota transplantation (FMT), live biotherapeutic products (LBPs), and defined microbial consortia, may enhance ICI responsiveness, with responder-derived FMT providing important early clinical proof of concept. However, inter-individual variability, donor-recipient compatibility, microbial engraftment, the lack of standardised analytical approaches, and unresolved safety and regulatory requirements continue to limit clinical translation. Pending prospective validation, reasonable clinical practice is to avoid unnecessary microbiome-disrupting antibiotics, systematically document diet and concomitant medications, evaluate FMT and LBPs within regulated clinical trials, and interpret microbiome profiles alongside established tumour and host biomarkers rather than as stand-alone tests. Current evidence therefore supports a cautious shift towards functional microbiome-guided precision oncology, providing a foundation for personalised strategies to improve cancer immunotherapy outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) screening reduces disease incidence and mortality through the detection and removal of precursor lesions and the earlier diagnosis of invasive cancer. However, most current programs remain predominantly age-based, applying broadly uniform tests and intervals to individuals whose underlying risk, lesion biology, screening adherence, and capacity to benefit may differ substantially. Advances in clinical prediction, molecular diagnostics, and artificial intelligence (AI) create opportunities to refine screening according to individual risk and clinical context. This narrative review examines the evolution of CRC screening from conventional population-based strategies toward a precision-screening framework comprising three complementary functions. Clinical risk stratification estimates background susceptibility using demographic, familial, behavioral, metabolic, medical, and previous-screening information. Molecular biomarkers provide biologically distinct information, ranging from inherited susceptibility to signals associated with prevalent colorectal neoplasia. AI may support multimodal risk integration, procedural lesion detection and characterization, and longitudinal reassessment as new clinical and screening information accumulates. These components should not be regarded as a mandatory sequential pathway or as interchangeable sources of evidence; rather, their value depends on the specific clinical question, predicted outcome, time horizon, and decision being supported. Current evidence shows that risk-adapted and multimodal approaches are feasible, but improved prediction or diagnostic performance does not necessarily translate into superior population outcomes. Most precision-screening strategies still lack prospective evidence demonstrating improvements in participation, diagnostic completion, advanced colorectal neoplasia yield, interval CRC, harms, resource use, equity, or cost-effectiveness compared with optimized established screening. The priority for translation is therefore not maximal technological integration, but selective use of additional information when it provides actionable incremental benefit while preserving the accessibility, effectiveness, and public-health strengths of organized screening.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Peptidylarginine deiminase 2 (PAD2) catalyzes protein citrullination and is implicated in inflammatory bowel disease and colorectal cancer. However, its role in regulating the intestinal epithelium and the influence of biological sex and the microbiome remain poorly defined. This study investigated the relationships among PAD2 deficiency, sex-divergent epithelial states, β-catenin regulation, and the intestinal microbiome. Global PAD2 knockout and wild-type littermate mice of both sexes were characterized under basal conditions and following dextran sodium sulfate-induced colitis. Intestinal epithelial phenotypes were assessed by histology, immunofluorescence, immunoblotting, quantitative RT-PCR, and immunoprecipitation. Gut microbial communities were evaluated by shotgun metagenomics, while broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment, fecal protein immunoblotting, and recombinant human PAD2 exposure in vitro were used to examine relationships among antibiotic-sensitive factors, β-catenin regulation, and epithelial phenotypes. PAD2 deficiency was associated with distinct epithelial states in male and female colons before injury. Male KO mice displayed increased β-catenin phosphorylation and increased susceptibility to DSS colitis, whereas female KO mice demonstrated increased total β-catenin abundance and preservation of structural epithelial features following injury. Female KO microbiota exhibited genotype-associated differences in microbial community composition by exploratory Bray-Curtis PERMANOVA. Broad-spectrum antibiotic treatment altered the female epithelial phenotype, reduced active β-catenin, and progressively depleted luminal PAD2-immunoreactive proteins. Exogenous recombinant human PAD2 increased epithelial protein citrullination and altered active β-catenin abundance in HT29 cells. Collectively, these findings demonstrate both sex-specific and sex-divergent colonic phenotypes while supporting a framework connecting PAD2 biology, epithelial architecture, and the microbial environment during intestinal maintenance and injury.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains the second most common cause of death in the United States. Morbidity and mortality of CRC are significantly reduced by early detection through colonoscopy, but rural screening rates are lower (and mortality rates higher) than urban rates. Understanding factors influencing screening adherence in rural populations is crucial for reducing disparities in cancer mortality. This study examines differences in out-of-pocket colonoscopy payment category between rural and urban populations. This cross-sectional study used data from the National Health Interview Survey 2019 and 2021. Our main exposure was rurality, and our main outcome was how much the individual paid out of pocket for the most recent colonoscopy: none, part, or all of the cost. We estimated a multinomial logistic regression model, adjusted for sociodemographic covariates. Rural residents were more likely than urban residents to report paying all of the cost (4.12% vs. 3.01%, p = 0.042). Sociodemographic covariates were differentially associated with out-of-pocket colonoscopy spending levels; compared to non-Hispanic whites, significantly more Hispanic individuals reported paying all of the cost (OR: 1.54, 95% CI: 1.03-2.30), and being uninsured or having other or unknown insurance status versus having private insurance was a strong predictor of higher out-of-pocket cost. We found a modest but statistically significant rural-urban difference in patient-reported out-of-pocket colonoscopy payment. Variation in patient financial responsibility may represent part of the broader access barriers experienced by rural populations. Initiatives directed towards reducing the financial burden of colonoscopies and improving access to alternative screening modalities may help reduce disparities and improve rural outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bulk T cell receptor (TCR) sequencing enables scalable immune repertoire profiling but does not measure the transcriptional states required to infer T cell functional programs. Paired single-cell RNA/TCR sequencing offers a single-cell functional prior by jointly observing TCR identity and transcriptomic states. However, transferring this prior to bulk repertoires is challenging: sparse and noisy single-cell profiles can distort the functional reference, and the probabilistic relationship between TCR identity and transcriptome-inferred functional state makes direct cell-level alignment unstable, potentially biasing repertoire-level functional composition estimation. We present scMAC, a single-cell-guided framework for functional context completion that infers TCR functional representations reflecting transcriptome-derived T-cell states. scMAC builds a denoised functional reference by integrating multi-scale expression modeling with gene-semantic priors derived from large language model encodings of gene and protein descriptions, improving gene-level functional coherence. It then learns a prototype-guided TCR-to-function mapping that combines paired cell-level latent alignment with functional prototype regularization, enabling robust repertoire-level functional composition estimation. Across real single-cell and paired RNA/TCR datasets, scMAC outperformed existing single-cell representation methods in fine-grained cell-state representation, gene functional consistency, expression recovery, and disease-relevant pathway analysis, achieving an adjusted Rand index of 0.656 on a colorectal cancer dataset with 83 cell subtypes. For repertoire-level functional composition estimation, scMAC closely matched single-cell-derived functional proportions, with an R2 of 0.979 and a Bray-Curtis distance of 0.075. These results support scMAC as a practical route for transferring single-cell-derived functional knowledge to bulk TCR repertoire analysis beyond clonotype identity and clonal abundance. scMAC is publicly available at https://github.com/Bioinformatics7181/scMAC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Anastomotic leak (AL) is a serious complication following colorectal cancer (CRC) resection. Its influence on long-term oncologic outcomes, including recurrence and survival, remains controversial. This retrospective cohort study aimed to evaluate the prevalence of AL following CRC resection with anastomosis for stage 1-3 CRC. Clinical, operative, oncologic, and follow-up data were collected. AL was diagnosed within 30 days postoperatively. Primary outcomes included recurrence and mortality. A total of 204 patients were included, of whom 25 (12.3%) developed AL. CRC recurrence occurred in 28.0% of patients with AL compared with 24.6% without AL ( AL following CRC resection was associated with earlier mortality and a trend toward earlier recurrence, although no independent association with long-term oncologic outcomes was demonstrated. A larger prospective study with standardized leak definitions would better clarify the relationships between AL and CRC outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Severe constipation may cause profound disability despite daily bowel movements. Surgical decision-making is particularly challenging when gastrointestinal dysmotility coexists with neuromuscular disease and impaired functional independence. A 60-year-old man with Charcot-Marie-Tooth (CMT) disease type 2 and wheelchair dependence spent four to five hours per day toileting despite osmotic laxatives and intermittent enemas. His distress and loss of independence had led him to seek access to voluntary assisted dying (VAD) services. Colonoscopy identified no obstructing colorectal lesion. Whole-gut transit testing showed preserved proximal transit, delayed colonic transit, and possible delayed rectal emptying. Formal anorectal physiology testing was not completed. Following shared decision-making with the patient, family, colorectal surgeons, and stomal therapy clinicians, he underwent laparoscopic loop ileostomy on April 2, 2026. Laparoscopy demonstrated minor omental adhesions, caecal adherence to the right abdominal wall, and dilated, flaccid bowel with reduced tone but some residual peristaltic activity. Early recovery included urinary retention. Ileostomy output decreased from 1.8 to 0.9 L/day after loperamide and psyllium were commenced. By postoperative day seven, he had changed his own appliance and was medically ready for discharge, pending stomal therapy clearance. At two months, he reported independent stoma management, bowel care taking minutes, and improved daily function and quality of life. Slow-transit constipation and colonic inertia should not be treated as interchangeable diagnoses or as evidence of a specific neuromuscular lesion. Loop ileostomy may offer a potentially reversible diagnostic and therapeutic trial when the benefit of colectomy is uncertain, although longer-term follow-up is needed to assess its durable benefit.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Despite advances in systemic therapy, pulmonary metastasectomy remains a key option for selected patients with metastatic solid tumors, offering long-term survival. Prognosis is influenced by many factors including disease-free interval and metastatic burden. This study evaluates survival outcomes and prognostic factors in a mixed-tumor cohort from a Middle Eastern tertiary cancer center. This retrospective cohort study included all patients who underwent pulmonary metastasectomy for solid tumors at King Hussein Cancer Center between October 2014 and December 2024. Demographic, clinical, imaging, surgical, pathological, and follow-up data were collected from electronic medical records. Overall survival (OS) and pulmonary recurrence-free survival (P-RFS) were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, and prognostic factors were assessed using Cox proportional hazards models. Analyses were performed using SPSS version 27. A total of 236 patients underwent 371 procedures. The mean follow-up was 31.9 months (95% CI:28.3-35.3). Median OS was 3.99 years (95% CI:2.69-5.28), with a 5-year OS rate of 42.0%. Mean P-RFS was 6.81 years (95% CI: 6.16-7.46), with the median not reached. On univariable analysis, worse OS was associated with metastatic lesion size ≥ 3 cm, bilateral metastases, thoracotomy, longer hospital stay, and increased tumor burden. R0 resection and DFI ≥ 12 months were protective. In multivariable analysis, independent predictors of worse OS were metastatic lesion size ≥ 3 cm (HR: 1.827, p = 0.015) and DFI < 12 months (HR for ≥ 12 months: 0.515, p = 0.002). Patients with colorectal cancer demonstrated numerically longer overall survival and lower pulmonary recurrence rates than patients with sarcoma (5-year OS: 44.8% vs. 32.2%; pulmonary recurrence: 18.8% vs. 34.4%). However, tumor type was not significantly associated with overall survival in univariable Cox regression analysis. Pulmonary metastasectomy is an important treatment option for patients with lung metastasis from different solid tumors that provides durable long-term and pulmonary recurrence-free survival in appropriately selected patients. Longer DFI and smaller metastatic lesion size independently predict improved outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) polarized toward an M2-like phenotype are critical drivers of immunosuppression in colorectal cancer (CRC). While Vasorin (VASN) is implicated in poor prognosis, its specific role in orchestrating the tumor immune microenvironment remains elusive. VASN expression and immune infiltration were analyzed using TCGA transcriptomics and single-cell transcriptomics, validated via immunohistochemistry and immunofluorescence in CRC patient cohorts. Molecular interactions were delineated utilizing chromatin immunoprecipitation (ChIP), dual-luciferase reporter assays, and genetic rescue strategies. In vivo, VASN promoted tumor growth and suppressed CD8 This study identifies a novel VASN-YAP-MYL9 axis that reprograms macrophages to mediate immune escape. These findings broaden our understanding of CRC immune evasion and provide a rational framework for targeting VASN to remodel the immunosuppressive microenvironment and augment therapeutic efficacy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Since 2022, the "13 en Santé" health mediation program has been implemented in Marseille, France, to reduce social health inequalities, in socioeconomically disadvantage neighbourhoods, with a particular emphasis on promoting participation in population-based organised cancer screening programs. Led by multidisciplinary teams including health mediators, nurses, coordinators, and volunteers, the intervention is structured around three core components: (i) territory exploration to develop knowledge of local communities and resources; (ii) culturally appropriate health education delivered through outreach activities to reach underserved populations; and (iii) individualised navigation support tailored to needs and level of autonomy. This study evaluates the effectiveness of this program in promoting breast, colorectal, and cervical cancer screening. A controlled before-after design based on two cross-sectional knowledge-attitude-practice surveys was conducted in 2022 and 2024 in intervention or control neighbourhoods. Individuals aged 18-74 were randomly selected and interviewed via door-to-door questionnaires. Weighting was applied to account for stratified sampling and to align age and sex distributions with census data. For each cancer, weighted logistic regression models assessed associations between health mediation exposure and screening uptake and awareness at both individual and population levels. Overall, 4,523 individuals were included across the two cross-sectional surveys. The program successfully reached individuals facing cumulative socioeconomic barriers to healthcare access. No significant population-level association was observed between health mediation and cancer screening uptake or awareness. At the individual level, declared exposure to health mediation was associated with significantly higher uptakes of breast and colorectal cancer screenings (breast: 74% vs. 54%, OR = 2.3 [1.1-4.5]; colorectal: 50% vs. 30%, OR = 2.8 [1.3-5.8]). In addition, colorectal cancer screening awareness was significantly higher among exposed participants (93% vs. 83%, OR = 8.1 [2.1-31]). This study provides the first evidence that reported individual exposure to a multicomponent health mediation intervention was significantly associated with an important increase in breast and colorectal cancer screening uptake in disadvantaged European neighbourhoods. Although the limitations of this observational study preclude causal conclusions regarding the intervention's effectiveness, these findings suggest that health mediation may be a promising strategy for reducing inequalities in cancer prevention and warrant further investigation. It also highlights screening-specific mechanisms of action that should be considered to further optimise intervention effectiveness.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Reliable tumor origin assessment from routinely archived specimens remains challenging, particularly for diagnostically ambiguous liver malignancies. Although formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded (FFPE) tissues are widely available, deep and quantitative site-specific N-glycoproteomics of these specimens is limited by formaldehyde-induced crosslinking and incomplete peptide recovery. We developed GlyFFPE, a quantitative platform for site-specific N-glycosylation profiling from FFPE archival tissues, and applied it to discovery and independent verification datasets from colorectal cancer liver metastasis (CRLM) and liver hepatocellular carcinoma (LIHC) patients. We then integrated glyco-signatures with clinicopathological variables using an ensemble machine-learning classifier and evaluated performance in a temporal validation cohort. Model robustness and incremental value were assessed using a pathology-only comparator, repeated nested cross-validation, feature-selection stability analysis, and a same-institution temporal cohort. GlyFFPE enabled deep site-specific N-glycoproteome profiling from FFPE tissues and revealed metastasis-associated glyco-signatures characterized by elevated levels of high-mannose glycans on cell-adhesion molecules, prominently CEACAM1 and CEACAM5. The two-glycopeptide panel from CEACAM high-mannose signature showed modest discrimination between CRLM and LIHC in an independent TMT-PRM verification cohort (AUC = 0.73), indicating the need of expanding the targeted panel. The model integrating glyco-signatures with clinicopathological variables substantially improved diagnostic performance, achieving glycoproteomic-assisted discrimination in a same-institution temporal cohort. Repeated nested cross-validation provided a more conservative performance estimate with a mean AUC of 0.92 and a mean AUPRC of 0.96. Feature-selection analysis identified repeatedly selected molecular features, although moderate feature-set variability remained because of the limited cohort size. In addition to classification, GlyFFPE revealed metastasis-associated glycosylation remodeling, including increased high-mannose occupancy on alpha-1-acid glycoprotein 1 (ORM1) and coordinated alterations in extracellular matrix-associated glycoproteins. GlyFFPE establishes an FFPE-compatible workflow for site-specific N-glycosylation profiling and identifies candidate molecular signatures that complement routine pathological assessment for tumor origin evaluation in challenging liver malignancies. Given the modest cohort size and the same-institution temporal evaluation, multicenter, blinded external validation are required before clinical implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Concurrent systemic chemotherapy and local radiotherapy represent the clinical standard of care for a broad spectrum of malignant tumors, and these modalities can elicit endogenous anti-tumor immune responses. However, the hypoxic tumor microenvironment (TME) of solid tumors severely impairs the therapeutic efficacy of chemotherapy, radiotherapy, and immunotherapy, leading to treatment failure and tumor progression. We engineered a platinum-osmium hybrid nanozyme (PO) via the self-assembly of an oxaliplatin (Oxa) prodrug, osmium, and polyvinylpyrrolidone, which potentiates the synergy of combined therapy through cascade catalytic reactions. PO exhibits catalase-like activity to decompose endogenous hydrogen peroxide into oxygen, thereby reversing tumor hypoxia, and glutathione peroxidase-like activity to deplete intracellular glutathione, which synergistically augments the efficacy of chemotherapy and radiotherapy. Under the reductive TME, PO is activated to release bioactive Oxa, in conjunction with osmium-mediated radiosensitization, PO induces severe DNA damage, activates the cyclic GMP-AMP synthase-stimulator of interferon genes pathway, and triggers robust immunogenic cell death, thus eliciting a systemic anti-tumor immune response. Furthermore, PO modulates the expression of metastasis-associated epithelial-mesenchymal transition proteins to inhibit tumor invasion and metastasis. Both in vitro and in vivo studies demonstrate that PO exerts superior therapeutic efficacy against metastatic colorectal cancer compared with free Oxa. Notably, the biodegradable nature of PO minimizes systemic toxicity and ensures favorable biocompatibility. This work presents a degradable hybrid nanozyme strategy that integrates chemotherapeutic, radiosensitizing, and immunomodulatory functions to overcome the hypoxic TME barrier, thus improving the therapeutic outcome of hypoxic and metastatic colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a growing public health concern in Palestine, yet limited evidence is available on locally relevant behavioral, dietary, socioeconomic, and contextual predictors. Machine learning (ML) may support prevention-oriented risk stratification by identifying complex predictive patterns among potentially modifiable factors. This study aimed to identify important predictors of CRC among Palestinian adults and evaluate ML models for CRC classification after excluding screening-related variables. A case-control dataset of 216 participants was analyzed, including 108 CRC cases and 108 cancer-free controls. Initially, 57 variables were reviewed, and 39 candidate predictors were retained after excluding non-modifiable variables and the outcome. Screening-related variables, including previous colonoscopy and fecal occult blood testing, were excluded from the primary modeling analysis because they may reflect diagnostic workup, screening access, or healthcare utilization. Multiple feature-selection methods were evaluated, including filter, wrapper, embedded, and hybrid approaches. Ten optimized ML classifiers were trained and internally validated using stratified 5-fold nested cross-validation, with preprocessing, feature selection, hyperparameter optimization, and model training performed within the training folds. Model performance was assessed using accuracy, AUC, sensitivity, specificity, F1-score, and Matthews correlation coefficient. SHAP analysis was used to interpret the optimized Ensemble models following hybrid feature selection. After excluding screening-related variables, the best model-combination performance was achieved by Forward Selection with the Ensemble classifier, with an accuracy of 90.3% ± 4.3, a balanced accuracy of 90.28%, a sensitivity of 89.81% ± 5.59, and a specificity of 90.74% ± 4.18. Hybrid feature-selection approaches also showed competitive performance with Ensemble learning. Hybrid LASSO + GA with Ensemble and Hybrid mRMR + PSO with Ensemble both achieved a balanced accuracy of 89.81%. SHAP analysis consistently identified physical activity as the most influential predictor, followed by dietary, socioeconomic, and contextual variables, including fruit consumption frequency, yearly income, occupation, and place of residence. After excluding screening-related variables, ML models that relied on lifestyle, socioeconomic, and contextual predictors showed promising internal validation performance in classifying CRC among Palestinian adults. Hybrid feature-selection methods combined with Ensemble learning represent promising candidate pipelines for future validation. However, the findings remain exploratory and require external validation in larger, independent cohorts before clinical or public health implementation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal carcinoma is rare in children and adolescents, and it usually presents with non-specific signs and symptoms, leading to delayed diagnosis and poor prognosis. Based on postoperative histopathological findings, this study examines the clinical features and computed tomography (CT) imaging presentations of colorectal cancer in pediatric patients, aiming to enhance radiologists' recognition of pediatric colorectal carcinoma, thereby providing a reliable imaging reference to support clinicians in the diagnostic decision-making process. Nine cases of colorectal cancer confirmed by surgical pathology in our hospitals from January 2013 to June 2025 were collected. All patients underwent multi-slice spiral CT plain and enhanced scans before surgery. The clinical information of the children was analyzed by reviewing the hospital's electronic medical record system, and the CT imaging findings were retrospectively compared with the surgical pathology. Four of nine patients were diagnosed with poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma, two with poorly differentiated adenocarcinoma combined with signet ring cell carcinoma, two with mucinous adenocarcinoma combined with signet ring cell carcinoma, and other one with signet ring cell carcinoma. One of nine cases had liver metastasis and one case had metastasis to the left ovary. CT scans show that the main manifestations of intestinal lesions are focal wall thickening, accompanied by varying degrees of luminal narrowing, infiltration of surrounding tissues, heterogeneously enhancing lesion with mucosal hyperenhancement and discontinuity. Multi-slice spiral CT demonstrates potential value in the preoperative diagnosis and staging of colorectal cancer in children. By integrating the pathological basis of the tumor and highlighting its significant CT imaging features, it is helpful to enhance the accuracy of radiologists' diagnosis of this disease, and provide reliable imaging evidence for clinicians to make a clear diagnosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study evaluates the clinical utility of combined SDC2 and ADHFE1 methylation analysis for colorectal cancer (CRC) detection using a methylation-sensitive restriction endonuclease (MSRE)-based assay. Leveraging the specificity of MSRE, we developed a streamlined amplification assay that directly analyzes methylation status of SDC2 and ADHFE1 after mixing nucleic acids with PCR reagent. A cohort of 274 participants was stratified into six groups: CRC (n = 117), advanced adenoma (AA, n = 22), polyps (n = 30), intestinal disease control (IDC, n = 39), other gastrointestinal disease control (OGDC, n = 24), and healthy controls (HC, n = 42). SDC2 and ADHFE1 methylation levels in fecal samples were assessed, and diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis. The CRC group exhibited significantly higher SDC2 and ADHFE1 methylation positivity rates compared to all comparator groups, including AA, polyps, IDC, OGDC, and HC (P < 0.01). No significant differences were observed in the methylation positivity rates of SDC2, ADHFE1 or their combination across different TNM stages and levels of tumor differentiation. Joint SDC2 and ADHFE1 analysis increased sensitivity for CRC detection to 82.9% (vs. 64.1% and 65.0% for ADHFE1 and SDC2) with an AUC of 0.865 (95% CI: 0.817-0.913). For early-stage CRC (stages I + II), the dual-gene panel achieved an AUC of 0.872. However, the ability to discriminate between AA and HC (AUC: 0.693) or IDC (AUC: 0.615) remained limited in our dual-gene assay. The combined SDC2/ADHFE1 MSRE-based assay significantly improves diagnostic sensitivity for CRC, demonstrating superior differentiation of CRC from benign intestinal pathologies and precancerous lesions (AA and polyps). This non-invasive approach shows promise as a supplementary tool for CRC screening.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) has been proven to be related to the prognosis of cancer. Nevertheless, there are very few studies on the prognostic significance of CTCs in colorectal cancer (CRC). In this study, we investigated the impact and clinical significance of the number of circulating tumor cells (CTCs) and the expression of glioma-associated oncogene 1 (Gli1) on the prognosis of colorectal cancer (CRC). This study encompassed a total of 310 colorectal cancer patients who had not received radiotherapy or chemotherapy. Simultaneously, the circulating tumor cells of these 310 patients were isolated and enumerated. The expression of Gli1 in circulating tumor cells (CTCs) was determined by in situ hybridization with RNA (RNA-ISH) method. The results were analyzed in combination with the clinical and pathological parameters of the patients as well as their treatment outcomes. Survival analysis was also conducted to determine its prognostic significance. Gli1 expression was found in 23.15% patients at baseline. Patients with Gli1 expression had significantly poorer treatment response and metastasis. Besides, Gli1 on CTCs was an independent prognostic indicator for poorer progression-free survival and overall survival. The study demonstrated that Gli1 expression and CTC count are promising prognostic indicators in patients with CRC. Further studies are needed to clarify the value of integrating the indicator with current clinical strategies in improving the survival of CRC patients.
