ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitors (VEGFIs) are essential for the treatment of metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Given the ineffectiveness of epidermal growth factor receptor inhibitors in managing RAS-mutant mCRC, long-term VEGFI therapy is often required; however, it is associated with an increased risk of proteinuria. As the use of VEGFI in later-line mCRC treatment has become more prevalent, proteinuria has emerged as a critical dose-limiting toxicity. However, its effect on the treatment outcomes remains unclear. This study examined the incidence of proteinuria during extended VEGFI use and its effect on overall survival (OS) in RAS-mutant mCRC. This single-center retrospective study analyzed patients with RAS-mutant stage IV mCRC treated with first-line VEGFIs at Gifu University Hospital. Proteinuria incidence was estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. OS from a 12-month landmark was compared according to the occurrence of dipstick proteinuria 2+ or greater within the first year using Cox regression. Among 185 patients, the Kaplan-Meier cumulative incidence of dipstick proteinuria 2+ or greater was 11%, 37%, and 45% at 1, 2, and 3 years, respectively. Of 123 patients in the 12-month landmark cohort, 13 had early-onset proteinuria. The age- and sex-adjusted HR for subsequent mortality was 1.81 (95% CI 0.84-3.86; p = 0.128). Proteinuria accumulated during extended VEGFI therapy. Early-onset proteinuria may be associated with poorer subsequent OS, although the wide confidence interval precludes a definitive conclusion. These findings underscore the importance of careful proteinuria monitoring during long-term VEGFI treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Surgical treatment remains an essential component in the management of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) despite advances in medical therapy. Although minimally invasive surgery is preferred, technical challenges related to chronic inflammation and altered anatomy may limit laparoscopic approaches. Robotic surgery has been increasingly adopted, but its role in IBD surgery remains to be clearly defined. To synthesize the available evidence on the feasibility, safety, and perioperative outcomes of robotic surgery in patients with IBD. A systematic review was conducted according to PRISMA guidelines. Studies were identified through an electronic search of the PubMed database for reports evaluating outcomes of robotic surgery in IBD. Eligible studies included case series, comparative studies, and systematic reviews published in English. Primary outcomes were conversion to open surgery and postoperative complications; secondary outcomes included operative time, length of stay (LOS), reoperation, readmission, and anastomotic leak. Thirty-four studies were included. Robotic surgery was consistently associated with longer operative time. However, postoperative morbidity, major complications, anastomotic leak, reoperation, and mortality rates were comparable between techniques. Robotic approaches demonstrated lower and favorable conversion rates, particularly in complex inflammatory phenotypes or pelvic procedures. Length of stay and estimated blood loss were similar or numerically lower in several robotic cohorts. Robotic surgery is a safe and feasible minimally invasive approach for IBD patients, with perioperative outcomes comparable to conventional surgery. Its potential advantages may be most relevant in complex or technically demanding cases, although high-quality prospective studies are needed to better define its role.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Metastatic colon cancer commonly exhibits resistance to ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation. However, the mechanisms linking metabolic regulation to ferroptosis during metastatic progression remain incompletely understood. Here, we identified fatty acid-binding protein 2 (FABP2) as a regulator associated with ferroptosis sensitivity and liver metastatic phenotypes in colon cancer. Multi-omics analyses of clinical specimens showed reduced FABP2 expression in advanced colon cancer, which was associated with metastatic progression and poor survival. Mechanistically, FABP2 interacted with β-catenin, altered its intracellular localization, and was associated with reduced β-catenin/TCF4-dependent transcription of glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4), a key regulator of ferroptosis resistance. FABP2 overexpression increased ferroptosis sensitivity, whereas FABP2 downregulation promoted GPX4-dependent ferroptosis evasion and metastatic phenotypes. Pharmacological inhibition of Wnt/β-catenin signaling or GPX4 activity partially attenuated the effects of FABP2 loss. Together, these findings identify FABP2 as a factor associated with ferroptosis regulation and metastatic progression in colon cancer, and provide additional insight into the interplay between lipid metabolism, Wnt/β-catenin signaling, and ferroptosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although cancer patients have a high burden of mental illness, it is less clear whether patients with mental illness experience a higher-than-expected cancer risk. This systematic review investigated the associations between a wide range of types of mental illness and subsequent cancer risk. Five electronic databases were searched for articles published from database initiation to October 24, 2024. Studies using nationwide Nordic register data to conduct a prospective analysis of the association between mental illness diagnosis and cancer incidence were included. When data from three or more countries were available for a given type of mental illness, random effects meta-analyses were performed; otherwise, narrative syntheses were conducted. A total of 7,767 non-duplicate articles were screened, of which 20 were included. Meta-analyses showed no association between schizophrenia diagnosis and overall cancer risk; however, a high level of heterogeneity was detected between studies. Individuals with schizophrenia appeared to have a higher risk of breast cancer (pooled standardized incidence ratio [SIR]: 1.28, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 1.08-1.52), and lower risks of rectal cancer (pooled SIR: 0.75, 95% CI: 0.59-0.95) and prostate cancer (pooled SIR: 0.53, 95% CI: 0.48-0.59), compared to individuals in the general population. A higher risk of overall cancer was observed for mood, anxiety, and stress-related disorders, as well as autism and intellectual disability, in multiple studies; however, the results differed by cancer types and sex. In summary, these findings suggest an altered risk of cancer among individuals with mental illness living in Nordic countries. Further research is needed to enable the development of targeted cancer prevention strategies to reduce mental health disparities in cancer protection.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
As one of the most common types of malignant brain tumors, brain metastases are associated with poor clinical outcomes. Lung cancer, breast cancer, colorectal cancer, and renal cell carcinoma are the most frequent primary tumors causing brain metastases. This study explores the clinicopathological characteristics and diagnostic challenges of brain metastases from rare tumors to provide references for clinical diagnosis and treatment. This study retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 14 patients with brain metastases originating from rare tumors, treated from 2013 to 2025. The data included primary tumor pathological types and follow-up records, supplemented by a literature review. Among the 14 patients, the primary tumor types included 3 cases of ovarian serous carcinoma, 3 cases of papillary thyroid carcinoma, 2 cases of hepatocellular carcinoma, 2 cases of urothelial carcinoma, 1 case of breast rhabdomyosarcoma, 1 case of uterine leiomyosarcoma, 1 case of penile squamous cell carcinoma, and 1 case of prostate adenocarcinoma. The median age was 62.9 years, and the average maximum tumor diameter was 4.7 cm. Common symptoms included headache and limb weakness. Pathological immunohistochemical analysis revealed key markers such as WT-1, TG, hepPar-1, GATA3, NKX3.1, caldesmon, MyoD1, and P40 were positive staining. Brain metastases from rare tumors lack specific clinical manifestations, and definitive diagnosis relies on pathology and immunohistochemistry. Multidisciplinary comprehensive treatment may improve prognosis, but overall survival rates remain low, necessitating further exploration of novel strategies such as targeted therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Enterobacteria harboring the polyketide synthase (pks) island (clbA-clbS), which encodes colibactin (pks⁺ enterobacteria), is a putative risk factor for colorectal cancer. Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) is the current standard for detection. Primer-independent shotgun metagenomic sequencing (SMS) is increasingly used; however, thresholds and analysis parameters for identifying pks⁺ enterobacteria remain unstandardized. This study aimed to evaluate how accurately SMS can reproduce PCR-defined pks⁺ status and identify practical cutoffs by analyzing fecal samples from 223 healthy adults in a Japanese cohort. PCR identified 60/223 (26.9%) participants as pks⁺. SMS detected at least one clb gene in 85/223 (38.1%) at ≥ 90% identity; 49 of these agreed with PCR positives. Among the single-gene rules, clbB yielded the best discrimination (area under the curve (AUC) = 0.826) across 70-90% identity. The total-read rule across 19 clb genes performed best overall (AUC = 0.838), with higher AUCs above the 60% threshold (all p ≤ 0.045). The rule requiring detection of at least eight clb genes was inferior (AUC = 0.734-0.773). Detection performance depended on gene length; longer clb genes (> 1,500 amino acids) achieved higher accuracy (AUC ≥ 0.800). Optimized SMS can reproduce PCR-based detection of pks⁺ enterobacteria in feces with high accuracy. clbB and a cluster-level rule aggregating reads across clbA-clbS are effective, although tightening the sequence-identity threshold did not consistently improve performance. The standardized criteria proposed here enable cross-study comparability and may accelerate epidemiologic assessment of pks⁺ enterobacteria and its clinical translation for colorectal cancer prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Although anastomotic level after low anterior resection (LAR) for rectal cancer is largely determined by tumor location, its relationship with postoperative bowel function and quality of life remains clinically important. This study compared functional outcomes, fecal continence, sexual function, and health-related quality of life between patients undergoing colorectal anastomosis (CRA) and coloanal anastomosis (CAA) after curative-intent LAR. This retrospective cohort study included 126 patients who underwent LAR for rectal cancer between January 2019 and June 2024 (CRA, n = 84; CAA, n = 42). Health-related quality of life was assessed using the EORTC QLQ-C30 and QLQ-CR29 questionnaires, fecal continence using the Wexner score, and fecal incontinence-related quality of life using the FIQL scale in patients with Wexner scores > 8. Firth penalized logistic regression and multivariable linear regression were used to evaluate clinically significant fecal incontinence, Wexner scores, and selected EORTC domains, adjusting for age, sex, tumor level, neoadjuvant radiotherapy, diverting stoma, and time since surgery. Global health status was comparable between groups. In unadjusted analyses, the CAA group had higher stool frequency, flatulence, and embarrassment scores and a higher prevalence of clinically significant fecal incontinence than the CRA group (28.6% vs. 8.3%; p = 0.004). After adjustment, anastomosis type was not independently associated with clinically significant fecal incontinence (adjusted odds ratio, 2.30; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.56-13.40; p = 0.261), Wexner score (adjusted β, 0.04; 95% CI, - 3.69 to 3.76; p = 0.984), global health status, or selected EORTC domains. No adjusted EORTC association remained significant after false discovery rate correction. Diverting stoma formation was independently associated with a higher Wexner score (adjusted β, 2.28; 95% CI, 0.61-3.95; p = 0.007). Sexual function did not differ significantly between groups. Although patients undergoing CAA had worse bowel function in unadjusted comparisons, these differences were not independently attributable to anastomosis type after adjustment for relevant clinical and treatment-related factors. Global quality of life was comparable between groups. Postoperative functional outcomes after rectal cancer surgery appear multifactorial and should not be attributed to anastomosis type alone.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Quantitative faecal immunochemical test (FIT) is a simple triage tool to stratify patients with suspected colorectal cancer. The aim of this audit is to evaluate the colorectal referrals from primary care to the Urgent Suspected Cancer (USC) pathway in our health board. A pre-interventional cycle was conducted from January to March 2024. Subsequently, FIT letter was introduced. Following its implementation, a follow up cycle was carried out to evaluate its effectiveness in guiding referrals for patients with suspected colorectal cancer from April to June 2024. The referrals were compared against NICE guideline DG56 "Quantitative faecal immunochemical testing to guide colorectal cancer pathway referral in primary care". In the pre-intervention cycle, there are a total of 870 referrals through the USC pathway, of which only 456 (52.4%) referrals were accompanied with FIT test. A FIT letter was introduced to streamline the USC pathway and ensure that USC outpatient slots were used appropriately. After implementation, there are a total of 748 referrals, with 430 (57.5%) referrals with FIT test. This demonstrated an improvement of 5.1% compared to the pre-intervention ( This closed loop audit demonstrated a significant improvement in appropriate colorectal cancer referrals from primary care to the USC pathway. This intervention enhanced the prioritisation of USC referrals, decreased delays and ensured more appropriate use of outpatient appointment slots.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
One of the main causes of cancer-related death globally, colorectal cancer (CRC), is becoming more common in emerging nations. CRC morbidity and death are considerably decreased by effective screening. Family doctors are essential to the implementation of CRC screening. To assess the knowledge, attitudes, practices (KAP), and perceived barriers related to CRC screening among family physicians working in the Riyadh second health cluster. In 2025, board-certified family doctors in Saudi Arabia's Riyadh second health cluster participated in a cross-sectional questionnaire-based survey. A validated self-administered computerized questionnaire covering demographics, KAP, and perceived barriers to CRC screening was used to gather data. A total of 98 physicians participated. Most physicians demonstrated poor knowledge (82.7%) and poor screening practices (82.7%), despite generally positive attitudes toward CRC screening (56.1%). Formal training was significantly associated with better knowledge and attitudes. Patient-related barriers included fear of diagnosis and lack of awareness, while lack of time was the most prominent physician-related barrier. System-related barriers included long waiting times and a lack of patient education tools. Attitude was significantly associated with both knowledge and practice, and a strong positive correlation was observed between attitude and practice scores ( Despite the fact that family doctors showed favorable sentiments regarding CRC screening, there are still significant knowledge and practice gaps. Implementing CRC screening may be improved by addressing time constraints, improving physician training, and bolstering system-level support.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy is a standard treatment for locally advanced rectal cancer, yet acquired resistance limits durable tumor control. Whether stress-adaptive acetyl-group metabolism contributes to this resistance remains unclear. We performed a genome-wide CRISPR-Cas9 loss-of-function screen under fractionated irradiation and integrated the results with transcriptomic and proteomic profiling of radioresistant colorectal cancer models established by stepwise irradiation. CRAT function was interrogated using genetic perturbation, catalytic-dead reconstitution, acetylation-mimetic p65 rescue, RELA depletion, stable-isotope tracing, free coenzyme A quantification, NF-κB reporter assays, chromatin immunoprecipitation-qPCR, and xenograft and syngeneic tumor models. CRAT was prioritized through cross-platform convergence of the CRISPR screen with transcriptomic and proteomic signatures of radioresistant cells, and post-treatment tumors with poorer pathological regression showed higher CRAT and nuclear p65 immunohistochemical scores. CRAT manipulation had limited, model-dependent effects on basal proliferation but more pronounced effects after irradiation, where CRAT loss reduced clonogenic survival and was associated with increased oxidative stress and persistent DNA damage. Stable-isotope tracing showed that irradiation increased acetate-to-acetylcarnitine flux and expanded the free coenzyme A pool in control cells, whereas CRAT loss disrupted this acetyl-group buffering. Mechanistically, CRAT catalytic activity helped maintain irradiation-induced p65 Lys310 acetylation, H3K27ac enrichment at NF-κB-responsive loci, and NF-κB-associated transcriptional output through a p300/CBP-sensitive acetylation axis. p65-K310Q rescue and RELA depletion supported p65 acetylation and RELA-dependent transcription as downstream contributors to, rather than sole mediators of, CRAT-dependent radioprotection. In syngeneic MC38 tumors, Crat deletion enhanced the response to fractionated radiotherapy. These findings support CRAT-dependent acetyl-group metabolism as a contributor to an NF-κB-associated radioprotective program and nominate this metabolic dependency as a candidate vulnerability for radiosensitization in colorectal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Peritoneal surface malignancies (PSM) are primary or secondary neoplastic deposits involving the peritoneum and are commonly associated with colorectal, gastric, appendiceal, gynecological, pancreaticobiliary, and other intra-abdominal or extra-abdominal cancers. Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is one of the most frequent and clinically consequential emergency presentations in this population, yet diagnostic and therapeutic pathways remain heterogeneous. We aimed to develop evidence-informed recommendations for emergency management of MBO in patients with PSM by integrating a systematic review, meta-analysis and a structured international expert consensus process. This systematic review, meta-analysis, and Delphi consensus followed PRISMA, Cochrane, and relevant MOOSE reporting principles. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 2025 (English language). Five predefined PICO/PIRT questions addressed: (1) the diagnostic role of CT, plain abdominal X-ray, or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; (2) nonoperative medical management versus surgical or endoscopic therapy; (3) surgical versus endoscopic treatment after failure of nonoperative management; (4) bowel resection versus stoma or bypass in surgical candidates; and (5) endoscopic stenting versus endoscopic ultrasound-guided bypass with lumen-apposing metal stents in endoscopic candidates. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and MINORS for non-comparative studies; certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses (REML) produced odds ratios (OR), mean differences (MD), pooled means, or pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was summarized using I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. Evidence profiles informed statements voted on by the WSES-PSOGI-SICO expert panel during the 2025 WSES Congress. No comparative diagnostic study evaluated abdominal X-ray or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; two small retrospective CT-based series supported contrast-enhanced CT for mapping obstruction and excluding urgent complications, but no diagnostic meta-analysis was possible. For medical versus procedural treatment, medical management was associated with lower morbidity (OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.07-0.39) and shorter length of stay (MD - 9.48 days, 95% CI - 12.65 to -6.32), while success, mortality, and overall survival remained inconclusive. For surgery versus endoscopy, surgery showed higher clinical success (OR 2.57, 95% CI 1.47-4.50), whereas endoscopy shortened hospital stay (MD 3.35 days, 95% CI 1.46-5.23); mortality did not differ (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.70-1.49). Among surgical options, resection showed a signal toward higher perioperative mortality than bypass or ostomy (OR 3.55, 95% CI 1.45-8.68). Endoscopic stenting showed a pooled clinical success rate of 0.71 (95% CI 0.62-0.79), whereas evidence on LAMS was limited to one retrospective study. All guideline statements reached 100% agreement among voting participants. Despite the low certainty of available evidence, integration of systematic review findings with expert consensus provides a structured international framework to support decision-making in emergency presentations of PSM-related MBO. These consensus-based recommendations are intended to assist clinicians in harmonizing care across peripheral and referral hospitals, while emphasizing individualized multidisciplinary judgement and the need for future higher-quality evidence.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The tumour immune microenvironment shapes colorectal cancer progression and therapeutic vulnerability, but host metabolic programmes linked to immune-inflamed tumour states remain incompletely defined. Microbiome-derived and postbiotic-related metabolites influence epithelial, stromal and immune signalling, yet their downstream tumour transcriptomic readouts have rarely been assessed as host-side indicators of immune microenvironment state. Four mechanistically defined postbiotic-related host axes were curated: short-chain fatty acid, tryptophan/AhR, polyamine and ferroptosis/redox. Axis scores were calculated as mean z-standardized expression of curated genes in TCGA colorectal cancers and evaluated in GSE39582. Associations with marker-based immune/stromal signatures, microsatellite instability, cytolytic activity, stage and overall survival were tested using Spearman correlations, Wilcoxon tests and Cox models with false-discovery-rate correction. In TCGA, the tryptophan/AhR axis showed the strongest coupling to marker-based immune and myeloid signatures, including macrophage-, Treg-, NK-cell-, CD8 T-cell-, Th1-like and cytolytic-activity programmes. Tryptophan/AhR, short-chain fatty acid and ferroptosis/redox axes were enriched in MSI-H and immune-high tumours, whereas the polyamine axis showed weaker immune associations. Short-chain fatty acid and ferroptosis/redox axes decreased recurrently in advanced-stage disease across cohorts. No universal prognostic axis emerged, although the short-chain fatty acid axis retained a stage-adjusted association with improved overall survival in GSE39582. Postbiotic-related host transcriptomic axes provide interpretable tumour-level readouts connecting metabolic cues with immune microenvironment states in colorectal cancer. They should be considered hypothesis-generating host-side immune-context readouts rather than ready-to-use clinical signatures.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Oxaliplatin frequently causes chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy (CIPN), including impaired hand dexterity; however, factors associated with dexterity impairment remain unclear. This study aimed to compare hand function, dexterity, strength, and pain according to neuropathy severity, and to identify factors associated with impaired hand dexterity. A total of 206 patients received oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy, of whom 102 (49.5%) developed CIPN and were included in this cross-sectional study. All participants were aged ≥ 40 years and had received at least three cycles of oxaliplatin-based chemotherapy at a tertiary research hospital. Neuropathy severity was classified according to the National Cancer Institute Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events as Grade (I-III). Outcome measures included grip strength measured with a hand dynamometer, pinch strength assessed with a pinch meter, fine motor skills and hand dexterity evaluated using the Minnesota Manual Dexterity Test (MMDT) and Nine-Hole Peg Test (NHPT), hand function assessed using the Michigan Hand Outcomes Questionnaire (MHOQ), pain intensity measured with the PainDETECT Questionnaire, and CIPN symptoms evaluated using the European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire-Chemotherapy-Induced Peripheral Neuropathy 20 (EORTC QLQ-CIPN20). Group comparisons were performed using one-way ANOVA or Kruskal-Wallis tests with Tukey or Dunn post-hoc analyses, respectively. Ordinal logistic regression (complementary log-log link) identified predictors of neuropathy severity, while multiple linear regression analyses assessed factors associated with hand dexterity. Significant between-group differences were observed in grip and pinch strength, hand dexterity performance, MHOQ subparameters, CIPN20 scores, and PainDETECT scores (p < 0.05). Neuropathy severity was significantly associated with cumulative oxaliplatin dose and gender (p < 0.05), with higher cumulative doses increasing the risk of severe neuropathy. Regression analyses demonstrated that grip strength, gender, and CIPN20 motor scores were significant predictors of hand dexterity performance in both MMDT placing and turning models (p < 0.001). Lower grip strength and higher motor neuropathy scores were associated with poorer dexterity performance. Increasing neuropathy severity was associated with poorer hand function, reduced strength, and impaired manual dexterity. Cumulative oxaliplatin dose and sex were significant predictors of neuropathy severity, whereas grip strength and motor neuropathy symptoms were important determinants of hand dexterity performance. ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07203066, registered on 24 September 2025.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Identifying dMMR (mismatch repair deficiency)/MSI (microsatellite instability) status in colorectal cancer (CRC) is standard in developed countries and is valuable for prognosis, management, and family screening. Universal testing is unfeasible in developing nations due to economic and resource constraints, limiting essential testing for optimal patient care. This study investigated the prevalence of dMMR/MSI CRC in Sri Lanka and introduced a predictive score for CRC patients in our population, which can be used to guide the selection of patients for cost-effective dMMR/MSI testing. A cross-sectional analysis was conducted on colorectal carcinomas from Teaching Hospital Peradeniya, National Hospital Kandy, Colombo South Teaching Hospital, and General Sir John Kotelawala Defence University Hospital for two and a half years. Data collected included gender, age, tumour site, TNM stage, and family history of CRC. Haematoxylin and eosin-stained tumour slides of colectomy specimens were assessed for histopathological features. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) was performed for the four DNA mismatch repair proteins MLH1, MSH2, PMS2, and MSH6. Cases that were inconclusive by IHC were tested for MSI using PCR. Descriptive analysis included frequency, percentage, mean, standard deviation (SD) and range. Multivariable binomial logistic regression was conducted to select predictive variables. Of 185 patients, 104 (56.2%) were women. The mean age was 62.5 years (SD:11.8; range: 19-84). Of all cases, 23 (12.4%) were found to be mismatch repair deficient. Multivariable analysis showed significant association with age less than 60 years (p = 0.001), right sided tumour (p = 0.001), family history of CRC (at least one first or second degree relative) (p = 0.028), mucin percentage ≥ 20% (p = 0.038), solid region percentage ≥ 15% (p = 0.019), highest iTILs ≥ 3 per high power field (p < 0.001), and Crohn-like peritumoral inflammation (p = 0.004). Considering the intercept values, rounded off to integers, a score was obtained for predicting dMMR/MSI CRC. The cutoff value for the prediction of dMMR status was taken as ≥ 6 from a maximum value of 20 (sensitivity: 0.957, specificity: 0.681). In resource-limited settings, screening CRC patients with the proposed predictive score could cost-effectively guide dMMR/MSI testing. This preliminary score needs further validation in a larger independent cohort to ensure its reliability and broader applicability.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A 30-year-old male with a known case of rectal adenocarcinoma, post-low anterior resection (LAR) and oxaliplatin with capecitabine chemotherapy, presented with fluorodeoxyglucose (FDG)-avid extensive multiple peritoneal and hepatic deposits on Positron Emission Tomography-Computed Tomography (PET-CT), suggestive of metastatic disease. After histological examination, these lesions were pulse granulomas with vegetable matter deposits, causing a florid foreign body-type giant cell reaction. This case represents a rare presentation of foreign body granuloma masquerading as a metastatic deposit. It is an important diagnostic pitfall where benign foreign body granulomas can mimic metastatic disease both radiologically and clinically, emphasizing the role of histopathology in definitive diagnosis and guiding appropriate patient management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Leiomyosarcomas (LMSs) of the gastrointestinal tract are rare malignant tumors arising from smooth muscle cells. It is known for its aggressive nature and poor prognosis. Among gastrointestinal sites LMS, colonic involvement is exceptionally uncommon and often misdiagnosed as other more common colorectal malignancies such as adenocarcinoma or gastrointestinal stromal tumors (GIST). We report a case of a 37-year-old woman who presented with fever, vomiting, occasional abdominal pain, and constipation. Imaging revealed a left-sided abdominal mass likely of malignant nature. Histopathological examination following surgical resection confirmed the diagnosis of LMS, with immunohistochemistry showing positivity for smooth muscle actin, desmin, and negativity for CD117, DOG1, and CD34, excluding GIST. She thereafter received adjuvant chemotherapy with six cycles of doxorubicin and dacarbazine. There has been no recurrence until 9 months of follow-up postchemotherapy. Primary LMS of the colon is an extremely rare entity with nonspecific clinical features. A high index of suspicion, supported by immunohistochemical analysis, is crucial for accurate diagnosis. Early surgical intervention remains the mainstay of treatment, although prognosis remains guarded due to tumor's aggressive nature.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Pelvic peritoneal apposition (closure) following abdominoperineal resection (APR) for rectal cancer remains controversial. While some surgeons advocate peritoneal closure to prevent adhesions, others recommend leaving the pelvis open to avoid tension-related complications. This observational cohort study compared early postoperative outcomes between these two surgical approaches. This 10-year retrospective cohort study included 54 patients undergoing APR (open or laparoscopic) between January 2010 and January 2020 at Medical College, Kolkata. Patients were stratified into two groups: peritoneum apposed ( n = 29) versus peritoneum left open ( n = 25). Follow-up ranged from 2 to 10 years. Primary outcome was early postoperative small bowel obstruction (EPSBO); secondary outcomes included postoperative infection, length of hospitalization, and disease stage. EPSBO occurred in 10 patients (18.5%), with 9/10 in the apposed group and 1/10 in the open group (odds ratio [OR] 10.8, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22-95.4, P = 0.030). Postoperative infection was significantly more common in the apposed group (11/29, 37.9%) than in the open group (3/25, 12.0%; OR 4.48, 95% CI 1.08-18.5, P = 0.038). Peritoneal apposition was more frequently performed in patients >50 years of age ( P = 0.044). Only one patient required surgical exploration for acute obstruction; the remaining nine recovered with conservative management. In this cohort, leaving the pelvic peritoneum open after APR was associated with significantly lower rates of EPSBO and postoperative infection compared to peritoneal apposition.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
For locally advanced esophageal and rectal cancers, radiotherapy (RT) provides essential local control but is frequently limited by acute and late toxicities that erode survival and quality of life (QoL). Over the last decade, evidence has implicated radiation dose to the heart, lungs, bowel, and pelvic bone marrow in increased postoperative morbidity, cardiopulmonary deaths, and hematologic toxicity, compromising chemotherapy delivery and long-term outcomes. The physical properties of proton beam therapy (PBT), which eliminate exit dose and reduce integral dose, offer a fundamental advantage. Systematic evidence confirms PBT consistently lowers low- to intermediate-dose exposure to organs at risk (OARs). For esophageal cancer, robust dosimetric data show reductions of approximately 50-65% in mean heart dose and 40-50% in lung V5, translating to reduced total toxicity burden (TTB) and perioperative complications in randomized and real-world studies. In rectal cancer, PBT reduces pelvic bone marrow V10 by 40-55% and small bowel V15-V30 by 30-50%, a prerequisite for improving the tolerability of intensive regimens. While definitive Phase III survival data are awaited, current evidence supports the selective use of PBT to improve the therapeutic index of radiotherapy, allowing its benefits to be realized with less collateral damage.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The present study aimed to survey the antibiotic resistance patterns and toxin gene expression levels in different PCR ribotypes and sequency types of C.difficile isolated from patients with colorectal polyps. A total of 305 stool specimens were collected from patients with colorectal polyps. The antimicrobial susceptibility of C. difficile isolates was determined using the Liofilchem A total of 37 C. difficile isolates were isolated from 305 stool samples (12.1%). Overall, 35.1% (n = 13/37), 48.6% (n = 18/37), 35.1% (n = 13/37), and 43.2% (n = 16/37) of C. difficile isolates were positive for tcdA, tcdB, cdtA, and cdtB genes, respectively. Out of 23 toxin gene-positive C. difficile isolates, 8 isolates were tcdA-/tcdB+/cdtA+/cdtB+, 5 isolates were tcdA+/tcdB+/cdtA+/cdtB-, and 4 isolates were tcdA+/tcdB-/cdtA-/cdtB+. The most prevalent RTs among C. difficile isolates were 012 (34.78%; n = 8), 126 (21.73%; n = 5), and 001 (17.39%; n = 4). The most frquenctly detected sequence types were ST-2 (n = 9; 39.13%), followed by ST-54 (n = 6; 26%). Toxigenic C. difficile isolates showed the lowest resistance rate to vancomycin (8.7%; n = 2/23) and metronidazole (13%; n = 3/20), respectively. The rates of vancomycin resistance in RT001 (25%) and RT126 (20%) C. difficile isolates were higher than those in other RTs. tcdB gene expression was significantly high in RT027 (8.15 fold), and RT078 (6.25 fold). Meanwhile, the tcdA relative expression level was significantly high in RT027 (6.25 fold), RT078 (4.75 fold) and RT126 (4.35 fold). The significant increase in toxin gene expression observed in RT012, in addition to the hypervirulent ribotypes RT027 and RT078, is particularly concerning and highlights the potential for RT012 to become an emerging clinical challenge.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The elderly population represents an increasing proportion of patients undergoing surgery for colorectal cancer. Their risks and outcomes may differ from the general population. This study aimed to identify risk factors associated with anastomotic leak (AL) and the outcomes related to this complication in elderly patients, using a large retrospective cohort from a high-volume colorectal surgery unit. A retrospective cohort study was conducted including patients aged ≥ 75 years who underwent colorectal cancer surgery between January 2015 and March 2019 at a tertiary centre. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify predictors of AL. Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses assessed long-term survival. A total of 416 patients (mean age 81.3 ± 4.7 years, 56% male) were included, with AL occurring in 12.26% (n = 51). Independent predictors of AL included preoperative hypoalbuminemia < 3 g/dL (OR 7.70, p = 0.009), mechanical anastomosis (OR 3.13, p = 0.033), and elevated CRP on postoperative day 3 (OR 1.14 per unit, p < 0.001). Intraoperative drain placement was protective (OR 0.34, p = 0.040). AL was associated with higher major complication rates, prolonged hospital stay, and increased 30-day and 5-year mortality (p < 0.0001). Discharge to rehabilitation centre or hospital-at-home discharge remained associated with AL (OR 4.57, p = 0.011). Independent predictors of mortality included emergency surgery, AL, ECOG ≥ 2, and Clinical Frailty Scale ≥ 5. These findings may support improved preoperative decision-making, patient counselling, and development of strategies to optimise outcomes in high-risk elderly patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Extracellular vesicle (EV)-derived RNAs may provide complementary molecular information beyond conventional serum tumor markers for colorectal cancer (CRC) diagnosis. This study evaluated the diagnostic value of EV-derived SNORD46 and AL592064.2 alone and in combination with carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and carbohydrate antigen 19-9 (CA19-9). An exploratory EV small-RNA microarray was performed using samples from three patients with CRC and three healthy donors. The clinical dataset included 160 patients with CRC and 160 healthy donors and was stratified into a model-development cohort (112 CRC and 112 healthy donors) and a frozen internal hold-out validation cohort (48 CRC and 48 healthy donors). A multivariable logistic regression model integrating SNORD46, AL592064.2, CEA, and CA19-9 was developed. The probability threshold was determined in the development cohort and applied unchanged to the validation cohort. Model performance was evaluated using discrimination, calibration, bootstrap validation, stage-specific analysis, reclassification metrics, and exploratory decision-curve analysis. In the internal hold-out validation cohort, the four-marker model achieved an AUC of 0.910 (95% CI 0.846-0.963), with a sensitivity of 77.1% and specificity of 91.7% at the prespecified probability threshold. The clinical reference model based on CEA and CA19-9 achieved an AUC of 0.801, and the four-marker model demonstrated a significant improvement in discrimination (ΔAUC = 0.109; 95% CI 0.032-0.186; DeLong P = 0.0053). For stage I-II and stage I CRC, the AUCs were 0.879 and 0.842, respectively. Model calibration in the validation cohort showed a calibration slope of 0.759 and a Brier score of 0.118. The EV-derived SNORD46 and AL592064.2-based four-marker model improved diagnostic performance beyond conventional CEA and CA19-9 in an internally validated cohort. These findings support the potential value of EV-derived small RNA biomarkers as complementary components of future multimarker diagnostic strategies for CRC, while external validation and evaluation in clinically representative populations remain required.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Incisional hernia is a common late complication after extensive abdominal surgery and may significantly impair quality of life. The incidence and risk factors of incisional hernia in patients undergoing cytoreductive surgery (CRS) combined with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC) for peritoneal surface malignancies of colorectal or appendiceal origin remain insufficiently studied. This study aimed to evaluate the incidence of incisional hernia and to identify factors associated with incisional hernia in this specific patient population. This retrospective, single-center cohort study included 147 patients who underwent CRS+HIPEC between January 2018 and January 2024. Demographic data, tumor characteristics, surgical details, and comorbidities were obtained from a prospectively maintained database. All patients underwent midline laparotomy, and HIPEC was performed using either mitomycin C or oxaliplatin with 5-fluorouracil/leucovorin via the closed technique at 42-43 °C for 30-90 min. Patients were followed for at least 18 months, and incisional hernia was diagnosed by physical examination and/or radiologic imaging. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were used to identify associated factors. The mean age was 54.07 ± 11.70 years, with an equal sex distribution, and the mean follow-up was 30.7 ± 16.2 months. During follow-up, 83 patients (56.5%) developed an incisional hernia. Prior open abdominal surgery (OR 2.621; 95% CI 1.155-5.946; p = 0.021) and a history of hernia (OR 13.682; 95% CI 2.928-63.941; p < 0.001) were significant predictors in univariable analysis and remained independently associated with incisional hernia in multivariable analysis. The incidence of incisional hernia after CRS+HIPEC is high, and patients with previous open abdominal surgery or preexisting hernia should be considered at increased risk during preoperative assessment and postoperative follow-up.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The current research ecosystem on gastrointestinal (GI) cancers-including anal, colorectal, esogastric, pancreatic, hepatocellular, and biliary tract cancers-relies heavily on randomized controlled trials (RCTs), which involve high costs and limited transportability. Fewer than 10% of therapeutic recommendations for pancreatic adenocarcinoma are based on high-level evidence, a proportion that has not improved between 2011 and 2022. Furthermore, substantial research waste undermines interventional research in GI cancer: 30-37% of completed GI cancer trials lack publicly available results, and only 59% of gastric cancer trials are published as full-text articles. Such waste in research negatively impacts evidence synthesis and guidelines recommendations. While interventional research is the only way to assess the efficacy of a new drug, observational studies and real-world evidence (RWE), using health records, cohorts, registries and/or administrative databases, may offer complementary insights, especially for research questions that cannot be studied by RCTs. In particular, RWE can evaluate treatments in elderly or comorbid patients often excluded from trials, inform decisions for rare tumors such as digestive neuroendocrine neoplasms, and evaluate real-world effectiveness of treatments such as targeted therapies or immunotherapy. While historically RWE reliability was often criticized for biases and data quality issues, methodological advances, such as target trial emulation and data standardization, have enhanced its validity, and it is now increasingly used to support regulatory decisions by agencies like the Food and Drug Administration and the European Medicines Agency. Better integration of high quality interventional and observational approaches is essential in GI cancer research. Guidance on when to use interventional versus observational studies, depending on the clinical question, may help put this integration into practice. This synergy could reduce research waste, accelerate evidence generation, and help identify more effective personalized treatments for GI cancer patients.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The incidence of early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) has increased globally, but its clinical characteristics, treatment patterns, and outcomes remain incompletely characterized, particularly in Asian populations. We compared clinical presentation, treatment patterns, and survival outcomes of EOCRC and late-onset colorectal cancer (LOCRC) in Korea. Using the nationwide K-CURE database, we identified patients diagnosed with colorectal cancer between 2012 and 2019. EOCRC was defined as colorectal cancer diagnosed before 50 years of age. Clinical characteristics, initial treatment patterns, and survival outcomes were compared between EOCRC and LOCRC. Propensity score matching and multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression analyses were performed. Among 20,941 patients, 2,044 (9.8%) had EOCRC, and the proportion remained near 10% throughout the study period. Stage distribution and tumor differentiation were comparable between EOCRC and LOCRC. Patients with EOCRC more frequently received multimodality treatment across disease stages. In unadjusted analyses, EOCRC was associated with lower overall mortality (HR, 0.61; 95% CI, 0.56-0.66), cancer-specific mortality (HR, 0.79; 95% CI, 0.72-0.86), and non-cancer mortality (HR, 0.13; 95% CI, 0.09-0.18), with consistent findings in propensity score-matched and multivariable analyses. The mortality difference was greatest in localized disease and remained evident across stages and primary tumor sites. In molecular subgroup analyses, the association between EOCRC and lower mortality was stronger in MSI tumors than in microsatellite-stable tumors, with a significant interaction, whereas no significant interaction was observed according to KRAS mutation status. EOCRC was not associated with more advanced disease at diagnosis than LOCRC and was associated with lower observed mortality, which should be interpreted in the context of baseline patient characteristics and treatment patterns.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Using the fecal immunochemical test (FIT) with risk factors for advanced colorectal neoplasia (AN - the combination of colorectal cancer and advanced precancerous polyps) could improve the yield of colonoscopy in both screening and diagnostic settings. In this systematic review, we evaluated: (1) yield and efficiency of FIT alone vs. FIT plus risk factors for screening and among FIT positive individuals; (2) study quality for these two settings. Following literature searches of Ovid MEDLINE and Embase from January 2010 to March 2026, two reviewers independently identified published English-language studies that evaluated FIT performance with and without risk factors among average-risk adults aged ≥ 40 years undergoing screening colonoscopy and among FIT positive subjects, independently extracted descriptive and numerical data, and evaluated study quality. We compared colonoscopy yield and efficiency of FIT alone versus FIT with risk prediction models and risk factors in screening and diagnostic studies. From 1891 articles, we identified 9 screening studies and 10 diagnostic studies for a positive FIT. Both groups of studies were homogeneous in design and of good quality. In the nine screening studies, age, sex, BMI, family history of CRC, and smoking were most often used with varying model metrics and varying degrees of discrimination, and with modest-to-moderate improvements in efficiency at the cost of missing a proportion of AN. Among the ten diagnostic studies, the combination of fecal hemoglobin, age, sex, and smoking had the greatest improvement on yield and efficiency, but also missed a small proportion of AN. In the screening setting, the yield of colonoscopy for AN improves when risk factors are used to stratify who is first screened with FIT vs. colonoscopy. In the diagnostic setting, risk factors help prioritize FIT-positive patients for diagnostic colonoscopy because of high risk for AN.

Overall complication rates (35.7% vs. 22.2%, p = 0.458) and Clavien-Dindo grade ≥ 3 complications (10.7% vs. 3.7%, p = 0.418) did not differ significantly between the exRHC and TC groups. The 3-year relapse free survival (RFS) was 86.3% for exRHC and 80.3% for TC (p = 0.63), and the 3-year overall survival (OS) was 92.6% and 91.6%, respectively (p = 0.778). In advanced mid-transverse colon cancer with D3 lymph node dissection and central MCA ligation, exRHC associated with a higher risk of postoperative ileus and longer hospital stay than TC. Given similar oncologic outcomes, TC may be a more favorable surgical option owing to its faster recovery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) is one of the most common and deadliest digestive tract malignancies, but its diagnostic and prognostic markers still need further exploration as targets for risk stratification and treatment response. COAD cohorts were retrieved from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) databases. Differences in gene expression were analyzed using relevant R packages, followed by gene function enrichment analysis and Weighted Gene Co-expression Network Analysis (WGCNA). Next, the Kaplan-Meier method and LASSO regression analysis were employed to screen for prognostic signature genes associated with the survival of COAD patients. Furthermore, comprehensive analyses were conducted to assess the role of this signature gene in immunomodulation and genetic mutation. Single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) analyses were performed using the GSE166555 dataset. Additionally, CCK-8, colony formation, wound healing and Transwell assays were used to evaluate the biological functions of the signature gene in COAD cells. Differential expression analysis and WGCNA led to the identification of 156 candidate genes, which were primarily enriched in functional pathways including the cell cycle, P53 signaling pathway, and cellular senescence. Subsequently, LASSO regression combined with survival analysis screened out ZNF556 as a characteristic prognostic gene for COAD. The expression level of ZNF556 correlates with the infiltration of plasma cells, mast cells, and monocytes, and is further associated with the expression of multiple immune checkpoint genes. Additionally, gene mutation analysis revealed a significant correlation between mutant TP53 and ZNF556 expression. ScRNA-seq analysis further indicated that, in the context of COAD, ZNF556 may exert a key regulatory role in the differentiation of epithelial cells, thereby facilitating tumor initiation and progression. Furthermore, subsequent experiments confirmed the cancer-promoting effect of ZNF556, whose expression was positively regulated by mutant TP53. ZNF556 was highly up-regulated in COAD tissues, with high expression correlating with poor prognosis and difference in TIICs. It functions as a diagnostic, immunological and prognostic biomarker for COAD, and a potential therapeutic target.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Recent evidence has suggested that neoadjuvant chemotherapy may provide clinical benefit for patients with locally advanced colon cancer. Immunotherapy may provide additive or synergistic effects when combined with chemotherapy. This study's objective is to assess the efficacy, safety, and tolerability of neoadjuvant dostarlimab in combination with capecitabine-oxaliplatin (CAPEOX) versus CAPEOX in patients with T4N0 or stage III mismatch repair proficient/microsatellite stable (pMMR/MSS) resectable colon cancer. AZUR-4 (NCT06567782) is a multicenter, phase 2, open-label, randomized (3:1 ratio) study of 120 patients across multiple countries. Eligible patients are aged ≥ 18 years with resectable pMMR/MSS colon adenocarcinoma with no prior treatment. Four cycles (21 days) of CAPEOX ± dostarlimab will be administered as neoadjuvant treatment. After completing neoadjuvant treatment, patients will undergo surgery 3 to 6 weeks later, with additional adjuvant chemotherapy administered after surgery at the investigator's discretion; no additional dostarlimab will be administered. Primary endpoints are major pathological response, determined by local assessment, and safety. Secondary endpoints will assess the feasibility and pathological response to the regimen. Exploratory endpoints include biomarker readouts and pathological response rate in biomarker subsets. AZUR-4 will evaluate the effect of neoadjuvant dostarlimab + CAPEOX in patients with previously untreated T4N0 or stage III pMMR/MSS resectable colon cancer, a population for whom improved treatments are urgently needed. The robust sampling and advanced analysis of pretreatment and posttreatment blood, tissue, and tumor samples planned for this trial should assist in elucidating immune profile analyses to support the discovery of novel predictive biomarkers in this population.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Post-translational modifications (PTMs) play a pivotal role in regulating RNA-binding proteins (RBPs), which are crucial in the progression of colorectal cancer (CRC). This study aims to explore the role of PTMs in modulating RBPs and their implications for CRC pathogenesis. We characterized phosphorylation, ubiquitination, and malonylation of RBPs in CRC using previously generated post-translational multi-omics datasets from paired CRC and adjacent non-tumor tissues in our previous studies. Functional enrichment analysis was conducted to identify pathways associated with RBPs carrying different PTMs in CRC. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) networks were generated using STRING, and hub genes were identified with the Cytoscape plugin CytoHubba. We also investigated the intersection of RBPs with distinct PTMs and evaluated the expression and prognostic relevance of FLNA (filamin A). Our findings revealed aberrant PTMs of RBPs in CRC, with ubiquitination sites showing the most frequent alterations, followed by phosphorylation, while malonylation exhibited the fewest changes. Functional enrichment analysis indicated that these PTMs contribute to distinct biological processes, including RNA metabolism, protein synthesis, and translation regulation. PPI network analysis showed that RBPs with different PTMs were interconnected in complex networks, identifying several potential RBPs closely related to CRC. Notably, FLNA emerged as a unique RBP modified by all three PTMs. FLNA mRNA and protein abundance were reduced in CRC, and phosphorylation of FLNA at S2319 was also decreased. Higher FLNA expression was associated with worse overall survival. FLNA-associated genes were enriched in pathways related to epithelial-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and KRAS signaling. Multi-PTM profiling revealed distinct and convergent modification patterns among CRC-associated RBPs. FLNA emerged as a potential multi-PTM candidate associated with CRC-related molecular and clinical features. These findings provide a framework for further investigating the biological relevance of PTM-regulated RBPs and their potential implications for the development of molecularly targeted strategies in CRC.

STAT1 knockdown attenuated Lgals3bp mRNA induction and reduced LGALS3BP abundance in these fractions without comparable reductions in TSG101 or ALIX. FGFR4 overexpression was associated with altered protein composition in EV-enriched extracellular fractions and STAT1-dependent LGALS3BP induction. These findings identify the FGFR4-STAT1-LGALS3BP relationship as a component of extracellular remodeling in CRC.

Expanded multigene panel testing identified pathogenic or likely pathogenic germline variants in 28.0% of patients with suspected hereditary polyposis, while established polyposis-predisposition genes accounted for a diagnostic yield of 20.0%. The marked molecular heterogeneity observed supports the value of comprehensive germline testing for molecular diagnosis and hereditary cancer risk characterization.

Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most common cancer in men and the second in women, accounting for 9.4% of cancer-related deaths worldwide in 2020. Increasing evidence highlights the role of gut microbiota in CRC pathogenesis, prognosis, and therapeutic response. Data from Middle Eastern and North African populations remains scarce. This study aimed to analyze gut microbiota profiles in Egyptian patients with CRC and to explore their associations with dietary and lifestyle factors. A pilot case-control study was conducted, involving patients with CRC and healthy controls. Gut microbiota composition was assessed using 16S rRNA gene sequencing, with analysis of microbial diversity and differential taxonomic abundance at the family and genus levels. Dietary patterns, physical activity, and demographic variables were evaluated for their associations with microbial profiles. CRC patients exhibited greater microbial heterogeneity, with higher Bray-Curtis distances compared to controls. Several taxa, such as This pilot study identifies clinically relevant, exploratory associations between lifestyle factors and CRC-related microbial signatures in an understudied population. All findings should be considered hypothesis-generating, given the small sample size and cross-sectional design. These results highlight the potential role of modifiable behaviors in microbiome-informed risk stratification. Larger, multi-center studies incorporating multi-omics approaches are warranted to confirm and extend these preliminary observations.

Nevertheless, the study was not adequately powered to exclude a clinically relevant difference in POD incidence given the substantially lower-than-expected event rate, as no statistically significant between-group difference was detected. ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Venlafaxine, a serotonin-norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor, has been investigated in oncology for several supportive care indications and, more recently, for potential anticancer activity. However, the available evidence remains fragmented across clinical and preclinical studies. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the available evidence regarding the role of venlafaxine in oncology, including established supportive care applications and emerging anticancer potential. A systematic literature search was conducted in PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science from database inception to 22 August 2026. Original clinical and preclinical studies evaluating venlafaxine in cancer populations or experimental cancer models were eligible. Clinical and preclinical evidence was synthesized separately using a narrative approach. Methodological quality was assessed using Joanna Briggs Institute tools for clinical studies and the SYRCLE Risk of Bias tool for animal studies. 25 studies were included, comprising 23 clinical studies and 2 preclinical studies. The strongest clinical evidence supported venlafaxine for treatment-related hot flashes, particularly among breast cancer survivors receiving endocrine therapy, with the strongest randomized, placebo-controlled trial evidence showing significantly greater reductions with venlafaxine than placebo (P < 0.0001 for higher doses); within-group percentage reductions are also reported but should not be interpreted as treatment effects. Evidence for chemotherapy-induced peripheral neuropathy was inconsistent, with potential benefit for acute oxaliplatin-related neurotoxicity but insufficient support for prevention or routine treatment of chronic CIPN. Evidence for other supportive care outcomes, including oral mucositis-associated pain, fatigue, sleep quality, depressive symptoms, and quality of life, was limited. Venlafaxine was generally well tolerated, although adverse effects varied by dose and comparator. Preclinical studies investigated anticancer activity, but not equivalently: one in melanoma models showed direct antiproliferative/pro-apoptotic effects of venlafaxine via JNK1/2-Nur77 signaling, whereas a colorectal cancer study showed only context-dependent antagonism of norepinephrine-driven tumor progression, with no significant effect of venlafaxine alone. No clinical evidence currently supports venlafaxine as a direct anticancer treatment. Venlafaxine has an established evidence-based role in supportive oncology for treatment-related hot flashes, whereas its role in CIPN and other supportive care indications remains uncertain. Emerging anticancer findings are limited to preclinical models and should be considered hypothesis-generating. Further randomized clinical trials are needed for supportive care indications, while additional mechanistic and preclinical validation is required before venlafaxine can be considered for clinical evaluation as an anticancer therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) has a high incidence, and both metastasis and drug resistance remain formidable challenges in clinical management. Owing to their multi-target activity and favorable safety profiles, natural products have become a prolific source for anticancer drug discovery. Benzoylaconine (BAC) is a secondary metabolite of aconitine with markedly attenuated toxicity that retains anti-inflammatory, analgesic, and antitumor properties; however, its antitumor effects and the underlying molecular mechanisms in CRC are poorly defined. This study was designed to systematically characterize the impact of BAC on the malignant phenotypes of CRC cells and to identify its potential molecular targets. HCT116 and SW480 cells were used as model systems. Proliferation was assessed by MTT and EdU assays; migration and invasion by wound-healing and Transwell assays, respectively; cell cycle and apoptosis by flow cytometry. Network pharmacology was applied to predict core targets and construct a protein-protein interaction network. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations examined binding; SPR verified direct binding to CDK2 and MMP2. RNA-seq identified differentially expressed genes and enriched pathways. Western blotting validated key protein changes. Patient-derived CRC organoids (PDOs) were established to evaluate BAC efficacy; organoid viability was assessed by CellTiter-Glo® 2.0 assay, and morphology by bright-field microscopy. BAC dose- and time-dependently inhibited CRC cell proliferation and EdU positivity, slowed wound closure, and reduced Transwell invasion, indicating impaired migration and invasion. Flow cytometric analysis revealed that BAC induced G1/S cell cycle arrest and apoptosis. Network pharmacology identified CDK2 and MMP2 as key targets; molecular dynamics and SPR confirmed stable binding (KD ≈ 3.9 and 4.4 μM). RNA-seq showed enrichment of pathways related to cell cycle regulation and tumor invasion. Western blotting revealed that BAC dose-dependently downregulated CDK2, CDK6, MMP2, Cyclin E1, and Cyclin D1, and upregulated p21. BAC also inhibited the proliferation of colorectal cancer organoids. BAC induces G1/S cell cycle arrest in CRC cells, likely through modulation of the CDK2/MMP2 signaling axis, thereby suppressing proliferation, migration, and invasion while promoting apoptosis, and may represent a promising lead for CRC therapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) poses a major public health concern, with emerging evidence highlighting the critical role of the gut microbiota in CRC progression. Considering that diet is a major modifiable factor influencing CRC risk, partly through its interaction with the gut microbiome, this systematic review evaluated the effects of dietary intervention RCTs, including supplements, functional foods, whole foods, and dietary patterns, on the gut microbiome in elevated-risk individuals. A search of PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science, and manual sourcing of systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and reference lists of relevant papers identified 5,558 records. Following screening, seven studies met inclusion criteria, focusing on microbial diversity and taxonomic composition. Findings demonstrate that effects on microbial diversity metrics were minimal and were observed only with a general healthy eating dietary pattern, navy bean powder interventions, and with one rice bran intervention. No consistent patterns emerged by intervention type (functional compounds, whole foods, or dietary pattern), intervention duration, or by diversity metric. In contrast, genus-level compositional shifts were more frequently reported, although directionality varied by dietary exposure. Enrichment of Faecalibacterium, Bifidobacterium, and Lactobacillus was reported in some rice bran and navy bean interventions, whereas reductions in Akkermansia, Ruminococcus, Bacteroides, Prevotella, and Porphyromonas were observed in others. Among the four trials assessing microbial-derived metabolites, some were associated with increased short-chain fatty acids and plant-derived metabolites while others reported reductions in secondary bile acids, p-cresol sulfate, and branched-chain bacterial fatty acids. Overall, this review highlights the potential of dietary strategies to modulate the gut microbiome in populations at risk for CRC, while also addressing critical gaps in the current evidence and offering direction for the development of evidence-based dietary interventions that incorporate microbiome assessment. Limited RCTs and heterogeneity in outcomes limit generalizability. Future research should conduct rigorous RCTs across the lifespan, using microbiome and metabolite analyses such as shotgun metagenomics, meta-transcriptomics, or metabolomics and examining understudied dietary patterns to guide CRC prevention. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD42024530038, identifier CRD42024530038.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to synthesize evidence from recent randomized controlled trials (RCTs) evaluating the efficacy of regorafenib, fruquintinib, and TAS-102 in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Using a network meta-analysis, we compared long-term survival outcomes (overall and progression-free survival) in the overall population and in patients with KRAS mutations, to guide treatment decisions and inform therapy selection in molecularly defined subgroups. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library up to 6 November 2025 for randomized controlled trials reporting overall survival (OS) and/or progression-free survival (PFS) in patients with metastatic colorectal cancer (mCRC). Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane RoB-2 tool and heterogeneity with I2. A Bayesian network meta-analysis using non-informative normal priors and a random-effects consistency model was fitted; convergence was assessed with the Gelman-Rubin diagnostic. Comparative safety was not formally meta-analyzed. Ten RCTs (n = 3959) were included, with no randomized head-to-head comparisons among the active treatments. Compared with placebo, all active treatments significantly improved overall survival (OS): fruquintinib HR 0.66 (95% CrI 0.53-0.84), regorafenib HR 0.69 (95% CrI 0.51-0.88), TAS-102 HR 0.69 (95% CrI 0.55-0.85), and TAS-102 plus bevacizumab HR 0.41 (95% CrI 0.28-0.59). Combination therapy ranked first; indirect differences among the three single agents were not consistently statistically significant. In patients with KRAS-mutant tumors, fruquintinib and TAS-102 were associated with numerically favorable OS estimates compared with placebo [HR 0.71 (95% CrI 0.51-1.01) and 0.74 (95% CrI 0.50-0.99), respectively], whereas regorafenib did not [HR 0.81 (95% CrI 0.52-1.19)]. These statistical differences versus placebo do not demonstrate superiority over regorafenib, and rank probabilities are exploratory. Fruquintinib and TAS-102 plus bevacizumab are effective later-line options for mCRC. In patients with KRAS-mutant CRC, fruquintinib may be a reasonable option, but available indirect evidence does not establish its superiority over TAS-102 or regorafenib. These findings provide a trial-level, KRAS-stratified synthesis of the available placebo-controlled RCT evidence and should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating, rather than as evidence of a predictive effect of KRAS status or of rank-based superiority among the agents. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/display_record.php?ID=CRD420251275994, identifier CRD420251275994.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Patients with early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) experience various symptoms and comorbidities throughout the treatment continuum. Identifying the intricate relationship between symptoms and comorbidities in EOCRC can provide a deeper understanding of the underlying mechanisms that shape the patient's entire experience. This study aimed to compare the association between symptoms and comorbidities in patients by age of onset to identify key relationships between symptoms and comorbid disease in EOCRC. Data of 985 patients enrolled in a prospective colorectal cancer (CRC) cohort between 2013 and 2021 in the Republic of Korea were analyzed. At baseline, patients were assessed for 33 symptoms and functions, as well as 14 comorbidities, and were subsequently stratified into two age groups: <50 (EOCRC) and ≥50 years (late-onset CRC [LOCRC]). Symptoms and comorbidity relationships were examined using correlation-based network analysis. In total, 13.5% of the participants had EOCRC. In the EOCRC group, 44 patients (33.1%) had existing comorbidities. The symptom and comorbidity networks were more complex in EOCRC than in LOCRC. Fatigue was a central symptom in both age groups. The EOCRC group exhibited positive correlations between musculoskeletal disease and psychiatric disorder, stool frequency, and multiple symptoms. The LOCRC group showed pronounced correlations between embarrassment by bowel movement and multiple symptoms and between health functioning parameters and fatigue. Cancer-related fatigue was an important feature in both groups. These findings underscore the importance of considering these factors to enhance quality-of-life care outcomes during and after CRC treatment.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
After curative surgery for colorectal cancer (CRC), patients undergo surveillance because of the risk of recurrence; however, only a subset develops recurrence amenable to further curative-intent treatment. The primary aim of follow‑up is to identify patients with potentially curable recurrence. A retrospective analysis was performed of stage I-IV CRC patients who underwent curative-intent treatment and entered postoperative surveillance at Isala between 2014 and 2018. Follow‑up was conducted according to Dutch guideline‑based protocols for 60 months. Patients were categorized as having no recurrence, a potentially curable recurrence, or a non-curable recurrence. Prognostic factors at start of follow-up for potentially curable recurrence were assessed using competing‑risk Cox regression, with non-curable recurrence and death as competing events. For patients with recurrence, mode and time of detection were evaluated. During a median follow-up of 60 months, recurrence occurred in 22.4% of 1118 patients. The cumulative incidence function (CIF) of a potentially curable recurrence was 8.0%. Independent variables associated with a potentially curable recurrence were age HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.96-0.99), minor postoperative complications HR 1.78 (95% CI 1.16-2.72), stage III CRC HR2.76 (95% CI 1.19-6.38) and stage IV CRC HR 11.02 (95% CI 4.44-27.37). Among patients with a recurrence, CEA ≥ 5 ng/mL was present in 63% of all recurrences, but less often in the potentially curable group (57% vs. 69%, p = 0.057). Median time to detection of a potentially curable recurrence was 16 months (IQR 20). The overall number needed to follow-up (NNFU) to detect one potentially curable recurrence was 9.8, with the lowest NNFU observed in stage IV CRC (2.3) and in rectal cancer (6.9). Standard follow-up enabled the detection of potentially curable recurrence in 8% of CRC patients. The substantial variation in NNFU across subgroups and the limited sensitivity of CEA underscore the need for more personalized, risk‑adapted surveillance strategies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To explore, as a preliminary study, the quantitative parameters of single-index and continuous-time random-walk (CTRW) magnetic resonance (MR) diffusion models and their association with lymph node metastasis, vascular invasion, and some prognostic factors in patients with rectal cancer. This retrospective, exploratory study included a total of 43 patients who were pathologically diagnosed with rectal cancer and underwent preoperative MRI between February 2022 and November 2023. The data were fitted using the single-index and CTRW diffusion models to derive ADC, Dm, α, and β parameters. Differences in quantitative diffusion parameters were assessed for lymph node metastasis, vascular invasion, and p53 status using t-tests and rank-sum tests. The associations of quantitative diffusion parameters with lymph node metastasis and vascular invasion were evaluated using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis. Lymph node metastasis was positive in 25 patients and negative in 18 patients; vascular invasion was positive in 30 patients and negative in 13 patients. In this initial investigation, the Dm and β values derived from the CTRW model showed a certain association with lymph node metastasis (AUCs of 0.76 and 0.76, respectively). Regarding vascular invasion, only the Dm value showed a certain association (AUC of 0.76), while the β value did not demonstrate a significant association after adjustment.The combination of Dm and β demonstrated stronger associations, with AUCs of 0.83 and 0.83, respectively. In this exploratory study, the diffusion parameters derived from the CTRW model may be associated with lymph node metastasis and vascular invasion in rectal cancer, but this requires external validation.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (MALT) lymphoma is a rare entity, accounting for approximately 1.6% of all MALT lymphoma cases. Its clinical and endoscopic presentation is generally nonspecific, and given the limited number of reported cases, no consensus exists on the optimal therapeutic strategy. A 47-year-old male with a 15-year remission history of stage IIb nodular lymphocyte-predominant Hodgkin lymphoma (NLPHL) underwent abdominopelvic CT for recurrent urinary tract infections, revealing a suspected sigmoid neoplasm with locoregional lymphadenopathy. Colonoscopy showed two adjacent but noncontiguous subepithelial erythematous lesions (15 mm and 10 mm) with surrounding "chicken skin" mucosal pattern. Initial biopsies demonstrated chronic inflammation only. At endoscopic reassessment, endoscopic mucosal resection (EMR) was performed, yielding a histological diagnosis of MALT lymphoma. Following multidisciplinary discussion, the patient underwent four cycles of rituximab monotherapy, achieving complete remission on reassessment CT. At eighteen months of follow-up, he remains asymptomatic without clinical, radiological, or endoscopic evidence of relapse. We report the first described coexistence of colonic MALT lymphoma and prior NLPHL, without an established biological association given the absence of comparative molecular studies. This case highlights the role of EMR when conventional biopsies are nondiagnostic and demonstrates the efficacy of rituximab monotherapy in this rare entity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumors are neoplasms that can be recognized by a patient's immune system. Recognition of tumor antigens (TAs) triggers the recruitment and proliferation of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes. Although tumor-infiltrating T cells have long been the primary focus of research, B cells also accumulate in tumors and participate actively in TA recognition. The use of molecular display technologies for the functional profiling of tumor-infiltrating B cell (TIB) repertoires enables large-scale screening for TAs and identification of unique TIB clones that mediate selective tumor recognition. Approaches combining microfluidic technologies for reconstructing natural TIB repertoires with yeast display were used in this study to identify antibodies that recognize TAs. It has been shown that nonspecific adhesion of yeast cells to the surface of primary tumor cell cultures from patients may be a key factor hindering the isolation of tumor-specific clones. Overcoming nonspecific binding of yeast cells enables the selection of tumor-specific clones by biopanning. Clone 3.15, isolated from the TIB repertoire of a colorectal cancer (CRC) patient, recognizes TAs on the surface of a number of tumor cell lines, as well as on primary tumor cell cultures from CRC patients. We suggest that the further use of these technologies will not only expand the diversity of molecular tools for targeted immunotherapy and tumor diagnostics but will also provide a more detailed understanding of the molecular mechanisms underlying the generation and recognition of TAs.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Rectal prolapse (RP) is a pelvic floor disorder that can cause rectal protrusion, defecatory dysfunction, and fecal incontinence. Patients increasingly use large language models (LLMs) for health information, yet the reliability and readability of LLM responses to patient-oriented questions about RP remain unclear. To compare the reliability and readability of five LLM platform-model configurations in answering English-language patient-oriented questions about RP. In this web-based cross-sectional study, worldwide Google Trends queries from the preceding 5 years were identified using the MeSH term "rectal prolapse." Two colorectal specialists screened the queries and standardized them into 15 patient-oriented questions. The questions were submitted to ChatGPT, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot, Perplexity, and DeepSeek under standardized single-turn, zero-shot conditions, with one response collected per question from each platform-model configuration. Two independent evaluators assessed the responses using DISCERN, the Ensuring Quality Information for Patients (EQIP) instrument, the Global Quality Score (GQS), and the JAMA benchmark criteria. Using evidence-based guidelines and question-specific checklists of key clinical content, the evaluators also independently assessed clinical factual accuracy and completeness and identified potentially harmful recommendations and critical omissions. Readability was evaluated using the Automated Readability Index (ARI), Gunning Fog Index (GFI), Flesch-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Coleman-Liau Index (CL), Simple Measure of Gobbledygook (SMOG), and Flesch Reading Ease Score (FRES). DISCERN ( The five LLMs generally produced clinically accurate information about RP. No potentially harmful recommendations were identified. Yet information quality and source transparency differed among models, some responses omitted critical clinical information, and readability was poor across all five. LLMs are currently better suited as professionally reviewed adjuncts to patient education than as substitutes for specialist assessment or individualized clinical decision-making.
