ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer immunotherapies require accurate preclinical models that recapitulate the complex cellular interactions within the human tumor microenvironment. While patient-derived organoids have emerged as powerful tools for cancer research, standard cultures lack the stromal and immune compartments necessary to evaluate immunotherapeutic mechanisms. This limitation hampers the development of next-generation targeted cytokine therapies. We applied a 3D immune-containing colorectal cancer assembloid platform integrating patient-derived organoids, cancer-associated fibroblasts and allogeneic peripheral blood mononuclear cells within a collagen matrix. We characterized cellular responses to interferon-gamma (IFNg) and engineered IFNg receptor agonists targeted to fibroblast activation protein (FAP) through single-cell transcriptomics, immunohistochemistry, cytokine profiling, and functional T-cell migration assays. The assembloid model successfully recapitulated key features of IFNg signaling, including tissue growth suppression, enhanced chemokine secretion (CXCL10), and CD8 This 3D assembloid model provides a physiologically relevant platform for dissecting complex tumor-immune interactions and optimizing targeted immunotherapies. This approach enables the study of epithelial-stromal-immune crosstalk in cancer and offers a robust preclinical framework for screening and mechanistically validating next-generation targeted cytokine therapies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The SHURUI single-port (SP) robotic system is a novel platform with serpentine instruments designed for reduced-access surgery. Clinical experience in gastrointestinal malignancies remains limited. This exploratory, descriptive case series reports initial technical experience with the SHURUI SP system in a consecutive series of gastric and colorectal cancer resections. This retrospective case series included six consecutive patients who underwent SP robotic gastrointestinal cancer surgery between November 2025 and December 2025 at a single tertiary center. Procedures comprised rectal cancer resection with total mesorectal excision ( All six procedures were completed without conversion. Median operative time was 332.5 min (155-402); median estimated blood loss was 70 mL (10-200). No intraoperative complications or transfusions occurred. Postoperative Grade II complications occurred in two patients (33.3%): anastomotic bleeding requiring transfusion and wound infection. Grade I transient fever occurred in two additional patients (33.3%). No Grade III-V complications, reoperations, or 30-day mortality occurred. All resections achieved R0 margins; median lymph node yield was 18.5 (12-28). Median hospital stay was 14 days (12-20). Mean total hospital cost was ¥30,573 ± ¥14,725, exclusive of robotic platform and instrument fees, which were waived during this initial evaluation period. In this initial series, the SHURUI SP robotic system achieved complete resection without conversion in all six cases. R0 resection was obtained in every case with no severe early complications; however, the small sample size precludes definitive safety assessment, and oncologic adequacy requires long-term follow-up. The system proved technically feasible for complex gastric and colorectal cancer resections, though the absence of an integrated energy channel necessitated an auxiliary port in all cases, and operative times reflected an early learning curve. Larger comparative studies with long-term follow-up are needed to define the role of this platform.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Klippel-Trénaunay syndrome (KTS) is a rare congenital vascular anomaly characterized by capillary malformation, underlying low-flow venous/lymphatic malformations, and bone- and/or soft-tissue limb hypertrophy of the affected extremity. At present, there is no consensus on the optimal management of KTS, particularly in the context of gastrointestinal bleeding. We describe a case of gastrointestinal bleeding in a patient with KTS who presented with colorectal venous malformations with phleboliths, multiple splenic vascular malformations, penile varicosities, and hypertrophy of the right lower extremity and the right buttock. A colonoscopy revealed a circumferential mucosal elevation with bluish discoloration extending from 15 cm above the anal verge in the colorectum, and active bleeding was observed at 12 cm from the anal verge. Endoscopic submucosal sclerotherapy with 1-1.5 mL of lauromacrogol (1%) per site and a total volume of 30 mL, combined with band ligation using six bands, was performed. This approach has rarely been reported and resulted in significant relief from bleeding. At the 6-month follow-up, the patient's symptoms and hemoglobin levels remained stable, with no other complications. Although KTS remains incurable, early endoscopic recognition facilitates diagnosis, and endoscopic therapy may serve as an important treatment modality for gastrointestinal involvement.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Achieving a microscopically radical (R0) resection is essential in rectal cancer surgery to reduce local recurrence, distant metastases, and improve long-term survival. This retrospective cohort study aimed to identify factors associated with microscopically non-radical (R1) excision in patients undergoing surgery for rectal adenocarcinoma at a Swedish tertiary referral center. Patients with rectal adenocarcinoma operated on between January 2015 and December 2020 at Skåne University Hospital, Malmö, were identified through the Swedish Colorectal Cancer Registry and complementary chart review. Clinical, pathological, and perioperative variables were compared between patients with R0 and R1 resections. R1 resection was defined as a circumferential resection margin (CRM) ≤0.1 mm or an involved longitudinal resection margin. Factors associated with R1 status were analyzed using univariable and multivariable logistic regression. Among 348 included patients, 17 of 309 (5.5%) with available resection status had a microscopically non-radical resection (R1), while resection status was missing for 39 patients. Distal tumor location was strongly associated with R1 status: tumors ≤7 cm from the anal verge had an increased risk of non-radical excision [adjusted odds ratio (aOR)=3.77, 95% confidence interval (CI)=1.23-14.2]. Longer operating time was related to R1 resection (median 531 Distal tumor location and advanced pathological tumor stage are key risk factors for microscopically non-radical resection in rectal cancer, whereas an extensive lymph node yield appears protective. These findings support meticulous preoperative planning and tailored surgical strategies for low rectal tumors to minimize the risk of R1 excision.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The global incidence of colorectal cancer (CRC) is rising at an alarming rate, particularly among individuals under the age of 50, referred to as early-onset CRC (EOCRC). While genetic predisposition accounts for approximately 20% of the total cases, the majority are influenced by environmental and lifestyle factors. Among these, the rising prevalence of obesity is a major modifiable contributor to EOCRC pathogenesis. This narrative review explores the multifaceted role of obesity in EOCRC, focusing on how diet-induced adiposity reshapes the gut microbiota and host metabolic signaling. We synthesize evidence on how obesity-associated dysbiosis, characterized by the depletion of protective, short-chain fatty acid (SCFA)-producing bacteria and the enrichment of genotoxic pathobionts, compromises intestinal barrier integrity and promotes a "leaky gut" phenotype. In addition, we explore the systemic consequences of obesity-driven inflammation, including M1-polarized macrophage infiltration into adipose tissue, dysregulated adipokine signaling, and the hyperactivation of the insulin-IGF-1 axis. By integrating epidemiological data with molecular mechanisms, this review highlights how the synergy between metabolic dysfunction and microbial alterations creates a fertile niche for early-onset carcinogenesis. These findings underscore the importance of targeting lifestyle interventions to mitigate the rising burden of obesity and reduce the risk of EOCRC progression.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to explore the experiences and perceived changes in self-management behaviors among older patients with a permanent stoma during adaptation, providing insights for the development of targeted supportive interventions. Semi-structured, in-depth interviews were conducted with 13 older colorectal cancer patients with a permanent stoma. All interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. The data were analyzed and thematically refined using Colaizzi's seven-step method. Three overarching themes and several sub-themes were identified. Theme one, decision-making dilemmas and uncertainty, included insufficient and poorly tailored decision support resources and challenges in processing complex self-management information. Theme two, reconstructing daily life and identity after stoma formation, encompassed disruptions in body image and daily routines, emotional struggles between rejection and acceptance, and the development of a new normal in living with a stoma. Theme three, developing resilience through accumulated experience and self-management practice, involved learning through repeated self-adjustment, drawing on previous life experiences as coping resources, and redefining life priorities after illness. The findings suggest that older patients living with a permanent stoma experience self-management as an ongoing process involving decisional challenges, psychological adjustment, and the gradual reconstruction of resilience. Healthcare professionals should provide continuous decision support, psychological care, and family-inclusive interventions while adopting a strength-based approach that recognizes patients' existing abilities and lived experiences. Supporting patients in reflecting on their adaptation experiences and accumulated coping strategies may enhance self-efficacy and facilitate sustained self-management.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Conventional adenomas and serrated lesions are two major precursor lesions of colorectal cancer. They arise through distinct carcinogenic pathways, namely the conventional adenoma-carcinoma sequence and the serrated neoplasia pathway. These pathways differ substantially in their underlying molecular mechanisms, implying that the risk factor profiles for the two types of lesions may be different. However, existing evidence remains fragmented, and an integrated comparative synthesis of these differential associations is lacking. In this review, we synthesize and compare current evidence on the mechanistic characteristics and lifestyle, metabolic, and nutritional determinants of conventional adenomas and serrated lesions. By synthesizing the available evidence on the two precursor pathways, this review may contribute to a better understanding of conventional adenomas and serrated lesions, and offer insights for future research into their distinct risk factors, underlying mechanisms, and implications for colorectal cancer prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is the third most commonly diagnosed cancer worldwide. In 2020, approximately 560,000 new CRC cases were estimated in China. First-degree relatives (FDRs) of people with CRC have an elevated CRC risk and are recommended to begin screening earlier. Despite this elevated risk, screening uptake among FDRs remains suboptimal, and the reasons for non-uptake in the Chinese context are not fully understood. To explore perceived barriers and facilitators to CRC screening among FDRs of patients with CRC in China and to identify implications for health education and screening services. We used a qualitative phenomenological design. From April to May 2025, FDRs of patients attending the Colorectal Surgery Department of Ningbo Second Hospital were recruited purposively. Of 56 eligible relatives, 24 agreed to participate. Interviews and preliminary analysis proceeded iteratively, and data saturation was judged to have been reached after 10 interviews. Data were analyzed using Colaizzi's seven-step phenomenological method. Analysis of participant interviews identified four barriers to screening: limited awareness and underestimation of familial risk; fear and psychological resistance; financial and time burdens; and limited access to screening services. Four facilitators were also identified: witnessing a relative's illness and treatment; personalized and targeted health education; convenient and accessible screening services; and policy and social support. Screening decisions were shaped by interacting individual, practical, and health-system factors. The findings suggest potential targets for intervention at individual, service, and policy levels. This three-level framework is a conceptual implication of the qualitative findings and requires evaluation in larger and more diverse settings.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
V-domain immunoglobulin suppressor of T-cell activation (VISTA; also termed VSIR, PD-1H or B7-H5) is increasingly recognised as an immune checkpoint whose biological and clinical significance depends less on total expression than on the tumour microenvironment (TME) in which it operates. Rather than acting as a linear T-cell exhaustion receptor, VISTA integrates tumour chemistry, stromal architecture, innate and adaptive immune states, and therapy-induced feedback inhibition. It is expressed by tumour cells and multiple immune populations, including macrophages, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, dendritic cells, neutrophils, regulatory T cells and activated or quiescent T cells. VISTA can also function through pH-dependent and pH-independent ligand-receptor interactions. This review reframes VISTA as a TME-gated regulatory system. Low pH, hypoxia, transforming growth factor beta (TGF-β), histamine, aldehyde metabolism, Yes-associated protein (YAP)/TEA domain (TEAD) signalling, macrophage polarity, antigen-presenting-cell fitness and spatial immune exclusion can jointly determine whether VISTA marks immune resistance, immune activation under feedback restraint or tumour-cell-intrinsic evasion. This context helps explain the divergent prognostic associations of VISTA across pancreatic, gastric, colorectal, lung, breast, bladder, gynaecological, skin, brain, mesothelial and haematological malignancies. Therapeutically, VISTA should therefore not be treated as another universal immune-checkpoint target. More plausible strategies include pH-selective antibodies, ligand-axis disruption, local or nanoparticle delivery, targeted degradation, tumour-cell-intrinsic pathway inhibition and combinations that convert suppressive TME niches into antigen-presenting and cytotoxic niches. A TME-centred framework can make VISTA biology clinically interpretable and guide biomarker development, trial design and rational combination immunotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal malignancies remain leading causes of cancer mortality, yet their sensitivity to immunotherapy differs sharply across anatomical sites, histologies, molecular subtypes, and disease stages. Immune checkpoint blockade has established durable clinical benefit in microsatellite instability-high colorectal cancer, advanced gastric and esophageal cancers, hepatocellular carcinoma, and biliary tract cancer, while pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and microsatellite-stable colorectal cancer remain largely refractory. Recent phase III trials have moved immunotherapy into perioperative treatment. Concurrently, claudin 18.2-directed chimeric antigen receptor T cells, T-cell receptor-engineered cells, bispecific antibodies, personalized vaccines, and oncolytic viruses are converting previously speculative strategies into clinically testable platforms. This review integrates contemporary trial evidence with mechanisms of immune escape, biomarker development, and combination toxicity. The resulting framework prioritizes evidence maturity across diverse gastrointestinal tumor types worldwide.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Plasma cell-free DNA (cfDNA) is a heterogeneous and rapidly changing biological pool derived from malignant cells, normal tissues, and hematopoietic cells. The abundance and molecular composition of circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) are determined not only by tumor burden but also by tissue architecture, vascular access, cell-death programs, chromatin organization, nuclease processing, systemic clearance, treatment exposure, and clonal evolution. These biological determinants shape the mutation, methylation, fragmentation, nucleosomal, and temporal features exploited by contemporary liquid-biopsy assays. Accurate clinical interpretation therefore requires both sensitive detection and reliable source attribution, particularly the distinction of tumor-derived variants from constitutional germline alterations and clonal hematopoiesis. In this review, we integrate the biological origins and processing of plasma cfDNA with analytical strategies for low-tumor-fraction detection and critically evaluate the evidence supporting postoperative molecular residual disease (MRD), recurrence surveillance, treatment-response assessment, resistance monitoring, and ctDNA-guided therapy across solid tumors. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing prognostic validity, treatment-predictive value, and demonstrated clinical utility. Current evidence is strongest in colorectal cancer and, more recently, ctDNA-selected urothelial cancer, whereas routine ctDNA-directed intervention in resected non-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer remains insufficiently validated. By linking cfDNA biology to an explicit hierarchy of clinical evidence, this review defines both the established applications and the major limitations that must be addressed before broader implementation of ctDNA-guided precision oncology.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Digestive tract cancers (DTCs) impose substantial health risks for women of childbearing age (WCBA), yet their global burden and future trajectories remain incompletely characterized. This study quantified the global burden of five major DTCs among WCBA from 1990 to 2021 using Global Burden of Disease (GBD) 2021 data and projected trends through 2050. Incidence and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) rates were assessed to characterize global, regional, and age-specific variations in DTCs burden. Temporal trends were estimated using Joinpoint regression, health inequalities quantified via the slope index of inequality (SII) and concentration index (CI), and future burden forecasted using a Bayesian age-period-cohort (BAPC) model. In 2021, colorectal cancer (CRC) accounted for the largest burden among WCBA, with 85,224 incident cases and over 1.6 million DALYs. Regionally, East Asia had the highest burden of gastric cancer (GC) and CRC, whereas South Asia had the greatest burden of esophageal cancer (EC) and lip and oral cavity cancer (LOC). National disparities were pronounced; Afghanistan exhibited the highest GC burden (ASIR: 13.77; ASDR: 630.33 per 100,000), contrasting with Kuwait (ASIR: 0.27; ASDR: 12.12). Between 1990 and 2021, the incidence of GC and EC declined, while LOC showed a persistent increase, with peak burden observed among women aged 45-49 years. Health inequality analyses indicated narrowing global gaps for GC and EC but widening disparities for LOC. Projections to 2050 suggest continued declines for GC, EC, and CRC, alongside an increasing burden of LOC. The rising burden of LOC, compounded by expanding health inequalities among WCBA, underscores the need for targeted, region-specific interventions. Given that WCBA face distinct challenges including fertility preservation concerns, more aggressive disease phenotypes, and profound impacts on family and economic stability, these findings highlight the critical importance of age-specific cancer control strategies. Strategies, including expanded screening and equitable healthcare access, are critical to mitigate disparities and improve outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Acrolein is a highly reactive aldehyde generated endogenously during lipid peroxidation and encountered through environmental and dietary exposures. Although acrolein has established electrophilic, genotoxic, and oxidative-stress effects, the extent to which acrolein-linked gene perturbation is represented in colorectal cancer (CRC) transcriptomes and relates to tumor immune-stromal heterogeneity remains incompletely characterized. We integrated direct human acrolein target evidence from the Comparative Toxicogenomics Database (CTD) with TCGA-COAD/READ bulk RNA-sequencing profiles and a single-cell RNA-sequencing subset from GSE231559. The CTD curation yielded 179 unique direct human targets. Bulk analyses included 624 primary-tumor and 51 solid-tissue normal profiles. Single-cell analyses included six tumor and three normal libraries, yielding 24,128 retained cells assigned to eight broad marker-supported compartments. Target dysregulation burden, immune-stromal expression programs, and library-aware single-cell target localization were evaluated as transcriptomic summaries. In addition, RT-qPCR was performed in HCT 116 colorectal carcinoma cells to experimentally evaluate four measurable CTD targets (NFKBIA, GSTP1, VIM, and GPX4) after acrolein exposure. The bulk tumor-normal analysis identified 5,594 differentially expressed genes at FDR < 0.05 and |log2 fold change| ≥ 1. Of 179 CTD acrolein targets, 155 were measurable in the bulk dataset and 43 met the differential-expression threshold. Mean absolute normal-reference target burden was higher in tumors than normal tissue (1.96 vs. 0.75; difference 1.21; Welch Acrolein target-linked expression perturbation is detectable in CRC and is associated with immune-stromal heterogeneity across bulk and single-cell transcriptomic scales. RT-qPCR provides targeted experimental support for acrolein-responsive expression changes in NFKBIA, GSTP1, VIM, and GPX4 in HCT 116 cells. These findings support a toxicogenomic framework for hypothesis generation but do not measure acrolein exposure in patients, establish causal toxicological effects in human tumors, or demonstrate a specific intercellular signaling mechanism. Additional mechanistic, protein/adduct, dose-response, and independent-cohort validation will be required to determine the biological significance of the observed associations.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Postpolypectomy surveillance plays an important role in the prevention of colorectal cancer. However, optimal surveillance intervals for individuals with multiple prior colonoscopies remain unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between prior colonoscopy frequency and advanced neoplasia detection rate (ANDR) according to cumulative colorectal neoplasia treatment history using real-world data from individuals with multiple prior colonoscopies. This two-center retrospective study analyzed colonoscopies performed between 2010 and 2020 in patients aged ≥40 years. The number of colonoscopies performed within the preceding five years was routinely recorded for each examination. The primary outcome was ANDR. Surveillance intervals were considered appropriate when the ANDR was ≤7%. Analyses were stratified according to cumulative prior lesion history as follows: none, adenoma, advanced adenoma, intramucosal carcinoma, or invasive carcinoma. Among 22,066 colonoscopies, ANDR was 17.4% at first-ever examination and progressively decreased with increasing recent colonoscopy frequency: 7.2% with no colonoscopy within five years, 3.9% after one, 3.4% after two, and 2.3% after three or more examinations. ANDR remained ≤7% in patients without lesions or with only non-advanced adenomas within an interval of five years or longer before the index colonoscopy. In contrast, ANDR exceeded 7% at intervals of five years or longer in patients with advanced adenoma or intramucosal carcinoma, whereas patients with invasive carcinoma showed persistently high detection rates even at shorter intervals. Low-risk patients showed a persistently low ANDR, whereas closer surveillance may be justified for patients with advanced adenoma, intramucosal carcinoma, or invasive carcinoma.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO) is a common complication after colorectal cancer (CRC) surgery. However, its association with health-related quality of life (HRQOL) in postoperative patients remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the association between a history of ASBO and HRQOL after CRC surgery. We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of patients who underwent CRC surgery at Shinshu University Hospital. HRQOL was assessed using a modified 32-item questionnaire comprising four domains. A total of 126 patients were included (ASBO group, n = 25; control group, n = 101). The primary outcome was the daily life domain score. Multivariable linear regression analyses were performed to examine associations of ASBO with HRQOL. Patients in the ASBO group had a higher proportion of poor performance status ( A history of ASBO was associated with poorer HRQOL after CRC surgery. Further studies are warranted to clarify these associations and validate the questionnaire.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Small-bowel obstruction (SBO) is a postoperative complication caused by postcolorectal surgery adhesions. Laparoscopy reduces its incidence, and systemic inflammation may contribute to adhesion formation. This study aimed to determine if preoperative inflammation-based markers are associated with SBO development after laparoscopic colon cancer surgery. This retrospective study included 539 patients who underwent elective laparoscopic colon cancer surgery from 2017 to 2021. Demographics, surgical variables, and preoperative inflammation-based markers-including C-reactive protein (CRP), white blood cell (WBC) count, platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), the lymphocyte-to-monocyte ratio (LMR), neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR), and prognostic nutritional index (PNI)-were assessed. SBO was defined as a clinically and radiologically confirmed adhesive ileus. Fifteen patients (2.8%) developed SBO. Receiver operating characteristic curve analysis was performed for BMI and all preoperative inflammatory markers. This analysis identified body mass index (BMI) ≤21.61, LMR ≤2.38, and NLR ≥3.07 as optimal cutoffs. CRP and WBC count showed low AUCs (0.560 and 0.580, respectively) and were not significant risk factors for SBO. Univariate analysis demonstrated that low BMI, low LMR, high NLR, stoma construction, and intra-abdominal infectious complications were significantly associated with SBO development. Multivariate logistic regression analysis identified low BMI (p = 0.022), low LMR (p = 0.047), and intra-abdominal infectious complications (p < 0.001) as independent predictors; PNI trend was not significant. Low BMI, low LMR, and postoperative intra-abdominal infection were associated with postoperative SBO after minimally invasive colon cancer surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Indocyanine green (ICG) fluorescence imaging is increasingly used in colorectal surgery, but reliable intraoperative subserosal injection for lymphatic mapping remains technically challenging because puncture depth control and prevention of dye spillage are essential. We developed a standardized subserosal ICG mapping technique using an adjustable laparoscopic injection needle under direct laparoscopic or robotic visualization. The serosa adjacent to the tumor is punctured with the needle tip adjusted to local bowel wall thickness, and ICG is delivered using a saline-ICG-saline sandwich technique. To minimize contamination, the outer sheath of a suction tube is positioned close to the puncture site as a protective guide for the injection needle, allowing immediate re-sheathing after injection; laparoscopic gauze is added when necessary. Fluorescence imaging is then performed to visualize lymphatic flow and fluorescent nodal basins. In our initial 10-patient experience, detection was achieved in 9 patients without puncture-related complications.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Daikenchuto is a traditional Japanese herbal medicine (Kampo) that has been widely used because of its low cost and minimal side effects. It is used for early patient recovery after abdominal surgery and to prevent postoperative paralytic ileus in various surgeries, including colon and rectal cancer. Many studies have reported the usefulness of perioperative administration of Daikenchuto; however, few have examined its association with healthcare economics. This observational study used data from the National Database (NDB) Sampling Dataset. This study included patients with colon or rectal cancer who underwent colectomy, anterior resection (AR), low anterior resection (LAR), or abdominoperineal resection (APR) between January 2013 and December 2022. The comparison was based on Daikenchuto administration. Overall, 3,759 patients underwent colectomy (Daikenchuto -: 3,111 vs. Daikenchuto +: 648), 675 underwent AR (567 vs. 108), 1,269 underwent LAR (1,105 vs. 164), and 348 underwent APR (310 vs. 38). Postoperative hospital stay was shorter in patients who received Daikenchuto: for colectomy, 13.8 vs. 13.0 days (P = 0.001); for AR, 15.3 vs. 13.0 days (P = 0.002); for LAR, 17.6 vs. 14.5 days (P < 0.001); and for APR, 22.9 vs. 19.7 days (P = 0.007). Medical costs per patient were lower among patients receiving Daikenchuto by 25,412 yen for colectomy, 68,494 yen for AR, 92,407 yen for LAR, and 94,361 yen for APR. Perioperative Daikenchuto administration was associated with shortened the length of hospital stay and lower postoperative hospitalization costs in colon and rectal cancer surgeries.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted elective endoscopy and non-urgent procedures, but its impact on inpatient colorectal cancer (CRC) treatment in Japan remains incompletely quantified. We conducted an interrupted time series analysis using the Diagnosis Procedure Combination (DPC) inpatient database. Eligible admissions were patients hospitalized between April 2018 and December 2021 with colorectal cancer codes from the International Classification of Diseases, 10th Revision (ICD-10; C18, C19, and C20) who underwent endoscopic submucosal dissection (ESD) or colorectal surgery. We excluded planned chemotherapy readmissions, recurrence cases, admissions with multiple non-ESD surgeries, and records with missing tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) information. Three periods were defined: Period 1 (Apr 2018-Apr 2020), Period 2 (May 2020-Apr 2021), and Period 3 (May 2021-Dec 2021). Monthly inpatient case volumes were modeled using segmented regression with Prais-Winsten estimation and seasonal adjustment. Of 276,458 eligible admissions, 260,919 were analyzed. At the start of Period 2, adjusted inpatient cases decreased significantly for ESD (-26%; 887 adjusted vs 1,194 predicted; p<0.001) and colectomy (-6%; 2,746 vs 2,928; p=0.043), whereas rectal resection/abdominoperineal resection showed no significant level change (-5%; p=0.189). In stage-stratified analyses limited to surgical resections, Stage I surgical volume decreased significantly at the start of Period 2 (-13%; p=0.010) with no clear reduction for Stages II-IV. In Japan, the early COVID-19 period was associated with short-term reductions in inpatient ESD and Stage I surgical volume, whereas surgical treatment volumes for more advanced disease showed no clear immediate reduction after the first emergency declaration. Because this was an administrative, inpatient-only analysis, the study does not directly assess diagnostic delays, stage migration, or downstream oncological outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The objective of this study was to identify the factors influencing postoperative morbidity in patients with colorectal cancer (CRC) and synchronous peritoneal metastasis (PM). This multicenter prospective observational study was conducted by the Japanese Society for Cancer of the Colon and Rectum. Patients with CRC and synchronous PM were recruited from 28 institutions in Japan between October 2012 and December 2016. Postoperative morbidity was the primary endpoint of the analysis, and diverse variables were included for evaluation via logistic regression analysis. A total of 137 patients, including 78 men and 59 women, were enrolled in this study. The median age was 67 years. Among patients with synchronous PM, 55 had PM alone, classified as M1c1, whereas 82 had PM with metastases to other organs, classified as M1c2. In multivariate analysis, M1c2 status and operation time >170 minutes were significantly associated with postoperative morbidity (odds ratio [OR] = 3.89, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.31-11.51, p = 0.01; and OR = 4.56, 95% CI 1.32-11.51, p = 0.01, respectively). In the overall cohort, postoperative morbidity was not significantly associated with overall survival. This study demonstrated that M1c2 is an independent risk factor for postoperative morbidity. When planning surgery for peritoneal metastasis, particularly in patients with distant organ metastases, the elevated risk of postoperative morbidity should be carefully considered in surgical decision-making.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Horseshoe kidney is a rare congenital anomaly frequently associated with anatomical variations in the vascular and urinary systems. In colorectal surgery, these abnormalities increase the risk of inadvertent injury and require particular attention. We report the case of a 61-year-old woman (body mass index 40) who had undergone a radical hysterectomy for endometrial cancer 27 years earlier and had been followed up in our gynecology department. An elevation in tumor marker levels was noted during follow-up, and metastasis of endometrial cancer was suspected in the ascending colon. To minimize the risk of ureteral injury during minimally invasive surgery in an obese patient who had a history of hysterectomy and a horseshoe kidney, laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with fluorescent ureteral navigation was performed. The right ureter was clearly identified using fluorescence during surgery and completely secured. The histological examination revealed endometrial cancer metastasis in the ascending colon. In this patient with obesity and a horseshoe kidney, laparoscopic surgery using a fluorescent ureteral catheter was successful. A review of the relevant literature is also provided herein.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Longitudinal changes in the fecal microbiome and metabolome during concurrent chemoradiotherapy (CCRT) for rectal cancer remain incompletely characterized. In this prospective single-center cohort, 19 patients with rectal cancer were enrolled and 17 were included in the longitudinal analysis after two prespecified sampling-window exclusions. Fecal specimens were scheduled at nine time points: R0, collected before the first dose of capecitabine and before radiotherapy, and R3 through R24 at three-fraction intervals during treatment. Twenty unmatched healthy volunteers provided one fecal specimen for a descriptive pretreatment comparison. Full-length 16S rRNA gene sequencing and untargeted metabolomics were performed. Longitudinal microbial counts were analyzed using negative-binomial generalized linear mixed models, and metabolite features were analyzed using linear mixed-effects models; participant was included as a random intercept, and Nineteen genera and 27 of 176 analyzed species showed significant linear time trends during CCRT (FDR < 0.05). This small, intensively sampled cohort identifies exploratory fecal microbial and metabolic trajectories during capecitabine-based CCRT. The findings do not establish causal mechanisms, microbial functions, disease specificity, or biomarker performance and require independent confirmation in larger cohorts.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Abnormal circular smooth muscle contractility is considered a key factor in the pathogenesis of diverticular disease (DD), contributing to increased intraluminal pressure and diverticulum formation. Altered cholinergic responsiveness of colonic smooth muscle has previously been reported in DD. Although angiotensin II (Ang II) regulates gastrointestinal smooth muscle contraction through angiotensin type 1 (AT1R) and type 2 (AT2R) receptors, its role in DD remains poorly understood. The aim of the present study was to investigate alterations in contractile responses to Ang II and cholinergic stimulation in the circular muscle of the colon in DD. Colonic tissue was obtained from 16 patients with DD and 16 control patients undergoing colorectal surgery. Immunofluorescence was performed to determine the localization of AT1R and AT2R. Ang II levels in colonic muscular tissue were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA), AT1R and AT2R protein expression were evaluated by Western blotting, and their mRNA expression was assessed by RT-qPCR. Circular smooth muscle strips were subsequently studied using AT1R was predominantly localized in colonic smooth muscle cells, whereas AT2R was mainly detected in the myenteric plexus and nerve fibers. Compared with controls, DD tissues exhibited increased local Ang II levels and higher AT2R protein expression, accompanied by increased AT2R mRNA expression. Bethanechol-induced contractility was reduced in DD, whereas both peak and mean 5-min Ang II-induced contractile responses were enhanced. Losartan significantly reduced the mean 5-min Ang II-induced contractile response in both groups. However, both peak and mean responses remained significantly greater in DD than in controls following AT1R blockade. Neither TTX nor PD123319 significantly affected Ang II-induced contractions. The present study demonstrates altered colonic circular smooth muscle contractility in diverticular disease, characterized by enhanced responses to Ang II and reduced responses to cholinergic stimulation. The distinct muscular and neural distribution of AT1R and AT2R, respectively, suggests that altered local Ang II signaling, together with altered cholinergic regulation, may contribute to the pathogenesis of DD.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
A 48-year-old man with Crohn's disease (CD), who had previously undergone two intestinal surgeries, was referred to our hospital for treatment of perianal lesions. After referral, routine endoscopic follow-up was performed on the remaining colon and the accessible terminal ileum in conjunction with examination under anesthesia (EUA) for the perianal lesions. In the ninth year following referral, dysplastic epithelium was detected in the ileum on the oral side of the anastomosis during EUA and endoscopic assessment. Dysplasia was confirmed again during the third examination after repeated evaluations, leading to ileocecal resection. Histopathological analysis revealed intramucosal adenocarcinoma. Because systematic surveillance for small bowel cancer in CD has not been standardized, this early-stage lesion was detected incidentally during routine postoperative endoscopic follow-up. The patient remained free of both CD recurrence and cancer relapse for 7 years postoperatively.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
This study aimed to evaluate the predictive value of serum carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) changes for treatment response in colorectal cancer(CRC) patients receiving CAPOX chemotherapy, providing a reliable indicator for clinical efficacy monitoring. Clinical data of CRC patients who first received the CAPOX regimen at the Sixth Affiliated Hospital of Sun Yat-sen University between January 1, 2016 and January 31, 2026 were retrospectively collected. Parameters included operation date, chemotherapy administration dates, disease progression (PD) time, preoperative CEA, baseline CEA before chemotherapy, CEA before each cycle, and CEA within three months post-chemotherapy. Disease-free survival (DFS) was calculated. Patients were divided into Group 1: CEA is in the normal range (all values are ≤ 5ng/ml); Group 2: Decreasing or normalization type (not Group 1, and the last valid value ≤ 5ng/ml, or a decrease of ≥20% compared to the individual's previous peak); Group 3: Persistent or new-onset abnormal type (the rest, that is, the last value > 5 and the decrease from the peak value < 20%). Survival curves were plotted using the Kaplan-Meier method, and multivariate Cox regression was used to assess correlations between CEA changes, treatment efficacy, and DFS. Median DFS (mDFS) was 55.668 months (95% CI: 51.511-58.826) in Group 1 (n=84); 42.271 months (95% CI: 35.438-49.104) in Group 2 (n=47) and 19.980 months (95% CI: 11.198-28.762) in Group 3 (n=11). Dynamic changes in serum CEA have good predictive value for the efficacy of CAPOX chemotherapy in CRC. This predictive value is primarily significant in TNM Stage III patients and serve as an independent prognostic factor. Patients with decreased or persistently normal CEA levels have a better prognosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Secondary extramammary Paget's disease (EMPD) of the perianal region most commonly arises from an invasive colorectal adenocarcinoma; pagetoid spread from a non-invasive precursor, such as a high-grade tubular-villous adenoma (TVA), is rare. A 70-year-old man presented with a high-grade TVA of the anal canal and concurrent perianal EMPD. Initial immunohistochemistry of the perianal lesion showed CK7(-), CK20(+), and CAM5.2(+), supporting secondary EMPD of colorectal origin. Adenoma resection achieved negative margins (R0), with no invasive malignancy on imaging or endoscopy. Given staged resection, histological continuity could not be confirmed, and the lesions were initially managed as independent entities. Wide local excision with VY flap reconstruction was subsequently performed. The excised specimen showed diffuse CK20(+) and CDX2(+) with focal CK7 positivity, suggesting a colorectal-type secondary origin. GATA3 was positive in the Paget lesion but negative in the adenoma; this isolated discordant finding is discussed in the main text. The patient has remained recurrence-free for 3 years with preserved anal function. Focal CK7 positivity should not be interpreted as evidence against a secondary origin when CK20/CDX2 are diffusely coexpressed. When the precursor is suggested to be noninvasive, sphincter-preserving wide local excision with VY flap reconstruction appears feasible as an alternative to APR.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Arteriovenous malformations (AVMs) are generally considered congenital vascular anomalies, whereas postoperative iatrogenic AVMs and arteriovenous fistulas (AVFs) are rare. In colorectal surgery, newly detected aneurysm-like mesenteric vascular lesions during postoperative surveillance may be difficult to distinguish from aneurysms, pseudoaneurysms, AVMs, and AVFs. A 75-year-old woman underwent laparoscopic right hemicolectomy for transverse colon cancer. Preoperative contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) showed no vascular malformation or aneurysmal lesion. Six months after surgery, surveillance CT revealed a 3.8 mm aneurysm-like lesion in a peripheral branch of the superior mesenteric artery near the anastomotic site. Although the patient was asymptomatic and initially managed conservatively, the lesion enlarged to 6.7 mm over two years. Because a pseudoaneurysm with a potential risk of rupture could not be excluded, angiographic evaluation and treatment were performed. Angiography demonstrated three abnormal vessels arising from a terminal ileal arterial branch, early venous drainage into the ileal vein, and an associated venous aneurysm. The lesion was clinically diagnosed as an ileal AVM, although acquired AVF remained an important differential diagnosis. Transcatheter embolization using n-butyl cyanoacrylate was successful. This case suggests that AVM or AVF should be considered in the differential diagnosis of aneurysm-like mesenteric vascular lesions detected after colorectal surgery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
60% ~ 90% of patients with rectal cancer undergoing sphincter-preserving surgery experience persistent bowel symptoms, and patients also report varying degrees of social isolation. Those bowel symptoms are often particularly pronounced during the first month after surgery, when patients may also experience substantial challenges in resuming social participation. However, evidence regarding the association between bowel symptoms and social isolation remains limited, and the potential moderating roles of psychosocial resources are not well understood. To investigate the association between postoperative bowel symptoms and social isolation among patients with rectal cancer following sphincter-preserving surgery, and to further examine the moderating effects of perceived social support and psychological resilience. This secondary analysis used data from an ongoing prospective observational cohort study of patients with rectal cancer undergoing sphincter-preserving surgery at a tertiary hospital in China. Demographic and clinical characteristics, perceived social support, and psychological resilience were assessed preoperatively, while bowel symptoms and social isolation were assessed at the 1-month postoperative follow-up. Baseline and 1-month postoperative data were used in this study. Spearman correlation analysis and hierarchical multiple linear regression analysis were performed to examine the association between postoperative bowel symptoms and social isolation. Simple slope analysis and Johnson-Neyman (J-N) analysis were conducted to evaluate the moderating roles of perceived social support and psychological resilience. A total of 351 patients were included in the final analysis. Postoperative bowel symptoms were significantly and positively correlated with social isolation ( Postoperative bowel symptom burden was positively associated with social isolation among patients with rectal cancer following sphincter-preserving surgery. Higher perceived social support and psychological resilience were associated with weaker bowel symptom-social isolation relationships. These findings support an integrated supportive-care approach that combines bowel symptom management with psychosocial and social support to address postoperative social isolation and facilitate social functioning.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor budding (TB) is a histopathological marker of tumor aggressiveness and an established prognostic factor in colorectal cancer. In rectal cancer, however, TB is usually assessed on biopsy or resection material, and a reliable result may not be available when preoperative management is being considered. To develop and internally validate a radiomics model for preoperative discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB in patients with rectal cancer who proceed to upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC, with alternative feature sets and algorithms evaluated exploratorily. This retrospective study included 139 patients with pathologically confirmed rectal cancer who had received no neoadjuvant treatment. TB was assessed on postoperative resection specimens. T1WI, T2WI, arterial-phase contrast-enhanced T1WI, and DWI were analyzed. Radiomics features were extracted from the tumor core, a combined tumor-plus-2-mm expansion, and an isolated external 2-mm ring. Seven feature sets and four machine-learning algorithms were evaluated; the primary model was selected according to the highest repeated cross-validation AUC. Feature filtering, imputation, selection, and scaling were performed within the training portion of every split. Model performance was estimated using stratified five-fold cross-validation repeated five times and patient-level out-of-fold (OOF) probabilities. The primary core-ROI Elastic Net model achieved a repeated cross-validation AUC of 0.825 (range 0.809-0.839 across repetitions), with PR-AUC 0.781, sensitivity 0.604, specificity 0.851, and Brier score 0.173. Its patient-level mean OOF AUC was 0.829 (2,000 paired bootstrap replicates; 95% CI, 0.755-0.896). At a probability threshold of 0.50, patient-level sensitivity was 0.607 and specificity was 0.867. In conditional paired bootstrap comparisons, the core model showed higher AUCs than the clinical, peritumoral-ring, clinical-plus-expanded, clinical-plus-core, and clinical-plus-core-plus-ring models (BH-adjusted P = 0.004-0.005). The difference versus the expanded ROI was smaller and did not reach statistical significance after adjustment (P = 0.052). Multiparametric MRI radiomics features from the tumor core showed promising internal discrimination of low-grade versus intermediate/high-grade TB among patients who underwent upfront surgery without neoadjuvant treatment. The model may support preoperative TB risk stratification in this population, but external validation is required before clinical use.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperative surgery (LECS) enables accurate intraluminal localization and limited full-thickness resection while preserving gastrointestinal continuity. Although LECS has been used for selected primary duodenal tumors, its application to a postoperative duodenal recurrence of colorectal cancer has rarely been described. We report a case of localized duodenal recurrence after a right hemicolectomy that was completely resected using laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperation. An 83-year-old man underwent a laparoscopic right hemicolectomy with a D3 lymph node dissection for advanced ascending colon cancer. Histopathological examination demonstrated a microscopically positive dissected margin on the duodenal side, indicating a microscopically positive margin (R1) resection. Nine months later, surveillance upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and contrast-enhanced CT revealed a solitary lesion in the second portion of the duodenum without distant metastasis or radiological pancreatic involvement. Endoscopic ultrasonography showed a lesion extending to the fourth layer. An upper gastrointestinal contrast study was not performed; instead, the location and local extent of the lesion were assessed by upper gastrointestinal endoscopy, endoscopic ultrasonography, and contrast-enhanced CT. Because the multimodal assessment indicated that complete local excision was technically achievable, LECS was performed. Intraoperative endoscopy delineated a wider intraluminal extent than was apparent from the serosal surface and guided an en bloc full-thickness resection. The defect was closed in the short-axis direction by a continuous full-thickness suturing. Intraoperative endoscopy confirmed the luminal patency and a negative leak test. Histopathological examination showed an adenocarcinoma involving the submucosa and muscularis propria without duodenal mucosal involvement. The adjacent muscularis propria was inverted toward the lumen, suggesting inward progression from the outer aspect of the duodenal wall. Together with the previous R1, these findings supported a localized recurrence from microscopic residual disease. The resection margins were negative, and the patient has remained disease-free for more than 5 years. Laparoscopic and endoscopic cooperation enabled precise definition of the recurrent lesion, complete full-thickness local resection, and secure closure while preserving duodenal continuity. This approach may be useful for strictly localized duodenal recurrence when careful preoperative assessment indicates that complete local excision is achievable.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colonoscopy is the gold-standard screening test for colorectal cancer, yet its diagnostic yield relies heavily on adequate bowel preparation. Despite standard protocols, 20%-30% of procedures still have inadequate cleansing, which lowers adenoma detection, prolongs procedures, increases repeat examinations, and wastes resources. Preparation quality is influenced by multiple interacting factors: patient characteristics (age, comorbidities, medication use, adherence), regimen features (purgative type, dose, split-dose scheduling), and healthcare delivery (education quality, appointment timing). Most previous studies have examined these factors in isolation, leaving a gap in integrated, evidence-based guidance. This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on determinants of preparation quality, with emphasis on emerging strategies such as risk-stratified protocols, low-volume purgatives, digital health tools (mobile apps, SMS reminders), and AI-based real-time assessment. We aim to provide a practical framework for individualized preparation, thereby improving both the efficiency and quality of colonoscopy-based screening.

Ezetimibe is an FDA-approved orally administered drug that blocks intestinal cholesterol uptake, thereby reducing plasma cholesterol levels. Previous studies in our lab showed that ezetimibe binds the MDM2-p53 binding domain and may reactivate p53 in cancers. In p53-mutant HT-29 and SW620 cells, treatments had no significant effect, reinforcing p53-dependent sensitivity. In vivo early pharmacokinetics showed rapid clearance of ezetimibe and curcumin in co-administration. In the orthotopic CRC model, the combination of ezetimibe and curcumin was associated with modest late reduction in tumour bioluminescence from day 47 onward, indicating tumour size reduction that was not seen with ezetimibe treatment alone during the post-treatment observation period. The ezetimibe-curcumin combination reduces tumor burden in vivo, demonstrating its therapeutic potential. These preliminary findings suggest the ezetimibe-curcumin combination as a potential anticancer therapeutic and support further studies with optimized dosing and schedules. Currently, an in vivo preclinical study using holofibre technology is underway to determine pharmacokinetics and assess treatment effectiveness across several cancer types, with particular focus on Mdm2-overexpressing cancers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy is associated with cardiovascular events in patients with colorectal cancer, yet validated tools for pre-treatment cardiovascular risk stratification are lacking. Cardiac biomarkers are not routinely incorporated into baseline assessment and prospective evidence supporting their use remains limited. Our aim was to determine whether baseline high-sensitivity troponin T (hs-TnT) provides prognostic information for major adverse cardiovascular events during chemotherapy in patients with colorectal cancer. Within a prospective single-center observational cohort study at the Department of Internal Medicine and Hematology, Semmelweis University, consecutive patients with histologically confirmed newly diagnosed or recurrent colorectal cancer scheduled to receive 5-fluorouracil (5-FU)-based chemotherapy were enrolled between September 1, 2020, and June 2, 2024. Baseline hs-TnT concentrations were measured before treatment initiation, and patients were followed for the occurrence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs). Independent predictors of MACE were identified using penalized multivariable logistic regression. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis evaluated the discriminatory performance of baseline hs-TnT and determined the optimal cut-off value using the Youden index. Adequacy index analysis assessed the relative prognostic contribution of hs-TnT to the multivariable model. 180 patients were enrolled, with a median follow-up of 185 days, 44 patients (24.4%) experienced MACE, more than half of them occurred within the first two cycles of chemotherapy. Baseline hs-TnT demonstrated modest discrimination for predicting MACE (AUC 0.628, 95% CI 0.513-0.742). The optimal hs-TnT cut-off was 14 ng/L. In a multivariable analysis, elevated baseline hs-TnT (OR 2.35 per +10 ng/L, 95% CI 1.37-4.05) and Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor (VEGF)-inhibitor therapy (OR 2.38, 95% CI 1.23-4.60) were associated with MACEs. In a sensitivity analysis, excluding treatment-related hypertension from the composite endpoints, elevated baseline hs-TnT remained the only independent predictor. According to the adequacy index analysis, hs-TnT contributed 38.3% of the total prognostic information provided by the multivariable model. Baseline hs-TnT was independently associated with MACEs in patients with colorectal cancer receiving fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy. Although its discriminatory performance as a standalone biomarker was modest, hs-TnT provided incremental prognostic information for baseline cardiovascular risk assessment and may help identify patients who warrant closer cardiovascular surveillance.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
People with pre-existing mental health disorders (PMHD) often have lower cancer screening uptake and later-stage diagnoses. It remains unclear whether these disparities persist within highly accessible universal healthcare systems without strict gatekeeping. We simultaneously investigated the associations between PMHD and both screening participation and stage at diagnosis of breast and bowel cancers within the Taiwan health service. Using nationwide National Health Insurance and Cancer Registry data covering over 99% of the population, we compared outcomes between individuals with and without PMHD. Propensity score matching was applied for the screening cohort. Adjusted odds ratios were estimated using logistic regression, with subgroup analyses for severe PMHD. Overall, PMHD was associated with higher screening participation (adjusted odds ratios [aOR]: breast = 1.04, bowel = 1.12) and reduced odds of metastatic disease at diagnosis (breast = 0.72, bowel = 0.93), although the magnitude of these associations was modest, particularly for bowel cancer. Conversely, individuals with severe PMHD had significantly lower odds of screening (breast = 0.81, bowel = 0.88) despite high outpatient use. Furthermore, while the severe group retained reduced odds of metastatic breast cancer at diagnosis (aOR = 0.79), they showed no staging advantage for bowel cancer. While Taiwan's highly accessible universal healthcare system may contribute to a surveillance effect benefiting the general PMHD population, significant disparities persist for individuals with severe illnesses. Targeted interventions, procedural simplifications for self-administered tests, and multidisciplinary person-centred care models, may be needed to ensure health equity.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the treatment landscape of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet response remains heterogeneous. The inflammation-nutrition prognostic score (INPS), defined as the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) divided by the prognostic nutritional index (PNI), integrates systemic inflammatory burden and nutritional-immunological reserve and may provide complementary information in locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). We retrospectively analyzed 312 patients with LARC who received standard neoadjuvant chemoradiotherapy (nCRT), with or without concurrent PD-1/PD-L1 blockade, followed by total mesorectal excision (TME). Pretreatment INPS was calculated as NLR/PNI. The primary endpoint was objective response rate (ORR); secondary endpoints included pathological complete response (pCR) and progression-free survival (PFS). ROC, logistic regression, interaction, sensitivity, and Cox analyses were performed. Among 312 patients, 94 (30.1%) received ICI-containing regimens. Low INPS (<0.058) was associated with higher ORR (61.3% vs. 29.4%, P < 0.001) and pCR (38.7% vs. 11.8%, P < 0.001). INPS yielded an AUC of 0.765 (95% CI: 0.714-0.816) for ORR, compared with 0.712 for NLR, 0.668 for PNI, and 0.660 for PD-L1 CPS. In multivariable analysis, low INPS (OR = 3.31, 95% CI: 1.95-5.60, P < 0.001), MSI-H/dMMR status (OR = 4.67), PD-L1 CPS ≥ 10 (OR = 2.74), lower clinical T stage (OR = 3.15), and an ICI-containing regimen (OR = 2.55) were independently associated with response. A forced-entry disease-burden sensitivity model confirmed the association of low INPS (adjusted OR = 3.04, 95% CI: 1.74-5.30, P < 0.001). Low pretreatment INPS was independently associated with favorable response and PFS in LARC and provided incremental discrimination beyond MSI-H/dMMR and PD-L1 CPS. These findings support INPS as a candidate response-associated biomarker in LARC; prospective and external validation is warranted before routine clinical application.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colitis-associated colorectal cancer (CAC) is a serious long-term complication of inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) that develops through a chronic inflammation-dysplasia-carcinoma sequence. Persistent mucosal inflammation promotes epithelial barrier disruption, oxidative and genotoxic stress, dysregulated repair, and immune remodeling, thereby creating conditions that favor malignant transformation. Neutrophil extracellular trap (NET) formation and PANoptosis-an inflammatory programmed cell-death process integrating pyroptotic, apoptotic, and necroptotic machinery-represent two potentially interconnected components of this inflammatory environment. This narrative review examines the biological links between NETosis and PANoptosis in CAC, with emphasis on NET-derived nucleic acids, histones, myeloperoxidase, neutrophil elastase, reactive oxygen species, damage-associated molecular patterns, pattern-recognition receptor signaling, and cytokine networks. We further discuss microbiota-derived metabolites, candidate biomarkers, and therapeutic implications. Importantly, evidence is considered according to disease context: findings demonstrated in CAC are distinguished from mechanistic observations derived from IBD, sporadic colorectal cancer, and other inflammatory or tumor models, which are used to identify biologically plausible but not yet CAC-validated connections. Current data support bidirectional links between neutrophil activation and inflammatory epithelial cell death, but direct demonstration of a complete NETosis-PANoptosis feedback loop in human CAC remains limited. By bringing together these previously dispersed lines of evidence, this review clarifies where the NETosis-PANoptosis relationship is supported, where it remains inferential, and which molecular intersections may be most relevant for biomarker development and therapeutic investigation in CAC.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) is characterized by pervasive genomic instability, yet the molecular mechanisms linking replication stress responses to genome alteration and phenotypic evolution remain incompletely understood. Here, we performed an integrative multiomics analysis combined with functional validation to investigate the role of CLSPN, a key adaptor of the ATR-CHK1 pathway, in CRC. Machine learning-based feature selection identified CLSPN as a robust prognostic factor. Single-cell and spatial transcriptomic analyses revealed that CLSPN is preferentially enriched in highly proliferative tumor cell populations and spatially localized within tumor core regions. Elevated CLSPN expression was strongly associated with increased copy number variation burden (FGA, FGG, and FGL) and chromosomal instability, indicating enhanced tolerance to replication stress and accumulation of genomic alterations. This genomic instability was further linked to remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Functional assays demonstrated that CLSPN promotes proliferation, invasion, and migration while suppressing apoptosis in CRC cells. Collectively, these findings identify CLSPN as a key regulator of replication stress-driven genomic instability and highlight its role in shaping mutation-associated tumor evolution, providing a potential target for therapeutic intervention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Tumor antigens provide the molecular interface between malignant transformation and host immunity, but their biological significance is determined by more than their molecular existence. Antigen clonality, abundance, processing, human leukocyte antigen (HLA) presentation, dendritic-cell function, T-cell recognition, spatial immune organization, and the surrounding tumor microenvironment (TME) collectively determine whether an antigen becomes immunologically visible and therapeutically actionable. Across cancer progression, tumor-cell antigenic states and the TME undergo reciprocal selection: immune pressure can eliminate highly visible clones while favoring antigen-loss variants, HLA defects, immune exclusion, suppressive myeloid and stromal states, and treatment-resistant populations. Recent single-cell, spatial and three-dimensional imaging, as well as immunopeptidomic studies show that this evolution is heterogeneous across tumor regions and anatomical compartments rather than a uniform linear process. This review therefore advances an antigen-TME co-evolution framework linking primary tumors, lymphatic and nodal immune compartments, systemic dissemination, distant metastatic niches, therapy, minimal residual disease, and recurrence. It critically evaluates the strengths and limitations of the classical immunoediting model; compares melanoma, breast, colorectal, lung, prostate, sarcoma, and virus-associated cancers according to antigen source, clonality, presentation competence, immune architecture, and dominant therapeutic bottleneck; and examines clinical translation through checkpoint blockade, cellular therapy, vaccines, antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, immunopeptidomics, and computational antigen prediction. Particular attention is given to the gap between predicted peptide binding and verified presentation or immunogenicity, the need for longitudinal rather than single-biopsy profiling, and the requirement for prospective validation of artificial-intelligence models. The central conclusion is that tumor antigens become clinically meaningful only when antigenic state and microenvironmental context are assessed together, providing a more rigorous foundation for precision cancer immunotherapy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) and mismatch repair-deficient (dMMR) cancers are enriched for dependence on Werner syndrome RecQ helicase (WRN), a synthetic-lethal vulnerability mechanistically linked to expanded TA-dinucleotide repeats, non-B DNA structures, and replication-associated genome instability. However, WRN dependence is not universal among dMMR/MSI-H tumors, indicating that MSI status is an enrichment biomarker rather than a complete predictor of biological dependency. In this review, we synthesize recent advances in WRN structural and molecular pharmacology, with particular emphasis on colorectal cancer, where the strongest functional and pharmacological evidence currently exists. We distinguish four translational biomarker layers: pretreatment predictors of WRN dependency, target-engagement and DNA-damage pharmacodynamic markers, early treatment-response biomarkers, and acquired-resistance markers. We further examine reversible and covalent WRN inhibitors, mechanisms of primary and therapy-emergent resistance, immune and replication-stress-based combinations, and the expanding early-phase clinical landscape. Rather than proposing quantitative WRN dependency as a new biological concept, we present an evidence-graded pharmacological framework that links established substrate biology with drug exposure, target engagement, downstream DNA damage, treatment response, and resistance evolution. This framework may guide prospective biomarker development in MSI-H/dMMR colorectal cancer while identifying the evidence still required for broader application across other gastrointestinal malignancies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gut microbiota contributes to intestinal homeostasis through dynamic interactions with epithelial, immune and stromal cells. Disruption of the balance, often termed dysbiosis, has been associated with colorectal cancer (CRC). At the same time, selected commensal bacteria have shown protective effects. Toll-like receptors (TLRs) provide an important molecular interface through which host cells detect bacterial components and initiate cellular responses. This Mini Review examines current evidence that intestinal bacteria and their products modulate TLR signaling in CRC, with effects that may promote or restrain tumor development. The reported mechanisms involve CRC cells as well as immune and stromal compartments within the tumor microenvironment. The available evidence does not support assigning a fixed biological effect to a bacterial species or TLR. Instead, the reported outcomes appear to vary with the nature of the bacterial stimulus, the responding cell and the disease setting. Resolving this context dependence may clarify how host cells translate bacterial stimuli through TLRs into responses that influence CRC progression and treatment response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Early-onset colorectal cancer (EOCRC) impairs the health of China's working-age population and causes substantial socioeconomic costs. National long-term epidemiological data integrating trend segmentation, risk attribution and medium-term forecasting for domestic EOCRC remain insufficient. This study analysed China's 33-year EOCRC burden (1990-2023), identified trend inflection points, quantified modifiable risk-attributable burden and predicted epidemic trends to support tiered prevention strategies. Data on EOCRC burden among Chinese residents aged 15-49 were derived from the Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study 2023. We analyzed absolute cases and age-standardized rates of incidence, mortality, DALYs and prevalence. Joinpoint regression detected segmented nonlinear trends, and Autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models projected burden for 2024-2040. Dietary, metabolic and behavioural risk-attributable burden was quantified. From 1990 to 2023, national EOCRC mortality and DALY burden decreased continuously, whereas incident and prevalent cases increased significantly. Gender and age gradients existed: males and residents aged 45-49 carried the highest disease burden with slower improvement. Low milk and whole grain intake were the leading risk contributors, while high processed meat and high BMI showed rapidly rising attributable burden. All four burden indicators presented multi-stage trends and rebounded after 2020. ARIMA forecasts indicated age-standardized mortality and DALY rates would keep decreasing by 2040, yet male-dominated burden gaps remain prominent. China's EOCRC presents divergent long-term burden trends and stable age-sex disparities. The high burden in the 45-49 age group supports prioritizing this population for further screening evaluation, and male-oriented lifestyle interventions may help curb growing incidence and alleviate youth colorectal cancer burden.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
To systematically summarize the best available evidence on intraoperative barrier and no-touch techniques for the prevention of surgical site infection (SSI) in adult patients undergoing gastrointestinal (GI) surgery, and to provide an evidence base for developing standardized clinical practice protocols. Guided by the "6S" evidence model, a systematic literature search was conducted across multiple databases from their inception to March 1, 2026. The search encompassed all evidence pertaining to intraoperative barrier and no-touch techniques in GI surgery, including guideline organization websites (WHO, CDC, NICE, SHEA/IDSA, APIC, GIN, NGC, SIGN, RNAO, and medlive.cn), evidence-based databases (The Cochrane Library and JBI Evidence Synthesis), the trial registry ClinicalTrials.gov, and the databases PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, CINAHL, CBM, CNKI, VIP, and WanFang. Included studies comprised guidelines, expert consensus statements, evidence summaries, systematic reviews, narrative reviews, and randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Quality assessment, data extraction, and evidence grading were independently performed by two researchers trained in evidence-based nursing. A total of 18 publications were included: 5 guidelines, 3 expert consensus statements, 1 evidence summary, 3 systematic reviews, 3 narrative reviews, and 3 RCTs. Thirty best-evidence statements were synthesized across six domains: no-touch isolation technique (NTIT)-derived contamination control, intraoperative aseptic barrier precautions, intraoperative wound protection, selection of intraoperative irrigation solutions, intraoperative temperature management, and surgical teamwork and instrument management. This evidence summary provides a standardized, SSI-focused framework for barrier and no-touch practices in GI surgery. High-level evidence supports wound protectors, mechanical bowel preparation plus oral antibiotics in elective colorectal surgery, and intraoperative normothermia, whereas most NTIT-derived contamination-control practices are supported mainly by expert-consensus evidence and are recommended conditionally (Grade B). Clinical translation should be guided by the FAME (Feasibility, Appropriateness, Meaningfulness, and Effectiveness) framework and tailored to local hospital conditions and individual patient characteristics to minimize the risk of SSI.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal adenomas (CRAs) are the primary precancerous lesions in the development of colorectal cancer; establishing a simple, cost-effective and non-invasive tool for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy is of great significance for risk stratification. To investigate the association between peripheral blood metabolic and inflammatory markers and the risk of colorectal adenomas, and to develop a personalised risk prediction model for distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy. This study was a single-centre retrospective case-control study conducted at the Affiliated Hospital of Shandong Second Medical University. The study included 2,437 patients with colorectal polyps who underwent endoscopic resection between January 2020 and December 2025. Demographic characteristics, lifestyle factors and peripheral blood biochemical markers, with a particular focus on the triglyceride-to-glucose (TyG) ratio and markers of systemic inflammation. Patients with colorectal adenomas confirmed by histopathology. Model performance was assessed using the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), calibration curves and decision curve analysis (DCA). The study included 2,437 participants (mean age 58.57 years; 1,323 men [54.29%]), patients in the adenoma group (n=1,584) were significantly older and had a higher proportion of men compared with the control group (n=853). Multivariate logistic regression analysis revealed that male sex (OR, 1.621; 95% CI, 1.269-2.074), age ≥56.5 years (OR, 1.868; 95% CI, 1.515-2.205) and a TyG index ≥8.562 (OR, 1.271; 95% CI, 1.015-1.590) were independent risk factors for the development of colorectal adenomas. The AUC of this predictive model was 0.631 and 0.607 in the training and validation sets, respectively, indicates moderate discriminatory power. The model is well calibrated; analysis of the decision curve shows that, across a range of threshold probabilities, the model yields a positive net benefit compared with strategies involving either universal treatment or universal non-treatment. The findings suggest that male gender, advanced age and an elevated TyG index are independently associated with the risk of colorectal adenomas. The non-invasive nomogram developed in this study provides a simple risk stratification tool to aid in distinguishing adenomatous from non-neoplastic polyps in patients already scheduled for or undergoing endoscopy.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health challenge, with rapidly rising incidence in low- and middle-income countries, including Ethiopia. Survival outcomes are compromised by late-stage presentation, limited therapeutic capacity, and weak post-treatment follow-up. Although survival analysis is critical for characterizing CRC prognosis, insufficient attention has been given to the performance and validity of commonly applied survival models in Ethiopian populations, particularly when statistical assumptions are violated. To identify key clinical and treatment-related prognostic factors influencing overall survival among Ethiopian CRC patients and to assess the robustness and interpretability of Cox proportional hazard model (Cox PH model), stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty model, and Accelerated Failure Time (AFT) models, focusing on model adequacy under assumption violations. We conducted a retrospective cohort analysis of 161 colorectal cancer patients diagnosed between 2012 and 2016. Survival probabilities were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis, with group comparisons via log-rank tests. Multivariable modeling employed Cox proportional hazards, stratified Cox proportional hazard model, frailty, and accelerated failure time models. Model adequacy was evaluated through Akaike Information Criterion, concordance indices, and the Global Schoenfeld test for proportional hazards assessment. The Cox proportional hazard model violated the proportional hazards assumption (global p = 0.043), primarily due to histological subtype effects, indicating that the standard Cox proportional hazard model was not appropriate for this dataset. Assumption violations were mitigated using the stratified Cox proportional hazard model (global p = 0.122). Among accelerated failure time models, the log-logistic distribution provided superior model fit (AIC = 649.88; concordance = 0.724). Time-ratio (TR) interpretation showed that surgery extended survival by approximately 2.4-fold, whereas elevated baseline carcinoembryonic antigen levels and metastatic disease reduced survival duration by nearly half. Elevated carcinoembryonic antigen, distant metastasis, vascular invasion, and squamous cell histology were consistently associated with poorer prognosis, while surgery and chemotherapy remained protective across models. Rigorous model checking indicates that the conventional Cox proportional hazards model is inappropriate for this cohort due to proportional hazard assumption violations. Accelerated failure time modeling, particularly the log-logistic form, offered improved fit and clearer time-based interpretation of covariate effects. These findings underscore the importance of model validation in CRC survival research and highlight the need for improved early detection, surgical access, and targeted management of aggressive tumor subtypes to enhance patient outcomes in Ethiopia.
