ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Claudin 18, a tight junction protein, has emerged as a therapeutic target in various gastrointestinal cancers, notably gastric adenocarcinoma. However, its prevalence and clinicopathological significance in colorectal cancer (CRC) remain incompletely understood. In the current single-center, retrospective, immunohistochemical study, the prevalence and prognostic value of Claudin-18 was investigated in CRC. Claudin-18 expression was detected in 15.9% (17/107) of CRC cases, with negative/weak expression in 84.1% (90/107). No significant associations were observed between Claudin-18 expression and age, sex, tumor site, T stage, lymph node status, distant metastasis, TNM stage, histological subtype, or lymphovascular invasion (all p > 0.05). No significant associations were identified between Claudin-18 expression and age, sex, tumor location, histological subtype, or TNM stage. Furthermore, Claudin-18 expression independently predicted survival outcomes in CRC where Kaplan-Meier analysis demonstrated significantly worse overall survival (OS) in patients with strong/moderate Claudin-18 expression compared with Claudin-18 -negative/weak expression (log rank test, p = 0.024). Mean OS was markedly longer in Claudin-18 -negative/weak expression group (121.0 vs.76.6 months). Progression-free survival (PFS) analysis demonstrated a trend toward poorer outcomes among patients with increased Claudin-18 expression; however, the difference did not reach statistical significance (log-rank test, p = 0.066). Event-free survival (EFS) was also significantly reduced in patients with strong/moderate Claudin-18 expression (log-rank test, p = 0.022). Mean EFS was markedly longer in CLDN18 negative/weak expression (93.1 vs. 31.1 months). Multivariable binary logistic regression showed that the overall model was statistically significant (χ2(7) = 22.657, p = 0.002). However, none of the evaluated variables-including gender, age, lymphovascular invasion, tumor laterality, TNM stage, MSI status, histological type, and Claudin-18 expression-was independently associated with the outcome (all p > .05). Claudin-18 expression was not a significant predictor in the adjusted model (p = 0.931; OR = 0.63). In conclusion, despite its low prevalence in the current cohort, Claudin-18 expression was associated with poorer overall survival; however, its independent prognostic value was not established.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colon ischemia is the most common form of intestinal ischemia, yet case identification in epidemiological research remains challenging due to heterogeneous diagnostic criteria and absence of a specific International Classification of Diseases (ICD) code. The use of SNOMED (Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine) for gastrointestinal biopsies and surgical specimens enables a unique possibility to identify colon ischemia cases. In this validation study, 231 individuals with SNOMED code M54 (necrosis) and colorectal topography codes (T67-T68) were randomly selected from five Swedish regions. Medical charts were retrieved for 204 cases, where 143 contained sufficient information for evaluation. Cases were classified by clinical overall assessment and assigned an etiological group. Positive predictive values (PPVs) were calculated for overall colon ischemia based on histopathology alone and for etiological subsets where histopathology was combined with ICD codes. Of 143 patients with sufficient clinical information for validation, histopathological ischemic injury of the colon was confirmed in 141, corresponding to a PPV of 99% (95% CI, 95-99%). Combining SNOMED codes with selected ICD codes yielded a PPV of 84% (95% CI, 73-92%) for clinically confirmed idiopathic colon ischemia, increasing to 92% (95% CI, 79-98%) when more restrictive ICD-based criteria were applied. SNOMED-based histopathological case identification demonstrated a very high PPV for ischemic injury of the colon but could not distinguish idiopathic disease from ischemia secondary to identifiable clinical conditions. Combining SNOMED and ICD codes provides a feasible and reproducible strategy for identifying underlying causes of colon ischemia in Swedish nationwide health registers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed the management of mismatch repair-deficient/microsatellite instability-high (dMMR/MSI-H) colorectal cancer (CRC), yet the ~95% of patients with mismatch repair-proficient/microsatellite-stable (pMMR/MSS) disease derive little benefit owing to an immunologically "cold" tumor microenvironment (TME), poor T-cell infiltration, myeloid dominance, TGF-β-enriched stroma, and the systemically immunosuppressive milieu imposed by hepatic metastases. Clinically tested combinations-multikinase inhibitor plus anti-PD-1, Fc-enhanced dual checkpoint blockade, chemotherapy- or antiangiogenic-ICI regimens-have so far produced modest, largely non-durable response rates that are further attenuated in liver-metastatic disease, motivating approaches that pharmacologically remodel the TME rather than only release checkpoint restraint. To provide an evidence-stratified synthesis of nanotechnology-enabled immunotherapy in CRC that explicitly separates (a) clinically established evidence, (b) strategies under early-phase clinical investigation, and (c) concepts that remain preclinical or are extrapolated from other tumor types, and to derive from this appraisal a biomarker-enriched translational research agenda. Narrative, integrative (non-systematic) review. PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and ASCO/ESMO/AACR proceedings were searched from January 2010 through April 2026. Each strategy was appraised according to the highest available level of evidence, the tumor type and model system in which the evidence was generated, and its demonstrated CRC specificity. In current clinical practice, nanomedicine in CRC is essentially limited to nanoparticle-formulated cytotoxics exploited for pharmacokinetic advantage (e.g. liposomal irinotecan), whereas nano-enabled immunotherapy is confined to a small number of early-phase trials-most notably lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-formulated individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccines in ctDNA-positive resected CRC and hafnium-oxide nanoparticle radioenhancers-none of which has yet demonstrated a progression-free or overall survival benefit in MSS CRC. Against this background we critically appraise six classes of strategy: (i) LNP-based mRNA neoantigen vaccines; (ii) polymeric and inorganic nanocarriers for STING and TLR agonists; (iii) tumor-associated macrophage-repolarizing nanoparticles; (iv) nano-radiosensitizers and photothermal/photodynamic platforms priming immunogenic cell death; (v) nano-formulated checkpoint inhibitor delivery; and (vi) locoregional nano-strategies directed at hepatic metastasis-specific immunosuppression. For categories (ii)-(vi) the supporting evidence is predominantly murine (largely subcutaneous CT26/MC38 models) or extrapolated from immunologically "hot" tumors such as melanoma and non-small-cell lung cancer, in which both the underlying biology and the checkpoint backbone differ materially from MSS CRC. Recurrent translational barriers include low, highly heterogeneous nanoparticle accumulation in human tumors, dense TGF-β-rich stroma and elevated interstitial pressure, mononuclear phagocyte system clearance, liver-metastasis-specific tolerance that subcutaneous models do not reproduce, unresolved manufacturing/CMC and regulatory pathways, and the absence of validated pharmacodynamic biomarkers of intratumoral immune conversion. Nanotechnology offers a mechanistically coherent and experimentally testable-but at present clinically unproven-set of strategies for converting "cold" MSS CRC into immune-responsive disease. We therefore position nano-enabled immunotherapy as a research priority rather than an imminent standard of care, and argue that its clinical value can only be established through biomarker-enriched, paired-biopsy early-phase trials with pharmacodynamic endpoints of immune conversion and prospective stratification by metastatic site (particularly hepatic involvement) and consensus molecular subtype. This is a narrative rather than systematic review; it is therefore subject to selection and publication bias, and much of the evidence synthesized is preclinical and of limited direct translational certainty.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a leading cause of global cancer mortality, with gut microbiota (GM) dysbiosis playing a critical role in its pathogenesis. Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) offers a holistic, multi-target approach and has shown increasing promise in CRC prevention and treatment through GM modulation. This review systematically proposes the "TCM-GM-CRC" axis and elucidates seven interconnected mechanisms through which it mediates the anti-CRC effects of TCM: Reshaping microbial balance by inhibiting pathogens and enriching probiotics; repairing intestinal barrier integrity through upregulation of tight junction proteins and mucin production; suppressing oncogenic and pro-inflammatory signaling pathways by pathogenic bacteria; remodeling the tumor immune microenvironment through immunocyte regulation; modulating microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, and tryptophan derivatives; intervening in CRC cell metabolic reprogramming, including aerobic glycolysis and aberrant lipid metabolism; and inhibiting epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis. Key herbal formulas and active compounds discussed include Canmei Formula, Wu Mei Wan, Gegen Qinlian Decoction, Banxia Xiexin Decoction, and Pien Tze Huang, as well as single compounds such as berberine, evodiamine, curcumin, ginsenoside Rh4, and sophocarpine, which exert anti-CRC effects through distinct GM-mediated pathways. We emphasize the synergistic and multi-dimensional role of TCM in targeting GM and its functional metabolites to combat CRC. To deepen the understanding of the "TCM-GM-CRC" interaction mechanisms, future research should integrate multi-omics technologies, germ-free models, fecal microbiota transplantation, and clinical translation. Additionally, the development of "TCM-plus" combinatorial strategies, microbiota-targeted nanodelivery systems, and medically formulated foods is advocated to advance CRC precision prevention and treatment centered on GM.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Bulk-tissue transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) have identified colorectal cancer (CRC) susceptibility genes, but cell-type-specific regulatory mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we performed single-cell TWAS integrating matched germline genotypes and single-cell transcriptomes from normal colorectal mucosa (381 donors) and polyps (84 donors), cell-type-specific chromatin accessibility, and GWAS from 132,261 cases and 1,752,398 controls. We identified 546 gene-cell-type associations implicating 347 candidate susceptibility genes across seven normal and nine polyp epithelial populations, including 213 previously unreported genes, with 74% exhibiting cell-type-specific associations. Integrated co-expression and ChIP-seq analyses revealed distinct TF-risk gene networks, highlighting GATA6, MAX and RAD21 in normal mucosa, and TFAP4- and CEBPB-associated networks in premalignant polyp populations. Further multi-omics analyses supported dysregulation of 233 genes (67%), while drug-target analyses identified 63 potentially druggable genes. DepMap and CRISPR Cas9 analyses implicated 35 genes in CRC cell viability. These findings reveal cell-type-specific susceptibility mechanisms and prioritize candidate therapeutic targets for CRC prevention.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background: LGR5 and ANXA1 are markers for specific intestinal stem cell states. LGR5+/ANXA1- crypt base columnar cells (CBCs) maintain homeostasis, whereas ANXA1+/LGR5- regenerative stem cells (RSCs) are present in fetal and repairing epithelium. Both states have been described in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their clinical significance remains unclear. We aimed to determine how ANXA1 and LGR5 expression relates to molecular subtype, immune microenvironment and outcome in CRC. Methods: Dual-colour in situ hybridisation for ANXA1 and LGR5 was performed on tissue microarrays from 2163 patients in the randomised SCOT trial (ISRCTN59757862). AI-based digital pathology quantified marker-positive area by compartment and image based consensus molecular subtype (imCMS). Markers were related to clinicopathological, molecular and immune data, and to survival using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox analyses. Results: ANXA1 and LGR5 showed inverse enrichment among a diverse group of parameters. ANXA1 was highest in CMS1 and LGR5 in CMS2, with CMS3 and CMS4 being intermediate. ANXA1 dominance was associated with right-sidedness, mismatch repair deficiency, BRAF-V600E mutation, high stromal content, T4 stage, low stromal FoxP3 and high epithelial CD68 density. Combining both markers improved prognostic discrimination compared with either alone (cancer-specific survival p<0.001; recurrence-free interval p=0.004), with ANXA1 dominance remaining an independent predictor of recurrence after adjustment (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.08-1.90, p=0.014). Conclusion: Relative ANXA1 enrichment defines an aggressive, stroma-rich, macrophage-enriched CRC subgroup with poor prognosis.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Andrographolide, a labdane diterpenoid isolated from A. paniculata has been investigated for activity in a broad panel of biological contexts, including its anti-inflammatory, antiviral, and anticancer properties. Previously, A-ring analogs of andrographolide bearing silyl and trityl ethers at C19 have demonstrated improved in vitro anticancer activity in human cancer cell lines, with putative activity through the Wnt1/{beta}-catenin signaling axis. In order to investigate the activity of this series of C19 andrographolide analogs, alongside a cyclic A-ring acetonide analog, as anticancer agents in murine cancer cell models, we evaluated antiproliferative activity of these compounds in B16F10 melanoma, CT26 colorectal adenocarcinoma, Neuro2a neuroblastoma, and 4T1 mammary ductal carcinoma cell lines, and found that most compounds exhibited potent micromolar level anticancer activity. Among these, all trityl ethers exhibited nearly indistinguishable IC50 values of 4-20 M, and generally exhibited greater potency compared to C19 silyl ether analogs. This anticancer activity was further validated through apoptosis flow cytometry, wherein we concluded that our compounds induced apoptosis to a greater extent than the parent compound, andrographolide. Further, we examine the role of modulation of canonical Wnt1/{beta}-catenin signaling in a series of co-delivery assays with CHIR-99021, a selective GSK-3{beta} kinase inhibitor, and MSAB, a selective {beta}-catenin degrader. Finally, we demonstrate that a selection of silyl ether analogs of andrographolide elicit cell cycle arrest by flow cytometry in a manner that is decoupled to in vitro potency trends. Altogether, we report the first in vitro evaluation of trityl and silyl ether analogs of andrographolide within murine adherent cancer cells.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Intraperitoneal delivery of nanoparticles (NPs) holds promise in the treatment of peritoneal metastases (PM), and the use of electric fields may enhance their tissue penetration. Evaluating NP delivery requires evidence of intracellular payload release, which is challenging in autofluorescent tissues. Here, we combined electromotive drug administration (EMDA) with cationic RL-100 NPs co-loaded with doxorubicin (DOX) and a near-infrared aza-BODIPY tracer, reporting carrier-associated distribution, while phasor fluorescence lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) characterized the molecular environment of DOX. In colorectal carcinoma, NP-delivered DOX progressed from cytoplasmic puncta to nuclear accumulation, while carrier-associated fluorescence remained cytoplasmic, supporting intracellular release. EMDA enhanced NP penetration in ex vivo human peritoneum and healthy rat peritoneum. In a syngeneic rat model of colorectal PM, both free and NP-delivered DOX remained detectable to approximately 1200 um after EMDA, compared with < 200 um after passive delivery. NP-delivered DOX remained detectable 24 h after EMDA. Whole-animal and ex vivo imaging showed the highest carrier-associated signals in tumor nodules and tumor-bearing omentum. These findings support electrically enhanced intraperitoneal delivery and a dual-reporter approach to evaluate carrier distribution, drug penetration, and intracellular release, with potential applications in other autofluorescent tissues. Together, these capabilities provide a preclinical basis for investigating NP-assisted delivery.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Modern spatial proteomic methods, such as multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) imaging, offer a data-rich view of spatial biology in intact tissues. However, interpreting its complexity is a major bottleneck, limiting its potential for biological discovery and clinical translation. Current computational methods often rely on segmentation-based approaches that discard crucial morphological information and are limited to testing pre-defined hypotheses. Here, we introduce a self-supervised learning (SSL) framework that enables hypothesis-agnostic, context-aware discovery of biomarkers directly from mIF images. Our approach extracts rich feature representations that capture holistic architectural patterns, which integrate cellular morphology, marker interactions, and microenvironmental context without human supervision. Applying this framework to over 7,000 mIF tissue images from over 1,800 patients in two distinct cancer types, we demonstrate superior prognostic performance over conventional segmentation analyses. The method autonomously identified previously unknown and potentially clinically actionable biological patterns. In lung adenocarcinoma, these include a Ki67-mediated immune evasion phenotype, a subcellular pattern of GLB1 expression which aligns with low-grade EGFR-driven tumours, and distinct modes of tumour-immune interaction in PD-L1+ patients. We also find a regulatory T-cell-mediated immunosupressive environment promoting tumour budding in colorectal carcinoma. Our work establishes SSL as a powerful, scalable, and unbiased platform to decode tissue ecosystems while being fully explainable without pre-defined hypotheses. This paradigm shift transforms high-plex imaging from a hypothesis-testing tool into a hypothesis-generating engine that can accelerate the discovery of next-generation spatial biomarkers.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Brain metastasis is a significant cause of patient morbidity and mortality. There is increasing evidence that genomic instability features such as aneuploidy are associated with metastases to the brain and other organs. We analyzed the genomic instability of brain metastases among different cancer types. This included brain metastases from non-small cell lung, breast, melanoma and colorectal cancer. Our study identified a significantly higher degree of genomic instability in colorectal brain metastases compared to the other types of brain metastases. Nex, we examined the brain metastases for the types of aneuploidy events, namely chromosomal arm imbalances that involved gains or losses. Colorectal cancer brain metastases had specific chromosomal arm imbalance profiles that included gains of 13q and 20q which were significantly more frequent compared to the other cancer types. We examined other colorectal cancer metastatic sites in the lung, liver, lymph nodes and the primary colon. Examining colorectal cancer metastases more closely, aneuploidy gains across either arms for chromosomes 7 and 16 were also higher among brain metastases compared to liver, lung and lymph node metastases. Overall, this study shows that colorectal cancer brain metastasis has specific aneuploidy profiles different than other cancer types as well as being different among other metastatic organ sites.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
The gut microbiome encodes disease-relevant information not only in the abundance of individual taxa and functions, but in the way they co-occur and interact. Yet metagenomic analyses have largely relied on univariate approaches that evaluate features in isolation, systematically overlooking the combinatorial signals that arise from meaningful, disease-informative patterns of microbial co-occurrence. Here, we introduce a framework based on the Multidimensional Feature Selection (MDFS) algorithm to identify synergistic feature pairs - combinations of taxa and functions in which the information carried by a feature significantly increases in the presence of a partner. This includes features which carry no detectable individual information and may therefore be overlooked by univariate analyses. We first validated the approach on a meta-analysis of colorectal cancer (CRC) cohorts - one of the most competitive microbiome classification benchmarks available - using a leave-one-cohort-out cross-validation framework. Classifiers built solely on our synergy-derived features achieved performance comparable to the state-of-the-art benchmark (AUC = 0.84 vs 0.85). This confirmed that we were able to capture an informative disease signal while revealing microbial interactions not provided by univariate methods. A subset of the pairs was repeatedly selected by the models during feature selection, which indicated their stability. Post-selection effect size analysis revealed their consistent differences between cases and controls. To learn more about diseases beyond CRC, we extended our framework to 13 additional datasets spanning inflammatory bowel disease, cardiometabolic disease, liver cirrhosis and atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. We identified 80,790 synergistic pairs in eight of them as well as a set of candidate markers recurring across independent cohorts. Overall, synergistic pairs carried substantially more information about disease status than their individual constituents. Our framework therefore established meaningful microbial co-occurrence patterns which would not be possible with univariate methods alone. The framework is freely available at https://github.com/Kizielins/MDFS_synergies. Importance Most microbiome studies search for individual gut bacterial species associated with disease. However, bacteria do not act in isolation, and their combined presence or relative balance may be far more informative than any single microbe considered alone. This study presents a computational framework which identifies pairs of gut microorganisms whose co-occurrence or relative abundance carries significantly more information about disease status than their importance alone. Applied to stool metagenomic data from patients with colorectal cancer, as well as individuals with other conditions, we demonstrate that these synergistic interactions are: 1) widespread; 2) reproducible across independent patient cohorts; 3) and resolve disease-relevant microbial relationships which single-feature analyses do not report. Our framework offers a more complete view of how the gut microbiome is altered in disease and provides a principled basis for identifying robust, interaction-based biomarkers.

HELIOS: A spatial omics-informed multi-organ cell atlas enables AI-based tumour microenvironment profiling and biomarker discovery from routine histopathology
medRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-29 · Shen, Z.; Hu, H.; Braeutigam, K.; Wang, J.; Rodriguez-Justo, M.; Hawkins, M. A.; Collins Fekete, C.-A.
意义与启示：该研究将空间组学信息迁移至常规H&E图像，实现可扩展的单细胞级肿瘤微环境分析，为肠癌（含肝转移）的预后分层和生物标志物挖掘提供了无需额外检测的AI工具。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Spatial omics defines tumour microenvironments with high biological resolution but remains difficult to scale across large clinical cohorts. We developed HELIOS (H&E Learning Informed by Omics and Spatial Profiling), which transfers spatial-omics-derived cell identities into routine haematoxylin and eosin histology for interpretable single-cell tumour microenvironment profiling. HELIOS integrates 12.9 million cells from 60 specimens across 13 tissue types and four spatial profiling platforms, spanning eight epithelial, immune, stromal, and vascular populations. The resulting multiclass detector generalised across independent histopathology benchmarks. Applied to colorectal, breast, and lung cancers, HELIOS recapitulated molecular subtype-associated microenvironment states and identified prognostic immune and stromal phenotypes. Tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes were consistently associated with favourable outcomes, whereas neutrophil and fibroblast phenotypes showed cancer-specific associations. HELIOS-derived features remained prognostic after adjustment for clinicopathological and molecular variables. These findings demonstrate that spatial omics can provide scalable biological supervision for extracting clinically relevant tumour microenvironment features from routine H&E, supporting scalable risk stratification and biomarker development across clinical cohorts and retrospective pathology archives.

Spatialsnake: a flexible workflow for spatial transcriptomics analysis across platforms
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-29 · Lin, Z.; Zhang, Z.; Huang, N.; Lu, Z.; Xu, S.
意义与启示：该工作流支持多平台空间转录组分析，可灵活选择细胞群或组织区域，为结直肠癌肝转移的空间异质性研究提供工具。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background: Spatial transcriptomics technologies measure gene expression at different spatial resolutions and generate diverse data outputs. Existing workflows support a range of platforms and analyses, but combining methods and extending analyses to selected populations or tissue regions can require additional scripts and repeated data preparation. Findings: We developed Spatialsnake, a flexible workflow built on SpatialData and Snakemake for analysing processed outputs from Visium, Visium HD, Stereo-seq, Xenium and MERFISH. A common command-line interface supports single- and multi-sample analysis, with adjustable parameters and saved intermediate results. Users can select populations, tissue regions or distance-based neighborhoods, repeat clustering and annotation, and map refined labels back to the full dataset. Additional modules support cell-type composition estimation, spatial-domain identification, cell-cell communication inference, regulon analysis and sample-level comparisons. We demonstrate these functions using mouse-brain Visium and colorectal cancer Visium HD datasets. Joint analysis of three colorectal cancer sections retained 1,527,987 bins and enabled further analysis of 223,632 epithelial bins, linking epithelial subpopulation annotations to their locations within the complete tissue. Conclusions: Spatialsnake provides a unified workflow for spatial transcriptomics analysis across sequencing- and imaging-based platforms. Its flexible analysis modules support both whole-tissue analysis and further investigation of selected cell populations and tissue regions.

Ground-truth evaluation of sparse autoencoder features on spatial, single-cell and language-model embeddings
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-29 · Shahsavand, A.; Forghani, S.; Akbarzadeh, S.; Mahdavi Sabet, F.
意义与启示：可重复性不足以衡量SAE特征质量，需同时报告概念覆盖度与基因程序纯度；为肠癌空间/单细胞多组学特征提取提供方法学基准。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Sparse autoencoders (SAEs) are increasingly used to extract interpretable features from the embeddings of biological foundation models. Because SAEs trained with different random seeds learn different features, reproducibility across seeds has become a common test of whether these features can be trusted. We asked whether reproducible features are also meaningful, using embeddings whose concepts are known: five spatial transcriptomics embeddings of two colorectal cancer sections and Geneformer embeddings of single-cell RNA profiles, with cell lineages as concepts; synthetic data with planted cell states; and the residual stream of a small language model, with token classes as concepts. Varimax rotations of the same embeddings were almost perfectly reproducible, yet rotation features (PCA, varimax and ICA) covered at most three of seven lineages and three of eight token classes. Single SAE fits showed the opposite profile: they covered most concepts with purer gene programs but reproduced only 27-46% of their features. A consensus over five SAE fits combined the two strengths. It was reproducible (78-98% across sources) and as pure as single fits: 11-40% of its features carried marker genes of another lineage, against 44-70% for varimax. Against the strongest baseline, varimax sparsified to the SAE's sparsity, the consensus covered as many concepts on PCA and Geneformer embeddings and more on learned spatial and text embeddings. The consensus also had costs. It covered fewer lineages than single fits and, like all SAEs, missed weak planted states that rotations recovered; neither a longer single fit nor a second SAE trained on the consensus residual recovered what it discarded. Reproducibility alone therefore ranks features poorly: SAE features should be reported with the number of known concepts they cover and the purity of their gene programs, against a rotation of the same embedding sparsified to the SAE's sparsity.

Expanding the therapeutic window of bacteria for cancer therapy
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-29 · Im, J.; Komaranchath, M.; Windemuth, S.; Kim, H.; Hu, X.; Adapa, A.; Ashraf, M.; Cummins, K. A.; Coker, C.; Jang, Y.; Jin, H.; Leong, K. W.; Drapkin, R.; Bruce, J. N.; Canoll, P.; Danino, T.
意义与启示：该研究通过LPS修饰、缺氧-乳酸AND门控和脂蛋白缺失，将细菌最大耐受剂量提升1000倍，并在结直肠癌模型中实现75%完全缓解，为肝转移的细菌免疫治疗提供安全高效平台。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Engineered bacteria enable self-amplifying therapeutic delivery and immune activation, yet these same features drive systemic toxicity and off-target growth. Here, we create a "tumorobe" that overcomes these limitations by integrating reduced immunogenicity, tumour-restricted growth, and enhanced payload release. Specifically, we identify lipopolysaccharide modifications that reduce immunogenicity while preserving fitness, restrict growth to tumours using a hypoxia-lactate "AND" gate, and enhance extracellular payload release via lipoprotein deletion. This strain expands the maximum tolerated dose in a route-dependent manner by up to 1,000-fold. Across multiple murine models, including colorectal cancer and glioblastoma, the strain drives robust antitumour efficacy as both a standalone therapeutic and an immunotherapeutic delivery platform, achieving durable complete responses in up to 75% of colorectal tumours when armed with a cytokine payload. Together, these results establish a broadly applicable platform for safe and effective bacterial cancer therapy.

Hepatic Mitochondrial Alterations in GLP-1 Poor Responders Undergoing Roux-en-Y Gastric Bypass

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundThe expanding use of glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) has created a growing population of patients undergoing metabolic surgery after inadequate pharmacologic weight-loss response. Whether prior poor response is associated with distinct hepatic metabolic abnormalities or altered postoperative recovery is still unclear. Materials and MethodsIn this prospective observational study, 20 patients undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) were enrolled, including 10 patients with GLP-1 receptor agonist-refractory obesity (GRO), operationally defined as less than 5% total body weight loss after at least six months of adequate GLP-1 RA therapy, and 10 GLP-1 RA-naive patients (GNO). Five lean individuals served as hepatic reference controls. Paired liver biopsies obtained during RYGB and approximately six months postoperatively were evaluated using histology, BODIPY fluorescence, transmission electron microscopy, and Western blot analysis of AMPK-ACC signaling and mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation proteins. ResultsBaseline anthropometric and metabolic characteristics were broadly comparable between surgical cohorts. Nevertheless, GRO exhibited greater hepatic lipid accumulation, higher histological disease activity, more pronounced mitochondrial ultrastructural abnormalities, and reduced AMPK-ACC phosphorylation. Both cohorts achieved substantial six-month postoperative weight loss, although mean percentage total weight loss was lower in GRO than GNO (25.21% versus 29.51%). Paired tissue analyses demonstrated postoperative improvements in hepatic histology, lipid accumulation, and mitochondrial cristae integrity in both cohorts, with smaller improvements in GRO. Postoperative AMPK and ACC phosphorylation ratios remained lower in GRO, while mitochondrial protein analyses demonstrated complex-specific remodeling, including lower SDHB, UQCRC2, COX IV, and ATP5A abundance despite comparable NDUFS8 abundance at six months. ConclusionsPrior poor GLP-1 RA weight-loss response was associated with distinct hepatic histological, energy-sensing, and mitochondrial characteristics among patients undergoing RYGB. Although substantial surgical weight loss occurred in both cohorts, differences in hepatic tissue recovery and molecular profiles persisted at six months. These exploratory findings warrant validation in larger cohorts incorporating pharmacologic responders and direct mitochondrial functional assessments. HighlightsO_LIPoor GLP-1 receptor agonist response was associated with distinct hepatic metabolic abnormalities. C_LIO_LIPaired human liver biopsies enabled longitudinal assessment of hepatic remodeling after RYGB. C_LIO_LIGRO patients exhibited greater hepatic steatosis, mitochondrial disruption, and altered AMPK-ACC signaling. C_LIO_LIBoth cohorts achieved substantial weight loss, but hepatic histological and mitochondrial recovery was less pronounced in GRO. C_LIO_LIComplex-specific mitochondrial OXPHOS remodeling persisted six months after RYGB, despite postoperative improvement. C_LI

Cancer incidence in first-generation migrants and host populations in seven European registries, including Ukrainian-born migrants in Poland: a population-based study
medRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-28 · Alberts, C. C. J.; Georges, D.; Bray, F.; Ameijide, A.; Bordoni, A.; Carulla Areste, M.; Chirlaque Lopez, M. D.; Didkowska, J.; Galceran, J.; Van Herck, K.; Lanssens, A.; Migliore, E.; Ortelli, L.; Richiardi, L.; Sanchez Gil, A.; Verdoodt, F.; Visser, O.; Wojciechowska, U.; Gini, A.; Man, I.; Rosso, S.; Baussano, I.
意义与启示：移民癌症风险因出生国和癌种而异，出生国发病率可分层风险，提示肠癌筛查与预防需按移民来源国定制。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundWhere people are born shapes their cancer risk, yet European cancer surveillance rarely records migration background. We estimated cancer incidence in first-generation migrants and assessed whether birth-country incidence stratifies their cancer risk. MethodsWe harmonised data from six population-based cancer registries in Belgium, the Netherlands, Spain (Murcia, Tarragona), Italy (Turin), and Switzerland (Ticino) for 2003-17, examining breast, colorectal, cervical, stomach, liver, and lung cancer in first-generation migrants and host populations. Countries-of-birth were grouped into quartiles of GLOBOCAN age-standardised incidence by cancer site and sex (birth-country incidence categories). We estimated cumulative risks (CR) and migrant-to-host cumulative risk ratios (CRR). Ukrainian-born migrants in Poland were analysed separately for 2022-23. FindingsMigrants cancer risk increased with birth-country incidence for cervical, stomach, and liver cancer. For cervical cancer, CRR rose from close to 1 in migrants from low-incidence countries to 4{middle dot}9 (95% CI 3{middle dot}5-6{middle dot}9) in those from high-incidence countries in Turin. Breast and colorectal cancer diagnosis risk was lower than in host populations in every category. Across the six cancers combined, migrants had lower risk in 9 of 11 registry-sex strata, as lower breast, colorectal, and lung cancer risk outweighed higher cervical, stomach, and liver cancer risk. Ukrainian-born migrants in Poland (n=4450) had higher CR at most anatomical sites than the host population. InterpretationMigrants cancer risk relative to host populations depends on country of birth and cancer site. Birth-country incidence is a useful way of grouping migrants by risk. National averages can mask residual risk in subgroups, e.g. migrants born in high-incidence countries had up to five times the cervical cancer risk of host populations with rates near or below the WHO elimination threshold. Routine recording of country of birth can support risk-tailored prevention and cancer service planning for displaced populations. FundingZonMw-09150162210124; IARC-WHO; and participating cancer registries. RESEARCH IN CONTEXTO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSWe searched PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science from inception to Oct 15, 2026, without language restrictions, for population-based studies reporting cancer incidence among first-generation migrants in Europe compared with host populations. We used terms for migration (eg, "migrant", "immigrant", "country of birth"), cancer, and incidence. Existing studies specific on migrants in Europe remain sparse and fragmented, with most studies limited to individual countries, migrant groups, or cancer types. They differed in how migrants were grouped, in their reference populations, and in their methods, and often had small numbers per country of birth. A 2010 review reported higher incidence of infection-related cancers among migrants grouped as "non-western", and similar or lower incidence of breast and colorectal cancer, but heterogeneity prevented quantitative analyses. These differences have been attributed mainly to factors acquired before migration, notably infections, possibly compounded by differences in access to healthcare and preventive services, including lower participation in screening. Comparable estimates across European populations have been lacking. So has evidence on whether birth-country incidence can stratify migrants by cancer risk, and on what registries can capture after recent large-scale displacement. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first harmonised multi-country analysis to group first-generation migrants by cancer incidence in their country of birth, using data from population-based cancer registries. For cervical, stomach, and liver cancer, cumulative risk among migrants followed the incidence ranking of their countries of birth. For breast and colorectal cancer, it was consistently lower than in host populations, independent of the country of birth. In most settings, the combined burden of the six cancers was lower among migrants. Grouping countries of birth by publicly available national incidence estimates gives a first population-level picture of the cancer profile of migrant populations. A case study of Ukrainian-born migrants in Poland shows what registry data can and cannot analyse and describe after large-scale displacement. Implications of all the available evidenceRoutine recording of country of birth in cancer registries can generate evidence for equitable cancer control, supporting planning of prevention, screening and care services for settled and newly arrived migrants, particularly for infection-related cancers. The harmonised protocol and openly available analytic tools developed for this study can be applied by other registries for further research and routine surveillance. Harmonising migration-related data collection across European registries would strengthen surveillance and cancer service planning for displaced populations, and support equity-oriented cancer control policies.

Interval colorectal cancer risk by haemoglobin concentration in Australia's National Bowel Cancer Screening Program
medRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-28 · Ait Ouakrim, D.; Dowty, j.; McIntosh, J.; Goodwin, B.; Wilson, C.; Collins, K.; Ormiston-Smith, N.; Konn, P.; Austin, G.; Feletto, E.; Lew, J.-b.; Ladabaum, U.; Macrae, F.; Baxter, N. N.; Jenkins, M.
意义与启示：阴性FIT人群中，粪便血红蛋白接近20μg/g者间期肠癌风险升高近15倍，提示可据此风险分层并个体化调整筛查间隔。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
BackgroundInterval colorectal cancers (CRCs) are an important measure of screening performance. We assessed interval CRC risk after negative faecal immunochemical testing (FIT), its association with faecal haemoglobin (f-Hb) concentration, and differences by age and sex in Australia s National Bowel Cancer Screening Program (NBCSP). MethodsWe conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study linking Queensland screening and cancer registry records for NBCSP participants aged 50-74 years screened in 2018-2022. Eligible episodes had f-Hb below 20 ug/g in both samples. We excluded episodes with CRC diagnosed on or before follow-up start. Follow-up ended at CRC, the next screening episode, death, 24 months, or December 31, 2023. We estimated adjusted cause-specific hazard ratios (HRs), accounting for repeated episodes within participants, and cumulative incidence with death and subsequent screening as competing events. FindingsAmong 1,083,149 negative screening episodes from 700,734 participants, 586 interval CRCs occurred over 2,056,405 person-years. The incidence rate was 28.5 per 100,000 person-years, and 24-month cumulative incidence was 57.6 per 100,000 episodes (95% CI 53.1-62.5). Risk increased with age and was higher in males (adjusted HR 1.28, 95% CI 1.08-1.50). The complete-case quantitative cohort included 326,931 episodes and 138 cancers. Compared with maximum f-Hb of 0-5 ug/g, concentrations >15-<20 ug/g were associated with an adjusted HR of 14.93 (9.02-24.70). Corresponding 24-month risks were 35.7 (28.5-44.7) and 504.5 (323.4-787.0) per 100,000 episodes. Higher negative-range f-Hb concentrations were more common in older participants and males. The quantitative cohort showed no clear sex difference after adjustment for f-Hb. InterpretationCRC risk varies substantially among people with a negative screening result. Quantitative F-Hb levels may help identify who is at higher risk of interval CRC. Further research is needed to confirm these findings and assess the benefits, harms and costs of changing screening intervals. Research in contextO_ST_ABSResearch in contextC_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyWe searched PubMed October 2026, for Australian studies and international systematic reviews and meta-analyses, using combinations of "colorectal", "bowel", "interval cancer", "interval cancers", "interval colorectal", "negative FIT", "faecal haemoglobin", "fecal hemoglobin", "faecal immunochemical", and "fecal immunochemical", combined with "Australia", "Australian", "systematic review", or "meta-analysis". Additional searches examined international cohort studies published from January 1, 2020, to October 25, 2026. Australian national monitoring and a study in Western Australia showed that interval CRC was uncommon but more frequent among males and older participants. Both analyses were based on the 2018 screening cohort, before biennial screening had been fully implemented for all eligible people aged 50-74 years. Neither examined interval CRC risk across the negative f-Hb range. International reviews documented substantial variation in interval CRC incidence between screening programmes. More recent Danish and Dutch cohort studies showed that higher f-Hb concentrations below the positivity threshold were associated with greater interval CRC risk, including after successive negative screening rounds. A dose-response meta-analysis of 13 studies supported the prognostic value of negative-range f-Hb, but combined evidence on interval cancers, cancers detected at subsequent screening, and adenomas. These outcomes do not provide interchangeable estimates of risk before the next screen. The evidence therefore supported further investigation of quantitative f-Hb, but did not establish concentration-specific interval CRC risks for the NBCSPs two-sample protocol and 20 {micro}g/g positivity threshold. Added value of this studyThis study extends Australian evidence through longitudinal linkage of Queensland screening and cancer registry records from 2018-2022, including repeated screening episodes from more than 700,000 participants. It estimates interval CRC risk overall and by age and sex, and examines how that risk varies within the negative f-Hb range. Follow-up ended at the next screening episode, allowing interval cancers to be distinguished from cancers detected at later screening. The quantitative analysis showed a substantial concentration gradient in both relative and absolute risk, despite all included results being classified as negative. By providing absolute risks within the Australian screening setting, the study offers evidence directly relevant to evaluating whether participants with different negative f-Hb concentrations could benefit from different screening intervals. Implications of all the available evidenceA negative FIT result provides reassurance, but does not indicate the same level of interval CRC risk for every participant. Together, the international evidence and our findings support evaluating screening strategies that use quantitative f-Hb rather than relying solely on a positive or negative result in the Australian program. They do not establish which screening intervals or thresholds should be adopted. Further evaluation should determine whether tailoring screening reduces interval cancers and advanced disease without disproportionate increases in colonoscopy use, harms, or inequalities in access and outcomes.

Dense Longitudinal Multi Omics Reveals Microbial Metabolic Immune Succession During Immune Checkpoint Therapy
medRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-28 · Zandi, E.; Medetgul-Ernar, K.; Lenz, H.-J.; Alishahi, F.
意义与启示：单例结直肠癌肝转移患者纵向多组学揭示ICI应答伴随肠道微生物功能与免疫的时序演替，提示横断面研究可能遗漏瞬态功能状态，为肝转移免疫治疗机制研究提供新假设。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) can induce durable clinical responses, yet relationships among the gut microbiome, microbial function, intestinal metabolism, and host immunity remain incompletely resolved. We performed dense longitudinal multi-omics profiling of a single patient with colorectal cancer metastatic to the liver during ICI therapy and sustained tumor regression. Eleven serial stool samples spanning approximately 7.3 months were analyzed by 16S rRNA sequencing, microbial metatranscriptomics, metabolomics, lipidomics, and stool host-RNA immune profiling and aligned with serial clinical imaging. A major intestinal ecosystem transition accompanied the emergence of clinical response. Microbial abundance and transcriptional activity were frequently discordant, demonstrating that compositional profiling alone incompletely captured microbial dynamics. Taxon-resolved functional analysis revealed sequential microbial states rather than a single responder-associated configuration. Loss of early Bacteroides/Fusobacterium-associated functions accompanied purine/sphingolipid remodeling and changes in myeloid-associated immune signatures. At T5, a transient Bifidobacterium carbohydrate/fermentation program coincided with lactate/indole-3-lactate remodeling and broad adaptive T-cell, memory/regulatory, mucosal, and B-cell immune changes. At T6, marked Clostridium transcriptional emergence and lipid/coenzyme-A pathway activation coincided with fatty-acid/lysophospholipid remodeling and a distinct immune configuration. Historical HUMAnN reconstruction using original UniRef90 and MetaCyc resources confirmed taxon-specific, reaction-associated gene-family support for prioritized functional programs. These findings define a temporally ordered microbial-metabolic-immune succession during ICI response. Although this N-of-1 design cannot establish population generalizability, dense within-person multi-omics resolves transient functional states obscured by cross-sectional analyses and generates testable hypotheses for larger prospective cohorts and personalized studies of ICI response.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Cancer transcriptomes nominate many disease-associated long noncoding RNAs (lncRNAs), but functional prioritization remains difficult. Here, we integrated recurrent tumor upregulation, clinical association, co-expression network context, and malignant epithelial detectability across colorectal, gastric, and esophageal cancers, identifying five lncRNAs with convergent clinical and network support. We selected the intergenic lncRNA LINC01094 for functional characterization in colorectal cancer (CRC). Across 52 CRC cell lines, endogenous LINC01094 expression defined a transcriptional state linking higher expression to extracellular matrix, adhesion, and inflammatory programs and lower expression to DNA replication, mitochondrial, and ribosome/RNP programs. Acute CRISPR interference (CRISPRi)-mediated depletion in HCT116 cells produced a nearly inverse transcriptional response; among 764 GO terms significant in both analyses, 748 (97.9%) changed in opposite directions (Pearson r = -0.962). Functionally, LINC01094 depletion impaired cell growth in both HCT116 and Caco-2 cells. In HCT116 cells, depletion reduced DNA synthesis despite induction of replication-associated transcriptional programs and was accompanied by increased {gamma}H2AX, CHK1 Ser345 phosphorylation, and p21 accumulation without detectable apoptotic execution. {gamma}H2AX foci were also elevated within residual EdU-positive nuclei. The predominant LINC01094 transcript in HCT116 cells was nuclear-enriched, whereas SLPI, a reported effector of a cytoplasmic miR-1266-5p/SLPI ceRNA model in CRC, was not reproducibly altered following LINC01094 depletion in either CRC model. These findings link LINC01094 to maintenance of a CRC-associated transcriptional state and show that its acute disruption is accompanied by impaired productive DNA synthesis, replication-associated DNA-damage signaling, and checkpoint activation, supporting a broader, context-dependent role for LINC01094 beyond previously described pathway-specific models.

CBX3 Deletion Overcomes Ferroptosis Resistance in Colorectal Cancer by Targeting IFNγ/SLC7A11/SLC3A2 Axis
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-27 · Xiang, Y.; Fu, Y.; Desterke, C.; Batsche, E.; Jalil, A.; Elhage, R.; Duruel, C.; Beche, J.-C.; Frapy, E.; Skurnik, D.; Reisacher, C.; Christine, S.; Piaggio, E.; Arbibe, L.; Hamai, A.; CHANG, Y.
意义与启示：揭示CBX3表观调控IFNγ/STAT1/SLC7A11/SLC3A2轴维持氧化还原平衡以抵抗铁死亡，为肠癌（含肝转移）铁死亡联合治疗提供新靶点。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
System Xc- (SLC7A11/SLC3A2) maintains redox balance by supporting glutathione synthesis, thereby preventing lipid peroxidation and ferroptosis, and represents a promising therapeutic target in cancer. In this work, we revealed that an important epigenetic regulator, CBX3 deletion significantly increased intracellular ROS and lipid ROS level following ferroptosis inducing, particularly under IFN{gamma} stimulation, thereby sensitized CRC cells to ferroptosis in vitro using human CRC cells as well as in vivo using MC38 syngenetic tumors. RNAseq with mice syngeneic tumors revealed an 11-gene oxidative stress signature downregulated in Cbx3KO tumors after combined treatment; its low expression score correlated with improved overall survival in CRC patients. Among them, Slc7a11, Ptgs2, and Cth were identified as CBX3 direct target genes. Additionally, several amino acid transporters functionally coupled to Xc- antiporter, as Slc3a2, Slc7a5, Slc1a5 and Slc6a9, all significantly decreased in Cbx3KO tumor under RSL3+IFN{gamma} treatment. Mechanistically, CBX3 binds directly to the promoter of Slc7a11 or Slc3a2 to sustain their expression and redox balance to resist ferroptosis in CRC. Knockout of CBX3 in CRC cells significantly impaired RNA polymerase II recruitment to the promoter of SLC7A11 or SLC3A2 and reduced SLC7A11 and SLC3A2 expression, an effect that was further exacerbated under IFN{gamma} stimulation but restored by STAT1 deletion. Overall, CBX3 protects CRC from oxidative stress by maintaining the functional integrity of IFN{gamma}/STAT1/SLC7A11/SLC3A2 axis, positioning CBX3 as a potential therapeutic target for enhancing ferroptosis therapies in CRC.

靶向IGF2BP1通过破坏染色体乘客复合体致结直肠癌有丝分裂脆弱性
Targeting IGF2BP1 Creates a Mitotic Vulnerability in Colorectal Carcinoma
bioRxiv (预印本) · 2026-10-26 · Griesler, B.; Hagemann, S.; Winkler, R.; Wedler-Geyer, A.; Misiak, C.; Misiak, D.; Rausch, A.; Luetzkendorf, J.; Mueller, T.; Mir, K. U. I.; Ihling, C.; Otto, F. W.; Sinz, A.; Klusmann, J.-H.; Heuser, M.; Mueller, L. P.; Bley, N.; Huettelmaier, S.
意义与启示：揭示IGF2BP1通过转录后调控CPC维持有丝分裂完整性，为IGF2BP1阳性肠癌提供联合紫杉醇的精准治疗新策略。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Background Mitotic dysregulation is a common feature of colorectal cancer (CRC), yet the contribution of post-transcriptional mechanisms remain incompletely understood. We investigated how the oncofetal RNA-binding protein IGF2BP1 supports mitotic integrity and exposes therapeutic vulnerabilities in CRC. Methods We integrated patient cohort analyses with genetic and pharmacological perturbation of IGF2BP1, transcriptomics, proteomics, RNA-binding assays and functional studies. Xenografts assessed tumor formation, while BTYNB-paclitaxel responses were examined in CRC cell lines and patient-derived organoids. Results IGF2BP1 expression was elevated in CRC, increased with tumor stage, and associated with poor survival and proliferative gene signatures. Genetic depletion or pharmacological inhibition of IGF2BP1 impaired cell viability, induced mitotic abnormalities, and promoted apoptosis, whereas its re-expression enhanced tumor formation in vivo. Integrated molecular analyses identified the chromosomal passenger complex (CPC) as a previously unrecognized downstream target of IGF2BP1. IGF2BP1 bound transcripts encoding CPC components and its depletion consistently reduced their expression across multiple cancer cell models. BTYNB disrupted IGF2BP1 association with INCENP, CDCA8, and BIRC5 transcripts and accelerated INCENP mRNA decay. Functionally, INCENP depletion recapitulated the mitotic defects and impaired viability observed upon IGF2BP1 inhibition. Exploiting this mitotic vulnerability, BTYNB synergized with paclitaxel in CRC cell lines and across four independent IGF2BP1-positive patient-derived organoid models. Conclusions Our findings uncover an IGF2BP1-dependent post-transcriptional regulatory mechanism sustaining CPC expression and mitotic integrity in CRC. Targeting this mechanism exposes a therapeutically exploitable mitotic vulnerability and provides a rationale for combining IGF2BP1 inhibition with microtubule-targeting agents.

要点与启示：ctDNA是强预后标志物，但干预证据不一；需统一检测时机、动态解读与试验设计，避免在试验外据此决定治疗。
展开英文原题摘要与原文链接
ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Circulating tumour DNA (ctDNA) detection after curative-intent treatment is one of the strongest prognostic biomarkers in colorectal cancer (CRC), but its clinical utility remains incompletely established. Randomised trials have shown that ctDNA-informed management can reduce adjuvant chemotherapy exposure in selected stage II colon cancer, yet non-inferiority was not established in stage III disease, and cytotoxic escalation for ctDNA-positive molecular residual disease (MRD) has not improved recurrence-free survival. These mixed interventional results do not diminish the prognostic validity of ctDNA, but suggest that its clinical utility depends on four interacting considerations: the biological state represented by ctDNA positivity, the timing of testing and intervention, assay and sampling heterogeneity, and trial design. Serial ctDNA dynamics may provide additional biological and prognostic information, as sustained clearance, transient clearance, persistence, and re-emergence are unlikely to represent equivalent states of MRD. Western Pacific studies have led the field, including GALAXY and ALTAIR in Japan and Taiwan, DYNAMIC in Australia, FIND and CINTS-R in China, and CLAUDIA in Korea. However, regional implementation is constrained by uneven laboratory infrastructure, cost, regulatory access, and limited evidence from Southeast Asia and Pacific lower-resource settings. Outside clinical trials, ctDNA should refine prognosis rather than dictate omission, intensification, or initiation of treatment. Future trials should align assay performance, biological timing, and intervention mechanism, and use patient-centred endpoints capable of demonstrating that acting on ctDNA improves outcomes.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Racial/ethnic disparities in colorectal cancer mortality persist in the United States despite treatment advances. We examined racial/ethnic differences in guideline-concordant care (GCC) receipt and cancer-specific mortality, estimated the proportion of the Black-White disparity mediated through GCC, and tested for heterogeneity in the GCC-survival association across groups. Population-based cohort study using the Surveillance, Epidemiology, and End Results (SEER) Program. Adults with a first primary colorectal adenocarcinoma diagnosed 2010-2017 were included (N = 45,267). GCC was operationalized as a composite score (0-4) per NCCN recommendations. The primary outcome, cancer-specific mortality (CSM), was analyzed using Fine-Gray subdistribution hazard models. Race/ethnicity x GCC interactions were tested by likelihood ratio test; causal mediation decomposed effects into mediated and direct components. Among 45,267 patients (52% male), CSM occurred in 10,478 (23%) over a median 77 months. GCC receipt differed significantly across groups (all p < 0.001). Non-Hispanic Black patients had higher adjusted CSM than White patients (SHR 1.20, 95% CI 1.11-1.28); Asian/PI patients had lower CSM (SHR 0.86, 95% CI 0.78-0.95). A significant race x GCC interaction was identified (p = 0.0036), with a stronger GCC-CSM association among Black than White patients (interaction HR 0.907, 95% CI 0.847-0.971). GCC differences accounted for only 2.2% (95% CI 0.8-4.5%) of the Black-White disparity. Racial/ethnic disparities in colorectal cancer mortality were not substantially explained by differences in GCC receipt. A significant race/ethnicity x GCC interaction indicated that Black patients derived greater survival benefit per care component. Equitable care delivery is important but insufficient to eliminate persistent disparities; structural and social determinants must also be addressed.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Gastrointestinal cancer, particularly esophageal, gastric, or colon cancer, is a significant cause of morbidity and mortality in Mexico. There are substantial delays in the early identification and timely referral of primary care patients, resulting in more advanced-stage diagnoses and poorer clinical outcomes. Our aim was to issue a position statement from the Asociación Mexicana de Gastroenterología (AMG) to guide primary care physicians in the identification of alarm features, risk stratification, and timely referral of patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer. A multidisciplinary group of 20 specialists in the fields of gastroenterology, oncology, endoscopy, epidemiology, and public health, from both public and private institutions, developed the position statement through a structured consensus process. Clinical statements were drafted and voted on, they were organized by cancer type (esophageal, gastric, and colorectal), and three clinical algorithms were designed to support decision-making in primary care. Thirteen statements were issued on alarm features, risk factors, recommended diagnostic studies, and risk-stratified referral pathways (urgent, priority, and elective). The role of upper endoscopy and high-quality colonoscopy as diagnostic procedures of choice was emphasized, clearly distinguishing them from population-based screening strategies. This position statement provides a practical, evidence-based, expert consensus-informed guide, adapted to the Mexican healthcare setting, whose aim is to implement prevention strategies, reduce diagnostic delays, improve early detection, and optimize the referral of primary care patients with suspected gastrointestinal cancer.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is characterized by heterogeneous disease presentations and clinical courses. Accurate diagnosis and appropriate disease monitoring play an important role in improving long-term outcomes by preventing misdiagnosis and unnecessary treatment; enabling early detection of disease progression, treatment failure, and disease-related complications; and facilitating timely adjustment of treatment strategies. The Korean Association for the Study of Intestinal Diseases (KASID) developed guidelines for the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD in adults, reflecting the Korean clinical setting, to support clinical decision-making and improve the quality of patient care. To develop these guidelines, existing international clinical practice guidelines and expert consensus statements were comprehensively reviewed, along with updated evidence relevant to each clinical topic. Final recommendations were established through expert consensus using a modified Delphi process. These guidelines address major clinical areas in the diagnosis and monitoring of IBD, including initial diagnosis and baseline assessment, assessment of disease extent and activity, disease monitoring in ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, nutritional assessment, and colorectal cancer surveillance. These guidelines are intended to support individualized clinical judgment and should be applied flexibly, taking into account not only individual patient characteristics and clinical circumstances but also available resources, access to diagnostic and monitoring modalities, regulatory requirements, and reimbursement policies.

ABSTRACT（原文，未删改）
Peritoneal surface malignancies (PSM) are primary or secondary neoplastic deposits involving the peritoneum and are commonly associated with colorectal, gastric, appendiceal, gynecological, pancreaticobiliary, and other intra-abdominal or extra-abdominal cancers. Malignant bowel obstruction (MBO) is one of the most frequent and clinically consequential emergency presentations in this population, yet diagnostic and therapeutic pathways remain heterogeneous. We aimed to develop evidence-informed recommendations for emergency management of MBO in patients with PSM by integrating a systematic review, meta-analysis and a structured international expert consensus process. This systematic review, meta-analysis, and Delphi consensus followed PRISMA, Cochrane, and relevant MOOSE reporting principles. PubMed/MEDLINE and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to June 2025 (English language). Five predefined PICO/PIRT questions addressed: (1) the diagnostic role of CT, plain abdominal X-ray, or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; (2) nonoperative medical management versus surgical or endoscopic therapy; (3) surgical versus endoscopic treatment after failure of nonoperative management; (4) bowel resection versus stoma or bypass in surgical candidates; and (5) endoscopic stenting versus endoscopic ultrasound-guided bypass with lumen-apposing metal stents in endoscopic candidates. Study selection and data extraction were performed independently and in duplicate. Risk of bias was assessed with ROBINS-I for comparative non-randomized studies and MINORS for non-comparative studies; certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE. Random-effects meta-analyses (REML) produced odds ratios (OR), mean differences (MD), pooled means, or pooled proportions with 95% confidence intervals (CI); heterogeneity was summarized using I2, τ2, and 95% prediction intervals. Evidence profiles informed statements voted on by the WSES-PSOGI-SICO expert panel during the 2025 WSES Congress. No comparative diagnostic study evaluated abdominal X-ray or Gastrografin-enhanced X-ray in PSM-related MBO; two small retrospective CT-based series supported contrast-enhanced CT for mapping obstruction and excluding urgent complications, but no diagnostic meta-analysis was possible. For medical versus procedural treatment, medical management was associated with lower morbidity (OR 0.16, 95% CI 0.07-0.39) and shorter length of stay (MD - 9.48 days, 95% CI - 12.65 to -6.32), while success, mortality, and overall survival remained inconclusive. For surgery versus endoscopy, surgery showed higher clinical success (OR 2.57, 95% CI 1.47-4.50), whereas endoscopy shortened hospital stay (MD 3.35 days, 95% CI 1.46-5.23); mortality did not differ (OR 1.02, 95% CI 0.70-1.49). Among surgical options, resection showed a signal toward higher perioperative mortality than bypass or ostomy (OR 3.55, 95% CI 1.45-8.68). Endoscopic stenting showed a pooled clinical success rate of 0.71 (95% CI 0.62-0.79), whereas evidence on LAMS was limited to one retrospective study. All guideline statements reached 100% agreement among voting participants. Despite the low certainty of available evidence, integration of systematic review findings with expert consensus provides a structured international framework to support decision-making in emergency presentations of PSM-related MBO. These consensus-based recommendations are intended to assist clinicians in harmonizing care across peripheral and referral hospitals, while emphasizing individualized multidisciplinary judgement and the need for future higher-quality evidence.

本周热点与趋势总结

由本期文献提炼的课题组可执行信号
  1. 新辅助治疗策略在局部晚期直肠癌中取得重要突破。UNION III期试验（Lancet Oncology）首次评估短程放疗序贯卡瑞利珠单抗联合化疗对比标准治疗，主要终点病理完全缓解率显著提高（39.8% vs 15.3%），本次预设中期分析进一步显示无事件生存获益，支持该联合模式作为潜在新标准。
  2. ctDNA指导的微小残留病（MRD）管理成为早期结直肠癌精准治疗的核心议题。Cancer Pathogenesis and Therapy综述指出，术后MRD检测是强有力的独立预后标志物，可识别高复发风险患者并避免过度辅助化疗，但标准辅助化疗对MRD阳性患者的获益有限，亟需探索MRD驱动的治疗升级策略。
  3. 结直肠癌肝转移的机制研究持续深入。Iscience研究通过整合单细胞转录组、bulk RNA-seq及117种机器学习算法，鉴定出六基因机械敏感特征与肝转移相关；Journal of Gene Medicine报道RNA结合蛋白NOVA1通过稳定NRXN1 mRNA抑制免疫逃逸和肝转移，为CRLM提供了新的预后标志物和干预靶点。
  4. 表观遗传调控与代谢/自噬通路在结直肠癌进展中的作用受到关注。Clinical and Translational Medicine揭示PDLIM4启动子甲基化沉默通过 impairing BTF3自噬降解激活PI3K/Akt信号促进CRC，且粪便DNA检测PDLIM4甲基化具有无创筛查可行性；Cancer Medicine则发现PIK3C3在KRAS野生型与突变型晚期CRC中作用相反，影响5-FU敏感性和预后。
  5. 转移性结直肠癌后线治疗探索新组合。Cancer杂志报道脂质体伊立替康联合卡培他滨及贝伐珠单抗二线治疗mCRC的多中心单臂研究，显示该方案在奥沙利铂失败患者中具有可控的安全性和初步疗效，为伊立替康改良剂型的应用提供了临床证据。
  6. 肿瘤微环境与微生物组研究拓展了CRC预后评估维度。Cancer Medicine研究发现口腔致病菌共生体（P. stomatis、F. nucleatum sensu lato和P. micra）共定植与肿瘤免疫微环境改变及不良预后相关；UK Biobank前瞻性分析（Cancer Medicine）则揭示遗传风险与生活方式对早发型和晚发型CRC的关联存在年龄异质性，提示风险分层需考虑发病年龄。
